I_kwDOLUK0B86jJZJY.title: Relevance Augmentations
I_kwDOLUK0B86jJZJY.body: There's a few high impact elements to determine the relevance of a comment. Which is why in the default formatting scoring we have high ($5) credit per instance. ### image Relevance currently doesn't understand image contents. We can insert the image description inside of its "alt" attribute. ```html ``` ### link It could also be really interesting to pull the text contents from links to also score their relevance. We can insert a summary inside of its title attribute. ```html Example ``` ### code It would be interesting to discuss this in a separate proposal because this seems like it could be really complex to implement well. I_kwDOLUK0B86Q6xgM.body:

```
Originally posted by @0x4007 in https://github.com/ubiquibot/conversation-rewards/pull/58#discussion_r1691159526
```

So it will be a regex like `^Originally posted by @<username regex> in <url regex>$`

And when calculating the rewards, the original author should receive part of the author credit. Make it configurable with a percentage. I would default to 50% of the credit.

I_kwDOLUK0B86kf3pK.title: Transfers then Permits
I_kwDOLUK0B86kf3pK.body:
I would normally post this under the dedicated permit generation repo but it isn't live yet and it isn't clear how long that will be. 

We should make the default payments behavior to be a transfer and then render permits if the full payouts can't be afforded. 

For example, we have a low balance now and I haven't had the chance to top it up. If it can't afford all the payouts from that GitHub issue being closed, then it renders permits for everyone. 

However under normal circumstances we can afford to pay for everybody so it should do a direct transfer. 

This behavior should be able to be toggled as well- something like a reference to "automatic transfers mode"

This way, permits will never be fully phased out, but transfers would take precedence if the funding wallet can afford it.

I_kwDOLUK0B86qQAaK.body:

Excessive credit is being given to the author of the comment with any of those generated footnotes

https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-wallet/issues/47#issuecomment-2661604653

Do not count deduplicated footnotes.  I suppose we can target the `0` prefix in the footnote ID but it also makes me think we should think of a more robust targeting system for the future. In the near future, we should actually prefix the generated footnotes with something more precise like `dedupe-` or `no-credit` or even better, check the diff and only offer credit if the user wrote the link, not a bot. [^01^] 

If we can identify who wrote what, then we can extremely precisely reward credit where its due.

I_kwDOLUK0B86ps6wb.title: Review Incentives: Deleted Files
I_kwDOLUK0B86ps6wb.body:
Count the amount of removed lines for deleted files and subtract from the total lines changed count. 

The reason for this is because when reviewing it takes little/no cognitive overhead on the files view to skim over "file deleted" 

---

> Seems arbitrary and would eventually fail in some cases. It is complex to evaluate line changes because renaming a function for example could involve changing all the import across files and you would end with a +20 -20 for one rename.

This would yield $0.40 which isn't bad. 

The problem is that not every line changed takes the same cognitive overhead to process. 

Obviously most of the 17k removed was cypress code which can be easily reviewed just by reading "file deleted"

Perhaps we can reduce credit based on the deleted files removed line count. 

This will also solve for renames in case git doesn't catch it!

I_kwDOL-In886jLwQe.title: Improve Task Assignment Limit Handling
I_kwDOL-In886jLwQe.body:
**Problem**
Contributors are blocked from assigning new tasks due to the current task limit, even when they’ve addressed all open review threads and are waiting on reviewers. This bottleneck discourages contributors and slows down productivity.

**Proposed Solution**
1. Add logic to check if the assignee is the last commenter on all unresolved review threads. [^02^] [^01^]
2. Introduce a 24-hour timeout after the last comment before considering tasks "reviewer-lagged."
3. Allow contributors to bypass the limit in such cases without affecting their task slots.

**Concerns**
- Assignees might misuse this by "resolving" threads without addressing the issues.
- Additional safeguards may be needed to ensure resolution integrity.

**References**

- Original comment thread: [#100](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/issues/100#issuecomment-2535532258).

I_kwDOL-In887XwKKF.title: Re-open PR if re-assigned by admin
I_kwDOL-In887XwKKF.body:
Perhaps this is redundant but I've seen it a handful of times within the last few days.

- contributor submits PR
- user is ejected for deadlines or similar
- admin(s) decide to re-assign the contributor
- PR remains `closed` or it's re-opened and is stale due to commits pushed while `closed`
- in [this instance](https://github.com/ubiquity/stake.ubq.fi/pull/10) I'd expect to see the PR update automatically with the commits that the contributor pushed while `closed` (as is the case with [my own](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/185) I suspect)

---

1. If an admin re-assigns the contributor, automatically re-open their most recent PR.
2. I'm unsure (able to test it with my own PR #185 when it gets re-opened) if pushing a single new commit after it's re-opened will update all missing commits. However, if it does, then we should consider automating this too.

---

Outcomes:

1. We improve reviewer QOL. They re-assign and don't have to deal with telling the user they need to push a fresh commit or open a new PR.
2. We improve DX by automating the process of pulling in the most recent commits from that branch without them needing to force a commit just to refresh the PR for reviewers.

I_kwDOL-In887oecE7.title: Avoid redundant message information on start
I_kwDOL-In887oecE7.body:
## Overview
When a user is assigned to a task using the `/start` command, the assignment comment currently contains redundant information in both the user-facing table and the hidden structured metadata. Additionally, recent changes allowing time labels to be arbitrary are causing unwanted warning/errors about missing/unrecognized labels even when labels exist.

## Problem Statements
### 1) Redundant metadata in `/start` assignment comment
**Location:** `src/handlers/start/perform-assignment.ts` (approx. lines 50–76)

Currently:
- The visible assignment table (generated by `assignTableComment`) displays user-facing fields such as deadline, beneficiary/wallet, and warnings.
- The hidden metadata (generated via `logger.ok` and `structuredMetadata`) also includes fields that duplicate the visible content: `taskDeadline`, `taskAssignees`, `priceLabel`.

This duplication is unnecessary because the visible comment already exposes those values.

### 2) Unwanted warnings/errors about labels after making time labels arbitrary
After changing time labels to be “anything”, label validation/recognition is producing warning/errors on `/start` about missing labels when the labels are actually present but are unrecognized.

**Reference:** https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-disqualifier/issues/120#issuecomment-3868958145

## Goals
1. Ensure hidden metadata contains only technical/debug information not already visible in the user-facing comment.
2. Prevent spurious label-related warnings/errors when starting a task, especially in the context of arbitrary/custom time labels.

## Requirements
### A) Metadata de-duplication
- Remove redundant fields from the structured metadata/logging payload:
  - `taskDeadline`
  - `taskAssignees`
  - `priceLabel`
- Retain only non-redundant technical/debug metadata (examples):
  - commit revision hash
  - workflow execution context
  - internal processing details
- The visible assignment table must continue to display all necessary user-facing information (deadline, assignees/beneficiary, price, warnings).

### B) Label warning/error correction
- When `/start` is executed, do not emit warnings/errors that claim labels are missing if relevant labels exist on the issue/PR.
- Update label recognition/validation logic so that custom/arbitrary time labels do not trigger unwanted warning/errors solely because they are not recognized under a previous strict label set.
- Ensure warnings/errors are only produced when there is a real, actionable label problem (e.g., truly missing required labels), not due to overly strict parsing/recognition.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `taskDeadline`, `taskAssignees`, and `priceLabel` are removed from the hidden metadata/`logger.ok` structured metadata for `/start` assignment.
- [ ] Hidden metadata still includes only technical/debug details that are not already displayed in the visible assignment table.
- [ ] The visible assignment table comment content remains unchanged in terms of user-facing fields shown.
- [ ] `/start` no longer adds incorrect warning/error messages about missing labels when labels are present but previously unrecognized.
- [ ] Label validation supports arbitrary/custom time labels without generating unwanted warning/errors.

I_kwDOL-In886tw_bl.title: Expose Public API Endpoint
I_kwDOL-In886tw_bl.body:
For interoperability with https://devpool.directory/ and automatic task matchmaking assignment, we must host and expose a public API endpoint using Deno Deploy.

## Requirements

### Directory
When users log in, they should see only tasks they can start, considering task gating constraints. Users assigned to too many tasks should still see all directory tasks.

### Matchmaking
The system must select the top candidate for task assignment. If the top candidate is saturated with tasks, it should failover to the next best candidate.

### API Specification
- **Request Parameters**:
  - `userId` (number)
  - `issueUrl` (string)
  - `mode` ("validate" or "execute")
  - `userAccessToken` (optional)

### Repository Access Validation
- Validate GitHub App installation on target repositories
- Handle cross-repository access
- Graceful permission failure handling in development

### Dependencies
- Requires awareness of repository/organization configuration (resolved via merged feature in issue #54)

## Remarks
The public API approach replaces the git submodule solution due to Octokit's Node.js dependencies being incompatible with browsers. This provides a unified solution for both kernel and external consumers.

I_kwDOL-In887FInz-.title: Permanent Disqualifications
I_kwDOL-In887FInz-.body:
We should leave our tasks open and available for recruiting purposes. However there are clearly some contributors that take more resources than they add. The system should restrict them from their ability to participate.

We need a means to keep track of when the user is disqualified, and store a negative XP that corresponds with the wasted effort. [^01^]                         Perhaps we can store a "permit" with no permit details other than a negative amount. Not sure what makes the most sense given our current database architecture.

The simplest would be to store the task amount as a negative, but ideally we should actually calculate the sum total of the rewards that should have been paid out. For example if a contributor took the review time and effort from five other team members, we should sum total their rewards and count it as a negative to the contributor if they get disqualified.

When the user completes tasks successfully, we save their permit details in the database which can be used to calculate their positive XP.

In the config of this plugin, we should be able to set minimum XP to start based on priority levels and/or time levels.

Then we can do something like:

```
p0: -2000
p1: -1000
p2: 0
p3: 1000
p4: 2000
p5: 3000
```

We also should check the account age or activity so that we can't easily be Sybil'd. For example, the GitHub account must have activity from over a year ago to contribute.
[^01^]: ⚠ 75% possible duplicate - [Check For Unassigns; Disable Self Assigns](https://www.github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/issues/2#2)

I_kwDOL-In886h0Dyw.title: Add allowed roles to `requiredLabelsToStart`
I_kwDOL-In886h0Dyw.body:
There's the [requiredLabelsToStart](https://github.com/ubiquity/.ubiquity-os/blob/cde4662181090201af15fa2412b8fe2c60dc7f31/.github/.ubiquity-os.config.yml#L18) property which works this way:
1. User prints the `/start` command
2. https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop plugin checks that if the github issue (which user wants to self assign) contains at least 1 label from the `requiredLabelsToStart` config property then the plugin allows self assigning a github issue

We need a more sophisticated control over that parameter and want to support these use cases:
1. Collaborators (i.e. organization members) should be allowed to self assign only high priority tasks with longer time estimates
2. Outside contributors should be allowed to self assign only low priority tasks with lower time estimates

What should be done:
1. Refactor the https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop plugin to support specific roles for specific labels
2. Add unit tests for the features

Expected config (example):
```
        requiredLabelsToStart:
          time:
            - name: "Time: <1 Hour"
              roles:
              	- MEMBER
                - OUTSIDE_CONTRIBUTOR
            - name: "Time: <2 Hours"
              roles:
              	- MEMBER
                - OUTSIDE_CONTRIBUTOR
            - name: "Time: <4 Hours"
              roles:
                - MEMBER
            - name: "Time: <1 Day"
              roles:
                - MEMBER
            - name: "Time: <1 Week"
              roles:
                - MEMBER
          priority:
            - name: "Priority: 1 (Normal)"
              roles:
                - OUTSIDE_CONTRIBUTOR
            - name: "Priority: 2 (Medium)"
               roles:
                 - OUTSIDE_CONTRIBUTOR
            - name: "Priority: 3 (High)"
              roles:
                - MEMBER
            - name: "Priority: 4 (Urgent)"
              roles:
                - MEMBER
            - name: "Priority: 5 (Emergency)"
              roles:
                - MEMBER
```

P.S. Not sure if the `OUTSIDE_CONTRIBUTOR` role exists in the github API but there should be something similar

I_kwDOL-In886UYgdZ.title: Properly handle task limit
I_kwDOL-In886UYgdZ.body:
The original implementation allowed for productive contributors to work on two tasks concurrently. With a starting two task limit:
| Condition                                              | Task Adjustment       | Explanation                                                                                             |
|--------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| If any reviewer approved the pull                      | +1 task per pull      | It's likely that the pull is good, just waiting on other slow reviewers to confirm.                      |
| If reviewers take longer than 24 hours                 | +1 task per pull      | Don't wait for lazy reviewers to be able to start a new task.                                            |
| If any reviewer requested changes                      | -1 task per pull      | They should focus on addressing the changes as a top priority.                                           |

_Originally posted by @0x4007 in https://github.com/ubiquibot/command-start-stop/pull/19#discussion_r1731441502_
            

For the sake of this conversation a completed PR is when the conditions are met in the above table.

In the current state the code checks if any review is approved or if there is 0 reviews but 24 hours have passed since the creation of the PR, however it doesn't check if there's any requested changes so it will count it as completed even if there 1 approve and 1 requested changes.

There is still a problem when the reviewer requests changes and the contributor resolves those changes but waits for the reviewer to make a new review so they can't start another task.
There's two possible solutions: check if the reviewer was requested more than x hours ago or check that changes have been marked as solved

I_kwDOL-In886dZXe0.title: New config property `requiredLabelsToStart`
I_kwDOL-In886dZXe0.body:
Right now our main goal is to show investors that the project is capable of generating a revenue. 

So basically we need to concentrate on tasks related to:
1. Partner onboarding (i.e. [UbiquityOS Marketplace GUI](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer))
2. Charging fees
3. Making the kernel stable
4. Making core plugins stable

We have the following organizational issues right now:
1. All core team members are doing everything with a lack of focus. 
2. There's too much PRs to review (from outside contributors) and none-important issues (that don't "move the needle") to discuss.

For example check these issues:
- https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-sdk/issues/34
- https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel/issues/154

Although both of the issues above have the "Priority: 3 (High)" label in reality their business value is 1 (on a scale from 1 to 4). **The "Priority" label must reflect a business priority, not a development one.**

As a part of this issue we should add a new property `requiredLabelsToStart` which accepts an array of labels required to call the `/start` command.

Example config:
```
- plugin: http://localhost:4000 # or the URL where the plugin is hosted
  name: start-stop
  id: start-stop-command
  command: "\/start|\/stop"
  with:
    requiredLabelsToStart: ["Priority: 3 (High)", "Priority: 4 (Urgent)", "Priority: 5 (Emergency)"]
    # ...other props
```

In the example above it will be possible to start an issue only if it has required business priority labels.

When current issue is finished we'll:
1. Review all github issues and update the "Priority" label to reflect a business value
2. Set `requiredLabelsToStart: ["Priority: 3 (High)", "Priority: 4 (Urgent)", "Priority: 5 (Emergency)"]` for all of our organizations

This way we:
1. Shift core team focus only on issues that have a business impact
2. Reduce number of PRs to review and issues to discuss (because outside contributors will have to solve only high business priority issues)
3. Save money and time only to what matters

I_kwDOMBcers6UtmI6.title: Bot strings language localization

Original comment: https://github.com/ubiquibot/command-start-stop/pull/25#discussion_r1736233348

There may be [cases](https://github.com/ubiquibot/command-start-stop/issues/22) when partner would need to customize the plugin's text response to some commands. 

Possible use cases:
- different text messages for different business logic flows
- translation to other languages

It could be useful to keep a separate `json` file of used strings in the plugin repository. This way plugin developers would host `json` file in the plugin's repo while partners would be able to customize the whole "text strings" file without cluttering the config too much.

Example config with a new param `customStringsUrl`:
```
- plugin: http://localhost:4000
  name: start-stop
  id: start-stop-command
  description: "Allows a user to start/stop a task without negative XP impact"
  command: "\/start|\/stop"
  example: "/start" # or "/stop"
  with:
    reviewDelayTolerance: "3 Days"
    taskStaleTimeoutDuration: "30 Days"
    maxConcurrentTasks: 3
    startRequiresWallet: true
    ## ...
    ## ...
    ## NEWLY ADDED CONFIG PARAM
    customStringsUrl: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dev/new-pugin/development/strings.json
```

So as a part of this issue we should add a basic plugin config and an example usage of the `customStringsUrl` param so that future plugin developers could fork this repo and use configurable text messages instead of hardcoding them in the code.

I_kwDOMyHsAM6uEbN1.title: premade configs that are hands-off for partners
I_kwDOMyHsAM6uEbN1.body:
## Premade Configurations vs. Default Plugin Manifests

We aim to streamline the experience for pilot partners by providing **premade configurations**. This approach reduces the need for partners to manually configure plugins. In addition, we provide two alternative ways to modify configurations:

1. Utilize [this feature request](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugins-wishlist/issues/65).
2. Contact customer support for manual adjustments.

### Default Plugin Behavior

1. When a plugin uses `defaults` that are **not** sourced from a **premade config**, it retrieves its configuration from the plugin's `manifest.json` in its respective repository.
2. These defaults originate from `pluginInputs.ts` and are used across multiple infrastructure components, including:
   - This UI
   - Natural language configuration edits
   - Plugin schema and input validation (kernel-side)
   - Other relevant subsystems

#### Opinionated Defaults

There is a general concern about **opinionated defaults**. Instead of enforcing such defaults, we should **only share premade configs with partners**, eliminating the need for them to define their own configurations.

Reference: [Discussion on opinionated defaults](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/151#discussion_r1991092437)

### Configuration Modes

Currently, there are three configuration modes:

- **Minimal**
- **Full Defaults**
- **Custom**

These modes, up to this point, have not been enforced to be unopinionated. Some configurations are highly opinionated and may not align with the principle of **non-opinionated defaults**.

---

## Proposed Solutions

### 1. Establish a Collection of Premade Configurations
- Define a structured set of **premade configs**.
- Ensure each premade config abstracts its functionality at a high level.
- Reduce the cognitive load on partners.

### 2. YAML-Based Template Structure
To further simplify configuration management, I suggest we use a **YAML template** with the following structure:

```yaml
metadata:
  name: "UbiquityOS Standard Config"
  description: "The fully-enabled and battle-tested configuration which we use across all organizations at Ubiquity."
  version: "1.0"

plugins: ...
```

This template includes:
- **Metadata**: Describes the premade configuration.
- **Plugins**: Lists installed plugins with relevant settings.

This abstraction ensures partners **"don’t have to think about it."**

---

## Handling Plugin Expansion

### Default Non-Expanded Behavior
@gentlementlegen [suggests](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/issues/40#issuecomment-2670919061) that plugins should be installed in a **non-expanded state**. This means:

- **Infra fetches only the non-opinionated defaults** when retrieving the plugin’s manifest.
- **If plugin details are expanded**, infra should fetch its specific config **before** relying on the manifest.

### Supporting Only Premade Configs
If we only allow **premade configs** and restrict editing to **already installed plugins**, then:

- Each `premade` configuration will be expanded by default.
- This ensures we avoid relying on **non-opinionated defaults**, which may not align with intended user experiences.

---

## Conclusion

- **Premade configurations** should be the standard approach.
- A **YAML-based template** simplifies configuration abstraction.
- **Non-expanded installations** should default to non-opinionated configurations.
- **Expanded plugin configurations** should fetch predefined configurations before falling back to defaults.

By enforcing these principles, we create a **streamlined, user-friendly**, and **low-maintenance** approach to plugin configuration management.

I_kwDOMyHsAM6jvFl7.title: Set `organization/repository` names in the plugins' configs

Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel/issues/224

Plugin installer should always set `organization/repository` value in the config's [plugin](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/.ubiquity-os/blob/67df7f5643edcaa3899304481f7ff4ef74a1041a/.github/.ubiquity-os.config.dev.yml#L3) property for all of the plugins.

plugin installer UI should set `org/repo` value:
```
- plugin: ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings
```

I_kwDOMyHsAM6xG7v9.title: Allow Users to Select and Configure Specific Plugin Branches
I_kwDOMyHsAM6xG7v9.body:
Currently, the plugin installer GUI assumes users always want to configure and install the version of a plugin found on a single, predefined branch (initially hardcoded to `development`, later updated to the repository's default branch). However, plugins often have different versions, features, or configuration schemas across various branches (e.g., `main`, `development`, feature branches, release tags).

Users need the ability to explicitly select the desired branch for a plugin they are configuring, and the system must ensure that the correct manifest is used for rendering the UI and the correct identifier (Action reference or URL) is saved in the configuration file.

**Desired Behavior / Acceptance Criteria:**

1.  The configuration editor should display a dropdown allowing users to select from the available branches of the plugin's source repository.
2.  When editing an existing plugin configuration, the dropdown should pre-select the branch specified in the saved configuration identifier (`owner/repo@branch` or parsed from URL).
3.  When editing an existing plugin configuration, the editor UI should initially render based on the manifest fetched from the *configured* branch.
4.  When the user selects a different branch from the dropdown, the editor UI should dynamically update by fetching and rendering the manifest from the newly selected branch.
5.  When saving the configuration, the `plugin` identifier stored in the `uses` array must accurately reflect the user's selected branch:
    *   For Action-based plugins: `owner/repo@selectedBranch`
    *   For URL-based plugins: The correctly transformed URL corresponding to the `selectedBranch` (e.g., `https://...-selected-branch-suffix.domain.com`).
6.  UI elements should be consistent with the rest of the application.
7.  Informational/success toast notifications should auto-dismiss.

## Main issues

We will have problems saving different branches because it is technically correct to have two similar plugins pointing to two different branches. Similarly the plugin would not know we want to change the target branch but will instead stack plugins from different branches together.

I_kwDOMyHsAM6eqPpC.title: Predefined configs
I_kwDOMyHsAM6eqPpC.body:
Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/pull/13

Right now partner is able to setup bot config individually per plugin.

We should offer predefined configs so that instead of customizing each plugin individually partner could simply select a predefined config.

Simply put partner should be able to:
1. Setup each plugin individually (already implemented)
2. Create a new config from a predefined config template in one click

For the start I think we should support 2 config templates:
1. Config with all plugins from https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace and all default values
2. Minimal:
  - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop
  - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pricing
  - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards

Notice: the UI should support multiple predefined configs.

I_kwDOMyHsAM6fUNMp.title: Add parameter descriptions for core plugins in the `plugin-input.ts`
I_kwDOMyHsAM6fUNMp.body: Right now all core plugins have a `manifest.json` file ([example](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/blob/ee4f7c698f0e221381df7c73f56457e1ca4d22ea/manifest.json)) describing plugin's: - name - description - listeners - command examples - configuration parameters The issue is that when plugin configuration is displayed in https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer there're no any configuration parameter descriptions so it's really hard for a partner to find out what parameters are meant to be used for: What should be done for all of the core plugins in https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace: 1. Make sure the readme file is relevant (i.e. has a relevant config example and configuration parameter descriptions) 2. Make sure there's a `name` property in the `manifest.json` (some of the core plugins miss it) 3. Make sure there's a `description` property in the `manifest.json` 4. Add descriptions of plugin configuration parameters in the `plugin-input.ts` file (for example [this](https://github.com/Meniole/command-query-user/blob/042533ebbbfebaf5f5754b1d4a2fcf1d8afd94ad/src/types/plugin-input.ts#L7) code generates [this](https://github.com/Meniole/command-query-user/blob/ecb3c906d0e21b1557b23a8465fb2760b3f87abf/manifest.json#L16) manifest). Simply put we should add the `description` field for all of the plugin parameters in the `plugin-input.ts` file. Description should include general info and possible parameter options. Notice that in the `manifest.json` file the `configuration` schema is created dynamically: 1. [update-configuration.yml](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/blob/ee4f7c698f0e221381df7c73f56457e1ca4d22ea/.github/workflows/update-configuration.yml) workflow runs 2. Configuration schema is fetched from [plugin-input.ts](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/blob/ee4f7c698f0e221381df7c73f56457e1ca4d22ea/src/types/plugin-input.ts) 3. [manifest.json](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/blob/ee4f7c698f0e221381df7c73f56457e1ca4d22ea/manifest.json) is updated ([example commit](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/commit/56232c8c67d198cc46cf61c9b3fd0b90cce57df7)) Then we'll display all configuration parameter descriptions in https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer on creating/editing a config. Update: parameter description PRs: - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings/pull/49 - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pricing/pull/56 - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/94 - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-disqualifier/pull/52 - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-wallet/pull/24 - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-query/pull/25 - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-ask/pull/41 - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/pull/202 - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-merging/pull/30

I_kwDOMyHsAM6f8A40.title: Organization selection choices
I_kwDOMyHsAM6f8A40.body:
> I am only seeing two orgs but I am in more orgs that that, how are they chosen?

Orgs to select for editing come from the below method currently

https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/orgs?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-organizations-for-the-authenticated-user

```ts
public async getGitHubUserOrgs(): Promise<string[]> {
    const octokit = await this.getOctokit();
    const response = await octokit.rest.orgs.listForAuthenticatedUser();
    return response.data.map((org: { login: string }) => org.login);
  }
```

1. Who is using this installer? I'd assume a redirect after https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel/issues/171 is complete to the installer UI which would naturally be the owner of the org. Then potentially who after that? Admin & Owner? Partner defined?

2. What orgs should be shown when a partner uses the installer?

- Orgs that they are an admin of or just owner of, collaborator of?
- Should the partner determine which roles can edit the config or do we enforce rules, if we enforce then what should they be?

I_kwDOLS1KZ85_UpnT.title: Create NPM Module

Plugin developers need to import the configuration to modify the output of their plugins. We should make this as simple as possible with an NPM module. This module should abstract away the following:

1. fetching the repository configuration
2. fetching the organization configuration
3. merging to a single configuration
4. config validation

Pseudo code (I didn't deeply think through this):

```ts
import { getConfig } from "@ubiquibot/configuration";
const config = await getConfig(context);
```

> I meant that the configuration could be it's own repository that we distribute as an npm package. This way any project that needs the configuration can just add something like "@ubiquibot/configuration" in the npm packages of the project, this way you get access to the configuration easily, with the parsing / generation methods as well.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_LhiQ.title: Follow-up from #1152 (issue #689): test the "Only active" path of the provider bulk buttons
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_LhiQ.body:
PR #1152 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1152) fixed issue #689. A Codex tier narrowed to individual subscriptions now counts as checked, so "Uncheck shown" works for it. The PR merged in commit 3c12bc88a09fabfb7f948aa242400990c156cc93 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/3c12bc88a09fabfb7f948aa242400990c156cc93). This issue holds the one review finding from that PR that is still open on development.

The review found no P0, P1 or P2 problems. The fix itself is correct, including on the path below. The gap is only that no committed test covers that path.

## 1. No test covers the "Only active" filter with a narrowed Codex tier (P3, test coverage)

**Where.** Line numbers are at merge commit 3c12bc88. Both files are unchanged on development b24353e5, so the lines are the same there.

- `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts:839`: `providerPicker`, the VM fixture the new tests use.
- `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts:865`: `providersOnlyActiveInput: { checked: false }` is hard-coded, so "Only active" is always off.
- `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts:867-868`: `providersVisibleEntries` and `providersFilterIsActive` are stubs. The real filter code never runs.
- `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts:876-886`: the VM slice list leaves out `renderProvidersPicker`.
- `static/admin.js:9833`: the real `providersVisibleEntries`. With "Only active" on, it keeps the `codex` row when any of its subscriptions is selected (`providerCodexSelection().selected > 0`).
- `static/admin.js:10162`: `renderProvidersPicker`. It recomputes `providersVisibleIds` and calls `updateProvidersStatus`.
- `static/admin.js:10179`: `applyProvidersSelection`. When "Only active" is on, it re-renders through `renderProvidersPicker` instead of patching the rows in place.

**Problem.** The #1152 description says the "Only active" filter caused the same defect as the Codex tier filter. "Only active" can leave a narrowed Codex row as the only row shown, and before the fix "Uncheck shown" was disabled there too. The committed tests (`:891`, `:902`, `:912`) cover only the tier-filter case. They never turn "Only active" on, never run the real visibility filter, and never run the re-render that follows a bulk click with "Only active" on. Nothing else covers it: the only other reference to the control is the element-wiring check in `tests/admin-models-catalog.test.ts:763`.

**Failure scenario.** Someone later changes `providersVisibleEntries` or `renderProvidersPicker`, for example by keeping the Codex row only when `providerSelection.has("codex")`, or by computing `providersVisibleIds` before the counts change. The operator has selected only subscription `sub-a` and turns on "Only active". Then either the narrowed Codex row disappears from the list, or it is shown with "Uncheck shown" disabled, which is the #689 bug again. All tests in `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts` still pass. During review, a scratch VM test that ran the real `providersVisibleEntries` and `renderProvidersPicker` with selection `["sub-a"]` and "Only active" on failed on the pre-fix base 36503598 and passed on the PR head. That shows a test can catch this. It was not committed.

**Suggested fix.** Add the real filter and re-render code to the `providerPicker` VM, then add one case for this path:

- Add `between("const providersFilterIsActive =", "/**\n * Provider health")` (it holds `providersFilterIsActive` and `providersVisibleEntries`, `static/admin.js:9829-9856`) and `between("const renderProvidersPicker =", "const applyProvidersSelection =")` to the slice list.
- Remove the `providersVisibleEntries` and `providersFilterIsActive` stubs. Add the inputs the real code reads: `providerTierFilter`, `providersSearchInput` and `providersSortSelect` (each with a `value`), plus `providersEntryMatchesQuery` and `providersDisplayOrderIds`. Either slice those from `static/admin.js:9813` and `:9695` or stub them. Stub `renderProvidersMessage` and `buildProviderEntry` and keep the DOM stubbed as it is now.
- Let the fixture take an `onlyActive` flag that sets `providersOnlyActiveInput.checked`. Keep the current tier-filter cases working, for example by setting `providerTierFilter = "subscription"` where they now pass `visibleIds: ["codex"]`.
- New test: selection `["sub-a"]`, "Only active" on, tier filter `all`. Assert that the shown ids are exactly `["codex"]` and that "Uncheck shown" is enabled with the text "Uncheck 1 shown". Click it, then assert the selection is empty, the list re-renders with no rows, and "Uncheck shown" is disabled.
- Check that the new test fails if `providersVisibleEntries` drops the `providerCodexSelection().selected > 0` clause, or if `updateProvidersStatus` goes back to counting with `providerSelection.has(id)`.

The fixture runs `admin.js` code in a VM. Keep the test in `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts`, because that is the only file with the `sonarjs/code-eval` exemption in `tools/lint/eslint.config.mjs`. A new file would need a change under `tools/lint/`, which is a protected path.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_LfXQ.title: Follow-up from #1151 (issue #687): keep Codex off when its row is unchecked, block a save that leaves no tier active, fix the save toast count
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_LfXQ.body:
PR #1151 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1151) fixed issue #687. It was merged in commit c47b6f87f4d28570d6b1e71b3752a4e2dc1c39a3 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/c47b6f87f4d28570d6b1e71b3752a4e2dc1c39a3). This issue holds the review findings from that PR that are still unresolved on development. All of them are P3, and none blocked the merge.

Since #1151, the provider picker in `static/admin.js` sends staged ids that the roster no longer lists, for example a `codex:<hash>` subscription whose account was removed. Before, it dropped them. Items 1 to 3 are cases where that new behaviour leaves the panel and the server out of step.

I checked each item against development b24353e5. The only later change to `static/admin.js` is #1152 (issue #689). It changed which bulk buttons are disabled in `updateProvidersStatus` and fixes none of these items. I ran the shipped picker functions from b24353e5 in a `node:vm` context, together with the server's `normalizeSelectedProviderIds`, `isProviderEnabled` and `codexAccountEligibility`. That run still reproduces items 1 and 2. Item 3 is plain from the code.

Line numbers are at merge commit c47b6f87. Where #1152 moved a line, the line on development b24353e5 is in brackets.

In the examples, A, B and C are configured Codex subscriptions, and R is a saved `codex:<hash>` whose account is no longer configured.

## 1. Unchecking the Codex row leaves Codex on when a missing Codex id is staged (P3)

**Where.**

- `static/admin.js:10366-10376` [10370-10380]: `setProviderChecked`. For the Codex row it deletes `codex` and the configured subscription ids only (`:10373` [10377]).
- `static/admin.js:9801-9803`: since #1151, the serializer sends every missing id that is still staged.
- `static/admin.js:10064`: the "Codex is off" warning is suppressed on purpose while any missing id is staged.
- `src/provider/selection.ts:161-166` (`isProviderEnabled`): any `codex:*` id turns Codex on. `:177-182` (`codexAccountEligibility`) narrows the account pool to the listed hashes.

**Problem.** Unchecking the Codex row does not remove a missing `codex:*` id, so the save still names one Codex subscription. On the server that keeps Codex on, with a pool narrowed to an account that does not exist. Before #1151 the same save sent nothing for Codex and turned it off.

**Failure scenario.** The configured subscriptions are A and B, and the saved selection is `[R, A, surplus]`. The operator unchecks the Codex row. The staged set becomes `{R, surplus}`, and Save sends `[surplus, R]`.

- On the server, Codex stays enabled with zero eligible accounts (`src/codex/routing-serial.ts:295-305`), and `/v1/models` keeps listing the Codex models (`src/models/catalog.ts:112`).
- The panel shows the Codex row unchecked and "1 of 3 providers active: Surplus.", plus the missing-subscription warning. Because of the suppression at `:10064`, nothing says that Codex is still on.

**Suggested fix.** When the Codex row is unchecked, also delete the staged missing `codex:*` ids, because turning the tier off covers them. Alternatively, show the Codex row as partial (indeterminate) while a missing `codex:*` id is staged, so the operator can see that Codex is still on. Add the case to the VM-based picker test in `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts`.

## 2. Save stays enabled for a selection that leaves no tier active (P3)

**Where.**

- `static/admin.js:10155` [10159]: Save is disabled only when the staged set is empty.
- `static/admin.js:10282` [10286]: `saveProviderSelection` has the same guard.

**Problem.** A staged set that holds only missing ids is not empty, so Save stays enabled even though no tier is checked. One click then stores a restriction that routes nothing.

**Failure scenario.** The saved selection is `[R, surplus]`. The operator presses "Uncheck all", which leaves `{R}` staged. Save is enabled. The summary reads "0 of 3 providers active." and the panel warns "Both paid tiers are off". Saving stores `[R]`: Codex is nominally on with no eligible account, and every other provider is off, so no request can route. Without a missing id, the same "Uncheck all" empties the selection and Save stays disabled. The #1151 PR description lists this under Known limitations.

**Suggested fix.** Disable Save, or ask for confirmation, when the serialized list is non-empty but no roster tier is checked: `providersSelectedIds().length > 0` and `providersRosterIds().filter(isProviderChecked)` is empty. Put the same check in `saveProviderSelection`, so a save cannot bypass the button.

## 3. The save toast counts staged ids, not active tiers (P3)

**Where.** `static/admin.js:10308` [10312]: the success toast reads `` `${formatNumber(providerSelection.size)} providers active` ``.

**Problem.** `providerSelection` holds ids, not tiers. A missing id counts as a provider, and a narrowed Codex tier counts once per subscription. The panel badge (`:10131` [10135]) and the summary count tiers, so the toast disagrees with both. #1151 added the missing-id case. The narrowed-subscription case was already there.

**Failure scenario.**

- After saving `[R]`, the toast says "1 providers active", while the summary says "0 of 3 providers active.".
- With subscriptions A, B and C configured, saving `[A, B, surplus]` reports "3 providers active" for two active tiers. The badge says "2 active".

**Suggested fix.** Count tiers the way the badge does: `providersRosterIds().filter(isProviderChecked).length`. Also make the noun singular for a count of one. #1169 also changes this save handler and asks for the toast to be counted from the saved selection, so the two fixes can land together.

## 4. The #1151 PR description has a non-standard footer (P3, no code change)

**Where.** The description of PR #1151.

**Problem.** The description ends with `---` and `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_…)_`. The house form for PR descriptions is the line `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`, a blank line, then the session URL. Merged #1136 uses the house form.

**Failure scenario.** Nothing at runtime. Only the description text is affected, and nothing in the code or the merge depends on it.

**Suggested fix.** Edit the merged PR's description to the house form, or close this item as not worth doing.

## Related

- #1169 (from #1150): the Providers tab drops checkbox edits made while a save is pending. It touches the same `saveProviderSelection` code as item 3.
- #1060, Sentinel's candidate PR for #687, is still open. #1151 supersedes it, and closing it is left to the owner.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_Kncw.title: Follow-up from #1150 (issue #669): Providers tab drops checkbox edits made while a save is pending
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_Kncw.body:
PR #1150 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1150) fixed issue #669 for the Models tab. It was merged in commit f2457327beae47f991c31038365a5cbd2deb917b (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/f2457327beae47f991c31038365a5cbd2deb917b). This issue holds the review finding from that PR that is still unresolved on development.

The review's P2 finding was that a whitelist save which returns after `invalidateAdminModels` leaves the Models panel in a false "Unsaved changes" state. That defect is already tracked in #668, and I added the post-#1150 evidence there: https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/issues/668#issuecomment-6243849742. It is not repeated here.

## 1. The Providers tab drops checkbox edits made while a save is pending (P3)

**Where.** Line numbers are at merge commit f2457327. On development b24353e5 the same lines are 17 higher (shown in brackets).

- `static/admin.js:10263` [10280]: `saveProviderSelection`.
- `static/admin.js:10277` [10294]: the POST body is `providersSelectedIds()`, read when Save is clicked.
- `static/admin.js:10289` [10306]: `const savedIds = Array.isArray(payload?.provider_ids) ? payload.provider_ids : providersSelectedIds();`. The fallback reads the selection again after the response arrives.
- `static/admin.js:10291` [10308]: `providerSelection = new Set(providersSavedSelection);` replaces the staged selection with the saved one.
- `static/admin.js:9883` [9893] and `static/admin.js:9953` [9963]: the provider and subscription checkboxes are not disabled while a save is pending. `updateProvidersStatus` disables only the bulk buttons, Discard and Save.
- `static/admin.js:10388` [10405]: the `providersList` change listener updates `providerSelection` at any time, including while a save is pending.

**Problem.** This is the same bug #669 fixed for the Models tab. On success, the save handler overwrites the staged selection with the saved one. Any checkbox the operator changed after clicking Save is lost, and the panel looks clean, so nothing tells them. If the response has no `provider_ids`, the fallback reads the selection after the response arrived and records an edit that was never sent as saved. The current server always returns `provider_ids` (`src/admin/codex.ts`, `handleAdminProviderSelectionSet`), so the fallback only matters for an older server or a proxy that strips the field.

**Failure scenario.** The roster is `a, b, c` and the saved selection is all three, which is the no-filter state. The operator narrows the staged selection to `[a]` and clicks Save. While the POST is pending, they check `b`.

- If the response includes `provider_ids: ["a"]`, both saved and staged become `[a]` and the panel shows no unsaved changes. The `b` check is gone, and routing keeps `b` disabled although the operator just enabled it.
- If the response has no `provider_ids`, saved and staged both become `[a, b]` and the panel shows no unsaved changes. The panel now says `b` is saved and active, but the server stored only `[a]`, so routing still skips `b`.

I reproduced both cases by running the shipped `static/admin.js` from development b24353e5 in a `node:vm` context. The test used the real provider state, the selection helpers, `saveProviderSelection` and the `providersList` change listener, with only fetch and rendering faked:

```
with provider_ids:    {"requests":[{"provider_ids":["a"]}],"state":{"saved":["a"],"staged":["a"],"saving":false},"unsaved":false}
without provider_ids: {"requests":[{"provider_ids":["a"]}],"state":{"saved":["a","b"],"staged":["a","b"],"saving":false},"unsaved":false}
```

**Suggested fix.** Do what #1150 did for Models (`modelsSelectionAfterSave`, `static/admin.js:9075`):

- When Save is clicked, take a snapshot of the staged set (`const submittedSelection = new Set(providerSelection)`) and the ids to send (`const submittedIds = providersSelectedIds()`). Send exactly `submittedIds`.
- On success, set `providersSavedSelection = providersSelectionFromIds(Array.isArray(payload?.provider_ids) ? payload.provider_ids : submittedIds)`.
- Rebuild `providerSelection` from the saved set, then replay the edits made since Save was clicked. Drop every id in `submittedSelection` that is no longer in `providerSelection`, and add every id in `providerSelection` that was not in `submittedSelection`.
- Do the replay on the internal staged set, not on the serialized `provider_ids`. `providersSelectedIds()` turns "every provider checked" into `[]`, and the `codex` umbrella stands in for its subscriptions, so diffing the serialized lists would give the wrong answer.
- Count the toast from the saved selection.

Add a fixture-VM test like `tests/admin-models-save-pending.test.ts` that covers four cases: a check while the save is pending, an uncheck while the save is pending, a response with no `provider_ids`, and a Codex subscription toggled while the save is pending.

Two related issues are separate and should stay that way: #680 (a provider save response that arrives after a target change is still applied) and #679 (edits made during a roster GET are replaced). A fix here can add the same load-generation check (`providerSelectionLoadId`) that #680 asks for.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnpgMA.title: The whitelist save callback ignores admin-target invalidation
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnpgMA.body:
## Confirmed defect

modelsLoadId is advanced by invalidateAdminModels when the API target or credential changes, but the save completion at static/admin.js:8527-8540 never checks its originating target or generation before installing modelsSavedSelection/modelsSelection. A late response can replace the new target's whitelist and mark it saved, and the next edit then submits that foreign selection to the new target.

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded`
- Location: `src/../static/admin.js:8521-8540`
- Source PR: #322 (closed, merged=true), original head `c17a5d9057d942b79c038d9f8f19e0d7fb871952`, merge `610f203132d4b01b4f4bb3741eb8db7546ad7d16`

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_JqUg.title: Follow-up from #1160 (issue #1139): make stale-lock recovery in the signing helper race-free and resolve #1159 onto it
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_JqUg.body:
PR #1160 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1160), which fixed #1139, merged as https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/ed0ecdda85ee261bc8388558bb26c2c86f5ac9a5. Its review found no P0 or P1 issues and all four checks were green, so it merged. The review left the five findings below open: one P2 and four P3.

I checked each one against development at `b24353e5`. `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` and `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` have not changed since the merge, so findings 1-3 still apply as written. Finding 4 still applies too: #1159 conflicts with development in all three files. Line numbers are at the merge commit `ed0ecdda`.

The helper is the Mac-local `gpg.program` wrapper, installed by hand. Nothing in the VPS release path or in ubiquity/sentinel calls it, so none of this touches a deployed interface. Every failure seen in the review was fail-closed (exit 2). No run published a deleted key under a current manifest stamp.

## 1. P2: breaking a stale lock is check-then-delete, so waiters remove each other's fresh locks

**Where:**
- `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:156-162`: the stale-lock branch of `take_lock`.
- `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:158-159`: the owner check and the `rm -rf "$lock"` that follows it.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md:591` and `:602-603`: "Rebuilds are serialized and published whole" and the stale-lock sentence.

**Problem:** When a lock holder is killed mid-rebuild, every waiter reaches the 15-second mark at about the same time. Each one reads the owner file, sees that it is unchanged, and runs `rm -rf "$lock"`. The read and the delete are two steps, so this sequence is possible:
1. Waiter W1 and waiter W2 both read the stale owner.
2. W1 removes the lock, loops, and wins `mkdir`.
3. W2, which already passed its check, runs `rm -rf` on W1's fresh lock.

Several calls then hold "the" lock and rebuild at once. That breaks the serialization the decision entry and the PR description promise. The PR body says "a lock is only removed while its owner file is unchanged", and the recovery test (`tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts:248`) runs only one caller.

**Failure scenario:** The review's stress setup was a stale lock plus a leftover `.new.*` stage (a SIGKILLed holder), an input change, then 16 concurrent sandboxed calls. Over 60 rounds (960 calls), 15 calls exited 2 with one of these errors:
- `cannot create .../<uid>.lock/owner: Directory nonexistent`: another waiter deleted the lock between this call's `mkdir` and its owner write.
- `cannot break the stale rebuild lock ...` with `rm: ... Is a directory`: two `rm -rf` runs raced on the same tree.
- `cannot set the stale seed ... aside`: two holders were swapping at once.

In one more round, two calls exited 0 but the fake gpg saw no key, so real gpg would have failed those signings. In 7 of the 60 rounds the agent was stopped 2-3 times instead of once. For the owner, this means some sandboxed `git commit -S` calls fail after a crash or a killed signing, even though the helper says it recovers.

**Suggested fix:** Serialize the lock breakers:
1. Take a second `mkdir` lock, `$lock.break`.
2. Under it, check that the owner file is still the stale value you read.
3. Remove `$lock`, then `rmdir "$lock.break"`.

A breaker that cannot take `$lock.break` goes back to waiting. When the `rm` fails, `continue` the loop instead of calling `die`. Add a test: a stale lock plus N concurrent calls must all exit 0, with exactly one `gpgconf --kill`.

## 2. P3: a negative `held` breaks a live lock

**Where:** `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:140-141` (`now` is sampled, then the owner file is read) and `:156` (the `[ "$held" -lt 0 ]` branch).

**Problem:** `take_lock` reads the clock before it reads the owner file. Suppose the lock is released, and a new holder takes it and writes its start time in the next second, all between those two reads. Then `started` is `now + 1`, `held` is -1, and the `-lt 0` branch treats the lock as stale. The check at `:158` passes, because the owner the waiter just read is still the current one. So the waiter deletes a live lock.

**Failure scenario:** The review reproduced this deterministically by slowing the owner read so it crosses a second boundary while a second holder takes the lock. The waiter printed `breaking the stale rebuild lock ... (owner: 222 1792271135)` 0.44 s after that holder took the lock, and removed it. With a 0.5 s owner-read delay, 25 rounds of 16 calls broke 197 live locks, though with 0 failures and 0 double rebuilds. Without the delay, about 150 rounds under dash and 30 under `bash --posix` showed no lock breaks. So this is rare in practice. When it happens it allows two concurrent rebuilds, the precondition for finding 3. It can also fail the CI assertion "each input change rebuilds the seed, and stops its agent, exactly once" (`tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts:219`) at random.

**Suggested fix:** Read the owner file first, then sample `now`. Then `now >= started` for any owner written before the read. A negative `held` can then only mean clock skew, so treat it as live (or re-sample) instead of stale.

## 3. P3: the "reappeared" guard and the final `mv` are check-then-act

**Where:** `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:211-214`, in `rebuild_seed`.

**Problem:** The guard checks that `$seed` does not exist and then runs `mv "$stage" "$seed"`. If two calls hold the lock at once (through finding 1 or 2), both can pass the guard. The first `mv` renames its stage to `$seed`. The second `mv` then moves its stage into the published seed, as `$seed/<uid>.new.XXXXXX`. `has_leftovers` and `discard_leftovers` (`:174-187`) only look at siblings of `$seed`, so nothing removes it.

**Failure scenario:** This is theoretical: it did not show up in the 60 killed-holder rounds. Holders A and B both pass the guard. A publishes its stage. B's stage, holding copies of the private keys, lands inside A's seed, and B signs from A's seed. If a key was deleted between B's manifest read and A's, B's nested copy of that deleted key stays on disk inside the current seed until the next input change. gpg does not read it, but the copy persists, which is the outcome #587 and #1139 set out to prevent.

**Suggested fix:** Fixing findings 1 and 2 removes the precondition. As a backstop, after the swap, check that `$seed` contains no `*.new.*` or `*.old.*` entries, and fail closed (removing them) if it does. Alternatively, use `mv -T` where it exists. It is GNU-only, so feature-detect it: the owner's Mac uses BSD `mv`.

## 4. P3: open PR #1159 (#1141) conflicts with development in all three helper files

**Where:** `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` (the rebuild section, from `:197`) and `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts`.

**Problem:** #1159 rewrites the same part of `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` as #1160: a per-uid `dsh-gnupg-<uid>/seed` layout, one hashing process, and refusing planted seed config files. #1160 merged first, so #1159 now has to be resolved by hand. #1160's Known limitations section names the moves needed:
- The lock and sibling names come from `$seed` (`$seed.lock`, `$seed.new.*`, `$seed.old.*`), so they work unchanged with the new layout.
- #1159's planted-config check belongs in `read_recorded`.
- #1159's `copy_inputs` must write into `$stage`, not `$seed`.

**Failure scenario:** `git merge-tree` of #1159's head `2892d609` against development `b24353e5` reports content conflicts in all three files. A resolution that keeps #1159's in-place copy brings back the writes into a published seed that #1160 removed. A resolution that keeps #1160's `read_recorded` unchanged drops #1159's refusal of planted `gpg-agent.conf`/`gpg.conf` files (the pinentry-capture issue in #1141). In either case CI could stay green, because each PR's tests cover only its own half.

**Suggested fix:** Resolve #1159 onto development by hand as described above. Then re-run `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` and a concurrency stress (stale lock plus N concurrent calls) on the combined helper before #1159 is re-reviewed. If findings 1-3 are fixed first, fold them into the same resolution.

## 5. P3: the PR description ending does not match house style (no repository change)

**Where:** the description of #1160.

**Problem:** It ends with the session URL followed by `---` and `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_`, which the PR tooling appended. Merged #1123, #1124 and #1136 instead end with "Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)", a blank line, then the session URL. Patching the body through MCP and through the REST API produced the same rewrite.

**Failure scenario:** None for the code. The record differs from the rest of the series, as already noted for #1134 and #1137 in #1141.

**Suggested fix:** If the record should match, the owner can edit the description. No commit is needed.

## Not a finding: the owner's install step from #1139 is still open

`Resolves #1139` closed the issue at merge, but item 2's machine step was never something the PR could do. Merging installs nothing on the Mac. If it is not already done, run `diff ops/gpg-dsh.sh ~/bin/gpg-dsh`, check that the installed helper does not seed `gpg.conf`, `gpg-agent.conf` or `public-keys.d`, and then run `install -m 0755 ops/gpg-dsh.sh ~/bin/gpg-dsh`. If you do that before findings 1-3 are fixed, the helper's only weak spot is recovery after a killed or hung signing. The common case, a burst of commits after one key change, is fixed.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_Ip0w.title: Follow-up from #1158 (issue #1131): keep the owner-index wait off VPS failure responses and pace the fill
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_Ip0w.body:
PR #1158 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1158), which fixed #1131, merged as https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/27fcf4ed99d020b15711d613d127266c691f001d. Its review found no P0 or P1 issues and all four checks were green on the reviewed head `24fae239`, so it merged. The review left the four non-blocking findings below open.

I checked each one against development at `2c7f1378`. None of the files involved have changed since the merge, so all four still apply. Line numbers are at the merge commit `27fcf4ed` and are the same on `2c7f1378`.

#1158 changes no interface that ubiquity/sentinel uses. Its diff is limited to the three `src/sentinel/replay-retention*.ts` files and one test, and the sentinel repository references none of them.

## 1. P2: on the VPS, the 500 ms owner-index wait sits in front of client-visible failure responses

**Where:**
- `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:354`: `prepareChunkOwners` waits for the fill for up to `BOOTSTRAP_OWNER_INDEX_WAIT_MS`.
- `src/sentinel/replay-retention-schema.ts:52`: `BOOTSTRAP_OWNER_INDEX_WAIT_MS = 500`.
- `src/handler/http.ts:22-41`: `scheduleSentinelBackgroundTask` defers work only when `globalThis.EdgeRuntime.waitUntil` exists.
- Where the replay task is awaited inline when it does not exist: `src/handler/terminal-log.ts:478` (non-SSE failure response), `src/handler/terminal-route.ts:170` (propagated gateway exception), `src/handler/terminal-route.ts:268-271` (pre-capture rejection) and `src/handler/terminal-route.ts:465-468` (thrown inference failure with no captured body).
- The two waits a failed request can hit: `src/sentinel/replay-retention.ts:872` (`reserveSentinelReplayCapacity` calls `runBootstrapBatch`) and `src/sentinel/replay-retention.ts:110` (`admitSentinelReplayStatusMetadata` calls `bootstrapBeforeMutation`).

**Problem:** The Known limitations section of #1158 says the callers that wait are "capture and status tasks that run after the response", and that a request waits "once per process and sweep". Neither holds on the VPS. Nothing in the Bun VPS process defines `EdgeRuntime.waitUntil`, and no caller passes a `waitUntil`. So `scheduleSentinelBackgroundTask` returns false, and each call site above awaits the replay task before it returns the response or rethrows the error. Also, every batch that arrives while a fill is running waits, not only the first one.

**Failure scenario:**
1. The store's sweep is at its chunk phase. #1131 notes production may be stuck at `1|`.
2. The process restarts. Filling the index then takes about 0.6-3 s (20,000-100,000 owner rows at about 30,000 rows/s).
3. In that window, a failed request can wait twice: up to 500 ms in the refused reservation, then up to another 500 ms in the refused capture's status write. Before #1158 each of these calls read one 64-row slice, which took a few ms.

A review probe with a slowed fill measured 501-506 ms per status admission and about 910 ms for a refused reservation. About 500 ms of the 910 ms is the bootstrap wait; the rest comes from how the probe slowed reads. The extra latency is bounded and transient, and it affects failure responses only.

**Suggested fix:**
- Give the inference-path callers (`reserveSentinelReplayCapacity` and the status-metadata admission) a zero or very small wait, and keep the bounded wait for maintenance and admin views only. A batch that does not wait leaves the sweep where it is, which it already does when the wait times out.
- Or, on those paths, start the fill without waiting for it.
- Correct the doc wording so that the owner decides the 500 ms value (an open owner question on #1158) knowing that on the VPS it sits in front of failure responses.

## 2. P3: the background fill runs unpaced, and keeps reading after another process finishes the sweep

**Where:** `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:300-303` (`fillChunkOwnerIndex`), which loops over `advanceChunkOwnerIndex` (`:276-297`).

**Problem:** The fill reads one 64-row slice after another with no pause between them. It stops only when it completes or when this handle no longer holds the index. If another process finishes the sweep, this handle's fill keeps reading until it completes, or until a later `bootstrapBeforeMutation` or `reserveSentinelReplayCapacity` call on this handle sees the complete ledger and drops the index.

**Failure scenario:** With 100,000 owner rows, the fill makes about 1,600 back-to-back 64-row list calls in about 3 s, validating each row on the main thread while the process serves traffic. If a second process completes the sweep in the meantime, the first process still runs the full scan. The cost is wasted reads and CPU, bounded by one full owner scan. Correctness is not affected.

**Suggested fix:** Yield or pace between slices. Stop the fill early when a cheap ledger read shows the sweep is complete or carries a different `bootstrap_sweep` id.

## 3. P3: after a ledger-only restore, the retired stand-in stalls the restored sweep until restart

**Where:** `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:469` (`settleChunkOwnerIndex` installs the retired stand-in), `:354-356` (a retired index is never waited on and never ready), and the restore note at `:238-240`.

**Problem:** Once a commit on a handle moves sweep S past its chunk phase, the handle holds a retired stand-in for S that never fills. If an older copy of the ledger alone is then restored, with S back at a chunk cursor, that handle can never judge S's chunks again.

**Failure scenario:**
1. On process A, sweep S passes its chunk phase, so A holds `emptyChunkOwnerIndex(S, true)`.
2. Someone restores only an older ledger copy, with S at a chunk cursor.
3. Every batch on A finds the retired stand-in, judges no chunk, and returns the ledger unchanged. Admissions on A stay refused until A restarts.

The existing note already says to restart every process after such a restore, for safety, and that instruction also covers this case. It does not say that skipping the restart also stops progress.

**Suggested fix:** Mention the liveness effect next to the restore note, or in the ops/runbook text for ledger restores.

## 4. P3: no test has a process die before its owner-index fill finishes

**Where:** `tests/sentinel-replay-bootstrap-retry.test.ts:705-732` ("a process that restarts every few calls still finishes the sweep").

**Problem:** The test seeds 200 legacy manifests, which is 4 slices. The fill reads them in a few ms, so every fresh handle completes its index during its first call. The test therefore cannot catch a regression that only shows when a process lives for less than one full fill, which is the production concern at 20,000-100,000 owner rows. The test at `:733` ("the owner index fills without further requests") covers background progress on a single handle only.

**Failure scenario:** A change that, for example, left a new handle waiting on, or sharing state with, a fill that an earlier handle never finished would still pass this test, because in it no handle ever leaves a fill unfinished. In production, at 20,000-100,000 owner rows, a restart during the 0.6-3 s fill is exactly that case.

**Suggested fix:** Add a variant that holds the fill with `holdNextList` (`:194`) across a handle swap, then assert that the next handle's fill completes and the sweep advances.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_IamQ.title: Follow-up from #1157 (issue #1133): fix a quota-test clock race and close gaps in the spec-pin and contract tests
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_IamQ.body:
PR #1157 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1157), which fixed #1133, merged as https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/efc3d90dd2a08e371aa709908f555ea386e6f1bb. Its review found no P0 or P1 issues and CI was green, so it merged. The review left the four P3 findings below open.

I checked each one against development at `2c7f1378`. None of the files involved have changed since the merge, so all four still apply. Line numbers are at the merge commit `efc3d90d`. While checking, I corrected two of the review's descriptions; both corrections are noted below.

## 1. P3: a clock race makes a Claude Code quota test fail at random

**Where:**
- `tests/claude-code-accounts.test.ts:486-495`: the test "quota proof is exact-model and expires at its recorded reset boundary".
- `src/provider/claude-code-quota.ts:524`: `recordClaudeCodeQuotaOutcome` reads its own clock when no `nowMs` is passed.
- `src/provider/claude-code-quota.ts:486` and `:479`: that reading becomes the proof's `observed_at_ms`.
- `src/provider/claude-code-quota.ts:150`: a proof only counts when `observed_at_ms <= nowMs`.

**Problem:** The test reads `const now = Date.now()` at line 486, then records a 429 outcome without passing `nowMs`. `recordClaudeCodeQuotaOutcome` takes its own `Date.now()` at line 524 and stores it as the proof's `observed_at_ms`. The assertion at line 495 then asks for the proof at the earlier `now`. If the millisecond clock ticks between the two readings, `observed_at_ms` is `now + 1`, the check at line 150 fails, and `claudeCodePoolProofForModel` returns null.

Correction: the review blamed the default argument of `observation()`. That value is not what the proof stores. The clock that matters is the one inside `recordClaudeCodeQuotaOutcome`, so passing `now` to `observation()` alone would not fix it.

**Failure scenario:** It has already failed twice in CI, both times on PRs that touch neither file:
- #1157, run 39063762168, attempt 1: validate failed with `AssertionError: null == true` at line 495. A rerun of the job passed.
- #1162, validate job 117507578190 in run 39070721689: the same test failed the same way. The merge step stops on any red check, so #1162 was not merged.

Any PR can hit this, and each hit blocks a merge until someone reruns the job.

**Suggested fix:** Pass the captured clock in. Add `nowMs: now` to that `recordClaudeCodeQuotaOutcome` call, and use `observation("1", now)` so both readings agree. Then check the other tests in the file for the same pattern: a proof recorded with the internal clock and read back at an earlier `Date.now()`. The next test, at line 503, already passes `response_observed_at_ms: now` and reads the proof at a later clock, so it is safe.

## 2. P3: the nullable-field contract test only covers the default Codex route

**Where:**
- `tests/openapi-nullable-request-contract.test.ts:41-52`: both request builders use `DEFAULT_TEST_MODEL`.
- `tests/openapi-nullable-request-contract.test.ts:65` and `:76`: the Chat and Responses sweeps.

**Problem:** The test sends null for each published nullable field, 20 on Chat and 18 on Responses, but only to `DEFAULT_TEST_MODEL`, which runs on the Codex route. These routes are never sent a null:
- Cerebras (`src/provider/cerebras-handlers.ts`)
- Lithos (`src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts`)
- DeepSeek (`src/deepseek/handlers.ts`)
- OpenRouter (`src/provider/openrouter-handlers.ts`)

#1157 lists this under Known limitations.

**Failure scenario:** A later change adds a strict parser to one provider, for example a `temperature` check in `cerebras-handlers.ts` that rejects null. A client sends `temperature: null` to a Cerebras model, as `/openapi.json` allows, and gets a 400. The contract test still passes, because it never sends to that route.

**Suggested fix:** Run the same sweep once per provider route. Use each provider's test model and the existing harness mocks for its upstream.

## 3. P3: `--verify-source` may accept a commit that only exists in a fork

**Where:**
- `scripts/check-openai-spec-drift.ts:52`: `pinnedSpecSource` builds the fetch URL.
- `scripts/check-openai-spec-drift.ts:124-128`: the digest check.
- `scripts/check-openai-spec-drift.ts:250-266`: `--repin`.

**Problem:** `--verify-source` fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-openapi/<commit>/openapi.yaml` and checks that the bytes match the pinned sha256. That proves the bytes belong to the pinned commit. It probably does not prove that the commit is in openai/openai-openapi's own history. GitHub serves commits from any fork in the same fork network under the parent repository's path. `--repin` uses the same URL, so it would record such a commit without complaint. I have not reproduced this here; it rests on how GitHub serves fork-network commits.

**Failure scenario:**
1. Someone runs `spec:drift --repin <sha>` with a commit pushed to a fork of openai/openai-openapi, and commits the new pin.
2. In CI, `--verify-source` fetches that commit through the parent URL, the digest matches, and the gate passes.
3. The pin now names a commit OpenAI never published.

The change still needs a reviewed edit to `scripts/openai-spec-pin.json`, so the risk is low.

**Suggested fix:** In `--repin`, and optionally in `--verify-source`, confirm that the official default branch contains the commit. For example, the GitHub compare API from the pinned commit to the default branch should report `ahead` or `identical`, never `diverged`. Alternatively, make review of every pin change an explicit rule.

## 4. P3: the `/uos/` route-parity scan misses paths built from a prefix, and has no allowlist

**Where:**
- `tests/openapi-runtime-contract.test.ts:131-137`: the three dispatch patterns.
- `tests/openapi-runtime-contract.test.ts:176-188`: the scan for `/uos/` string literals.

**Problem:** The parity test finds routes in two ways. It matches three fixed `req.method === "..." && path === "..."` shapes, and it treats every `"/uos/..."` string literal under `src/` as a route that must be published.
- A path built from a prefix that has no trailing slash is seen by neither, for example `` `${UOS}/probe` `` with `const UOS = "/uos"`, or a path joined from segments.
- A real non-route literal, such as a doc link `"/uos/probe"`, fails the test, and there is no allowlist to add it to.

Correction: the review said template and concatenated paths are missed. I ran the scan's regex on sample sources. It does catch `` `/uos/${name}` `` and `"/uos/" + name`: both are reported as unpublished, so the test fails rather than staying silent. A log message that contains spaces, such as `"/uos/probe is deprecated"`, is not matched. The gap is the prefix and joined forms above.

**Failure scenario:** A new module defines `const UOS = "/uos"` and dispatches `` path === `${UOS}/probe` ``. The route ships unpublished, and both parity tests pass. Separately, a later change adds a doc link `"/uos/probe"` to an error message. The test fails, and the only way to pass it is to publish the path or reword the message.

**Suggested fix:** Longer term, export the UOS route table from the router and compare the published paths against it, as #1133 suggested. When the first real non-route literal appears, add an explicit allowlist constant to the test.
