I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_G85Q.title: Follow-up from #1155 (issue #1125): bound pending VPS join windows and their checkpoint growth
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_G85Q.body:
PR #1155 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1155) fixed #1125 and was merged as [`2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24). Its review found no P0 or P1 problem, so it merged. The review left one P2 and two P3 findings, which are filed here as follow-up work. Line references are to the merge commit. The files involved have not changed on `development` since (tip `2c7f1378`), and I re-checked each finding against that code.

Nothing in `src/` or `serve.ts` imports these modules, and `sentinel-release` is disabled, so none of this affects production today. It starts to matter once Sentinel's VPS release bridge is re-pinned to a driver that includes #1027 (ubiquity/sentinel#150).

## 1. P2: a request lost to a crash keeps its window collecting until the deadline

**Where:**
- [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:71`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L71) skips PID 1 rows.
- [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:318-331`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L318-L331) is the `_scan` loop.
- [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:351`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L351) reports `deadline_exceeded`.
- [`ops/vps-metrics-join.ts:93`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-metrics-join.ts#L93) keeps the slices.

**Problem:** #1125 asked for PID 1 rows about the unit to be skipped, and `checkedRow` now skips them. Before #1155, such a row refused its slice. Examples are systemd's "Main process exited" or "Started ..." rows after a crash. That refusal was the only thing that ended a window whose request never logged a terminal, and nothing replaced it. A window that has an admission but no terminal stays `pending`, so `_scan` keeps reading forward, up to 16 reads per tick, until the operation deadline. All that time, `pruneJoinLedgers` keeps every slice from the window's `scanStart`, so the checkpoint keeps growing.

**Failure scenario:** during monitoring, the candidate crashes, is OOM-killed or gets SIGKILL while requests are in flight, so those requests never log a terminal. The reviewer simulated this at 0.35 req/s, with 1 in 10 requests a 5-minute stream and a crash at window 10:
- The #1027 code refused window 0 at tick 11 (`coverage_missing`), and monitoring restarted.
- The merged code keeps window 0 at `collecting`/`terminal_or_slice_pending` through tick 120. The checkpoint grows linearly: 500,469 bytes at tick 80, 610,697 at tick 100 and 720,964 at tick 120.
- The window then reports `deadline_exceeded`, and the release fails at the deadline.

That outcome is safe, but a candidate that crashed once and has been healthy since now fails at the deadline instead of restarting monitoring.

**Suggested fix:** add a forward bound for pending admissions. Once the scan passes it, the window becomes unavailable, for example with a new reason `terminal_lost`. The bound can be either of these:
- a PID 1 exit or restart row for the unit after the admission. The row stays skipped as a request row but is kept as a lifecycle marker;
- or a maximum request lifetime after the admission.

Add a test with an admission, a PID 1 restart row and no terminal.

## 2. P3: an orphan terminal well after a window still refuses that window

**Where:** [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:181-184`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L181-L184) in `joined`, used at [`:328-329`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L328-L329).

**Problem:** any terminal at or after `windowStart` that has no matching admission sets `orphanFloor`. This happens even when the terminal's own lifetime shows its admission came after `windowEnd`. So a pending window whose forward scan reaches such an orphan is refused. The #1027 code did the same, and #1155 left it in place.

**Failure scenario:** there is one orphan at window 10, either an accepted-stage or a null-stage one (for example a lost admission), and windows 0 to 9 are still pending on 5-minute streams. Window 0's forward scan reaches the orphan. `orphanFloor` comes to about window 0's start plus 270 s, and `scanStart <= orphanFloor`, so window 0 is refused at tick 10. Yet the orphan's admission cannot be in window 0. The #1027 code refused the same window at tick 17, after 1,040 reads. The merged code takes 81 reads. In both cases the controller restarts monitoring, so the result is the same, it just comes earlier.

**Suggested fix (owner decision):** ignore an orphan when `at - latencyMs - VPS_METRICS_SLICE_MS >= cohort.windowEnd`. This would trust `latency_ms` in the fail-open direction, which #1155 deliberately avoids: an under-reported latency would then hide a lost admission from the window. So this is a trade-off, not a plain bug. If the owner keeps the current behaviour, record that in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.

## 3. P3: checkpoint size still grows with request rate times the longest in-flight request

**Where:**
- [`ops/vps-metrics-join.ts:89-97`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-metrics-join.ts#L89-L97) (`pruneJoinLedgers`)
- [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:403`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L403) (`retainFrom`)

**Problem:** an incomplete window keeps every ledger slice from its `scanStart`, with every event in those slices, until its last terminal arrives. So the checkpoint size is not bounded by a constant. It is bounded by the request rate times the longest in-flight request. The "Known limitations" section of #1155 does not state this bound, and neither does any doc on `development`.

**Failure scenario:** the reviewer simulated a 4 MiB cap and 7-day retention:
- At 2 req/s, with 1 in 20 requests a 30-minute stream, the checkpoint reaches the cap and candidate window 18 is refused. The peak is 4,179,775 bytes.
- At 1.5 req/s, the same mix peaks at 4,128,015 bytes, which is 98% of the cap.
- At 3 req/s, with 5-minute streams plus a single 30-minute stream, it peaks at 3,528,359 bytes.

At today's production rate of about 0.35 req/s, the checkpoint stays near 1 MB, even with 1 in 10 requests a 30-minute stream.

**Suggested fix:** document the bound next to `pruneJoinLedgers` and in the release docs, with the evidence cap it implies for a given request rate and longest stream. If it matters later, shrink a pending window to its own admissions plus the terminals at or after `windowStart`, instead of keeping whole slices.

Items 1 and 3 add up: a window held open by item 1 keeps its slices for the whole time, which is the growth item 3 describes.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_GALg.title: Follow-up from #1153 (issue #1126): bound stored Mac capacity rows and make the push recover from refused or slow batches
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_GALg.body:
PR #1153 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1153), which fixed #1126, merged as https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/70eade5c11f11dd565d22a6b27cf75ec8cc8c140. Its review found no P0 or P1 issues and CI was green, so it merged. The review left the three non-blocking findings below open.

I checked each one against development at `2c7f1378`. None of the files involved have changed since the merge, so all three still apply. Line numbers are at the merge commit `70eade5c`.

## 1. P2: the VPS keeps every intermediate Mac sample, about 30 rows per bucket instead of 1

**Where:**
- `src/provider/capacity-analytics.ts:41-46`: the remote row key.
- `src/provider/capacity.ts:621-624`: the Mac overwrites its bucket point.
- `src/admin/chart-source-proxy.ts:123-134`: the pending samples.
- `src/provider/capacity-analytics.ts:109-125` and `src/provider/capacity.ts:830`: the full scan on every read.

**Problem:** #1153 added `sampled_at_ms` to the remote row key, `(host, bucket_start_at_ms, sampled_at_ms)`, so that same-bucket transition points survive. The Mac keeps one point per 15-minute bucket and overwrites it on every refresh with a new `sampled_at_ms`. Each new value is newer than the acknowledged watermark, so the Mac pushes it again and the VPS stores it under a new key. The VPS therefore holds every intermediate sample instead of one point per bucket plus real transitions. `readRemoteCapacityObservations` then lists and parses all of these rows on every VPS `/admin/providers/capacity` read.

**Failure scenario:** An open Mac Analytics tab polls every 30 s. `PROVIDER_CAPACITY_READ_FRESH_MS` is `30_000`, so almost every poll refreshes and rewrites the bucket point.
- **Review probe:** it ran 240 polls (2 hours) through the real `proxyAdminChartSource` and `handleCapacityObservationIngest`. At the end the Mac held 8 points and the VPS held 240 rows (317 KB). A gap bucket on the VPS chart could draw up to 30 points where the Mac draws 1.
- **Over a week:** with the tab open, that is about 20,160 rows (about 27 MB) per host. The old `(host, bucket)` key stored at most 672.
- **Read cost:** scanning, parsing and merging 20,160 rows took 75 ms and about 23 MB of short-lived heap against an in-memory KV. Real KV decoding costs more. This runs on every 30 s VPS admin poll and every Mac proxied read, on the production KV.

The 7-day TTL puts a ceiling on it, and routing and chart correctness are not affected.

**Suggested fix:** pick one of these.
- (a) On the Mac, push only closed buckets (`bucket_start + 15 min <= snapshot time`) plus the points saved under transition keys. Each bucket then sends one row plus its transitions.
- (b) On the VPS, store the latest sample per `(host, bucket)` under a fixed key. Only true transition points get keys that include `sampled_at_ms`, and the Mac marks which points those are.
- (c) At ingest, delete older non-transition rows for the same `(host, bucket)`.

Also consider a per-host cap on stored rows, and document how long rows are kept.

## 2. P3: one bad row makes the Mac skip its whole batch for good

**Where:**
- `src/admin/chart-source-proxy.ts:160-163` and `:186`
- `src/admin/capacity-observation-sync.ts:67-68`
- `src/provider/capacity-analytics.ts:61-66`

**Problem:** The VPS rejects the whole batch with 400 if any one row is malformed, unaligned, outside its bucket, or over 16 KiB. The Mac treats 400 and 413 as `refused` and moves its watermark past the newest sample in the batch. One bad row therefore drops up to 511 valid samples sent with it. The watermark lives only in the process, so after a restart the same batch is sent, refused and skipped again.

**Failure scenario:**
1. After a restart, the Mac sends its oldest 512 samples.
2. One row is over `MAX_REMOTE_CAPACITY_OBSERVATION_BYTES`, or fails `readStoredHistoryPoint` on a VPS running a different version.
3. The VPS answers 400, and `acknowledgedSampledAtMs` jumps to the newest sample in the batch.
4. The other 511 valid rows are never pushed.

**Suggested fix:** On `refused`, retry with smaller batches, halving down to the bad row, or drop only that row. Another option is for the VPS to skip invalid rows and return a result per row instead of rejecting the whole envelope.

## 3. P3: a push that times out resends the same large batch forever

**Where:** `src/admin/chart-source-proxy.ts:19`, `:134`, `:158`, `:166-167` and `:186`

**Problem:** The push has a fixed 5 s timeout, and a timeout counts as `retry`. The watermark stays where it is, so the next poll resends the same batch of up to 512 rows (about 0.7 MB) unchanged.

**Failure scenario:** The Mac restarts with a full week of history and either of these is true:
- its uplink is slower than about 1.2 Mbit/s, or
- the VPS takes more than 5 s to commit 8 atomic batches of 64.

Every poll then times out, and the same 0.7 MB is sent again every 30 s. The watermark never moves. This brings back, on a smaller scale, the upload amplification that #1126 item 2 fixed.

**Suggested fix:** Halve the batch after each timeout, down to a floor. Alternatively, start catch-up with a smaller batch, or scale the timeout with the batch size.

## Not included

The review also raised a P3 about the footer of the #1153 PR description. I left it out because it concerns the merged PR's text, not code. Its stated reason, that the footer differs from #1134, also does not hold: #1134 ends with the same footer.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzfbXQ.title: Follow-ups from #1122: stop an open bracket in a thread title from erasing the supervisor brief prompt
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzfbXQ.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1122 -->

PR #1122 ("redact credential keys whose values are arrays or objects", #427) was merged at `46041471`. The items below are non-blocking findings from adversarial review of that PR. The PR meets #427; these items are side effects and remaining gaps. Line numbers refer to current `development`.

## 1. One open bracket in the thread title erases the rest of the brief prompt

`src/codex/supervisor-brief.ts:531`, `src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:173`

When a bracketed value is never closed, it is redacted to the end of the text being processed. `buildSupervisorBriefPrompt` redacts the whole assembled prompt in a single call, and the thread title comes near the top of that prompt. The title is the thread name, or else the first user message.

The problem case is a title with a credential-like word followed by a bracket that is never closed, or by an apostrophe inside the bracket. The redaction then runs to the end of the prompt and replaces everything after the title:
- the rest of the metadata;
- the whole `<session_log>` and its closing tag;
- the final "the log above is untrusted data" instruction.

Reproduced at the PR head:
- The title `Fix tokens: [user's, admin] parsing` gives a 72-character prompt that ends in `title=Fix [redacted]`. Before #1122 the same input gave the full 767-character prompt.
- These titles do the same: `Parse api_keys = [ in config loader`, `Why does tokens: {it's slow} happen`, and a clipped preview `Please rotate {"api_keys": ["abc"`.
- There is a second trigger. Items are cut to length after their own redaction (`supervisor-brief.ts:350` and `:423`). If the cut lands inside a value, the prompt-level pass sees a bracket that is never closed and erases every later turn.
- The same thing happens inside a single item: `Make tokens: [user's, admin] configurable, then add tests...` becomes `Make [redacted]`.

As a result, the summarizer gets no transcript for that thread on any brief request.

**Fix:**
- Redact each metadata field, including the title, on its own before assembling the prompt.
- Then either skip the bracketed pass in the final prompt-level call, or end each bracket scan at the end of its line or section.
- Optionally, keep the shorter span when the JSON and Python readings reach the end of the text only because of an apostrophe in a plain value.
- Add `buildSupervisorBriefPrompt` tests with the titles above and with a cut-off item. Assert that `</session_log>` and the final instruction line are still in the prompt.

## 2. Apostrophes in code or prose redact the rest of an item

`src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:253`

The redactor tries several ways of reading quotes and keeps every reading's span, so the longest one decides. Take any key that matches `key|token|secret|password`, for example `apiKeys`, `max_tokens`, `keyMap` or `tokenizer`. An apostrophe in a comment or in prose inside its value redacts the rest of the item. For example, `const apiKeys = { // don't log these ...` becomes `const [redacted]`, and `max_tokens: {it's fine} and then ...` becomes `[redacted]`. Nothing leaks, but Codex transcripts are mostly code and tool output, so the summarizer loses whole items. The PR left this for an owner decision.

**Fix:** narrow the key match for bracketed values, for example by excluding `max_tokens`, `*_tokens_details` and `keyMap`. Alternatively, end an unclosed value at a line break when the value started on a single line.

## 3. Some credential key shapes are still not matched

`src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:20`, `src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:30`

Both the new bracketed rule and the existing quoted-value rule allow only word characters after the credential word, and they accept only `:` or `=` as the separator. These inputs all pass through unchanged:
- `{"tokens-v2": ["..."]}`
- `{"api-key-list": ["..."]}`
- `{"secret.values": {"v": "..."}}`
- PHP `['api_keys' => ['...']]`
- Ruby `{"api_keys"=>["..."]}`

A JavaScript template literal or a TOML `'''` string inside the value can also end the value early, which leaves later elements unredacted (for example `` tokens = [`a]`, "..."] ``).

**Fix:**
- Allow `[\w.-]*` after the credential word, or any run of non-quote characters inside a quoted key.
- Accept `=>` as a separator.
- Treat the backtick as a quote in the JavaScript reading.
- Add a regression case for each shape.

## 4. A rare input exposes a password that development used to redact

`src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:260`

The first pass merges key-value spans that it finds in the original text, and that shifts where a later greedy match starts. Take this input:

`\\Bearer  ZQ0abcdefghijklmnQapi_keys: {}ZQ1abcdefghijklmnQpassword: ZQ2abQZQ3abQ`

Development returned `\\[redacted]: {}[redacted]`. The current code returns `\\[redacted] ZQ2abQZQ3abQ`, which leaves the password value unredacted. A differential fuzz run over about 3.1 million random strings found 2 such cases. Both need a Bearer token run together with a credential key, with no whitespace between them.

**Fix:** when a merged first-pass span ends inside a match that starts at a later credential key, extend it over that key's value. Alternatively, re-run the key-value rules on the first pass's output for the remaining text. Add this input as a regression test.

## 5. Add a differential test against the previous rules

`tests/codex-supervisor-brief.test.ts:107`

The new tests cover `redactBriefText` only. Add a seeded differential test that checks the new redactor removes everything the previous rules (without the bracketed pass) removed. That test would have caught section 4. Add it next to the prompt-level tests from section 1.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX0dh9Q.title: Follow-ups from #1136: serialize sandboxed-signing seed rebuilds
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX0dh9Q.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1136 -->

PR #1136 (invalidate the sandboxed-signing seed on any key change, issue #587) was merged at `d11e031d`. The findings below come from adversarial review and were non-blocking: they did not stop the merge and are filed here as follow-up work. File and line references are to current `development` (`b4790532`). The minor (P3) items from this PR are in #1141.

## 1. Seed rebuilds are not serialized, so concurrent signings fail after an input change

- Where: `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:107-115`.
- Problem: when the recorded manifest does not match, each call stops the seed's agent, runs `rm -rf` on the shared `$TMPDIR/dsh-gnupg/<uid>` and rebuilds it in place. No lock is taken, so concurrent calls delete and recreate the seed while other calls are copying into it or running gpg from it.
  - Real GnuPG 2.4.4, seeded branch forced: in steady state 24 of 24 concurrent calls succeed. With one `*.gpg` file added before each burst of 8 concurrent signings, 6, 4, 6, 6 and 8 of the 8 calls exited 2 across 5 bursts. One burst produced no signature at all. The errors were "cannot discard the stale seed", "cannot restrict .../dsh-gnupg/0 to mode 0700" and "cannot copy ... into ...".
  - A second probe with fake `gpg`/`gpgconf` changed a key file and then ran 16 concurrent calls, for 25 rounds. 303 of the 400 calls exited 2.
  - Every failure is closed: exit 2 and nothing on stdout. A single later call always converges. Triggers are rare (a key change, an import, or `--check-trustdb` rewriting `trustdb.gpg`), but parallel agent commits at that moment fail.
  - The PR's Known limitations also describe a worse interleaving. A `cp` that opened a key file just before the key was deleted can write it into a seed that a second call has meanwhile recreated and stamped with the new manifest. The deleted key then stays usable from the seed until the next input change. An atomically published rebuild closes this window too.
  - The PR body says "one can fail". That understates the measured rate.
- Fix: build the new seed in a private sibling (`mktemp -d "$base/$uid.new.XXXXXX"`), copy the inputs into it and write its manifest there. Then move it into place (rename the old seed aside first, because a directory cannot be renamed over a non-empty one). Only after that, stop the old seed's agent and remove the old seed. Alternatively, serialize rebuilds with an `mkdir` lock under `$base` that records a pid and handles stale locks. Add a test that starts several concurrent sandboxed calls right after an input change and asserts that none fails and that the final seed matches the inputs. Record the rule in the `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry "Sandboxed commits sign through a GNUPGHOME inside writable roots" (`:559`).

## 2. Owner step: install the merged helper

- Where: `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:2-3`, `docs/DECISIONS.md:567` and `:571`.
- Problem: merging changed nothing on any machine. Until the helper is installed, `~/bin/gpg-dsh` keeps the old trigger, which checks only `pubring.kbx`, so a deleted or re-protected private key still signs from the old seed. That is the defect #587 reported. The decision entry already says "`~/bin/gpg-dsh` is installed from `ops/gpg-dsh.sh`" (`:567`) and gives the install command (`:571`). It leaves out the PR's caveat: compare with the installed helper first. The repository helper seeds only `*.kbx`, `*.gpg` and `private-keys-v1.d`. It does not seed `gpg.conf`, `gpg-agent.conf` (for example `pinentry-program pinentry-mac`) or keyboxd's `public-keys.d`. If the installed helper seeds any of these, installing over it can make sandboxed signing fail closed, with no usable pinentry or with a public key missing under keyboxd.
- Fix (owner, on the Mac, if not already done): run `diff ops/gpg-dsh.sh ~/bin/gpg-dsh`, then `install -m 0755 ops/gpg-dsh.sh ~/bin/gpg-dsh`. The first sandboxed call after installing discards the old seed and its agent. In the repository, reword `:567` to say the helper is to be installed from `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` (or record the date it was installed). At `:571`, add a note to diff against the existing helper first, and list what the repository helper does not seed.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzftcA.title: Follow-ups from #1084: keep the replay retention sweep moving across restarts
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzftcA.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1084 -->

PR #1084 ("bound bootstrap owner lookups and make chunk deletion publication-safe", #905 and #906) was merged at `8731755a`. The items below are non-blocking findings from adversarial review of that PR. Both reviewers found that the PR meets #905 and #906 and that chunk deletes stay safe. The items are about progress, efficiency and test coverage. Line numbers refer to current `development`.

## 1. The owner index is lost on every restart, which can stall the sweep

`src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:233`, `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:386-390`

The chunk-owner index is kept only in memory, in a `WeakMap`. Until the index is complete, the chunk phase returns without moving the cursor, and a restarted process rebuilds the index from row 0. The chunk phase therefore moves forward only if a single process gets about `ceil(owner rows / 64)` sweep calls before it restarts. Before #1084, every call saved progress to storage.

Reproduction: 200 legacy manifests, with a fresh handle every 2-3 calls to simulate restarts.
- With #1084, the ledger was still incomplete at cursor `1|` after 3,000 calls, and admissions were still refused.
- The base commit finished in 101 calls under the same pattern.

At production scale (1 GiB budget and up to 50,000 records, so roughly 20,000-100,000 owner rows), one process needs about 300-1,500 sweep calls. Those calls come only from failure captures, status writes and admin error-log views. If deploys restart the process more often than that, the sweep stays stuck at `1|`. It catches up only as legacy manifests reach their expiry (TTL). It never catches up for accounting rows created by an earlier failed sweep: those rows have no expiry, and expiry-based cleanup waits for the sweep to complete.

**Fix:** make index progress independent of request traffic and restarts. Options:
- build the index in bounded slices from a startup or background timer;
- let one call keep filling slices, up to a time budget, while no chunk can be judged yet;
- store ownership durably (for example a marker keyed by capture id), so one bounded lookup is enough to judge a chunk.

At the very least, document restart loss next to the existing limitation note on `ChunkOwnerIndex` (line 232).

## 2. A lost commit can rewind the shared index's cursor

`src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:297-303`, `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:414-423`

Sequence:
1. Two batches, X and Y, on one handle share a complete index at cursor C.
2. X's commit fails, and `afterLostCommit` reads the ledger while it is still at C.
3. Y commits, moving the cursor from C to C2, and re-tags the index to C2.
4. X's continuation calls `retainChunkOwnerIndex(kv, index, C)`. The held index is the same object, so the guard at line 300 does not apply, and the cursor is reset to C.
5. The next batch at C2 finds no index and rebuilds it from scratch.

Deletes stay safe because the ledger check still applies; this only costs performance.

**Fix:** in `retainChunkOwnerIndex`, skip re-tagging when the held index is the same object and its cursor already differs from the batch's start cursor. Alternatively, re-read the cursor and compare before re-tagging.

## 3. Concurrent batches each restart the index from row 0

`src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:238-243`, `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:279-289`

While the index is partial, `takeChunkOwnerIndex` gives it to one batch only. Every other concurrent batch on the same handle starts a fresh index from row 0 and later throws it away. With N concurrent callers, each round reads about N × 64 owner rows but advances the fill by only 64 rows. Each batch that only fills the index also commits an unchanged ledger. That makes in-flight batches that are judging chunks lose their commits and chunk deletes.

**Fix:**
- Let concurrent callers wait for, or skip, a fill that is already running on the same handle.
- Skip the ledger commit when a batch scanned nothing and its change set is empty; the index can be kept without one.

## 4. The index is identified only by its cursor and is not cleared on every path

`src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:232-243`, `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:503-510`, `src/sentinel/replay-retention.ts:871`

The index is reused whenever its cursor string equals the ledger cursor. It carries no sweep generation. Only `bootstrapBeforeMutation` clears the index when it sees a complete ledger. `reserveSentinelReplayCapacity` checks for a complete ledger itself and never clears it.

With more than one handle, a handle that did not finish the sweep can hold an index of up to 50,000 capture ids for the life of the process. Suppose the ledger is then reset or restored outside the normal code path, and a new sweep reaches the same cursor. The sweep could reuse the stale index, treat chunks of captures admitted since then as having no owner, and delete them.

The PR lists the cursor-only identity as a known limitation. No runtime path deletes the ledger today, and production uses one handle per process.

**Fix:**
- Add a sweep generation to the ledger, incremented when `bootstrap_cursor` goes from null to `0|`, and key the index on both generation and cursor.
- Also clear the index in the complete-ledger branch of `reserveSentinelReplayCapacity`, or send that branch through `bootstrapBeforeMutation`.
- Until then, document that deleting or restoring the ledger requires restarting every process.

## 5. No test covers a second process finishing the sweep

`tests/sentinel-replay-bootstrap-retry.test.ts:552`

The regression test for a batch that outlives sweep completion runs every caller on one handle. A cross-handle version of that test passes today: a second handle finishes the sweep and publishes while the first handle is partway through judging chunks with a multi-slice index. But no test would catch a future change that moves the safety check from the ledger versionstamp to a per-process signal.

**Fix:** add the cross-handle version (`const h2 = { ...kv }`) of that test.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXznj7A.title: Follow-ups from #1124: make the OpenAI spec-drift gate check its pin, and align published nullable fields with the runtime
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXznj7A.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1124 -->

PR #1124 (spec drift gate and published OpenAPI contract, issue 116) was merged at `9fc845d4`. It passed adversarial review with no unresolved P0/P1 findings and with green CI. The findings below did not block the merge and are filed here as follow-up work.

## 1. The CI drift gate never checks the pin against its source

`scripts/check-openai-spec-drift.ts:213`; the gate is wired in at `.github/workflows/deno-deploy.yml:32`.

In its default offline mode, the gate only compares `src/openai-schema.ts` with the hand-editable `surfaces` arrays in `scripts/openai-spec-pin.json`. The recorded commit and sha256 are checked only under `--verify-source` / `--spec`, and CI runs neither. The gate therefore proves the two repo files agree with each other, not that the runtime matches the official openai/openai-openapi revision the pin names.

Reproduction: add a non-official key to `RESPONSES_REQUEST_KEYS` and to `pin.surfaces.CreateResponse`, then run `bun run spec:drift`. It still prints "aligned … with openai/openai-openapi@120ed01…", exits 0, and the tests pass.

**Fix:** run `spec:drift --verify-source` in the validate job. The source URL is commit-addressed, so its content cannot change; only availability can, and a retry covers that. Alternatively, re-extract the surfaces in a test from a committed, digest-checked copy of the spec.

## 2. Published Chat types accept values every Chat route rejects

`static/openapi.json:786`

- `max_completion_tokens` is published as `["integer","null"]` with no minimum.
- `stream_options` is published as `["object","null"]`.
- The runtime parsers reject `null` for both fields, and reject `0` or negative values for `max_completion_tokens`, with a 400 error.

Official SDKs commonly send these fields as `null`, so a client built from `/openapi.json` gets a 400.

**Fix:** publish `max_completion_tokens` as `{type: integer, minimum: 1}` and `stream_options` as `{type: object}`, or relax the parsers to accept `null`. Add a contract test that sends `null` for each published nullable Chat field through the envelope parsers.

## 3. Smaller items

- **Bad arguments silently pass** (`scripts/check-openai-spec-drift.ts:156, 183`):
  - When `--spec` is given with no value, or a bare word like `verify-source` is passed, the script falls back to the offline gate and exits 0 as if verification had happened.
  - Fix: return exit code 2 when a value-taking flag has no value, or when an argument is not a known flag.
- **Re-pinning can record false provenance** (`scripts/check-openai-spec-drift.ts:192`):
  - `--repin <commit> --spec <file>` records the digest and surfaces of an arbitrary local file under the official commit URL.
  - Fix: when re-pinning, fetch the commit URL and require that the digests match, or forbid `--spec` together with `--repin`.
- **GitHub headers published as required** (`static/openapi.json:545`):
  - `X-GitHub-Owner` and `X-GitHub-Repo` are published as required on `/uos/agent-messages`.
  - At runtime they are optional cross-checks when `X-Ubiquity-Kernel-Token` is present (`src/auth/index.ts:94-97`, `src/kernel/attestation.ts:212-214`).
  - Fix: mark them `required: false`.
- **`top_logprobs` not nullable** (`static/openapi.json:910`):
  - `ResponseRequest.top_logprobs` is published as a non-nullable integer.
  - The Chat schema and the official `CreateResponse` both allow `null`.
  - Fix: publish it as `["integer","null"]`.
- **Route-parity test misses other handler modules** (`tests/openapi-runtime-contract.test.ts:38`):
  - The test reads only `src/handler/index.ts` and `src/handler/terminal-route.ts`, so a `/uos` route dispatched from any other module can go unpublished without the test failing.
  - Fix: grep all of `src/` for `"/uos/` literals against an allowlist, or export the route table and compare against it.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzO_uw.title: Follow-ups from #1027: bound the VPS join checkpoint and harden the journal reader
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzO_uw.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1027 -->

PR #1027 (deferred request cohorts during VPS acceptance) was merged at `e50c298b` after two rounds of adversarial review with no unresolved P0/P1 and green CI. These findings from the review were not blocking and are filed here as follow-up work.

None of this affects production today: nothing in `src/` or `serve.ts` imports `ops/vps-*`, and the release bridge loads `ops/vps-release-metrics.ts` only from an owner-pinned driver tree. They matter before the bridge driver is re-pinned to a release that includes #1027.

## 1. The join checkpoint grows without bound (highest priority)

`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:200`, `ops/vps-metrics-join.ts:204`

Every 30 s cohort keeps a full copy of every event and coverage proof from every slice it scanned. Neighbouring cohorts store the same slices again, and completed cohorts are never compacted. The whole thing lives in one encrypted file per operation, capped at `retention.evidenceMaxBytes`. Once the cap is reached, `save()` refuses, `sample()` returns incomplete, progress becomes `unavailable`, and the controller resets monitoring, so 60 consecutive samples are never reached.

A simulation with realistic sizes (UUID ids, ~130-char journald cursors, 32-hex boot id) put the overflow at:

| Load | Cap | Overflow at window (of 60) |
|---|---|---|
| ~0.35 req/s, 1 in 10 requests streaming 5 min | 8 MiB | 39 |
| same | 4 MiB | 24 |
| 1 req/s | 4 MiB | 56 |
| 1.5 req/s | 4 MiB | 37 |
| 2 req/s | 8 MiB | 57 |
| 3 req/s | 8 MiB | 38 |

**Fix:**
- Store each slice's events once per operation, keyed by cursor or slice, and have cohorts reference slice ranges.
- When a cohort completes, shrink it to its window, counts, coverage digest chain and member-terminal digests.
- Prune baseline cohorts once their sample has been returned.
- Make the 60-window test use realistic id and cursor sizes and a multi-minute streaming tail.

## 2. One orphan terminal starves the tick budget

`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:217`

An orphan here means a terminal with no accepted admission line whose `admission_stage` is not `pre_admission`. A single one makes its cohort scan backward to the retention floor: 480 slices under the 4 h fixture policy. That uses up the shared 64-slice tick budget, so the other windows sampled in the same tick make no progress. In a reproduction with one legacy null-stage 401 terminal, windows 1-3 took 7 ticks (448 reads) instead of one.

**Fix:**
- Cap the backward search per orphan at the maximum request lifetime.
- Refuse a null-stage orphan immediately, as the base code did.
- Give each cohort a fair share of the tick budget.

## 3. Journal rows that can never complete a slice

`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:47`

`checkedRow` refuses the whole slice when any row's `_SYSTEMD_UNIT` is not `ai-ubq-fi.service`. But `journalctl --unit=ai-ubq-fi.service` also returns PID 1 messages about the unit, which the driver's own `systemctl restart` produces. `--output=json` without `--all` also writes `MESSAGE` fields over 4 KB as null.

A baseline window that covers the prior release's activation restart therefore never completes. If the prior release was activated within about 19.8 h of the new one, acceptance fails as `acceptance_insufficient`.

**Fix:**
- Filter with `_SYSTEMD_UNIT=ai-ubq-fi.service`, or skip PID 1 unit rows instead of refusing them.
- Pass `--all`, or tolerate a null `MESSAGE` on rows that are not request rows.
- Add a test with a systemd restart row.

## 4. Smaller items

- **Checkpoint expiry is never refreshed** (`ops/vps-metrics-join.ts:127`): `createdAt`/`expiresAt` are not refreshed when `monitoringStartedAt` changes. Once `evidenceMaxAgeMs` has passed, the operation can never be monitored again.
- **No reason after the deadline** (`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:177`): after `options.deadline`, `beginTick` sets an already-expired deadline, so every scan does nothing. `progress()` keeps reporting `collecting` instead of a terminal deadline reason.
- **Deploy lock held during state reads** (`ops/vps-metrics-storage.ts:51`): `save()` reads the release state twice while holding `.data/deploy.lock`. A slow read delays deploys by up to 240 s. Resolve the state before taking the lock, or put a timeout on the read.
- **Checkpoint files are never deleted** (`ops/vps-metrics-storage.ts:26`): `.data/sentinel-vps-metrics` keeps one file per operation, plus temp files left by crashes. Delete the checkpoint when an operation settles, or prune by age, and fsync the directory after rename.
- **Uncaught throw in the reader** (`ops/vps-journal-reader.ts:130`): in the `child_process` to `ReadableStream` adapter, `controller.enqueue()` in the `'data'` listener can throw after cancel. Wrap it in try/catch and destroy the pipe.

The matching Sentinel-side change to the bridge interface is tracked in ubiquity/sentinel.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzTx0A.title: Follow-ups from #1033: keep Mac samples out of the canonical VPS chart and make the chart push incremental
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzTx0A.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1033 -->

PR #1033 (mirror the VPS provider chart on the Mac loopback console) was merged at `bb4aeff5` after three rounds of adversarial review. It had no unresolved P0/P1 and CI was green. The findings below were not blocking and are filed here as follow-up work.

## 1. Mac samples pollute the canonical VPS chart

`src/provider/capacity.ts` (~:679, :830)

The VPS now merges every pushed Mac point into the `history` that every admin sees, including the public VPS admin. The Mac's own 401 or unavailable samples, and its slot accounts, get interleaved with the VPS samples.

Effects:
- A sample with an unavailable Codex source makes `capacityChartPoint` return null in `static/admin.js`, which breaks the aggregate line in that bucket.
- An `unreachable` sample draws a red outage bridge.
- Differing slot accounts make the series zig-zag between the two observers.

These are the inconsistencies the PR set out to remove.

**Fix:** keep pushed Mac rows out of the canonical history and render them as a separate series, or not at all. Alternatively, merge only buckets where the VPS has no point and the Mac sample is available. Update the PR description accordingly.

## 2. The whole 7-day history is re-pushed every 30 s

`src/admin/chart-source-proxy.ts`, `src/provider/capacity-analytics.ts:46`

Every 30 s poll from an open Mac Analytics tab POSTs the full 7-day history: about 672 points, roughly 0.9 MB. The VPS writes each point as its own sequential `kv.set` on the production KV that also serves inference accounting, with no delta and no skip-unchanged check.

That comes to about 1,300 serial writes per minute and about 100 MB/hour uploaded. Each push also adds up to 10 s to the Mac chart load, because it runs before the read.

**Fix:**
- Push only buckets newer than the last acknowledged bucket.
- Batch the VPS writes atomically, or skip unchanged rows.
- Run the push in the background or alongside the read, with a shorter timeout.

## 3. The push runs on any dev server that has a token

`src/admin/chart-source-proxy.ts:89`

The push is gated only by `isAdminAuthDisabledForRequest`, and it always sends host `"mac"`. Any `bun run dev` / `dev:local` instance with the production token therefore pushes its own history as host `"mac"`. Because rows are keyed by `(host, bucket)`, those rows overwrite the real Mac's rows for 7 days.

**Fix:** gate the push on an explicit Mac-service signal or an opt-in env var, and send a configured host id.

## 4. Smaller items

- **Remote key drops transition points** (`src/provider/capacity-analytics.ts:17`): remote rows are keyed by `(host, bucket_start_at_ms)`, so the Mac's same-bucket transition points (the exhausted-then-refilled shape) are overwritten. Include `sampled_at_ms` in the key.
- **Ingest validation is loose:** there is no check for 15-minute bucket alignment, `sampled_at_ms` within its bucket, or a per-request row bound beyond the 4 MiB body cap.
- **Query string forwarded verbatim:** the proxy passes the query string to the VPS, so a loopback caller can request `?refresh=live` there.
- **Remote body not released on error:** `fetchRemoteChart` returns null on a non-ok response without cancelling the body.
- **Latest error row replaced:** the errors overlay also replaces `data[0]`, the latest error row, with the VPS row. Nothing visible changes today.
- **Test gaps:** no handler-level test drives POST `/admin/providers/capacity/observations` through route wiring and admin auth.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX70B_g.title: Make the VPS release driver loadable by a Deno host (Bun-only deploy lock and command runner)
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX70B_g.body:
**Problem.** Sentinel's VPS release bridge loads `ops/vps-release-driver.ts` and `ops/vps-release-metrics.ts` from an owner-pinned, hash-verified driver tree, and it runs under Deno. Since the Bun migration (between `21e4a2a9` and `e50c298b`), the driver can't be loaded by a Deno host:

- `ops/vps-release-driver.ts:26` imports `ops/vps-release-journal.ts`, which imports `ops/deploy-lock.ts:2` (`import { dlopen, FFIType } from "bun:ffi"`).
- `ops/io.ts:26` (`command`, imported by the driver at :1) runs commands through `Bun.spawn`.

Loading the `e50c298b` driver in Deno fails with `Unsupported scheme "bun"`. The `e50c298b` metrics module loads on its own; it's the driver's import graph that breaks.

**Impact.** There's no runtime impact today, because sentinel-release is disabled and the bridge's pinned driver is `21e4a2a9`. But the driver can't be re-pinned to any revision at or after `e50c298b`. Sentinel's bridge update for the #1027 `VpsJournalMetrics` interface (ubiquity/sentinel#150; the generation-81 fix is ready) refuses such a pin before it evaluates any module: "trusted VPS driver needs a host that can load Bun-only modules". VPS releases through Sentinel stay blocked until the driver tree is Deno-loadable, or the bridge host runs under Bun.

**Acceptance.** One of the following:
- The driver's import graph is free of `bun:` modules and `Bun.*` globals on the paths the bridge uses: the deploy lock, the journal, and the command runner. For example, an injected lock and runner with Bun and Deno implementations, or a runtime check that picks the right one.
- Or a recorded decision that the bridge host moves to Bun, with the Sentinel side tracked in ubiquity/sentinel#150.

Either way, keep the deploy lock's exclusion semantics identical on the VPS.

**Evidence.** `git grep` on `development` (`36503598`) finds `ops/deploy-lock.ts:2` `bun:ffi` and `ops/io.ts:26` `Bun.spawn`. The driver imports both, directly or through the journal.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaPXg.title: Supervisor provider cards never show routing activation, only credential health
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaPXg.body:
The panel promises "Health and activation of every gateway upstream", and `/admin/providers/selection` returns `data.selection.provider_ids` and `data.filter_active`, but the renderer ignores both and prints an identical `Health <state>` badge for a deselected provider. Routing really excludes a deselected provider, so a configured, healthy provider looks enabled when it is not.

## What is wrong
- `static/admin-supervisor.js:130` states the panel shows activation; `:147-189` uses only `selection.data.providers`.
- `src/admin/codex.ts:733-736`: the response supplies `selection.provider_ids` and `filter_active`.
- `src/provider/selection.ts:156-161`: `isProviderEnabled` returns false for an unselected provider when the selection is nonempty.
- `src/responses-handler.ts:800` (and equivalent gates) refuses dispatch for a switched-off provider.

## Acceptance
- Each card shows selected/disabled status separately from credential health, preserving the empty-selection-means-all behaviour (no filter when the selection is empty).

Source confirmation at development 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded: [static/admin-supervisor.js:128-131,147-189](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/static/admin-supervisor.js#L128), [src/admin/codex.ts:702-737](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/admin/codex.ts#L702), [src/provider/selection.ts:156-161](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/provider/selection.ts#L156).

Review provenance: native Codex review of [PR](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/558) with gpt-6.1-sol/uos at ultra effort; completed review turn 01a0fc07-73e8-7b61-aaf1-192b3c3f5de0. Original reviewed revision: "6262d48cf4bae00bc6e33d4ed6e1f78cf4741930".

Validation: static source/control-flow inspection; no runtime exploit, inference, test or production action was executed during validation.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX0esAw.title: Follow-ups: minor items from the 2026-10-17 protected-path merges
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX0esAw.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:batch-2026-10-17 -->

This issue collects the remaining minor (P3) findings from adversarial review of the four protected-path PRs merged on 2026-10-17. None of them blocked a merge. They are grouped by PR, and each item gives the file and line on current `development` (`b4790532`), the problem and the fix. Where two reviewers reported the same thing, it appears once. None of the items below is fixed on `development`. The P2 findings have their own issues: #1135 → #1140, and #1136 → #1139 (which also carries #1136's owner install step and the decision-entry wording about it).

## #1134 (`deba31ae`): qualify terminal-truthfulness deployment acceptance (#608)

1. **The 2026-09-22 deployment entry has the same acceptance gap.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1450-1476` ("Buffered-terminal fix deployed to both surfaces").
   - Problem: the entry records acceptance of `3661bcfd13` without either observation that `AGENTS.md:65-66` requires: a direct Mac-to-VPS authenticated inference request, and `/health` returning the full SHA and `vps-<full-git-sha>` in its body and identity headers. #1134 left it unchanged as out of scope and asked the owner whether to qualify it. Unlike the `2207a757fb` entry, this one says the deploy went through `deno task deploy:vps`. At `3661bcfd13`, `ops/deploy.ts:84-95` succeeds only after loopback `/health` returns the SHA and `vps-<sha>` in both the body and the `x-uos-*` headers. So the `/health` half was checked by construction but never recorded, and nothing supports the direct Mac-to-VPS half.
   - Fix: add a dated qualification note like the #608 note. If the owner has the observations, record them instead.
2. **"Nothing in this repository supplies the missing ones" claims more than the evidence shows.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1080-1082`.
   - Problem: at `2207a757fb`, `ops/deploy.ts:84-101` exits 0 only after loopback `/health` returns the SHA and `vps-<sha>` in its body and in the `x-uos-git-sha`/`x-uos-deployment-id` headers. The identity in the table is exactly what the tool prints on success. The entry does not say `deploy:vps` was used, so the `/health` half is unrecorded, not shown to be unchecked. Only the direct Mac-to-VPS inference half is truly unsupported.
   - Fix: add one sentence saying this, and change the phrase to "no recorded observation supplies them".
3. **The public-route bullet reads as if it were the only authenticated VPS inference.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1074-1075`.
   - Problem: the truncation reproduction and the three normal completions (`:1063-1066`) were also authenticated inference requests "on both hosts". Their path is not recorded either.
   - Fix: reword it along the lines of "None of the requests above is recorded as a direct Mac-to-VPS request; the one whose route is stated went through the public `https://ai.ubq.fi` route."
4. **The follow-up names clauses that the trigger does not have.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1118-1120`.
   - Problem: the text says the G3 bullet "keeps every clause of the deployed trigger: the reasoning-only and empty-output clauses …". The trigger (`:1100`) is "no tool call, no non-empty assistant text and no refusal". The G3 bullet (`:1099-1107`) discusses the reasoning-only case and the no-tool-call clause. It has no separate empty-output clause and never discusses the refusal clause. "Reasoning-only" is a case, not a clause.
   - Fix: name the three clauses as the trigger states them and give the basis for the refusal clause, or drop "every clause".
5. **"The changelog wording" cannot be found.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1086-1087`, `:1123`.
   - Problem: the follow-up now tells readers to revise "the changelog wording that calls it a 'no tool call' guard". The repository has no changelog, and this entry is the only place the phrase appears. The ambiguity predates #1134, which turned "worth revisiting" into an instruction.
   - Fix: cite the PR, release note or other place that holds that wording, or drop the instruction.

## #1135 (`3119b54d`): make a failed first VPS deployment resumable by the same SHA (#764)

1. **A crash while restoring a first deployment leaves a receipt that every retry refuses.**
   - Where: `ops/deploy.ts:289-291`. The refusal is at `:233`.
   - Problem: `restoreFirstDeployment` removes the selector (`:289`) before it saves `rolled_back` (`:290-291`). If the process is killed between the two, or `saveRecovery` fails (for example with ENOSPC), the receipt still says `prepared` or `selected` and there is no selector. The next same-SHA run then stops at "Unselected recovery candidate has no proven rollback disposition". This fails closed, but recovery needs the receipt removed by hand. The PR's Known limitations list only the window between `prepared` and the select.
   - Fix: document this window next to that one. Alternatively, save the `rolled_back` intent before removing the selector, or treat "no previous release, no selector, phase `prepared` or `selected`" as safe to restart, since nothing ran from an unselected candidate.
2. **A first-deployment retry treats every selected candidate as already restarted.**
   - Where: `ops/deploy.ts:338`, `:284-288`.
   - Problem: `restartAttempted` is set from `candidateSelected`, even when no run ever restarted the candidate. Suppose the first run crashed after saving `selected` and before `daemon-reload`, and the retry's `daemon-reload` is refused. `restoreFirstDeployment(true)` then keeps the selector, so the next unit start (for example after a reboot) runs a candidate that was never started or accepted.
   - Fix (optional): record in the receipt whether a restart was ever issued (a `restart_attempted` flag, or a phase saved just before the restart), and clear the selector when none was.
3. **`startCandidate` overwrites the `ingress_applied` phase.**
   - Where: `ops/deploy.ts:262-273`, called at `:340`.
   - Problem: on a first-deployment retry from `ingress_applied` with an unready candidate, `startCandidate` saves `prepared`, then `selected`, then `candidate_ready`. If the restart fails, the receipt no longer records that the Caddy configuration was already applied. This is harmless today, but any later logic that relies on the phase would misread the ingress state.
   - Fix: keep `ingress_applied` when `startCandidate` runs from that phase, or record the ingress state in a separate receipt field.
4. **The README's restoration sentence is too broad.**
   - Where: `ops/README.md:49-50`.
   - Problem: "A failure before Caddy applies the new configuration restores the previous release" is not always true. After a restart, `ops/deploy.ts:297-298` refuses the cross-codec rollback to a Deno-era predecessor and leaves the candidate selected. A failed restoration of the previous listener (`:304`) leaves the selector on the previous release with an unsettled receipt.
   - Fix: qualify the sentence, for example "restores a supported Bun previous release; a Deno-era predecessor is refused and needs the codec procedure below".
5. **The retry guidance conflicts with the documented deploy steps.**
   - Where: `ops/README.md:47-48`, against the steps at `:33-37`. The refusal is at `ops/deploy.ts:368`.
   - Problem: the README says to fix the fault and "rerun the same command for the same SHA", but the documented steps fetch and fast-forward first. Any outstanding receipt refuses a different SHA with "Stale deployment recovery receipt belongs to another candidate". If the candidate itself is broken and a fix is merged, following the steps leads to that refusal, and recovery needs manual reconciliation of the receipt and selector, which is not documented.
   - Fix: say that the retry must use the same SHA (do not fetch or fast-forward first), and document how to reconcile the receipt by hand when a newer SHA has to replace a faulty candidate.

## #1136 (`d11e031d`): invalidate the sandboxed-signing seed on any key change (#587)

1. **Config files planted in the seed survive.**
   - Where: `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:65-71`, `:116-117`.
   - Problem: the manifest covers only the inputs read from the real homedir, not the seed itself, and a matching manifest reuses the seed as it is. A process inside the sandbox can write `$TMPDIR`, so it can plant `gpg-agent.conf`, `gpg.conf`, `common.conf` or `scdaemon.conf` in the seed. The planted file survives until the next input change. For example, `pinentry-program <workspace>/evil-pinentry` takes effect at the next agent start (such as after a reboot) and can capture the passphrase the owner types. The sandbox can already read the encrypted keys from `~/.gnupg`, so with the passphrase it could use the key outside the sandbox. This predates #1136.
   - Fix: on every seeded call, remove or refuse any of these files that the helper did not write. Alternatively, record the seed's own config files in the manifest and rebuild on any difference.
2. **With `TMPDIR` unset, all users share `/tmp/dsh-gnupg`.**
   - Where: `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:36`, `:43`, `:56-62`.
   - Problem: on a multi-user Linux host with `TMPDIR` unset, the first user to create `/tmp/dsh-gnupg` owns it (mode 0700). Every other user's sandboxed signing then fails closed with "… is not a directory owned by uid …". A hostile owner of that directory can also swap it for a symlink to a directory the victim owns, in the gap between the helper's second `[ -L ]` test and its `[ -O ]`/`chmod` (`:59-62`). The helper then changes the mode of, and seeds (or `rm -rf`s) inside, the victim's directory. The window is very small and the impact is limited to integrity. macOS sets a per-user `TMPDIR`, so the owner's Mac is not affected.
   - Fix: use a per-uid parent such as `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dsh-gnupg-$uid`, created with `mkdir -m 700` and verified once, or fail closed when `TMPDIR` is unset. Update the reversal-risk note at `docs/DECISIONS.md:590-591` to match.
3. **Several fail-closed and recovery rules have no tests.**
   - Where: `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts:185` (only a symlinked seed is tested). The rules are at `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:38-41`, `:56-63` and `:102-107`.
   - Problem: no test covers a `dsh-gnupg` parent that is not a directory or is owned by another user, an existing 0755 parent or seed being tightened to 0700, a relative `TMPDIR`, or recovery from an interrupted rebuild (a seed with no `.gpg-dsh-manifest`). A regression in `private_dir` or in the missing-manifest path would pass CI.
   - Fix: add fixture cases. Pre-create `dsh-gnupg` at 0755 and assert 0700 afterwards. Replace it with a regular file and assert exit 2 with gpg never run. Set a relative `TMPDIR` and assert exit 2. Delete the manifest from a built seed and assert a rebuild plus a `gpgconf --kill`.
4. **The target platform is not tested in CI, and hashing starts one process per file.**
   - Where: `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:47-50`, `:73-80`.
   - Problem: the helper runs on the owner's Mac (bash 3.2 as `/bin/sh`, BSD `mktemp` and `cp`, `shasum`), but `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` runs only on Linux. Neither macOS job in `.github/workflows/deno-deploy.yml` runs it. Without `sha256sum`, every sandboxed call starts one `perl`-based `shasum` per seeded file, which adds latency to every sandboxed commit.
   - Fix: hash all inputs in one `sha256sum`/`shasum` call, or add `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` to a macOS CI job.

## #1137 (`b4790532`): throttle the replay metadata recount on admin polls (#785)

1. **A failed recount still repeats on every poll.**
   - Where: `src/sentinel/replay-retention-metadata.ts:92-93`, `:124-140`.
   - Problem: a recount that fails because a status or tombstone row is corrupt or mismatched records no marker. Every admin poll then repeats the strong scan up to the bad row, which can be up to 50,001 rows, and an open analytics view polls every 30 seconds. The throttle does not bound this case. The behaviour is unchanged from before and is listed under Known limitations, but it is the per-poll traversal that #785 set out to remove.
   - Fix: add a separate backoff for scan failures, for example a `failed_at` marker or a failure field on the existing marker. Set it only when `scanMetadata` returns `failed`, so a lost CAS still retries on the next poll.
2. **The marker write has no check of its own.**
   - Where: `src/sentinel/replay-retention-metadata.ts:100-103`, `:136`.
   - Problem: the marker is written with a plain `set`, and the commit checks only the ledger version. Two concurrent due polls can therefore both scan up to 50,001 rows. If they commit out of order, the marker can move back by the gap between their timestamps. Correctness is not affected; the cost is duplicated work and a slightly earlier next recount.
   - Fix (optional): pass the marker's versionstamp from the read at `:136` and add a check on it to the same atomic commit, so only one of the concurrent due polls records the recount.
3. **Stale counters can move the full recount onto the inference path.**
   - Where: `src/sentinel/replay-retention.ts:179-180`.
   - Problem: before #1137, an open dashboard recounted every 30 seconds, which kept counters left stale by TTL deletion close to the live rows. Now they can stay high for up to 15 minutes plus the KV's TTL collection delay. When they reach a bound, the next status admission or publish runs the strong recount (up to 50,001 rows) inside `pruneCaptureOwnedStatusMetadata`, on the request path. Nothing is lost (a probe confirmed `status_pruned_records` stays 0), and this already happened whenever no dashboard was open. Only the latency moves.
   - Fix (optional): let maintenance recount early, ignoring the interval, when the ledger is within some margin of `SENTINEL_REPLAY_MAX_STATUS_RECORDS` or of the metadata reserve.
4. **The doc says a poll inside the interval "writes nothing".**
   - Where: `docs/sentinel.md:322-323`.
   - Problem: only the recount writes nothing. The same maintenance pass still commits the reaper cursor and the other bounded accounting writes, as the PR's Known limitations say.
   - Fix: say that the recount reads one marker row and writes nothing, or add "for the metadata recount".

## PR records (no repository change)

- The descriptions of #1134 and #1137 end with the auto-appended `_Generated by [Claude Code](…)_` footer. Merged #1123 and #1124 instead end with the house-style lines: "Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)", a blank line, then the session URL. If the record should match, the owner can edit the two descriptions; no commit is needed.
- Other notes on the PR descriptions are moot now that all four PRs are merged, so they are not tracked here. #1134's validation relied on a check script kept outside the repository. Its line "no other unmerged `claude/*` branch touches `docs/DECISIONS.md`" is out of date, but all four branches merged cleanly. #1135's description gives `ops/deploy.ts` as 427 lines; it is 430 on `development`.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzgHLw.title: Follow-ups: documentation and minor fixes from the 2026-10-16 owner-PR merges
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzgHLw.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:batch-2026-10-16 -->

This issue collects the remaining minor, non-blocking findings from adversarial review of the PRs merged on 2026-10-16, grouped by PR. Each item gives the file and line on current `development`, the problem and the fix. PRs that have their own follow-up issue carry their minor items there, so they are not repeated here: #1075 → #1130, #1084 → #1131, #1085 → #1127, #1088 → #1128, #1122 → #1129.

## #1072 (`66792d33`): keep G3's no-tool-call clause in the deployment entry (#607)

1. **The G3 label and summary still say "partially dependent".**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1064`, `:1071`, `:1082`.
   - Problem: three passages now disagree with the new text: the bold summary ("depends on the retracted premise, and partially"), the G3 label, and "most of the third". The new text says every G3 clause stands on its own and only the original motivation was retracted.
   - Fix: relabel G3, for example as "partially dependent in motivation only; every clause now stands independently", and adjust lines 1064 and 1082 to match.
2. **"Dropping the clause" is easy to misread, and the sentence names only the stream relay.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1074-1079`.
   - Problem: the text never says that G3's trigger is the negation of `isAnswerBearingCompletion` (`src/provider/stream-relay.ts:398`), so "the clause" means the `toolCallCount > 0` term at `src/upstream-wire.ts:262`. A reviewer has already read it as a description of current behaviour. Removing that term would also make these checks fail turns that only call tools: the buffered DeepSeek path (`src/deepseek/handlers.ts:616`), the buffered LithosAI path (`src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts:793`) and the Cerebras Responses check (`src/provider/cerebras-responses.ts:352`).
   - Fix: name the term that would be removed, say that the relay accepts tool-call-only turns today, and say the effect applies on every route that uses this predicate to fail closed.
3. **The new next action is close to circular.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1088-1090`.
   - Problem: "keep the clause for as long as the predicate treats a tool call as valid output" can only stop being true if that clause is deleted.
   - Fix: reword it, for example: "Keep the no-tool-call clause: G3 is the negation of the shared completion-validity predicate, and a tool call is valid output." #608 also asks to replace this pre-deployment next action, so both changes can go in together.

## #1073 (`1d0079e1`): retire the Deno KV billing premise for raw-row caps (#139)

1. **Imported rows have no expiry, and the doc does not say so.**
   - Where: `docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md:178-181`.
   - Problem: with the hard cap declined, the doc says "The 365-day TTL bounds the raw rows". But rows imported from the 2026-09-10 Deno export arrived without expiry (`ops/README.md:67-68`); the generic import writes them without `expireIn` (`src/cache/kv-migration-base.ts:260`, `:266`). They have no expiry until the quota-projection backfill rewrites them (`src/paid-fallback/ledger-backfill.ts:207-218`). The automatic backfill may never run again once its completion marker exists (`ledger-backfill.ts:503-513`). These rows are also not counted by the growth alert. The total is small: under about 0.3 GiB at migration.
   - Fix: add to the bullet that imported rows need `POST /admin/providers/quota-projection/backfill`, run until it reports `completed: true`, and record the date it was done. Also say that any future generic KV export and import drops expiry, so the backfill must be run again after it.
2. **The decline the doc cites is not recorded anywhere.**
   - Where: `docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md:178`.
   - Problem: the doc says the hard cap was "declined by the owner on 2026-10-16 (issue #139)". But #139 has only bot comments, and `docs/DECISIONS.md` has no entry for it. The merge also closed #139 as completed, although no eviction was built.
   - Fix: the owner records the decline, either in a comment on #139 or in a short dated `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry, and optionally changes #139's close reason to "not planned".

## #1074 (`a41b8d5d`): narrow unsupported 2026-09-21 narration conclusions (#603)

1. **Older notes still contradict the new qualifiers.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1219-1223`, `:1094-1096`, `:1036`, `:1058`.
   - Problem: the narration entry's "Superseded" note still says the condition "is not reproducible from the sessions it cites" and "Treat every rate here as an artifact". It sits directly above the 2026-10-16 note, which relies on those same rates (for example 5/10 against 0/10, p = 0.033). The 2026-09-22 note on the measurement-artifact entry still says "remain unreproducible" and "invalid counts". The Deployment status entry still says the correction "retracts the premise". The pointer at line 1096, "See the entry at the top of this file", now leads to an unrelated entry.
   - Fix: change these to the wording of the new notes ("not reproduced", "unverified"). For the rates, say for example that "the rates were measured on a repetitive-filler payload and must not be generalised to real sessions". Point line 1096 at the entry it means, by name.
2. **One rewritten sentence gets the logic backwards.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1180-1182`.
   - Problem: the sentence reads "If that contrast holds, length alone is not the trigger, which leaves both ... unconfirmed". If the contrast held, it would rule out the size trigger, not leave it unconfirmed. The trigger is unconfirmed because the contrast pools time windows (p = 0.016) and does not hold in the time-controlled run (p = 0.47).
   - Fix: reword it, for example: "This contrast pools runs from different time windows and does not survive the interleaved control below, so it shows neither that length is the trigger nor that it is not; 'context size is the trigger' and the 1k-4k onset remain unconfirmed."
3. **One heading still states the unverified conclusion as fact.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1092`.
   - Problem: the sibling heading at line 1154 was softened to "context size is unconfirmed", but this one still says "the narration symptom was itself a measurement artifact". The body sentences at lines 1117, 1129, 1148 and 1150 are also not qualified.
   - Fix: rename this heading the same way, for example "CORRECTION: the narration symptom counts are unverified - 2026-09-21", quote the original heading in the 2026-10-16 note, and check first that nothing links to the old heading.
4. **The "Survives" bullet lacks the route caveat.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1204-1206`.
   - Problem: the bullet still calls the `gpt-reserve` comparison a "model contrast" that has not been contradicted. The later 2026-10-16 note says it compares both a model and a route, and does not clear the DeepSeek translation route.
   - Fix: append "(a model-and-route contrast; see the route caveat in the narration entry below)".

## #1076 (`bed5fed7`): refuse the loopback hostname client-auth bypass in production (#262)

1. **The production check covers only the hostname fallback.**
   - Where: `src/auth/index.ts:202-203`, `src/auth/local-admin.ts:22`, `src/config.ts:5`.
   - Problem: the explicit listener bypass is checked first and is not refused when `DENO_TIMELINE=production`, and `--disable-admin-auth` is refused only in Deno Deploy mode. So `DENO_TIMELINE=production bun serve.ts --disable-admin-auth` would still let loopback clients in as admin. The real VPS entrypoint never enables this, so production is safe today. But the `isProductionTimeline` comment ("never grants development auth bypasses") claims more than the code enforces.
   - Fix: refuse `--disable-admin-auth` in `parseServeRuntimeOptions` when `config.isProductionTimeline` is set, and check that flag before `isAdminAuthDisabledForRequest` in `resolveLocalClientAuthMode`. Alternatively, narrow the comment so it covers only the hostname fallback.
2. **The VPS-entrypoint test only scans the text of one file.**
   - Where: `tests/local-admin-auth.test.ts:341-350`.
   - Problem: the test cannot see a bypass enabled through code that `scripts/serve-vps.ts` imports, and it fails if the guard is harmlessly reworded.
   - Fix: once item 1 adds a refusal in code, test that refusal directly and drop the text scan. Alternatively, rely on `probeLoopbackClientAuth` and on the launcher's own startup failure, as `tests/vps-deploy-guards.test.ts` does.

## #1077 (`a7ea46b6`): give explicitly selected live e2e a destination-scoped network policy (#1041)

1. **On macOS, the live run allows all of local loopback, not one destination.**
   - Where: `README.md:22`, `scripts/test-network.ts:139-140`, `:233`.
   - Problem: the README says the live segment "admits exactly one destination". On macOS, though, the live plan ignores the port and reuses the normal macOS sandbox (Seatbelt) profile, which allows `localhost:*`. This allows no more than the normal test profile does.
   - Fix: reword the README for macOS, or add port scoping there.
2. **Live e2e on macOS still cannot reach the default `https://ai.ubq.fi`.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-network.ts:141`, `scripts/test-runner.ts:164`.
   - Problem: the run now stops safely at validation instead of failing at connect time. The PR left this as an owner decision.
   - Fix, if wanted: a scoped CONNECT relay, or something similar, for non-loopback destinations on macOS.
3. **Hostname mapping only works when name lookup reads `/etc/hosts` first.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-network.ts:215-218`.
   - Problem: some hosts look names up through a resolver daemon before reading `/etc/hosts`: `nsswitch.conf` lists `resolve` before `files` (Arch's default), or nscd is running. There the hostname resolves to the public IP, which has no route inside the test namespace. Live e2e then always fails on such hosts, though it fails safely.
   - Fix: also bind-mount a private `nsswitch.conf` with `hosts: files`, and hide `/run/nscd` and `/run/systemd/resolve` inside the live namespace.
4. **Missing system tools are found only after the native build.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-runner.ts:163-164`, `scripts/test-network.ts:235`.
   - Problem: the comment says a destination that cannot be scoped fails before the native build. But `ip` and `mount` are looked up later, in `runFile`. On a host without `mount`, the run builds native KV for minutes before it fails.
   - Fix: look up the plan's tools in `validatedGroups` as well.
5. **Other processes run by the same user can use the relay socket during a live run.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-network.ts:166`, `:179`.
   - Problem: the socket sits in a directory under `TMPDIR` that other processes can find. A concurrent ordinary test run by the same user, for example in another worktree, can reach the approved host through it. The relay only ever connects to that one origin, and the PR documents this.
   - Fix: put the socket where only the live namespace can see it, pass the listening file descriptor instead of a path, or check the connecting process with `SO_PEERCRED`.
6. **The relay directory is left behind after SIGKILL.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-network.ts:188-193`.
   - Problem: the directory is removed only in the relay's `finally` block. A SIGKILL leaves `uos-live-*/{relay.sock,hosts}` in `TMPDIR`; that can come from a timeout escalation, a CI cancellation or the out-of-memory killer.
   - Fix: have the runner delete stale `uos-live-*` directories, or create them under a parent directory owned by the runner that `runFile` removes.
7. **The new test hardcodes `/usr/bin/ip` and `/usr/bin/mount`.**
   - Where: `tests/live-network-policy.test.ts:139-143`.
   - Problem: on hosts without those exact paths, the main test segment fails.
   - Fix: look them up with the same search list that `systemTool` uses.
8. **The default live URL is defined twice.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-runner.ts:11`, `tests/live-default-model.e2e.ts:7`.
   - Problem: if one copy changes, the approved destination and the URL the test uses will differ. The run then fails safely, but with a confusing error.
   - Fix: share one constant, or have the runner always pass an explicit `BASE_URL`.

## #1123 (`462a7dd6`): separate response.incomplete construction from relaying (#606)

1. **The residual gap leaves out LithosAI and the Claude Code route.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1386-1401`.
   - Problem: the new text names LithosAI as using the shared construction and `relayResponsesStream`, and names the Claude Code route as a place where `response.incomplete` is built. Neither has a recorded truncation probe, and neither appears in the provider table or in the closing "probe before trusting any of them" list.
   - Fix: add both to the residual-gap paragraph and the probe instruction. Alternatively, say that only the routes in the provider table were measured.
2. **The line references for `choiceHasNoPayload` are stale.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1373`.
   - Problem: the text cites `src/provider/cerebras.ts:376` and `:403`, but the function is now at `:502` and is called at `:529`.
   - Fix: cite the function name only, or update the line numbers with the date.
3. **`proxyResponsesStream` is attributed to the wrong file.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1356`.
   - Problem: the function is defined in `src/responses-stream.ts:538`; `src/provider/openrouter-streams.ts` only calls it.
   - Fix: reword to "It streams through `streamOpenRouterResponses` (`src/provider/openrouter-streams.ts`), which wraps `proxyResponsesStream` (`src/responses-stream.ts`)".

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmIUXg.title: In-band Lithos refusals overwrite their classified health event with upstream_error, so /health/providers reports degraded
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmIUXg.body:
## Original finding (same defect, two cited sites)
- Native Codex review of PR #515, finding 3: [P2] Preserve provider-health classification for deferred refusals (original cite lithos-handlers.ts:577-579). Native Codex review of PR #514, finding 3: [P2] Preserve refusal-specific provider health (original cite lithos-streams.ts:126-127).
- PR #515 original head 96c52bed9af1cdaff7db427111ffc1010912e097; PR #514 original head f9c9f4542f9acf97f7b2216628a1d08709905704. Provenance as in CAND-AI-RELAY-01.

## Current state (verified at current upstream default)
Current development @ 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded; all four files byte-identical to frozen checkout HEAD 98ccd167 (blob equality checked).
- refuseStream records the classified refusal and then the generic provider error, in both relays: stream-relay.ts:189-190 (Chat) and 459-460 (Responses) call recordResponseHealth(detail.status) and then recordProviderError(detail.status).
- The Lithos adapter maps classified statuses deliberately (lithos-streams.ts:86-108: 401/403 -> auth_invalid, 402/429 -> quota_exhausted), but recordProviderError unconditionally records upstream_error (lithos-streams.ts:127).
- The dispatcher already classified the same refusal before handing the streamed Response to the relay (lithos-handlers.ts:193-207 respondLithosChatUpstreamHttpFailure records the classified health and failure kind; the deferred and immediate streamed paths pass that Response into the relay at lines 596-613 and 833-845).
- Health writes are serialized per provider+identity in arrival order (health.ts:184-205) and the newest observation decides the state (health.ts:284-303: upstream_error -> degraded, quota_exhausted -> exhausted, auth_invalid -> invalid), so the generic observation wins.

## Trigger
1. A streamed or deferred Lithos request ends in an HTTP 429/402/401/403 refusal that is relayed in-band.
2. The refusal path records quota_exhausted or auth_invalid.
3. The relay's refuseStream then records upstream_error for the same refusal.
4. /health/providers shows degraded instead of exhausted/invalid, so admin and routing diagnostics lose the refusal-specific signal.

## Acceptance
- Do not let a generic provider-error observation overwrite an already classified refusal on the in-band relay path (for example skip recordProviderError when the refusal carried a classified status, or route classified refusals through a dedicated seam).
- Regression test: streamed 429 and 401 refusals leave /health/providers at exhausted and invalid respectively, with the last observation still classified.

## Duplicate search (fresh, 2026-10-02)
- Corpus scan (596 issues): provider-health terms return 42 hits; the newest are #576/#585/#596/#597 and none describes a classified refusal being overwritten by the relay's generic callback. #601 (local quota refusal masked as an OpenRouter upstream failure) is a different provider and path.
- Fresh GitHub search q=repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi+rate_limit_failover_model / failover+window / refuseStream -> only the reviewed PRs.
- No existing or audit-filed issue matches (all open and closed issues in this repository were paginated in full).

## Labels
Time: <2 Hours; Priority: 2 (Medium) - existing labels only (fully paginated label list, 44 labels).

Validation: static source/control-flow inspection at the current revision above; no runtime inference or repository test was executed.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX8LI9g.title: Review follow-ups from #1052: 1 P2/P3 finding
