I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUuJujw.title: Avoid complete replay metadata recounts on every admin poll
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUuJujw.body:
Maintenance currently scans the full retained status/tombstone set and writes the ledger on every admin error poll, even when nothing expired. Bound or throttle this work while preserving TTL-accounting recovery and concurrent-writer safety.

Acceptance:
- Repeated healthy admin polls avoid unnecessary complete recounts and ledger writes.
- Real expiration still converges within a documented bound, and metadata pressure can safely reclaim capacity.
- Verify current rendered/API behavior and scan/write counts with a representative retained set; this finding is source-qualified, not a measured performance result.

Files: `src/sentinel/replay-retention.ts`, `src/sentinel/replay-retention-metadata.ts`, related tests.

Official review provenance (original severity differences are preserved):

PR #778; review 5397819151 by chatgpt-codex-connector[bot] at 2026-10-02T23:26:03Z; finding 4170648542; GitHub review-creation event 16316306361.

Reviewed head: `d39f407789e7b5803413030d64ce38e1012022ff`. Reviewed base: `ead493896decaeff4f48643f8844bc05f1295672`. Source: https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/778#discussion_r4170648542

Original finding text:

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Throttle the full metadata recount on admin polling**

After bootstrap completes, every maintenance call now strongly scans up to all 50,000 permitted status/tombstone rows and writes the ledger even when nothing expired. `handleAdminErrors` awaits maintenance, and the analytics view requests `/admin/errors?limit=1` every 30 seconds, so an open dashboard repeatedly turns a lightweight poll into a full KV traversal and can contend with inference storage or make the admin request slow at normal allowed cardinalities. Gate or throttle reconciliation, or make it resumable instead of running it unconditionally here.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL_jg.title: Recheck Codex auth-repair candidate expiry at the time of the planned write
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL_jg.body:
The CLI captures one clock reading before every probe and SSH read and reuses it for planning and for the write, so a candidate that expires during those reads can still be installed and reported as `repaired`.

## What is wrong
- `scripts/codex-auth-repair.ts:588`: `const nowMs = Date.now();` is taken before `probeLocalPool`, `collectCandidates` and `assessCandidates`.
- The same `nowMs` is passed to `planCodexAuthRepair` and to `applyPlannedRepair`, so the expiry comparison does not include the time the probes took.
- A token with seconds of remaining life can be adopted after a probe window of tens of seconds.

## Trigger
A candidate authenticates early but expires while later candidate probes time out: the planner still compares its expiry against the pre-probe clock and installs an expired token, reporting `repaired`.

## Acceptance
- Expiry is rechecked against the clock at the moment of the write, and adoption is refused (or the plan re-derived) when the token is no longer valid.
- A focused test covers expiry elapsing during assessment.

## Duplicate search
- Local index (`codex-auth-repair`, expiry) → 0.
- Fresh GitHub search, 2026-10-02: `repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi is:issue "auth repair"` → 0.
- Current upstream rechecked: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` (`development`); `scripts/codex-auth-repair.ts` is byte-identical to the reviewed snapshot.

## Provenance

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaVbA.body:

- `src/openai-telemetry.ts:805-808`: `recordCompletionUsage` always passes `true` to `recordTerminalUsage`, setting `telemetry.completed = true`.
- `src/handler/terminal-route.ts:356-361,461-505`: the terminal settlement/commit paths act on that outcome.

## Acceptance
- Completion and terminal telemetry are derived from `payload.status` (completed vs incomplete/failed), and a truncated or failed buffered response does not commit as successful.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE2zQ.title: OpenRouter stream telemetry loses ResponsesStreamError kinds (stalls reported as read errors)
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE2zQ.body:
The OpenRouter Responses relay classifies stream failures with helpers that only understand `OpenRouterStreamError`, while `proxyResponsesStream` surfaces the shared `ResponsesStreamError`, so stalls and premature EOFs are recorded under the wrong terminal and failure kinds.
## What is wrong
- `failureKindForStreamError` returns `error.kind` only for `OpenRouterStreamError` and otherwise `"read_error"` (`src/provider/openrouter-streams.ts:75`).
- `terminalTypeForStreamError` returns `deadline` only for an `OpenRouterStreamError` inactivity timeout or a DOM `TimeoutError`, else `error` (`:80-86`).
- The shared proxy passes the raw error to `onFailure` (`src/responses-stream.ts:442`), and the reader throws `ResponsesStreamError` with kinds `inactivity_timeout` (`:241`), `premature_eof` (`:325-326`) and `malformed_event` (`:64`, `:69`, `:75`, `:88`).
- Both helpers are called in the OpenRouter `onFailure` (`src/provider/openrouter-streams.ts:353-360`), so a stalled stream is recorded `error`/`read_error` instead of `deadline`/`inactivity_timeout`, and a premature EOF loses its `eof` classification.
## Current evidence
- `src/provider/openrouter-streams.ts:75`, `:80-86`, `:353-360`.
- `src/responses-stream.ts:39-46`, `:241`, `:325-326`, `:442`.
- Codex review: discussion_r4151221407 on PR #564 head 641a5cf7cb21; no later commits on the file.
## Reproduction
- Static only: trace `onFailure(ResponsesStreamError{kind:"inactivity_timeout"})` through the two helpers; both return the generic classification.
## Acceptance criteria
- `ResponsesStreamError` kinds map to the same telemetry vocabulary as the OpenRouter error kinds (`deadline`, `inactivity_timeout`, `eof`, malformed-event handling).
- Focused tests cover at least the inactivity and premature-EOF kinds.
## Duplicate search
- Snapshot search for the finding id and for `stream telemetry`, `inactivity`, `premature eof`: no issue. PR #564 is the source only.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX0eOjg.title: Follow-ups from #1135: test the same-SHA retry rollback when a previous release exists
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX0eOjg.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1135 -->

PR #1135 (make a failed first VPS deployment resumable by the same SHA, issue #764) was merged at `3119b54d`. The finding below comes from adversarial review and was non-blocking: it did not stop the merge and is filed here as follow-up work. File and line references are to current `development` (`b4790532`). The minor (P3) items from this PR are in #1141.

## 1. The behaviour change that runs in production has no regression test

- Where: `ops/deploy.ts:338` (`restartAttempted: candidateSelected`). It reaches `restorePrevious` (`:294-309`) through `recoverFailedActivation` (`:348`). The tests are in `tests/vps-deploy-guards.test.ts`.
- Problem: when a run starts with the candidate already selected, it now sets `restartAttempted` to true, even if this run issues no restart. Production always has a previous release, so this is the path that matters there. If the retry's `systemctl reload caddy` fails, recovery now selects and restarts the previous release, checks its loopback and public identity, and records `rolled_back`. With a Deno-era predecessor it applies the cross-codec refusal instead and leaves the candidate selected. Before #1135, recovery only swapped the selector and recorded `rolled_back` while the candidate kept running. Reviewers traced the new behaviour as correct and safer than the old one, and the PR lists the gap under Known limitations. But no fixture reaches `restorePrevious` through this retry path:
  - "VPS post-ingress failure retains candidate and retries without restart" (`:746`) reaches a reload failure on a selected retry only in phase `ingress_applied`, where no recovery runs.
  - "VPS actual rollback and persistent/cleared same-SHA retry preserve immutable bytes" (`:709`) covers the restart branch only when it is entered from a first run.

  A run can leave the candidate selected and ready in three ways: the cross-codec refusal fired, the previous listener was not ready during an earlier restore, or the process died between saving `candidate_ready` and the reload.
- Fix: add a fault hook that stops the deploy after `candidate_ready` is saved and before the Caddy reload, using the current-profile fixture. A first run whose restore fails because the previous listener is not ready also works. On the retry, fail the reload again. Assert that the previous release is restarted once (restart count +1), that the public identity is the previous SHA, and that the phase is `rolled_back`. Then assert that the next retry accepts. Add a legacy-profile variant that asserts the cross-codec refusal leaves the candidate selected and the receipt unsettled.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaALQ.title: Sandboxed-signing cache never invalidates on private-key deletion or passphrase change
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaALQ.body:
The recorded sandboxed-signing policy seeds a per-boot GnuPG homedir from `~/.gnupg` and re-seeds only when `pubring.kbx` changes. The installed helper confirms that trigger (it compares `stat -f '%m-%z' pubring.kbx` against a stamp and only then replaces `private-keys-v1.d`), so deleting a secret key or changing its passphrase without touching the public keyring leaves the cached private keys active for the life of the boot. `$TMPDIR` does not guarantee per-boot removal for every caller.

## What is wrong
- `docs/DECISIONS.md:117-118` documents the reseed condition as `pubring.kbx` changes only.
- `~/bin/gpg-dsh` lines 34-45 implement exactly that: STAMP vs `stat -f '%m-%z' "$REAL_HOME/pubring.kbx"`, then copy `*.kbx`/`*.gpg` and replace `private-keys-v1.d`.

## Acceptance
- The documented invalidation policy includes private-key changes and deletions (or explicitly discards the seeded homedir after signing), and the helper's trigger matches the documented policy.

- Preserve the deployment lock, checkout validation, exact release identity checks, failure status, and retention only after successful verification; reject incompatible or untrusted existing release state.
- Add a synthetic regression where public verification fails after candidate installation and a second invocation verifies that same candidate after the fault clears. Preserve fail-closed behavior while the fault remains.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzfiUw.title: Follow-ups from #1075: keep the admin token out of admin:models error output
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzfiUw.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1075 -->

PR #1075 ("classify admin:models BASE_URL loopback by parsed hostname", #751) was merged at `ff2fac04`. The items below are non-blocking findings from adversarial review of that PR. The PR meets #751. Line numbers refer to current `development`.

## 1. The admin token can be printed in error output

`scripts/admin-models.ts:76`, `scripts/admin-models.ts:30`, `scripts/admin-models.ts:32`

The `catch` block prints the fetch error message unchanged. If the token is not a valid header value, Bun rejects the header before connecting, and its error message contains the full value:

`Request failed: Header 'Authorization' has invalid value: 'Bearer <token>'`

That happens, for example, when a pasted token has a trailing zero-width space or an embedded newline. The deployment admin token then ends up in terminal scrollback, CI logs or agent transcripts. The old curl version never printed it.

Lines 30 and 32 also print `BASE_URL` exactly as given, including any `user:pass@` part.

**Fix:**
- Before the request, reject a token that does not match `/^[\x21-\x7e]+$/`. The error message should name the variable but not print its value.
- Remove the token from any error text before printing it at line 76.
- At lines 30 and 32, print `url.origin` (or a URL with the credentials removed) instead of the raw `BASE_URL`.
- Add a test that a token containing `\n` or U+200B fails without the token appearing in the output.

## 2. An uppercase `HTTP_PROXY` now sends loopback requests to the proxy

`scripts/admin-models.ts:70`

For `http://` URLs, curl ignores an uppercase `HTTP_PROXY`, but Bun's `fetch` honours it. Suppose only `HTTP_PROXY` is set and `NO_PROXY` does not list the loopback host. Then the default `http://localhost:8000` request goes to the proxy instead of the local server, along with any exported token, in cleartext. This contradicts the comment at lines 19-23, which says the request goes exactly to the host that was checked. Reproduced: with an unreachable proxy, the script failed, while curl with the same environment reached the local server.

**Fix:** when the hostname is loopback, bypass any proxy, for example by adding the hostname to `NO_PROXY` for the request (Bun honours it). Alternatively, document that `HTTP(S)_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` now apply. Add a test that the loopback request is not proxied.

## 3. The token is still sent over plain `http://` to non-loopback hosts

`scripts/admin-models.ts:24-40`, `scripts/admin-models.ts:71`

With a token exported, `BASE_URL=http://ai.ubq.fi`, or a LAN address over http, sends the admin credential unencrypted. This behaviour predates #1075.

**Fix:** in `resolveEndpoint`, when a token is set and the host is not loopback, refuse `http:` or require an explicit opt-in.

## 4. The script test fails in paths with spaces or non-ASCII characters

`tests/admin-models-script.test.ts:121`

`new URL("..", import.meta.url).pathname` keeps percent-encoding. In a clone under `/Users/me/My Repos/`, the child process's working directory therefore points to a directory that does not exist, and the test fails.

**Fix:** use `fileURLToPath(new URL("..", import.meta.url))` from `node:url`, as `scripts/test-runner.ts` already does.

## 5. The README misdescribes the old behaviour

`README.md:717`

"Both tasks exit non-zero on an HTTP error rather than printing an empty result" is only half right about the old behaviour. Before #1075, `:spark` printed an empty list and plain `admin:models` printed the error body; both exited with 0.

**Fix:** reword it, for example: "Both tasks now exit non-zero on an HTTP error (previously `:spark` printed an empty list and `admin:models` printed the error body, both with exit 0)."

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzfRZw.title: Follow-ups from #1088: order and time out provider-strip refreshes so old health is never shown as current
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzfRZw.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1088 -->

PR #1088 was the automated repair for #596 ("Failed provider-strip refresh leaves old health badges presented as current"). It was merged at `b89a9978` under the three-review-round rule. The items below are non-blocking findings from adversarial review of that PR. One reviewer found #596 met for its main case; the other found it not fully met. #596 was closed when the PR merged, so this issue carries the remaining work. Line numbers refer to current `development`.

## 1. #596 acceptance that is still unmet

#596's acceptance criterion: "A failed or non-2xx provider refresh marks the strip stale/unavailable or clears its previous health claims, so old badges are not presented as current."

What #1088 delivered: a single refresh can fail in several ways: a non-2xx response from `/admin/providers/selection` or `/admin/providers`, a body that does not parse, or a rejected fetch. In each case the rows are now replaced with "Provider health unavailable; previous observations cleared." (`static/admin-supervisor.js:190-209`).

What is still unmet:
- **Out-of-order refreshes.** Suppose an older refresh succeeds after a newer one has failed. The older refresh re-renders its rows with no stale marker and overwrites the "unavailable" state, so older badges are shown as current until the next 15-second tick. The reverse also happens: an older failure that finishes late wipes newer, valid rows (section 2).
- **Refreshes that never finish.** A provider request that hangs never fails, so the previous rows stay on screen as current for as long as it hangs (section 3).
- **A 2xx response with no providers.** If the selection response has an empty or missing `data.providers`, `renderProviders` returns early and the previous rows stay on screen as current (section 5). Today's server always returns the full roster, so only a schema change or a misbehaving proxy can trigger this.
- **No tests.** Nothing tests any of this, so reverting #1088 would still pass CI (section 4).

## 2. Provider refreshes are not sequenced

`static/admin-supervisor.js:194-210`, `static/admin-supervisor.js:740`

`load()` starts `void loadProviders()` on every tick and on every visibility change. There is no generation check and no abort, so whichever response finishes last wins. A reviewer reproduced both orders with a fake-DOM harness.

**Fix:** use the pattern already in `static/admin.js:3694-3705`. At the start of `loadProviders`, take `const id = ++providersLoadId`. After each `await`, return early when `id !== providersLoadId || !active`. Alternatively, keep a providers `AbortController` and abort the previous request, as `load()` already does for the sessions request.

## 3. Provider requests have no timeout

`static/admin-supervisor.js:199-202`

The two fetches have no abort signal. A stalled request leaves the old rows up with no stale marker; causes include a network drop, a VPN change or a laptop going to sleep. Every 15-second tick also adds two more pending requests to the same origin. On HTTP/1.1 these can use up the browser's connections to that host and delay other admin calls.

**Fix:**
- Pass `signal: AbortSignal.any([perRefreshController.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(REFRESH_MS - 1000)])` to both fetches.
- Mark the strip unavailable when a request times out, but not when it was aborted because a newer refresh started.
- Optionally show a "sampled at" time from `generated_at_ms`.

## 4. No regression test for the failure path

`tests/admin-supervisor-follow.test.ts:151`

The existing harness rejects every `/admin/providers*` request, and its `FakeSection.append()` discards the providers card, so no test ever reads the strip. Changing line 205 back to `if (selection) renderProviders(...)` still passes every test.

**Fix:**
- Make the harness keep the appended card.
- Add tests that render a healthy strip and then refresh with each of these failures:
  - a 502 from the selection endpoint;
  - a 500 from the health endpoint;
  - a body that does not parse;
  - a rejected fetch.
- After each failure, assert that the old "Health ..." text is gone.
- Add an out-of-order test with the fix in section 2, and a timeout test with the fix in section 3.

## 5. An empty provider list on a 2xx response keeps the old rows

`static/admin-supervisor.js:147-149`

**Fix:** when `entries.length === 0`, call `markProvidersUnavailable()` or render an explicit "no providers" state instead of returning.

## 6. Polish for the unavailable state

`static/admin-supervisor.js:136`, `static/admin-supervisor.js:190-192`

- When only the health request fails, the whole roster (tier, model count, endpoints) is now hidden, even though the selection data loaded fine. Before #1088 those rows showed "Health unknown", which claimed nothing false. Consider rendering the rows with health shown as "unknown · refresh failed".
- The message says "previous observations cleared" even on the first load, for example with an expired admin token, when nothing was shown before. Use different wording for a first load.
- The message is bare text inside an element with `role="list"`, so screen readers announce an empty list. Put the message in a `role="listitem"` element or a status element.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzfI4g.title: Follow-ups from #1085: restore revoke for expired keys and finish the #112 admin fixes
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXzfI4g.body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1085 -->

PR #1085 was the automated repair for #112 ("Make admin state changes race-safe and non-cacheable"). It was merged at `14e90623` under the three-review-round rule. The items below are non-blocking findings from adversarial review of that PR. Both reviewers found that it does not fully meet #112's acceptance criteria. #112 was closed when the PR merged, so this issue carries the remaining work. Line numbers refer to current `development`.

## 1. #112 acceptance criteria that are still unmet

| #112 acceptance criterion | Status after #1085 |
|---|---|
| Queue one follow-up defaults save when inputs change during an active save; an older response must not overwrite newer input values. | **Partly met.** The queue and the revision check exist. But when a defaults reload is running, the queued save is dropped and the newer edit is never saved (section 3). |
| Represent expired keys separately from Active and Revoked in badges and filters; unrevoke must not present an expired key as usable. | **Partly met.** The badge, the Expired tab and the summary count are correct when the list is rendered. Editing a key's expiry, or a key expiring while the page is open, leaves the old status, tab and buttons in place (section 4). After an unrevoke, the "remains expired" notice is overwritten before anyone can read it (section 7). |
| Require an explicit confirmation naming the key before revocation; cancellation sends no request. | **Met for named keys.** Cancelling sends no request. For an unnamed key the prompt reads `Revoke API key "this API key"?`, which does not say which key it is (section 10). |
| Add `Cache-Control: no-store` to every `/admin/*` success and error response, including authentication failures. | **Mostly met.** Every response that passes through `withCors` (`src/http.ts:52-64`) gets the header, including 401, 404, 405 and OPTIONS. An admin handler that throws gets the runtime's bare 500 without it (section 8). The admin page is also served at `/admin.html`, and that alias can still be cached (section 9). |
| Add deterministic tests for a delayed save, expired unrevoke, revoke cancellation, and route-wide cache headers. | **Not met.** The PR changed no test file (section 5). |

The PR also introduced a regression that none of these criteria covers (section 2). Fix it first.

## 2. Expired keys can no longer be revoked or deleted

`static/admin.js:6804`, `static/admin.js:6813`

The row's action gate used to check "not revoked". It now checks `statusKind === "active"`, and the other branch checks `statusKind === "revoked"`. A key that has expired but was never revoked therefore gets only the Edit button. The server deletes only revoked keys (`src/admin/api-key-mutations.ts:813`), so this key can be neither revoked nor deleted from the UI. The only workaround is to move its expiry into the future, which makes a possibly leaked key work again, and then revoke and delete it.

The browser also judges expiry by its own clock (`isExpiredAt`, `static/admin.js:918`), while the server uses the server clock (`src/api-key-policy.ts:278`). If the admin's clock runs fast, a key the gateway still accepts shows as Expired and has no Revoke button.

**Fix:** show Revoke for every key that is not revoked (`if (statusKind !== "revoked")`), and keep Unrevoke and Delete for revoked keys. Add a test that an expired key that was never revoked still renders a Revoke button.

## 3. A queued defaults save is lost during a reload and can be sent to another gateway

`static/admin.js:10414`, `static/admin.js:10480-10482`, `static/admin.js:8928`, `static/admin.js:10742`

When the admin edits a default while a save is in flight, `defaultsSaveQueued` is set. If the window regains focus in the meantime, the foreground refresh calls `loadDefaults({ preserveInputs: true })`, which sets `defaultsLoaded = false`. When the first save returns, the `finally` block clears the queue and calls `saveDefaults()`, which returns immediately at `if (!defaultsLoaded) return;`. The newer value stays in the input but is never sent, and the badge stays on "Saving latest changes...". A reviewer reproduced this; only the first value was POSTed.

The queued save is also not tied to the gateway target. After a target switch it can run against the new target and POST that target's freshly loaded values back to it, including client-side fallbacks for fields the server had left empty.

**Fix:**
- When `saveDefaults` returns early because defaults are not loaded, leave `defaultsSaveQueued` set.
- At the end of `loadDefaults`, once `defaultsLoaded` is true again, send the queued save.
- Record `defaultsLoadId` (or the target) when the save is queued, and drop the queued save if it no longer matches.
- On a target change, or a load without `preserveInputs`, clear the queue and increment `defaultsEditRevision`.

## 4. Key status does not update after an expiry edit or when a key expires

`static/admin.js:7306`

After a successful edit, only the Expires text is rewritten. The status badge, the row's `data-state`, the Revoke and Unrevoke buttons, the tab the row is filtered into and the access summary all keep their old values. If an admin sets an Active key's expiry to yesterday, the key stays green, stays in the Active tab and is still counted as active. If an admin extends an Expired key, it stays Expired with no Revoke button. A key that passes its expiry while the page is open also keeps showing Active.

**Fix:** after a successful edit, either call `renderKeys(allKeys, currentKeyView)` again, or recompute the status and update the badge, `row.dataset.state`, the Expires state and the buttons in place. Then call `updateAccessApiKeysSummary()`. Also consider re-rendering when the earliest upcoming expiry passes.

## 5. Add the tests #112 asked for

`tests/static-assets.test.ts`, `tests/admin-auth.test.ts`, `src/http.ts:64`

No test checks any of #112's behaviour. If someone deleted the `isAdminPath` line in `withCors`, CI would still pass, because the existing `no-store` assertions only cover routes that set the header themselves.

**Fix:** add these tests:
- A handler-level test that calls every admin route and an unknown `/admin/...` path, once with no token and once with a wrong token. It should also cover `GET`/`HEAD /admin` and an `OPTIONS` request, and assert `cache-control: no-store` on every response.
- An `admin.js` test (with a DOM stub or extracted helpers) that holds the first `POST /admin/defaults`, edits an input and then lets the first save finish. It should assert that a second POST carries the new value and that the input was not overwritten. Add the reload-during-save case from section 3 as well.
- A test that a `confirm()` returning false sends no `/admin/api-keys/revoke` request.
- A test that unrevoking an expired key shows the "remains expired" warning and leaves the row marked Expired.
- The Revoke-button test for expired keys from section 2.

## 6. The queued save skips the 500 ms debounce

`static/admin.js:10480-10482`

The queued follow-up save runs as soon as the previous save finishes. Suppose the admin types `100` into the global request-limit field and the first keystroke lands while a save is in flight. Then `kernel_policy_limit_requests=1` is saved at once and stays the global default until the next save.

**Fix:** when the queue is set, call `scheduleDefaultsSave()` instead of `void saveDefaults()`.

## 7. The "remains expired" notice is never visible

`static/admin.js:8714-8719`, `static/admin.js:8436`

`unrevokeKey` sets the badge to "Unrevoked <name> · remains expired" and then calls `refreshKeys()`. That call immediately replaces the badge with "Cached · refreshing", and later with "N API keys".

**Fix:** show the warning as a toast, or set the badge after `refreshKeys()` finishes.

## 8. Admin handlers that throw return a 500 without `no-store`

`src/runtime/http.ts:216-218`

An uncaught exception in an admin route skips `withCors` and reaches the runtime's fallback, which writes a plain 500 with no `Cache-Control` header.

**Fix:** catch errors around the admin dispatch and return the error response through `withCors`. Alternatively, have the runtime fallback set `no-store` when the path starts with `/admin`.

## 9. `/admin.html` can still be cached

`src/static.ts:79`, `src/http.ts:52-56`

The admin page is served at both `/admin` and `/admin.html`. `isAdminPath` matches only `/admin` and paths under `/admin/`, so in deploy mode `/admin.html` is still sent with `public, max-age=300`.

**Fix:** also match `/admin.html` in `isAdminPath`, or serve the admin page with `no-store`.

## 10. The revoke prompt does not name unnamed keys

`static/admin.js:6810`, `static/admin.js:8659`

Unnamed keys are passed in as `"this API key"`, so every unnamed key gets the same prompt.

**Fix:** when the name is empty, use the key id or prefix in the prompt.

## 11. Expired rows have no accent colour

`static/admin.js:6639`, `static/style.css:880-890`

Expired rows now get `data-state="expired"`, but the stylesheet only styles `active`, `warning` and `revoked`.

**Fix:** add a `[data-key][data-state="expired"]` rule, or give expired rows the `warning` state.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaPlw.title: Failed provider-strip refresh leaves old health badges presented as current
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaPlw.body:
After one successful load, a failed or non-2xx `/admin/providers/selection` (or `/admin/providers`) request leaves the previous provider rows in place with no staleness marking: the handler renders only when a selection payload was parsed, and the sessions panel independently keeps reporting successful samples. Operators keep seeing old health badges as current observations.

## What is wrong

- `static/admin-supervisor.js:744-755`: the sessions request keeps updating its own badge (`Sampled ...`) regardless of the provider-strip failure.

## Acceptance
- A failed or non-2xx provider refresh marks the strip stale/unavailable or clears its previous health claims, so old badges are not presented as current.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABN6XlfA.title: Make admin state changes race-safe and non-cacheable
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABN6XlfA.body:
The admin surface can lose a defaults edit made while a prior save is in flight, renders an expired-but-unrevoked API key as Active, unrevokes an already expired key without clarifying that it remains unusable, and revokes without confirmation. Most /admin/* responses also lack a uniform Cache-Control: no-store policy.

Acceptance:
- Queue one follow-up defaults save when inputs change during an active save; an older response must not overwrite newer input values.
- Represent expired keys separately from Active and Revoked in badges and filters; unrevoke must not present an expired key as usable.
- Require an explicit confirmation naming the key before revocation; cancellation sends no request.
- Add Cache-Control: no-store to every /admin/* success and error response, including authentication failures.
- Add deterministic tests for a delayed save, expired unrevoke, revoke cancellation, and route-wide cache headers.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUleDwA.title: Per-upstream truncation entry claims no other route can emit response.incomplete, but the shared relay can
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUleDwA.body:
The per-upstream truncation entry concludes that `response.incomplete` has exactly one construction site and that no other provider route can emit it. Current code has a second emitter in the shared provider stream relay, so the entry's gap analysis ("the untested surface is empty") no longer holds.

## What is wrong
- Entry text: "`response.incomplete` is built at exactly one place, `src/deepseek/responses.ts`" and "No other provider route can emit it" (`docs/DECISIONS.md:732`), plus "neither can currently emit the incompletion at all, so the untested surface is empty until either is deliberately wired in" (`:761`).
- Current code: `relayResponsesStream` settles `response.incomplete` whenever the provider translator's terminal kind is incomplete (`src/provider/stream-relay.ts:425-432`), and that relay is used by non-DeepSeek routes such as Lithos (`src/provider/lithos-streams.ts:214`).
- The distinction the entry needs is construction versus relaying/mapping, which is exactly what the review asked for.

## Acceptance
- The entry states where the incompletion can be constructed and where it can be relayed/mapped.
- The Surplus/OpenLux gap is re-scoped accordingly rather than describing the untested surface as empty.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABVAX3tA.title: Deletion races with publication
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABVAX3tA.body:
Original current-head App review finding from PR #888 at `265daa8e0dd544016fce8103d5cdfe3ce8ecab37` against `de16d5db5131732360824239875f49af5f335ea1`; review [5407274312](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/888#pullrequestreview-5407274312), state COMMENTED. Severity P1. This is an unfixed asynchronous review backlog item, not a delivery or runtime acceptance claim.

Original finding text:

The owner scan and deletion are separate. A writer can publish a manifest/accounting row after the scan but before deletion; since the delete checks only the chunk versionstamp, it can remove a live capture's payload.

Acceptance:
- Preserve live capture payload when publication interleaves with bootstrap.
- Account for orphan bytes or reclaim them with publication-safe ownership checks.
- Keep bootstrap work bounded and verify the affected real consumer with a focused deterministic regression.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABSpNGfw.title: Redact credential JSON values that are not bare quoted strings
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABSpNGfw.body:
P2 finding from the local Codex review of the ai.ubq.fi gateway P1 remediation. Reviewed delta `63aecbc53fe17dc02562c25d4af5c74c27416a33..045a86fca03b495990f97b91a240532d1f77e531`, integrated at `588142ed4871f20c01aa5224754ad02a36f476e5` and merged to `development` as `689fe1907ed8b5c76b8358176898d2dc2f36b8a9`.

## Problem

`src/codex_supervisor_secret.ts:16-18` only redacts a credential keyword whose value is a bare quoted scalar. The fallback pattern still requires the separator with no intervening key quote, so a quoted JSON key's own closing quote blocks every pattern once the value is an array or object. Evaluating the shipped pattern list directly against `redactSupervisorSecrets`:

- `{"api_keys":["opaqueSecretValueXYZ"]}` — 0 redactions
- `{"api_keys": ["eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9", "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9"]}` — 0 redactions
- `{"tokens":{"value":"opaqueSecretValueXYZ"}}` — 0 redactions
- `{"access_token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9"}` — 1 redaction (the round-1 named shape, now fixed)

This is pre-existing behavior rather than a regression from the repair, but it is the same "pattern cannot cross the closing quote" defect the P1 named, and the affected text is transcript content that leaves the host for the external summarizer.

## Acceptance

- Let the quoted-value patterns accept non-scalar values, or allow the closing key quote before the separator in the fallback, so a credential-like key whose value is an array or object is redacted too.
- Add focused regression cases for the array and nested-object shapes next to the existing quoted-JSON cases in `tests/codex_supervisor_brief.test.ts`.

Severity: P2, non-blocking. The module policy in the same file already accepts over-broad redaction, so the fix is in the direction of the module's own contract.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABVAX5Gg.title: Owner lookup defeats bounded bootstrap
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABVAX5Gg.body:
Original current-head App review finding from PR #888 at `265daa8e0dd544016fce8103d5cdfe3ce8ecab37` against `de16d5db5131732360824239875f49af5f335ea1`; review [5407274312](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/888#pullrequestreview-5407274312), state COMMENTED. Every chunk performs full accounting and manifest scans. The outer 32-entry budget does not bound these reads, so many retained captures and orphan chunks can make bootstrap prohibitively expensive and leave admissions unavailable.

- Account for orphan bytes or reclaim them with publication-safe ownership checks.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbubg.title: admin:models tasks classify loopback by URL prefix instead of the parsed hostname
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbubg.body:
**What is wrong:** `deno task admin:models` and `deno task admin:models:spark` decide whether a `BASE_URL` is loopback with the shell patterns `http://localhost*|http://127.*|http://[::1]*` (`deno.json:19-20`). Those are case-sensitive prefixes, not hostname checks: `http://localhost.example.com` and `http://127.0.0.1.example.com` are treated as loopback and queried with no credential requirement, while valid local endpoints such as `http://LOCALHOST:8000` or the expanded IPv6 loopback `http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:8000` are rejected as non-loopback. The `:spark` variant then pipes the response through `jq`, so a remote 401 leaves it with an empty list and exit status 0 — a silent "no models" result instead of the intended credential error.

**Where:** https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/deno.json#L19 and https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/deno.json#L20. The server classifies a parsed hostname instead: `src/auth/local-admin.ts:28-48` normalizes case and brackets and accepts `localhost`, `::1`, `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1` and the `127.0.0.0/8` range.

**Current proof:** present at development `5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b`; both task definitions are unchanged from validation head `dfcb82280f8c3236811cd3384f9bb1ac9a618ee9`. Source read only — no task, build, or runtime was executed for this validation. Originally reported from the PR #227 review.

**Trigger:** export neither token variable, then run `BASE_URL=http://localhost.example.com deno task admin:models` (no error) or `BASE_URL=http://LOCALHOST:8000 deno task admin:models` (spurious credential error).

**Acceptance:** parse the URL hostname once and classify it the same way the server does (case-insensitive, bracketed IPv6, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`), rejecting a non-loopback host without a token; a focused shell/Deno check covers `localhost.example.com`, `LOCALHOST`, and expanded IPv6 loopback. Keep the loopback defaults unchanged.
Source PR: https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/227

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUleA0w.title: Narration decision record keeps unsupported statistical conclusions
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUleA0w.body:
The 2026-09-21 narration entries in `docs/DECISIONS.md` still assert conclusions their own data do not support, and the correction entries repeat the same errors. The record is the repository's decision authority, so the surviving claims can steer future work.

## What is wrong
- Cross-route control: the model-versus-gateway conclusion rests on a comparison whose cells do not traverse the same gateway path (DeepSeek goes through its translation route while `gpt-reserve` does not), so it cannot clear the gateway for the DeepSeek route as written ("A translation or transport defect in this gateway would not spare one provider and hit the other on an identical body", `:675`).
- Pooled rate arithmetic: the six DeepSeek bands above 1k narrate 3+4+1+5+4+5 = 22 of 60 runs = 36.7%, recorded as "pooling to 38%" (`:678`, table `:658-667`).
- Effort conclusion: "reasoning effort is ruled out as the cause" (`:697`) is stronger than the measurement (only `gpt-reserve` was swept at medium and max; the DeepSeek sweep is underpowered at n = 10 per cell), and the same entry records 20-60% variation across DeepSeek tiers (`:654-667`).
- Falsification headline: the correction entry headlines "That is falsified" (`:589`) while its own time-controlled contrast is non-significant (`p = 0.47` each, `:615`), so context length is not excluded as a trigger.
- Window mismatch: the artifact correction compares full-session totals against the handoff's explicitly windowed observation (2026-09-21 13:26-13:56 UTC, handoff `:50`) and then concludes the measurement "cannot be reconstructed" (`:550-562`).
- Classifier mismatch: the artifact correction uses as counterexamples messages "followed by a tool call" (`:565`), while promise-narration is defined in the handoff as a trailing message with "no tool call after it" (handoff `:57-58`), so those examples are negatives under the recorded classifier.

## Acceptance
- The record either corrects each claim or narrows it to what the cited measurement supports: same-path control, 36.7% (37%) pooling, the effort conclusion limited to the matched max comparison and marked underpowered, falsification language replaced with "unconfirmed", counts compared inside the stated window, and the documented classifier applied before concluding the original count was an artifact.
- Historical 2026-09-21 entries may keep their original numbers, but each carries an explicit superseded/qualified annotation rather than being silently rewritten.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajRLQ.title: Add oldest-first byte-budget eviction for raw paid-fallback rows (age TTL only today)
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajRLQ.body:
## Context
PR #135 gave raw paid-fallback request rows a 365-day age TTL (anchored to `created_at_ms`, re-applied on every write) plus forever-kept hourly rollups. There is still no hard storage cap: the Deno KV plan includes 5 GiB then bills bash.75/GiB.

## Gap
- An age TTL is 'delete eventually', not 'stop at a budget'. Storage can grow beyond what we want to pay before rows age out.
- No byte/count ceiling exists; Deno KV expired keys may also linger briefly against storage.

## Proposed
Add a configurable oldest-first cap: timestamp-ordered eviction (the legacy analytics scheme used `[keyId, createdAtMs, requestId]` and is a precedent for the key shape) or a global age index, plus a lease-guarded maintenance sweep that deletes oldest-first in batch atomics until the byte budget is met. The rollups + balance history remain the research store and must never be evicted.

## References
- PR #135 design note (docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md 'Follow-ups') — original ask was an eviction policy of oldest when hitting limits.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUleFBA.title: Deployment entry still offers dropping G3's no-tool-call clause
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUleFBA.body:
The terminal-truthfulness deployment entry tells a future deployer to "justify or drop the no-tool-call clause" from G3. Dropping it would misclassify every tool-call-only turn as `empty_upstream_completion`, because the repository's completion-validity predicate treats tool calls as answer-bearing.

## What is wrong
- Guidance: "re-derive G3's trigger from the surviving evidence alone - keep the reasoning-only and empty-output clauses, and justify or drop the no-tool-call clause on its own merits" (`docs/DECISIONS.md:538-540`).
- Predicate: `isAnswerBearingCompletion` returns true when text, refusal or `toolCallCount > 0` (`src/upstream-wire.ts:259-260`); the relay fails a completed terminal closed only when that predicate is false (`src/provider/stream-relay.ts:394-405`).
- The retracted narration cases carried non-empty assistant text, so they never depended on the tool-call clause.

## Acceptance
- The entry retains the tool-call condition or states explicitly that it must be kept while the predicate treats tool calls as valid output.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUld_5A.title: Terminal-mapping handoff contradicts its own G1/G2/G3 rules
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUld_5A.body:
`docs/handoff/gateway-terminal-truthfulness-handoff-2026-09-21.md` contradicts itself between its research summary, its G1 stop-reason table, and its G2/G3 decision rules. The document is still cited as the program's specification, so a reader can implement the wrong terminal mapping.

## What is wrong
- G2 evaluates "at least one tool call" and then "a non-empty assistant message" before the stop reason (`:310-318`), so a `length` stop that already produced output matches the first rows and is reported as `completed`, defeating G1's `length` row (`:284-292`).
- G1 maps `stop` "(or absent)" to `response.completed` as unchanged behavior (`:288`), directly contradicting the research summary two sections earlier: "never treat an absent reason as proof of a normal stop" (`:257-260`).
- G3's trigger is "answer-bearing output is empty and no tool call was emitted" (`:344-345`), which is exactly the reasoning-only case, so it competes with G1's `length` mapping and with the Cerebras reasoning-only policy in `AGENTS.md:67-70`.

## Acceptance
- The document orders terminal validity after the stop-reason mapping, or states the precedence explicitly.
- An absent reason is treated as unknown/fail-closed rather than as a normal stop.
- G3 is scoped to zero output items so reasoning-only outcomes stay with G1/G2.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnqtkQ.title: The chat probe only recognizes localhost and 127.0.0.1

The probe is gated by isLocalDevelopmentOrigin(), which returns true only for hostname localhost or 127.0.0.1 over http (static/auth.js:17-22). A supported listener such as --host ::1 is never probed from http://[::1]:8000, and the server-side check (src/auth/index.ts:194) does accept ::1 and [::1], so the page reports "Missing token" while the server would grant the loopback bypass. I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnq5TQ.title: Documented capacity staleness is bounded at fifteen minutes but is actually unbounded
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnq5TQ.body:
## Confirmed defect

The doc says capacity history converges "on the next request or the next admin read", with "up to fifteen minutes" of staleness. The fifteen-minute figure is a one-probe-per-bucket debounce (:23-26), not an age bound: with no qualifying event an ordinary admin read selects the persisted view rather than refreshing, so a snapshot can be hours or days old while reads keep succeeding. Only ?refresh=live forces a probe.

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABU14-WQ.body:
A usable partial response that honors the client output token limit is recorded as upstream_error solely because its terminal is response.incomplete.

Acceptance:

- Preserve incomplete-response telemetry and avoid reintroducing the unconditional success overwrite fixed for #585.

Files: `src/provider/cerebras-responses.ts` and the focused affected-handler fixture.

Current source qualification at `ae3e13f255de8a05fc096ea97947c481ee731a25`: src/provider/cerebras-responses.ts:143-152 sends all non-completed terminals to recordCerebrasProviderHealth("upstream_error"), including response.incomplete. Fresh static inspection only; no runtime, provider, service, browser, or repository test was executed for this intake.

Duplicate check: complete all-state inventory is 232 of 232 issues. #585 addresses duplicate success observations after non-completed terminals; this finding concerns the upstream_error classification of ordinary usable token-budget incompleteness. #634 concerns null-content documentation and #618 Lithos double recording.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE3LA.title: Cold OpenRouter catalogue refresh delays unrelated model requests and ignores the enabled selection
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE3LA.body:
When the OpenRouter catalogue snapshot is cold and an API key is configured, `resolveOpenRouterUpstreamModel` awaits a catalogue fetch for any requested model id, and the Responses path awaits it before checking whether OpenRouter is enabled at all. Every coalesced request after a restart can therefore pay the catalogue timeout (now 20 s) even when the id cannot be served by OpenRouter.
## What is wrong
- `resolveOpenRouterUpstreamModel` returns early only when a snapshot is already warm or no key exists; otherwise it awaits `fetchOpenRouterModels()` and re-resolves (`src/provider/openrouter.ts:66-72`). It never rejects a non-OpenRouter-shaped id before the refresh, and the id shape is only checked by the post-refresh lookup (`openRouterUpstreamModelFor`, `:52-55`).
- The catalogue transport timeout is `OPENROUTER_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000` (`src/provider/openrouter.ts:22`), so the stall is up to 20 s.
- Chat path: the provider-enabled check now comes first, but with OpenRouter enabled a non-OpenRouter id (default or explicit Codex model) still awaits the cold refresh (`src/chat/envelope.ts:578`).
- Responses path: the await happens before the enabled check (`src/responses-handler.ts:806`), so even a disabled OpenRouter with a configured key still contacts the catalogue on a cold cache.
## Current evidence
- `src/provider/openrouter.ts:22`, `:52-55`, `:66-72`.
- `src/chat/envelope.ts:578`.
- `src/responses-handler.ts:806`.
- Codex reviews: discussion_r4151411427 and discussion_r4151411430 on PR #567 head 9b5dc6fa26ae; both files unchanged since that merge.
## Reproduction
- Static only: cold snapshot plus key present, request a Codex id, and follow both paths to the awaited refresh. Optional dynamic proof belongs to a registered host run, not this analysis.
## Acceptance criteria
- Ids that cannot be OpenRouter-shaped skip the cold refresh, and the provider-selection check precedes any refresh on the Responses path.
- Focused tests cover a cold snapshot with a Codex id and with OpenRouter disabled.
## Duplicate search
- Snapshot search for both finding ids and for `cold catalogue`/`cold refresh`: no issue. PR #567 is the source only.

Current upstream rechecked: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` (`development`). The affected implementation files are unchanged from the validator's `98ccd167cca1db4309e2d7f4d961b7109b119502` snapshot.

Source locations: [src/provider/openrouter.ts:22](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/provider/openrouter.ts#L22), [src/provider/openrouter.ts:52-55](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/provider/openrouter.ts#L52), [src/provider/openrouter.ts:66-72](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/provider/openrouter.ts#L66).

Codex review evidence: https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/567#discussion_r4151411427, https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/567#discussion_r4151411430, https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/567#pullrequestreview-5374454722.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaWkw.title: Buffered OpenRouter Responses returns an empty success instead of failing closed
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaWkw.body:
A buffered Responses 200 with empty/null output, no refusal and no tool call is returned to the client as a clean success: the handler only suppresses the semantic-output marker and never applies the shared answer-bearing guard the buffered fail-closed contract requires.

## What is wrong

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaJYA.title: Ended upstream calls answer sideband joins 101 and then a generic close instead of 404/410
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaJYA.body:
When a mapped call has ended upstream, its 404/410 handshake response arrives after the gateway has already answered the client's join with 101, and the bridge turns it into the generic failure close 1011. The call mapping stays valid for an hour, so every later join repeats the same non-terminal failure even though the pinned client contract treats a 404/410 sideband join as a terminated call that stops reconnects.

## What is wrong
- `src/live/sideband.ts:240-257`: the mapping is read, the socket is upgraded, and only then does the bridge dial upstream.
- `src/live/sideband.ts:213-215` (and `:180-184` for dial failure): upstream rejection becomes `finish(1011, ...)`.
- `src/live/upstream.ts:26`: `LIVE_CALL_ACCOUNT_TTL_MS = 60 * 60_000` keeps the mapping.
- `docs/research/v1-live-client-contract-2026-09-30.md:220,324,384,432`: 404/410 on the sideband join is classified as a terminated call and stops reconnects.

## Acceptance
- A terminal upstream rejection is surfaced to the joining client without first accepting the upgrade, or the mapping is retired so later joins answer the terminal status; reconnects stop as the client contract expects.

Source confirmation at development 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded: [src/live/sideband.ts:180-184,213-215,240-257](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/live/sideband.ts#L180), [src/live/upstream.ts:26,122-129](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/live/upstream.ts#L26), [docs/research/v1-live-client-contract-2026-09-30.md:220,324,384,432](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/docs/research/v1-live-client-contract-2026-09-30.md#L220).

- After the ladder is exhausted, the wait path restarts the requested tier (lithos-handlers.ts:408-414) and a success there never clears the field: the field keeps naming the last ladder tier that refused.

## Acceptance
- Set rateLimitFailoverModel from the final serving model: clear it (or set the requested tier) when the requested tier answers, and set the sibling only when the sibling actually served.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXFjcWA.title: Require native generation-order proof when stored expiry is unreadable
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABXFjcWA.body:
Require positive generation-order evidence before asking a native owner to refresh a different expired generation when the stored access-token expiry cannot be decoded.

The actual local review of d647494b96840aba0b2288c7930860fe847de277 against f392eb27a71539a4c162f9c96b624039dcf46612 identified a P2 regression: `verifyNativeProgress` skips its ordering comparisons when `previousExpiry` is null, and the new `requireUsableAccessToken=false` path can therefore request refresh even when the native file has an older or missing `last_refresh`. This conflicts with the repository's stale-credential safeguard. The finding came from read-only source analysis; runtime reproduction is pending.

Acceptance:

- An unreadable stored expiry plus a missing or regressing native generation stamp must refuse before the owner RPC and leave the pool unchanged.
- The intended newer, expired native generation still gets exactly one owner refresh and is adopted only after becoming usable.
- Synthetic regressions cover both paths; no live OAuth or inference probes are used.

Files: `src/codex/native-auth.ts:234-235`, `tests/codex-native-auth.test.ts`.

Provenance: PR #1016; actual `codex review --commit d647494b96840aba0b2288c7930860fe847de277` with task-scoped gpt-6.1-sol/max, provider uos, read-only mode; review exit 0, confidence 0.94, overall verdict `patch is incorrect`. When this strong KV read rejects while the compact runtime catalog remains readable—the scenario covered by the new test—the catch changes every caller's result to `null`, not just the catalog builder's optional enrichment. I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL3jQ.title: Restore the visible chart anchor when the follow-latest intent is stale
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL3jQ.body:
The provider-capacity chart consults a follow-latest flag that is only refreshed by the `scroll` event, so a refresh that lands between the operator's scroll and the queued event discards the anchor it just recorded.

## What is wrong
- `static/admin.js:2569-2574` (`syncCapacityChartScroll`) is the only writer of `capacityChartFollowsLatest`; it runs from the `scroll` listener.
- `static/admin.js:2071-2092` (`rememberCapacityChartScroll`) records `atNewestEdge` and a valid `anchorAtMs` from the synchronously measured scroll position.
- `static/admin.js:2094-2107` (`restoreCapacityChartScroll`) keeps the newest edge whenever `capacityChartFollowsLatest` is true, even when a valid anchor exists; it is called after every render (`:2737`), including the 30 s capacity refresh at `:10017-10022`.

## Trigger
Scroll away from the newest edge and let the 30 s refresh complete before the queued `scroll` event runs: the anchor is measured but ignored and the chart snaps back to the newest edge, where the synchronous `state.atEnd` ordering previously preserved the position.

## Acceptance
- Follow-latest intent is reconciled with the visible chart before it is replaced (for example by deriving intent from the same measurement that produced the anchor).
- The hidden-render guard (`clientWidth <= 0`) is retained, and a focused check covers "scrolled away, refresh completes before the scroll event".

## Validation note
The trigger above is read from source order; the rendered behaviour needs a real browser render or a relayed check before it is treated as observed (see handback relay request).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnLzhg.title: Resolve the DeepSeek thinking/tool_choice conflict from the canonical thinking mode
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnLzhg.body:
`deepSeekThinkingModeActive` reads the raw `thinking` field before the resolved reasoning effort, so the boundary guard disagrees with the wire translation in both directions.

## What is wrong
- `src/deepseek/index.ts:79-87`: a `thinking` record with `type: "enabled"` returns `true` regardless of `reasoning_effort`.
- `src/deepseek/handlers.ts:264-268` resolves `reasoning` to the wire effort (an explicit `reasoning_effort: "none"` wins) and `:494-500` deletes `thinking` before dispatch.
- `src/deepseek/handlers.ts:479-483` calls `deepSeekThinkingToolChoiceConflict(reasoning, rawRecord.thinking, rawRecord.tool_choice)` and returns 400 `tool_choice` when the raw field says thinking is on.

## Trigger
- `thinking: {"type":"enabled"}` + `reasoning_effort: "none"` + `tool_choice: "required"`: the wire would be thinking-disabled, but the gateway returns 400 whose advice ("set reasoning_effort to none") the caller already followed.
- `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}` + `reasoning_effort: "max"` + `tool_choice: "required"`: the guard passes while the wire sends `reasoning_effort: "max"` without `thinking`, so the provider's own rejection is relayed instead of the gateway-shaped error.

## Acceptance
- The guard is evaluated on the canonical resolved thinking mode, consistent with `docs/DECISIONS.md:901-903`.
- Enabled thinking plus explicit reasoning_effort none must not be rejected by a thinking-specific tool_choice guard; disabled thinking plus canonical reasoning_effort max must receive the documented gateway-shaped conflict response. A focused regression covers both canonical modes.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmIYFw.title: The requested tier's x-should-retry: false is lost when a later ladder tier names the wait window, so the requested tier is retried
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmIYFw.body:
## Original finding
- Native Codex review of PR #511, finding 3: [P2] Retain each tier's no-retry instruction across wait rounds (original cite lithos-handlers.ts:555).
- PR #511 original head db7c09d401e31dee04cb8ac4705e01f84f290003, base 7a98f1c399a1b73d005efe15ccecefe14d6ab516. Provenance: thread 01a0fc31-476b-7ef1-8572-516f5a22ca76 / turn 01a0fc31-6e01-7be2-b89e-2dfa8cb3e637 / review result 01a0fc3f-6550-7403-9581-b1a5d2dff963.

## Current state (verified at current upstream default)
Current development @ 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded; both files byte-identical to frozen checkout HEAD 98ccd167 (blob equality checked).
- x-should-retry: false is evaluated only for the attempt whose headers are being planned: lithos-rate-limits.ts:275-276 returns null for that attempt, and nothing stores the prohibition per tier.
- After the ladder is exhausted, the wait is planned solely from the last attempt's headers (lithos-handlers.ts:405 lithosRefusalWait(attempt.headers, ...)), and the resumed state unconditionally addresses the requested tier again (lithos-handlers.ts:408-414 sets attemptModel: input.modelRaw).
- The existing no-retry test gives both tiers identical prohibitions, so the mixed-header case stays uncovered.

## Trigger
1. The requested tier (for example the Ultra tier) answers 429 with x-should-retry: false and opens no window; the dispatch hops to its sibling (lithos-handlers.ts:394-400).
2. Every later ladder tier also refuses, and one of them returns a retryable 429 with retry-after-ms: 1000.
3. lithosRefusalWait plans the pause from that later attempt's headers and the resumed state retries the requested tier, even though the vendor explicitly prohibited retrying it.

## Acceptance
- Retain retry eligibility per tier across wait rounds and retry only a tier that did not prohibit retries; a tier that returned x-should-retry: false must not be dispatched again after the window.
- Regression test with mixed headers (requested tier x-should-retry: false, sibling retryable) asserting the requested tier is not re-dispatched.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmIV7Q.title: waitForLithosRetry discards the deadline reason, answering HTTP 499 request_cancelled instead of 504 gateway_timeout
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmIV7Q.body:
## Original finding
- Native Codex review of PR #511, finding 2: [P2] Preserve timeout reasons when aborting the refusal wait (original cite lithos-rate-limits.ts:120-122).
- PR #511 original head db7c09d401e31dee04cb8ac4705e01f84f290003, base 7a98f1c399a1b73d005efe15ccecefe14d6ab516. Provenance: thread 01a0fc31-476b-7ef1-8572-516f5a22ca76 / turn 01a0fc31-6e01-7be2-b89e-2dfa8cb3e637 / review result 01a0fc3f-6550-7403-9581-b1a5d2dff963 (exitedReviewMode).

## Current state (verified at current upstream default)
Current development @ 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded; the four files byte-identical to frozen checkout HEAD 98ccd167 (blob equality checked).
- waitForLithosRetry rejects a freshly constructed AbortError in both abort paths (lithos-rate-limits.ts:156 and 164) instead of rejecting with signal.reason.
- The request-level deadline signal is AbortSignal.timeout (inference-deadline.ts:42-43, createInferenceSignal), whose abort reason is a DOMException named TimeoutError; that identity is discarded by the wait.
- The deferred catch path feeds the error to respondLithosChatDispatchFailure (lithos-handlers.ts:485-492), which classifies it through lithosTerminalTypeForError (lithos-handlers.ts:182-191): a live downstream signal plus AbortError gives terminal cancelled and records cancellation.
- toLithosErrorResponse maps TimeoutError to 504 gateway_timeout but AbortError to 499 request_cancelled (upstream-wire.ts:594-599), so the caller receives 499 even though it is still connected.

## Trigger
1. The gateway deadline expires while a request waits out the vendor's refusal window (waitForLithosRetry is parked).
2. The abort rejects the wait with AbortError rather than the signal's TimeoutError.
3. respondLithosChatDispatchFailure reports cancellation and the response is 499 request_cancelled instead of 504 gateway_timeout.

## Acceptance
- Preserve the signal's abort reason (or otherwise map a TimeoutError deadline to gateway_timeout) in both abort paths of waitForLithosRetry.
- Regression test: a timeout that fires during the wait yields HTTP 504 gateway_timeout, while a client cancellation still yields 499 request_cancelled.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE27A.title: Cerebras collapse silently drops non-text content from system and developer messages
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE27A.body:
`collapseCerebrasSystemMessages` merges repeated system/developer messages into the single leading `system` message the Cerebras chat template accepts, but it keeps only text parts and filters the rest away, so caller-supplied non-text content disappears from the dispatched request.
## What is wrong
- `cerebrasSystemPartText` returns `""` for any part that is not a string and has no `text` field (`src/provider/cerebras.ts:269-274`), and `collapseCerebrasSystemMessages` then drops empty strings (line 305).
- A Responses request may carry a `developer` item with an `input_image` part (`src/input-normalization.ts:677` accepts `input_image`), and the shared projection turns a developer item into a `system` message whose content is an array that can contain image parts (`src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:67-88` builds the image parts, `:238-247` maps `developer` to `system`).
- The Cerebras Responses route applies that projection and then the collapse (`src/provider/cerebras-responses.ts:314-320`), so the image part is erased while `instructions` text remains: the model answers with no signal that content was lost, and nothing in the request is rejected.
## Current evidence
- `src/provider/cerebras.ts:266-281`, `:301-307` (filter `text !== ""`).
- `src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:67-88`, `:238-247`.
- `src/provider/cerebras-responses.ts:314-320`.
- `src/input-normalization.ts:677` (developer/`input_image` accepted).
- Codex review: discussion_r4121010720 on PR #544 head 5df4f1c14ae6; file unchanged since (last commit touching `src/provider/cerebras.ts` is 5df4f1c14a).
## Reproduction
- Static only: trace a `/v1/responses` request with `instructions` plus a `developer` item containing `input_image` through `toDeepSeekResponsesChatBody` and `collapseCerebrasSystemMessages`, and read the resulting single system message.
## Acceptance criteria
- Unsupported system/developer content is preserved in a valid merged representation or rejected explicitly with a 4xx; it is never silently deleted.
- A focused test asserts no silent content loss for a non-text part on this route.

I_kwDOORydAM8AAAABIaU_Sw.title: rpc.satelink.network in your whitelist: rate-limit semantics (402 with machine-readable payment body, not 429)
I_kwDOORydAM8AAAABIaU_Sw.body:
Hi — we operate `rpc.satelink.network`, which is in your `rpc-whitelist.json` for Polygon. Since your manager routes real traffic through us, two behaviors worth knowing so your selection logic handles us correctly:

1. **Anonymous free tier is 500 calls/day per IP (shared per /24).** Under the cap, calls serve normally (p50 ~44ms from our health data). Past it we return **HTTP 402** — not 429 — with a machine-readable body: an x402 v2 `accepts` block plus plain-JSON `how_to_pay`/`upgrade` fields (deposit address, per-call price, an estimate computed from the caller's own usage). If your manager treats non-200s as node failure, we'll look "down" for the rest of the UTC day once a busy IP caps out; treating our 402 as "rate-limited, rotate" (or reading `error.data.resets_at`) is more accurate.

2. **An authenticated tier exists if your users need more than the cap**: wallet-signature registration (`POST /v1/machine/register` — no email, no dashboard), $0.00003/call prepaid from a $0.50 minimum USDT deposit, or a one-shot x402 payment of $0.10 USDC on Base for a 1,000-call bundle, no account at all. Machine-readable details: https://rpc.satelink.network/.well-known/satelink.json

Happy to answer anything about the endpoint — and if a higher anonymous cap for your tool's users would help, we're open to it.

I_kwDOORydAM6973qC.title: Multicall3 batch contract reads
I_kwDOORydAM6973qC.body:
Multicall3 contract allows us to make batch contract reads with one RPC call.
Instead of using Multicall3 contract on the project level, we can implement it in the rpc-manager server so it's completely invisible to the end user who is using the RPC.

Benefits:
- More efficient - less network requests
- Faster - not by a lot but theoretically it should be because there is less overhead
- Less likely to hit rate limits - this is the biggest benefit of this because a lot of public RPCs have rate limits

The proposed flow:

1. The client sends an array of RPC calls to the server
2. The server transforms those RPC calls into one RPC call to the Multicall3 contract and sends it to the upstream RPC provider
3. The server receives the response and transform all results to the original format
4. The server sends the response back to the client which can process the results normally - no modification needed on the client part

This only applies to contract reads so only if the RPC method is `eth_call` and contract writes (`eth_sendTransaction` method) is not recommended for Multicall3 because it has some caveats

I_kwDOM5SPVc8AAAABVh8Nug.title: fix(config): allow contributors to start Priority 1 and 2 tasks under usdPriceMax threshold
I_kwDOM5SPVc8AAAABVh8Nug.body:
### Summary
In `.github/.ubiquity-os.config.yml`, `requiredLabelsToStart` currently maps all priority labels (Priority 0 through 5) to `allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly`. This creates an unintended contributor lockout where external developers are prevented from running `/start` or opening pull requests for priority-labeled tasks across the organization, despite `taskAccessControl.usdPriceMax.contributor: 1000` being explicitly enabled.

### Root Cause Analysis

1. **Configuration Anchor Discrepancy**:
   - In `.ubiquity-os.config.yml` (lines 48–51), `allRoles` is defined:
     ```yaml
     allRoles: &allRoles
       - collaborator
       - contributor
     ```
   - In `taskAccessControl`:
     ```yaml
       usdPriceMax:
         contributor: 1000
         collaborator: Infinity
     ```
     `contributor: 1000` indicates that external contributors are intended to participate in tasks up to $1,000 USD (unlike repos set to `-1` for preservation mode).
   - However, in `ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop@main` configuration (lines 94–106):
     ```yaml
     requiredLabelsToStart:
       - name: "Priority: 0 (Regression)"
         allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
       - name: "Priority: 1 (Normal)"
         allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
       - name: "Priority: 2 (Medium)"
         allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
       - name: "Priority: 3 (High)"
         allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
       - name: "Priority: 4 (Urgent)"
         allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
       - name: "Priority: 5 (Emergency)"
         allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
     ```
   - By comparison, `devpool-directory/.ubiquity-os/.github/.ubiquity-os.config.yml` maps Priority 0, 1, and 2 to `*allRoles`.

2. **Downstream Enforcement in `command-start-stop`**:
   - In `check-requirements.ts`, `checkRequirements()` checks `currentLabelConfiguration.allowedRoles.includes(userRole)`. Because external contributors resolve to `role: "contributor"`, any task bearing a Priority label rejects the `/start` command with:
     > `You must be a core team member, or an administrator to start this task`
     (Observed on over 105 issues across `ai.ubq.fi`, `stake.ubq.fi`, `pay.ubq.fi`, etc.)
   - In `new-pull-request-or-edit.ts`, when a contributor opens a PR linking an unassigned issue, the bot attempts an auto-start via `startTask()`. Because `checkRequirements()` fails, `startTask` returns an error status, executing `closeTriggeredPullRequest()` and auto-closing the contributor PR within seconds.

### Proposed Fix
Update `Priority: 1 (Normal)` and `Priority: 2 (Medium)` in `requiredLabelsToStart` to use `*allRoles`:

```diff
       requiredLabelsToStart:
         - name: "Priority: 0 (Regression)"
           allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
         - name: "Priority: 1 (Normal)"
-          allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
+          allowedRoles: *allRoles
         - name: "Priority: 2 (Medium)"
-          allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
+          allowedRoles: *allRoles
         - name: "Priority: 3 (High)"
           allowedRoles: *collaboratorOnly
```

External contributor tasks remain bounded by `taskAccessControl.usdPriceMax.contributor: 1000` and `maxConcurrentTasks.contributor: 2`.

---
*Context: Discovered while delivering the fix for `ai.ubq.fi#579` ($150 USD, verified and passing 12/12 CI checks in PR #831). Normalizing this unblocks external contributors across the DevPool pipeline.*

I_kwDOK6Xdq86uevBy.title: Enhance Kernel with Generalized Request Handling & Secure External API
I_kwDOK6Xdq86uevBy.body:
#### **Summary**  
Expand the kernel's ingress beyond GitHub webhooks by introducing a secure public API endpoint. This will allow external services to trigger GitHub Actions workflows, effectively turning Actions into a general-purpose backend.  

#### **Key Features**  
- **Public API Endpoint**:  
  - Accepts external requests to execute plugins via the kernel.  
  - Supports dynamic execution of actions, enabling broader integrations.  

- **Authentication & Security**:  
  - Requests must include:  
    - `installation ID` (this allows us to target the correct org)  
    - `repository ID` (optionally, to load a specific repo config)  
  - Partners must provide an **encrypted password** stored in their config.  
    - Uses **X25519 encryption** (same system as EVM private key storage).  
    - Clients pass a password in the request header, which the kernel decrypts.  
  - Rate-limiting to prevent abuse.  

- **Execution Flow**:  
  1. Kernel receives an authenticated request with at least `installation ID` and `password`.  
  2. It decrypts the password and verifies the request.  
  3. Executes the specified plugin and returns the response.  

- **Webhook Replies**:  
  - Requests can include a `response URL` header.  
  - The kernel posts the result from the action plugin to this URL upon completion.  

- **Future Enhancements**:  
  - Investigate **cross-plugin communication** via the kernel relay.  

#### **Next Steps**  
- Define API Contract (Headers, Payload Format)
- Implement Authentication & Decryption Logic
- Extend Kernel Request Handling to Invoke Plugins
- Add Support for Webhook Response Delivery

I_kwDOK6Xdq86tiane.title: Callbacks - event handlers and hybrid plugins
I_kwDOK6Xdq86tiane.body:
I want to improve the experience of setting up event handlers and hybrid plugins.
I imagine something like this

```js
.on("issue_comment.created", "action", handler1)
.on("issue.closed", "worker", handler2)
```

The SDK would handle calling the Action or run it normally as a Worker and in case you're running it locally it would execute Action handlers locally too. 
Sometimes the reason why we need to call it as an Action is because some libraries are not supported by CF Workers so it'd be also good to have an option to run it as an Action even if you're running it locally.
Current hybrid plugins use `ACTION_REF` to know which Action to call but it'd be great if we could somehow get it automatically but I realize that may be not feasible.

At this point I would also consider merging `createActionsPlugin` and `createPlugin` for seamless experience.

I also realized that maybe we don't need kernel credentials to trigger Action from the Worker but only a fine-grained Github token that would only have access to the repo. Because we don't change the payload but only forward it to the Action, we don't need to generate a new signature and we can keep the original.
