I_kwDOK6Xdq87x93vR.title: Fix /help flow: do not emit agent-rejected message for bot user
I_kwDOK6Xdq87x93vR.body:
## Summary
When running `/help`, kernel posts the help response but also emits:

`agent rejected: Only human users can invoke the agent (got user.type=Bot)`

This appears to be one symptom of a broader routing problem: bot-authored comments are being treated as valid triggers for bot and agent workflows. As a result, bots can end up conversing with themselves or each other, then emitting rejection noise because only humans may invoke the agent.

A concrete example of the broader failure is the bot-to-bot thread on:
https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/340

## Current behavior
- `/help` succeeds (help content is posted).
- Kernel also posts an unrelated agent rejection message for bot user type.
- Bot-authored comments and mentions can trigger downstream bot or agent handling.
- This creates self-replies or bot-to-bot reply chains and repeated `Only human users can invoke the agent` noise.

## Expected behavior
- `/help` should complete without agent-gating rejection noise.
- Agent human-user restriction should only apply to true agent invocation paths, not help command handling.
- Bot-authored comments must not trigger other bots.
- Mentions or commands emitted by bots must be ignored as invocation sources for downstream bot and agent workflows.

## Acceptance criteria
- Triggering `/help` produces only help output.
- No `Only human users can invoke the agent` message appears for `/help`.
- Comments authored by `user.type=Bot` are ignored by agent-invocation routing.
- Bot-authored comments do not trigger other bots or downstream agent workflows.
- No bot-to-bot reply chains occur from bot-emitted mentions or commands.
- Agent restriction behavior remains intact for true human-triggered agent invocation paths.

Relates to ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel#320

I_kwDOK6Xdq87pXo0Q.title: RFC: Move plugin build artifacts to dist/<source-ref> branches
I_kwDOK6Xdq87pXo0Q.body:
## Summary

We should stop committing generated plugin artifacts (`dist/**`) and generated `manifest.json` into source branches, and instead publish them into paired artifact branches.

Example:
- Source branch: `feat/my-feat`
- Artifact branch: `dist/feat/my-feat`

This change reduces development friction, removes build noise from PRs, and gives a clean separation between source code and generated outputs.

Additional scope (from linked follow-up): manifest generation should derive `manifest` commands and `ubiquity:listeners` from code, add a canonical `skipBotEvents` source, and keep existing `homepage_url`/`short_name` automation unchanged.

## Decisions (locked)

- `PluginInput.ref` must keep the exact same behavior/semantics as today.
- Artifact layout in artifact branches remains `dist/**`.
- Artifact branches preserve history (no reset/snapshot force-replacement model).
- `manifest.json` is generated on the artifact branch at branch root.
- Generated `manifest.json` should no longer be committed to the source branch.
- Manifest-related behavior changes must preserve current automation for:
  - `homepage_url`
  - `short_name`

## Current pain points

- Feature branches are polluted by generated files and CI commits.
- PR review signal is degraded by `dist/**` and manifest churn.
- Rebases/merges are noisier and more conflict-prone.
- Build/deploy metadata is mixed with source changes.
- Source-branch lifecycle and artifact lifecycle are not explicitly paired.

## Proposed model

### Branch mapping

- For source ref `R`, artifact ref is `dist/R`.
- If plugin config omits a ref, resolve default source branch `B`, then artifact ref is `dist/B`.
- If already on a `dist/*` ref, do not transform again.
- Keep source ref and artifact ref distinct in internal logic where needed, while keeping `PluginInput.ref` behavior unchanged.

### Artifact branch contents

- `manifest.json` at branch root.
- Built artifacts under `dist/**` (unchanged layout).
- Optional build metadata file is allowed (source SHA, source ref, workflow run URL), but not required for phase 1.

### Manifest generation scope (cross-repo behavior)

- Generate manifest `commands` from code, not manually maintained source branch values.
- Generate `ubiquity:listeners` from code.
- Introduce/use canonical `skipBotEvents` source definition in manifest generation logic.
- Preserve existing homepage metadata automation for `homepage_url` and `short_name`.

### Lifecycle rules

- Push/update source branch `R` updates artifact branch `dist/R`.
- Delete source branch `R` deletes artifact branch `dist/R`.
- Deletion should be idempotent (no failure if `dist/R` does not exist).
- Protect against recursion (publishing on `dist/*` should not trigger another publish to `dist/dist/*`).

## Cross-repo scope

### 1) `ubiquity-os/action-deploy-plugin`

- Build from source branch checkout as today.
- Publish generated outputs to `dist/<source-ref>` branch.
- Preserve artifact branch history when updating.
- Stop committing generated artifacts and generated manifest to source branch.
- Generate/write `manifest.json` at root of artifact branch.
- Keep runtime outputs in `dist/**`.
- Ensure manifest generation uses canonical `skipBotEvents` and derives `commands` / `ubiquity:listeners` from code.

### 2) `ubiquity-os-kernel`

- For GitHub plugins, resolve manifest/dispatch from artifact ref (`dist/<resolved-source-ref>`).
- Keep `PluginInput.ref` behavior exactly unchanged.
- Add explicit internal separation for source ref vs artifact ref where needed.
- Add backward-compatible fallback during migration (if artifact manifest missing, try legacy source ref).

### 3) `plugin-sdk`

- Mirror kernel manifest-resolution logic for GitHub plugins.
- Resolve manifests from artifact refs with migration fallback.
- Keep plugin key UX unchanged (`owner/repo@feat/x` remains valid input).

### 4) `ubiquity-os/deno-deploy`

- Stop committing manifest updates to source branch.
- Read/write manifest in artifact branch flow.
- Ensure deploy/delete behavior aligns with source branch lifecycle and paired artifact branch lifecycle.
- Ensure branch-name handling is deterministic with source-to-artifact mapping.

### 5) `ubiquity-os/deno-plugin-adapter`

- Validate compatibility with artifact-branch layout and deploy workflows.
- Update docs/examples to reflect artifact-branch model.
- Keep adapter output assumptions compatible with `dist/**` layout.

## Global impact

This affects shared actions and many downstream plugin repos using:

- `ubiquity-os/action-deploy-plugin`
- `ubiquity-os/deno-deploy`
- `ubiquity-os/deno-plugin-adapter`
- workflows that currently run `node dist/index.js` / `node dist/main.js`
- workflows that mutate/commit `manifest.json` on source branches

## Migration plan

1. Implement artifact-ref resolution + fallback in kernel and plugin-sdk.
2. Implement artifact-branch publishing in `action-deploy-plugin`.
3. Update `deno-deploy` manifest target + delete behavior.
4. Migrate downstream plugin workflows to new branch model.
5. Remove fallback after migration window.

## Risks and mitigations

- Risk: dispatch failures if artifact branch is missing.
- Mitigation: temporary fallback to source ref; clear error messaging and logging.

- Risk: recursive workflow triggers on artifact branches.
- Mitigation: branch filters and explicit guards for `dist/*`.

- Risk: branch cleanup drift.
- Mitigation: explicit delete workflow path and idempotent branch-delete logic.

## Testing plan

- Unit tests for source->artifact ref mapping and fallback.
- Unit tests for manifest fetch from artifact refs.
- Unit tests for branch create/update/delete flows in action repos.
- Integration test: push `feat/x` -> verify `dist/feat/x` has root `manifest.json` + `dist/**`.
- Integration test: delete `feat/x` -> verify `dist/feat/x` deleted.
- Integration test: command dispatch still works with unchanged `PluginInput.ref` behavior.
- Integration test: manifest output derives `commands` and `ubiquity:listeners` from code and `skipBotEvents` source is canonical.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Source branches no longer receive generated `dist/**` or generated `manifest.json` commits.
- [x] For source ref `R`, artifact branch `dist/R` is created/updated.
- [x] Artifact branches preserve commit history across updates.
- [x] Artifact branch contains root `manifest.json` and runtime files under `dist/**`.
- [ ] Kernel/plugin-sdk successfully resolve plugin manifests/dispatch from artifact refs.
- [ ] `PluginInput.ref` behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] Source branch deletion deletes paired artifact branch.
- [ ] No recursive `dist/dist/*` branch generation.
- [ ] Manifest generation derives `commands` and `ubiquity:listeners` from code.
- [ ] Canonical `skipBotEvents` source is used in manifest generation.
- [ ] Existing `homepage_url` / `short_name` automation remains unchanged.
- [ ] Migration fallback exists and is removed in a planned follow-up.

I_kwDOK6Xdq87O2axP.title: Integrate personal agent bridge into the kernel
I_kwDOK6Xdq87O2axP.body:
Currently the [bridge](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/personal-agent-bridge) only extracts the username and forwards the event using the kernel Github app credentials. The core functionality is only 90 lines of code.

The problem we already experienced is that the kernel changed the way the payload is sent (compression) - this made the bridge outdated but if it was in the kernel this wouldn't be a problem. Another inconvenience is that there's another HTTP request from the kernel to the bridge which additionally delays the execution.

It only makes sense that the bridge is a part of the kernel because it already uses kernel credentials, the code is minimal and reduces overhead and maintenance of the plugin.

I_kwDOK6Xdq87GCNgf.title: Adopt pino for structured logging
I_kwDOK6Xdq87GCNgf.body:
The console is cluttered with information that saturates Deno logs, and locally makes it impossible to debug. We should adopt a logger that is production ready and let us filter logs properly. A few options are there like Pino, Wisnton or log4js-node. Let's try with Pino but if it gives too much trouble with Deno we can consider the others. This will greatly improve locall debugging as well as Deno logs that are unreadable at the moment.

Use pino for core logging (fast JSON, child loggers, redaction, Bun-friendly). Ranking considered: 1) pino 2) log4js-node 3) winston.

Alternatives (brief):
- winston: large ecosystem, flexible transports; heavier & slower, more config surface.
- log4js-node: simple categories & appenders; weaker native structured JSON & redaction.

Scope / Tasks:
- [ ] Add deps: pino, pino-pretty (dev only)
- [ ] Create src/logger/logger.ts exporting base logger (level via LOG_LEVEL, pretty in non-production)
- [ ] Implement redaction for tokens / secrets (/_?token|private_key|authorization/i)
- [ ] Provide helper to create child logger per event: repo, issue/PR number, installation id, stateId
- [ ] Replace console.* in handlers (start with issue-comment-created, push-event, repository-dispatch)
- [ ] Update README: logging usage + environment variable (LOG_LEVEL)
- [ ] Add minimal test ensuring child logger preserves base bindings & level

Acceptance:
- All previous console outputs replaced or intentionally retained (none left in src except pre-init warnings)
- JSON logs in production; pretty output locally
- Redaction verified (no raw tokens in test log sample)

I_kwDOK6Xdq86YbhW8.body: - We hit 90% daily quota today. Given that we don't even have any partners using the system yet, this is looking grim. - I hope that we can find a way to optimize our KV usage (or we can figure some cheaper alternative, but I am skeptical.) - - ### Projected Costs - The good news is that our limits go from 1000 -> 33,333, so we get essentially 33x capacity for $5/month. - I estimate that once we get most of the planned plugins up and running, we'll be closer to 5k a day. - `6,666.6666666667` per $1 of cost - I think each large partner will cost us approximately $1 a month on KV - Smaller ones will probably be closer to the 1k we are using now. ### Next Steps Let's discuss how we can optimize the KV usage of the kernel.

I_kwDOK6Xdq86jvDdB.title: Add support for calling worker plugins from URL set in the manifest
I_kwDOK6Xdq86jvDdB.body:
Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/issues/33

[This](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/issues/33) task introduces a new property `homepage_url` (which is a plugin worker URL) in the [manifest.json](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/blob/8d8f06958ca1273f299ae0bc2a51a6c512411af9/manifest.json) file.  

The idea is that now the bot's config will contain only `org/repo` in the plugin's config. For example [here](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/.ubiquity-os/blob/67df7f5643edcaa3899304481f7ff4ef74a1041a/.github/.ubiquity-os.config.dev.yml#L3) instead of
```
- plugin: https://ubiquity-os-comment-vector-embeddings-development.ubiquity.workers.dev
```
we will set `org/repo` value:
```
- plugin: ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings
```

The kernel should support calling a worker URL if it is set in the [manifest.json](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/blob/8d8f06958ca1273f299ae0bc2a51a6c512411af9/manifest.json).

How it is supposed to work:
1. If `plugin` config property contains URL then call it as a worker (this is to support close sourced plugins + for backwards compatibility)
2. If `plugin` config property contains `org/repo` value then fetch plugin's [manifest.json](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/blob/8d8f06958ca1273f299ae0bc2a51a6c512411af9/manifest.json):
  - If `homepage_url` property is present in the manifest then call the plugin as a worker
  - If `homepage_url` property is missing then call plugin as a github action

Original [comment](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/issues/33#issuecomment-2549092026)

I_kwDOK6Xdq86L87fF.title: Merge configurations by unique IDs
I_kwDOK6Xdq86L87fF.body:
We should look into a more robust configuration merge.

Quote from discussion:

I know there isn't a concept of merging configurations together on GitHub Actions. 

This doesn't address the key point I am making. The cause we are discussing is a collision with dependency IDs. And whether there are real-world scenarios where configurations might lead to duplicate dependencies. 

From my experience creating GitHub Actions CI scripts, I haven't encountered situations where adding redundant dependencies was necessary. This makes the theoretical merging logic problem irrelevant to our practical implementation. 

We should focus on the actual conditions under which our configurations operate, rather than hypothetical scenarios that don't align with real-world use cases.

Basically I'm saying to drop support for using the same dependency more than one, particularly when associated with the same webhook event. See [this comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-kernel/pull/47#issuecomment-2154146051) for a suggestion on how to handle that.

_Originally posted by @0x4007 in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-kernel/issues/47#issuecomment-2162159354_

I_kwDOK6Xdq864RXhB.body: https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/issues/206#issuecomment-2910100809 We exceeded Azure quotas and should create a new subscription using only free tiers. The only downside is that the hybrid mode is deemed to be buggy sometimes, and that the limit of the free tier in Deno is still very low. If that proves to be successful, the only change required in the SDK would be to add a `Deno` class handling the logs and creating the proper URL in the metadata. We should also create a deployment Action that would streamline this. Afterwards, we should be able to migrate any of our projects to Deno.

I_kwDOK6Xdq86qC9fR.title: Allow commands and `issue_comment.created` to coexist
I_kwDOK6Xdq86qC9fR.body:
If the manifest describes a command for a plugin, and the plugin also listens for `issue_comment.created`, the `issue_comment.created` does not get called if it doesn't match the command. This can be problematic if a plugin needs to both listen to the command and take other actions on `issue_comment.created`.

The current workaround is to not specify the command, and just handle handle `issue_command.created`. The downside is that the command will not show when invoking the `/help` command. This is the case for `/demo` for example.

I_kwDOK6Xdq86mRcoU.title: Investigate `skipBotEvents` always true even when defined `false` in the configuration
I_kwDOK6Xdq86mRcoU.body:
## What happened

Even when set to `false` the `skipBotEvents` key within the configuration seems to be evaluated to `true` when decoded. Example:
```yaml
  - skipBotEvents: false
    testUbqKey: 1234
    uses:
      - plugin: ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-disqualifier@main
        skipBotEvents: false
        with:
          warning: 7 days
          pullRequestRequired: true
          eventWhitelist:
            - pull_request.review_requested
            - pull_request.ready_for_review
            - pull_request_review_comment.created
            - issue_comment.created
            - push
          watch:
            optOut:
              - ubiquibot
              - launch-party
              - staging
              - production
          disqualification: 14 days
```

Once decoded by the kernel gives

```json
  {
    "skipBotEvents": false,
    "testUbqKey": 1234,
    "uses": [
      {
        "plugin": {
          "owner": "ubiquity-os-marketplace",
          "repo": "daemon-disqualifier",
          "workflowId": "compute.yml",
          "ref": "main"
        },
        "skipBotEvents": true,
        "with": {
          "warning": "7 days",
          "pullRequestRequired": true,
          "eventWhitelist": [
            "pull_request.review_requested",
            "pull_request.ready_for_review",
            "pull_request_review_comment.created",
            "issue_comment.created",
            "push"
          ],
          "watch": {
            "optOut": [
              "ubiquibot",
              "launch-party",
              "staging",
              "production"
            ]
          },
          "disqualification": "14 days"
        },
        "runsOn": [
          "issues.assigned"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
```

which is incorrect.

## What was expected

The key should be `true` or `false`, same value as specified in the configuration.

## How to reproduce

- use the configuration mentioned above
- log the parsed configuration from the kernel
- observe the wrong values for `skipBotEvents`

I_kwDOK6Xdq86RBuui.title: Configuration validation and annotations on errors
I_kwDOK6Xdq86RBuui.body:
In the bot v1, when the configuration is changed, annotations are added to the configuration file if any error is encountered within the configuration. It would be really nice to have for v2 as it is a common scenario to have an invalid configuration and have no feedback about it because the error would only be visible within the worker logs.

The main challenge is that only plugins are aware of their configuration shape, so probably the kernel should call every plugin to check their validity, which would require an endpoint or some access to the configuration validators. At the same time, the `manifest.json` validity could be checked, relating to https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-kernel/issues/78.

Since this might imply quite a few network requests, we can also consider having this functionality as a separate Worker using [service binding](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/service-bindings/).

I_kwDOK6Xdq86gjjjR.title: Do not log "manifest not found" as errors
I_kwDOK6Xdq86gjjjR.body: When the kernel tries to fetch a manifest and fails, it logs an error to the console. The problem is that it clutters the logs within the Cloudflare Log Dashboard, because these errors are "expected". We should keep logging an error if the query to the manifest fails for something else than a 404, and simply log a normal log when not found saying "manifest not found for repo xxx". See the CloudFlare logs: Removing these expected errors would help focusing on the real runtime errors needing attention.

I_kwDOK6Xdq86hpKPK.title: Use `hono`
I_kwDOK6Xdq86hpKPK.body:
Right now the kernel is deployed on a cloudflare worker which starts [throwing errors](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel/issues/195) under heavy load.

It makes sense to refactor the kernel to use https://hono.dev/ in order to be able to deploy the kernel to different platforms like [vercel](https://hono.dev/docs/getting-started/vercel) or [azure](https://hono.dev/docs/getting-started/azure-functions).

I_kwDOK6Xdq86b9Kv_.title: Interactive setup
I_kwDOK6Xdq86b9Kv_.body:
The goal of this task is to simplify developer experience when setting up the kernel.
To do this we need to create an interactive CLI tool that will help with setting up the Github App and preparing Cloudflare for deployment of the kernel

This setup tool should be inspired by [Probot's setup flow](https://probot.github.io/docs/development/#generating-a-new-app)

### 1. Setup Cloudflare and Wrangler
- Make the user login with Wrangler
- Create a KV namespace and put the ID in wrangler.toml (we already have a [script](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel/blob/development/deploy/setup-kv-namespace.ts) that can be used and/or modified)

### 2. GitHub App Setup Automation
This can be done with [Github App Manifest](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/sharing-github-apps/registering-a-github-app-from-a-manifest)
- Automate creation of a GitHub App
- Subscribe to all required GitHub events
- Set necessary permissions for the App
- Convert the private key to PKCS#8
- Populate App ID, private key and webhook secret into `.dev.vars` file and in Cloudflare Worker secrets.

Additionally we can make an option in the SDK to disable signature verification in order to ease the development of new plugins.

I_kwDOK6Xdq86ba43c.title: LLM Command Router
I_kwDOK6Xdq86ba43c.body:
I would like to abstract all of the configured capabilities behind tagging @UbiquityOS. For example, we converted `/ask` to @UbiquityOS so you can more naturally ask a context aware question to your "AI team member." 

I think its useful to retain the `/` syntax, defined within the plugins, for shorthand. However we should have a small and cheap model (like 4o-mini?) that can read the repo's configured help menu, read their descriptions, and then invoke them on behalf of the user query. I think we can optimize costs further without the use of an LLM on a later date, as I don't see costs being a problem for awhile. 


| Command | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `/help` | List all available commands. | `/help` |
| `/allow` | Allows the user to modify the given label. | `/allow @user1 label` |
| `/query` | Returns the user's wallet, access, and multiplier information. | `/query @ubiquibot` |
| `/start` | Assign yourself to the issue. | `/start` |
| `/stop` | Unassign yourself from the issue. | `/stop` |
| `/wallet` | Register your wallet address for payments. | `/wallet ubq.eth` |

Examples:

@ubiquityos can i be assigned to the issue?
@ubiquityos please set my wallet address to 0x0000...
@ubiquityos let @0x4007 set priority labels.[^1^] 

This could be really nice as we grow the commands set further over time. 

[^1^]: We might need a more detailed description for this to work, or consider another approach like codebase search.

I_kwDOK6Xdq86CIIPo.title: Migration system for Supabase database
I_kwDOK6Xdq86CIIPo.body:
We should have a migration system set for our new Supabase instance. To this day, everything is done through the Supabase Dashboard and there is no track of the changes. This become even more critical as we are starting to setup RLS and CLS, which won't be reflected by a db diff dump, as stated in their docs.

This means if we need to create a new db, move it, rollback, run it locally, we would be unable to do so and should do everything manually to mimic the current db's state.

Supabase has a migration system implemented, and a CLI, so we should use these to keep our db updated with the latest schema. Maybe it is better to create a separate repository, as this doesn't really belong to this project specifically. Relates to https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot/issues/919

I_kwDOK6Xdq86VmWT3.title: Encrypted values can be stolen and reused
I_kwDOK6Xdq86VmWT3.body:
I know I've highlighted this issue in the past, but I'm not sure where. 

As I'm going around these conferences and trying to fundraisers/find partners we realize that to quickly set up partners, we basically just send them the ubiquibot config file. 

So the encrypted private key was leaked unintentionally. 

As part of the decryption process, we should also include the organization ID or repo ID as part of the salt. 

That way, if I copy my ubiquibot config in my organization and I leak it, and somebody else tries to use my same exact EVM private key encrypted the bot, it will fail to decrypt correctly because their repository ID is different for example.

I_kwDOOG47587ZF5zn.title: Include PR context
I_kwDOOG47587ZF5zn.body:
> Could you can try running `/rewrite` on https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/issues/154 please?

> It meets all the criteria for it, and would be great to see it in action. (My concern is that it does not factor in the PR or any code at all, which is a huge amount of missing context as it's unreasonable to expect all technical details to be mentioned in the conversation but their acceptance by reviewers is specification discovery in and of itself)


As a contributor who over the years has often taken on ambiguous specs and saw them through to completion, it has been my experience that, oftentimes a lot of ambiguous specs shift product-design and engineering effort onto contributors and it often goes unrecognized the amount of work that gets put in.

For this plugin to work as best as it can it must also have context of the active PR because, in my experience, a lot of what I implement gets accepted without it being mentioned in the spec/issue convo. It only appears in conversation through review if it needs tweaked or rejected so this means:

- anything off-spec which is undiscussed (an inherent acceptance of that deliverable) is unknown to the llm
- it does not surface reviews or PR comments

Finally, it's unreasonable to expect (I think) contributors who have done the extra product-design and engineering work to list all tech specs of their implementation into the issue, before then calling `/rewrite`. Better UX if the plugin/agent handles this themselves.

One recent example (although there are tens more I could think of):

- https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/issues/154 - barren, very little activity, no discussion around my suggestions which have all been accepted at this point
- https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/185 - context rich, laden with activity, huge amount of undiscussed technical details that have been accepted, plenty of changes requested by reviewers

^ All the llm gets to see is an empty conversation spanning back to March, then my impl details being ignored (so it likely won't (or shouldn't) accept them as new spec details), while the PR continues to move.


 _Originally posted by @Keyrxng in [#448](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/448#issuecomment-3552015169)_

I_kwDOMQ8E8c7zlvJq.title: fix: make cron resolve plugin manifests from dist mirror branches
I_kwDOMQ8E8c7zlvJq.body:
Cron currently resolves plugin manifests from source refs like `development`, but deployment now publishes action artifacts to mirror branches under `dist/<ref>`.

Reference failing job:
https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-merging/actions/runs/23183045224/job/67359962939

Observed failure pattern:
- cron requests `contents/manifest.json?ref=development`
- repositories that only publish manifests to `dist/development` return 404

Desired behavior:
- cron should prefer `dist/<ref>` when resolving plugin manifests and related content fetches
- if `dist/<ref>` is missing, cron should fall back to the original source ref for compatibility

Non-goal:
- do not switch cron workflow checkout to `dist/<ref>`; cron should continue running from source branch code checkout

I_kwDOMQ8E8c7kOefb.title: Stop adding hidden comment to update issues
I_kwDOMQ8E8c7kOefb.body:
Currently, to trigger an update within a given repository, the plugin adds an hidden comment to the issue, which in turn triggers the comment edited workflow within the repo. It works fine, bur on the long term the issue contains lots of garbage hidden content, since each update add content to that issue.

Instead, we should directly spawn an octokit instance which has the proper authentication and directly acts on the repository, to avoid creating content spam like we do now.

We could leverage KV to avoid using the json db storage and these issues.

I_kwDOMQ8E8c67s2K3.title: Make the merging run once a day
I_kwDOMQ8E8c67s2K3.body:
Currently the merging runs on `issues.assigned` event, which is not reliable since sometimes it can happen multiple times a day or sometimes never.

We should implement something similar to https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-disqualifier/issues/68 so that it runs once a day.

I_kwDOMQ8E8c6m2bGJ.title: Fix plugin runs
I_kwDOMQ8E8c6m2bGJ.body:
https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-merging/actions/runs/12859777499/job/35850693896

Currently, this plugin is not running because the configuration is wrong, and should be fixed.

I_kwDOMQ8E8c6Y9wDt.title: Contributor Approvals Should Not Be Considered
I_kwDOMQ8E8c6Y9wDt.body:
This doesn't make any sense to consider outsider approvals to automatically merge into our code, let alone default to 2. This logic should be removed. 

In theory it could be possible to run an org with a single member using this system but seems very unusual. I would remove this logic related to considering contributor approvals.  

https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-merging/blob/b9e0cf38c4bc11749f172b6212a35f95d26ab7ad/src/types/plugin-inputs.ts#L25

I_kwDOMQ8E8c6VnxKI.title: Exclude `contributor` approvals
I_kwDOMQ8E8c6VnxKI.body:
Related to https://github.com/ubiquibot/command-start-stop/issues/36

Any `contributor` role based approvals are invalid and should be excluded from any consideration in auto-merging. The only valid roles would be:

- `collaborator`
- `member`

_original [context](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/pull/290#issuecomment-2333291028)_

I_kwDOMQ8E8c6RECzQ.title: Change database pull-request tracking by organization configuration
I_kwDOMQ8E8c6RECzQ.body:
The watcher should use GitHub API to go through all opened pull-requests instead of relying on a database. The main advantage is that we could get rid of the database which sole purpose is to keep track of the pull-requests to watch.

              It keeps track of the pull request to check updates for. Eventually, we could replace that with a list of organizations inside the configuration, which would allow us to totally remove the need for a database.

_Originally posted by @gentlementlegen in https://github.com/ubiquibot/automated-merging/pull/1#discussion_r1694058679_

I_kwDOLGaFrM6ATBS4.title: Secure Secrets for Generalized Continuous Deploys
I_kwDOLGaFrM6ATBS4.body:
### Context

I spent quite a bit of time cleaning up the code and trying to make the deploys more general purpose so that we can include in our `@ubiquity/ts-template` to make it seamless for contributors to open pull requests and for our reviewers to be able to review their work. I severely underestimated the amount of time that this would take. However:

- I finally got it stable and fairly fast (I removed unnecessary steps) over the past few days. 
- Here's a test on a pull request: https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/pull/16#issuecomment-1962506213. 
   - I also fixed the details around commit hashes posting in chronological order, which used to be an issue. 
- Specifically the work is done in [build.yml](https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/blob/development/.github/workflows/build.yml) and then its passed along to this current repository (`@ubiquity/cloudflare-deploy-action`) starting with [action.yml](https://github.com/ubiquity/cloudflare-deploy-action/blob/06783ab3b6bf9e91f82ae5be48e5ac18def8b9fc/action.yml) in the root.
- From there, it goes to one script for dealing with cloudflare: [cloudflare-deploy.sh](https://github.com/ubiquity/cloudflare-deploy-action/blob/06783ab3b6bf9e91f82ae5be48e5ac18def8b9fc/.github/cloudflare-deploy.sh)
- And then finally it passes the output (the deployed URL) to the node script in [src/index.ts](https://github.com/ubiquity/cloudflare-deploy-action/blob/06783ab3b6bf9e91f82ae5be48e5ac18def8b9fc/src/index.ts) which posts the comment as the bot to the pull request (or commit - but this is commented out now.)

As you can see I was struggling with passing secrets around. I decided to review the old implementation and realized that the clever workaround to expose the secrets was to invoke the action "internally" from the successful completion of a previous action[^1^], as seen [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/a57f08925a2fa10c756d036b0e5aeb7b54cf81b0/.github/workflows/continuous-deploy.yml#L5-L7). 

I spent a lot more time than I anticipated on this project, and unfortunately I'm starting to run out of development time leading up to 1 March and I still have several other matters I need to tend to. Unfortunately I did not follow best practices and exposed all of what should be secrets as plaintext and hardcoded in the scripts. 

### Notes

- I created a dedicated Cloudflare account specifically for our automatic deployments across all Ubiquity repositories. The API key that is used is tightly scoped just to create and edit Workers deployments. This isn't really a security concern because my updated deploy logic will only deploy to `production` if its merged to the default branch (for most of our repositories its `development` but sometimes `main` - its simple to change in the repository settings) otherwise it will just make a preview on a unique cloudflare URL. 
- I created a dedicated GitHub App (Ubiquibot Continuous Deploys) with minimal permissions to just be able to add comments on pull requests and commits for posting the deploys. 

I don't think its fatal that these credentials are leaked, but it obviously is not following best practices. 

### Objectives

1. Update `@ubiquity/ts-template` with the correct action initiators (`init.yml`, then `build.yml` so that it can have access to secrets)
   - I think `init.yml` would be a dummy action; or to be smart we could make it handle `conventional-commits` and then run the build. All secrets should be available in `build.yml` so that it can apply our i.e. `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` and `SUPABASE_URL` in the build. That way the reviewers can see the built (and functional) app easily. 
2. Update `@ubiquity/cloudflare-deploy-action` to handle the event coming in from `build.yml`. Now it should be privleged and be able to read our secrets normally. Change my code to use the secrets instead of the hardcoded plaintext values. 
3. Rotate the credentials. 

### Reference

Here is the order of the old setup. 

1. https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/ca90b265210fe953d942387791a52bca879b538c/.github/workflows/build.yml
2. https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/a57f08925a2fa10c756d036b0e5aeb7b54cf81b0/.github/workflows/continuous-deploy.yml
3. https://github.com/ubiquity/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/deploy.yml

### Final Remarks

I was able to make it stable without using download/upload artifact; and without using `checkout` actions. We should try not using these because if I recall correctly, they were the biggest bottlenecks for the slowdowns in the runs. Right now the biggest bottleneck that I couldn't' really get around is the `yarn install` for running node. I think its fine to leave in. 

There was some bug with the wrangler CLI that I couldn't verify if the project already existed remotely. I must have been doing something wrong but I spent so many hours on it that I just decided to [replace it with a curl](https://github.com/ubiquity/cloudflare-deploy-action/blob/06783ab3b6bf9e91f82ae5be48e5ac18def8b9fc/.github/cloudflare-deploy.sh#L28-L31).

[^1^]: As explained plainly by ChatGPT: https://chat.openai.com/share/0455a2fe-1dd4-483b-86e5-b05e025ad485

I_kwDOO9rGXc8AAAABSlVCjQ.title: Honor no-transform and strip modern digest headers when rewriting HTML
I_kwDOO9rGXc8AAAABSlVCjQ.body:
The HTML revision decorator rewrites responses that upstream marked `Cache-Control: no-transform` (request or response directive), and it leaves modern `Content-Digest` and `Repr-Digest` headers intact, so rewritten HTML is delivered with hashes of the original representation.

Priority: P2 (Codex review severity, both findings).
Native review evidence: review `router` (ubq.fi-router) on vps, cwd `/home/codex/repos/ubiquity/ubq.fi-router`, reviewed base `91bebfb78f2b`, reviewed head `06748e4f494d2d8c815d4441c8f6e4d0f3dbca6e`, exit 0, session `01a0c9b3-f37e-7a41-8d70-05802d1070d2`.

Scenario, finding 1: a successful, unencoded HTML response carries `Cache-Control: no-transform`. The predicate still permits decoration, so `proxyRoute` modifies the payload despite the upstream's explicit requirement for byte-preserving delivery. The request directive has the same problem.

Scenario, finding 2: upstream HTML includes `Content-Digest` or `Repr-Digest`. The current removal list strips only legacy digest fields, so these survive; integrity-verifying clients reject the response because the hashes no longer match the modified body.

Acceptance:

- Decoration is skipped whenever the request or the response `Cache-Control` contains `no-transform`.
- Both modern digest headers are removed alongside the existing validators on any rewritten response, in addition to the legacy fields.
- Regression coverage includes no-transform in the request, no-transform in the response, and `Content-Digest`/`Repr-Digest` removal.

Files:

- `src/utils/revision-footer.ts:52-58` — digest header removal list
- `src/utils/revision-footer.ts:72-76` — no-transform predicate

Related: ubq.fi-router#6 is the open parent feature request for the revision footer (its earlier PRs #29-#33 are closed); it does not track these correctness defects.

Publication note: the reviewed head `06748e4f494d2d8c815d4441c8f6e4d0f3dbca6e` is not pushed to GitHub. Live `main` is the reviewed base `91bebfb78f2b`, and `src/utils/revision-footer.ts` does not exist on live main. Publish the branch or attach the patch so implementers can reproduce against the exact revision.

I_kwDOMhAZP88AAAABSlVCfw.title: Preserve token selector holdings and amount labels across inventory refreshes
I_kwDOMhAZP88AAAABSlVCfw.body:
The token selector rebuilds from a symbol-keyed inventory cache and from partial core-token refreshes, which merges same-symbol contracts, drops still-owned tokens, resets selection, and leaves the amount label showing the previous token after selection is restored.

Priority: P2 (Codex review severity, all three findings).
Native review evidence: review `uusd` (uusd.ubq.fi) on vps, cwd `/home/codex/repos/ubiquity/uusd.ubq.fi`, reviewed base `eb0386e074f1`, reviewed head `9463ed2cb48647e6b4dcb69d5256e1c489896fb8`, exit 0, session `01a0c9b3-f40b-7640-86d0-2a95b7eacb2d`.

Scenario, finding 1: a wallet holds two contracts with the same symbol. `InventoryBarComponent._handleRefreshData()` merges them by symbol and overwrites one holding. Switching the selector to that cache removes an address that the previous address-based iteration over `RefreshData.tokenBalances` retained, and because the preloaded group is hidden the lost token cannot be selected again.

Scenario, finding 2: after a successful trade, `_handleTransactionSuccess()` calls `inventoryBar.refreshBalances()`. `_loadBalances()` fetches only LUSD, UUSD, and UBQ and replaces the entire inventory cache. Rebuilding from that cache drops still-owned tokens such as USDC whenever an eligible core holding remains, resets their selection, and prevents another trade with them until the next successful centralized refresh.

Scenario, finding 3: a refresh makes the selected deposit token ineligible. The amount is labeled using the old selection before `_renderTokenOptions()` switches to LUSD. The balance subscription then auto-populates and quotes LUSD while the input still reads, for example, `Amount (UBQ)`, and neither auto-population nor `_renderOutput()` corrects the label.

Acceptance:

- The inventory cache is address-keyed before the selector relies on it, so same-symbol contracts remain distinct and nonzero holdings stay selectable, per `docs/DECISIONS.md:11`.
- Partial core-token refreshes preserve the complete wallet snapshot, keeping still-owned tokens selectable and their selection intact, per `docs/DECISIONS.md:13`.
- The amount label is computed after the options and selected address are restored, so it always matches the active token.

Files:

- `src/components/simplified-exchange-component.ts:177-179` — symbol-keyed selector source
- `src/components/simplified-exchange-component.ts:184-190` — partial refresh replacing the cache
- `src/components/simplified-exchange-component.ts:758-762` — amount label ordering

Related: uusd.ubq.fi#62 is open and partially overlaps. Its scope covers keeping nonzero wallet tokens selectable when pricing is missing and rendering selector entries from merged inventory balances, which maps to findings 1 and 2; finding 3 (amount label after selection restore) is not covered. This issue records the concrete same-symbol collision, partial-refresh loss, and stale-label regressions on the reviewed candidate.

Publication note: the reviewed head `9463ed2cb48647e6b4dcb69d5256e1c489896fb8` is not pushed to GitHub; live `main` equals the reviewed base `eb0386e074f1`.

## Background

## Scope

- Keep inventory dust filtering centralized with a shared minimum USD visibility constant.
- Avoid treating an empty token selector placeholder as LUSD.
- Keep nonzero wallet tokens selectable when USD pricing is missing or unavailable.

I_kwDOMhAZP87FNHmS.title: CowSwap Integration
I_kwDOMhAZP87FNHmS.body:
The users should be able to "deposit anything" and "withdraw anything" basically abstract the assets by natively incorporating CowSwap into the deposit and withdraw transactions on the UI. [^01^]

Deposit flow should allow them to select any asset, and then it should swap and send to our deposit contract. The deposit contract should then return UUSD tokens. This may have a minor conflict with #25 as it has an integration with a direct curve swap (the primary UUSD market.)

The reverse flow should also work, where the user can withdraw into any asset. Again, careful of the existing curve swap code.

---

I assume the best UX is to "lock" or disable the UI elements mid transaction.
1. the user invokes the flow by "depositing ETH"
2. the UI has a notice explaining the current step in the flow, that the user is swapping ETH for LUSD and locks the UI elements so they don't stop mid flow
3. [via a post hook](https://docs.cow.fi/cow-protocol/concepts/order-types/cow-hooks) the swap completes and then the user receives their UUSD.

---

This project requires changes to the UI and creating a CowSwap post hook smart contract.

I_kwDOMhAZP87COspK.title: Integrate Wallet Connect via Reown AppKit
I_kwDOMhAZP87COspK.body:
## Overview  
Enable seamless wallet connectivity in the dApp by integrating the Reown platform's AppKit toolkit, supporting wallet login, transaction approvals, and cross-chain interactions. This spec is focused on Ethereum-compatible chains using `WagmiAdapter`. The solution uses React/Next.js as the UI framework.

## Goals  
- Support secure wallet connections without exposing private keys  
- Provide users wallet management (login/logout, transaction signing)  
- Utilize Reown's AppKit for enhanced UX, security, and multi-chain support  

## Tools and Libraries  
- `@reown/appkit/react` - Core UI and functionality kit  
- `@reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi` - Adapter for Ethereum EVM chains  
- `wagmi` - Ethereum hooks for React wallet management  
- `@tanstack/react-query` - Data caching and syncing (used by AppKit)  

## Setup Steps

### 1. Project Initialization  
- Use Reown’s CLI to bootstrap your AppKit integration:  
```bash
npx @reown/appkit-cli
```
- Select your project name, framework (React or Next.js), and network library (`wagmi` recommended for EVM).  
- Enter project folder and install dependencies:  
```bash
cd your-project-name
npm install
```

### 2. Register Your Project on Reown Cloud  
- Create a free account at [[cloud.reown.com](https://cloud.reown.com/)](https://cloud.reown.com)  
- Create a new AppKit project; obtain the **Project ID** for configuration  

### 3. Environment Configuration  
- Create a `.env` file at the root of your repo, add:  
```env
NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID=your-reown-project-id
```

### 4. AppKit Setup in Code  
- Create a config file (e.g., `config/index.tsx`) to set up AppKit with WagmiAdapter and chains:  
```tsx
'use client';

import { createAppKit } from '@reown/appkit/react';
import { WagmiAdapter } from '@reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi';
import { mainnet, arbitrum } from '@reown/appkit/networks';

const wagmiAdapter = new WagmiAdapter({
  projectId: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID!,
  networks: [mainnet, arbitrum],
});

export const appKit = createAppKit({
  adapters: [wagmiAdapter],
  networks: [mainnet, arbitrum],
  projectId: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID!,
  metadata: {
    name: 'Your DApp Name',
    description: 'Description of your dApp',
    url: 'https://your-dapp-url.com',
    icons: ['https://your-dapp-url.com/icon.png'],
  },
  features: {
    analytics: true, // optional
  },
});
```

### 5. Wrap Your Application with AppKit Provider  
- In your React root component (e.g., `_app.tsx` for Next.js), wrap your app with AppKit’s provider for context management:  
```tsx
import { AppKitProvider } from '@reown/appkit/react';

function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }) {
  return (
    
      
    
  );
}
export default MyApp;
```

### 6. UI Integration and Wallet Connect Button  
- Use hooks like `useAppKitAccount()` to query wallet connection state and provide connection UI  
- Build wallet connect/logout buttons in your UI, styled with Chakra UI components for consistency  
- Example minimal connect button snippet:  
```tsx
import { useAppKitAccount, useAppKitModal } from '@reown/appkit/react';
import { Button } from '@chakra-ui/react';

function WalletConnectButton() {
  const { isConnected, disconnect } = useAppKitAccount();
  const modal = useAppKitModal();

  if (isConnected) {
    return Disconnect Wallet;
  }
  return  modal.open()}>Connect Wallet;
}
```

### 7. Handling Authentication & Transactions  
- Utilize AppKit hooks for transaction requests and approvals  
- Monitor wallet status and connect errors for UX feedback with UI toast notifications or modals  

### 8. Testing & Deployment  
- Test wallet connections on supported networks (e.g., Ethereum mainnet, Gnosis)  
- Test user flows: connect, disconnect, request signatures, transaction executions  
- Deploy with environment variables securely configured  

## References and Resources  
- [[Reown AppKit Documentation](https://docs.reown.com/appkit)](https://docs.reown.com/appkit)  
- [[Reown GitHub AppKit Repo](https://github.com/reown-com/appkit)](https://github.com/reown-com/appkit)  
- [[Reown CLI for AppKit Setup](https://docs.monad.xyz/guides/reown-guide)](https://docs.monad.xyz/guides/reown-guide)  
- Sample integrations with wallet connection buttons and React hooks  
- Chakra UI for React components and styling

I_kwDOMhAZP87RBkvu.body: A thought that occurred to me is if we make a "savings account" deposit button, we can simulate a banking experience. Proposed yield mechanic: Uniswap v4 concentrated liquidity at `0.9999 - 1.0001` I'm unsure how accurate the projection is, but anything above 5% is marketable as a "savings account" I think! > > > Given your screenshot data: > • Curve pool daily volume ≈ $27.9 k > • TVL ≈ $93.5 k > • Fee ≈ 0.04 % > → Fee yield ≈ 0.012 % per day ≈ 4.4 % APR before CRV boosts (close to the shown 2–3 %). > > Now suppose you moved that volume onto a Uniswap-style narrow-range LP: > 1. Range width = 0.02 % (0.9999–1.0001) > → ≈ 5 000 × capital efficiency vs full-range. > 2. Only a fraction of swaps cross your ticks — say 20–40 % in range. > 3. Fee tier = 0.01 %. > > Approximate effective boost: > > 4.4\% \times \frac{0.01}{0.04} \times 5000 \times 0.3 \approx 165\% \text{ APR} > > If the peg drifts slightly less, uptime rises, so ~100–300 % APR is plausible; if it drifts more, you fall out of range and it collapses back to single-digit yield. > > So: > > Expect maybe ~50 ×–70 × yield boost vs Curve, only while in-range. > Out-of-range = 0 fees; you’ll need automation or active rebalancing to realize the upper bound. Of course, it is implied that we would abstract all the operations away from the user i.e. swapping half the value into the other asset, depositing the liquidity etc.

I_kwDOMhAZP87GAn3A.title: feat: Enhanced wallet connection with auto-reconnect and account switching
I_kwDOMhAZP87GAn3A.body:
## Problem
Current wallet connection lacks modern UX features:
- No automatic reconnection on page refresh
- Manual account switching not detected
- Lost connection state between sessions
- Poor handling of wallet lock/unlock events

## Solution
Implement comprehensive wallet connection improvements including persistent sessions and automatic account switching detection.

## Features Implemented
1. **Persistent Wallet Sessions**:
   - Store connected wallet address in localStorage
   - Auto-reconnect on page load if wallet still has permissions
   - Graceful fallback if permissions revoked

2. **MetaMask Account Switching**:
   - Listen for accountsChanged events
   - Automatically update UI when user switches accounts
   - Refresh balances and transaction states

3. **Enhanced Event Handling**:
   - Detect wallet lock/unlock
   - Handle chain switching
   - Respond to permission changes

4. **Improved Connection Flow**:
   - Show 'Disconnecting...' state during disconnect
   - Force wallet selection on explicit connect
   - Better error messages for connection failures

## Technical Implementation
- Event-driven architecture with WalletService
- WALLET_EVENTS enum for type-safe event handling
- Robust error handling and retry logic
- Clean separation of concerns

## Benefits
- Seamless user experience across sessions
- No need to reconnect wallet on every visit
- Instant response to account changes
- Better integration with wallet features

I_kwDOMhAZP87E0PMi.title: Abstract away mints/redeems and swaps
I_kwDOMhAZP87E0PMi.body:
We should provide the user with the best deal, whether its to mint/redeem or swap off of curve. This UX implies that the user does not need to be knowledgeable about the mint/redeem mechanics. Instead, they can just reliably come to the interface and always get the best deal. 

It might make sense to change the terminology to be more like "deposit" and "withdraw", as if its a Ubiquity bank account. It is not clear to me what the best terminology is at the moment. 

Examples:

UUSD is trading at $0.99, and user wants LUSD:
- UI should redeem LUSD (1 USD = 1 LUSD)

UUSD is trading at $1.01, and user wants LUSD:
- UI should swap (1 UUSD = 1.01 LUSD)

UUSD is trading at $0.99, and user wants UUSD:
- UI should swap (1 UUSD = 0.99 LUSD)

UUSD is trading at $1.01, and user wants UUSD:
- UI should mint (1 UUSD = 1 LUSD)

I_kwDOMhAZP87GAnjX.title: feat: Implement centralized refresh service for periodic data updates
I_kwDOMhAZP87GAnjX.body:
## Problem
Multiple components independently fetch and refresh data (prices, balances, protocol settings) leading to:
- Redundant API calls
- Inconsistent data across components
- Uncoordinated refresh cycles
- Potential rate limiting issues

## Solution
Implement a centralized refresh service that coordinates all periodic data updates across the application.

## Implementation Details
1. **CentralizedRefreshService**:
   - Single source of truth for periodic updates
   - Configurable refresh intervals
   - Publish/subscribe pattern for data distribution
   - Intelligent batching of RPC calls

2. **Features**:
   - 15-second refresh cycle for dynamic data
   - Deduplication of requests
   - Error handling with exponential backoff
   - Performance monitoring

3. **Data Types Managed**:
   - Token balances
   - UUSD price
   - Protocol settings
   - Collateral ratios
   - Oracle prices

## Benefits
- Reduced RPC calls through intelligent batching
- Consistent data across all UI components
- Better performance and user experience
- Easier to monitor and debug data flow
- Prevents rate limiting issues

## Technical Approach
- Observer pattern for component subscriptions
- Centralized error handling
- Caching layer for frequently accessed data
- Graceful degradation on service failure

I_kwDOMhAZP87GAnJx.title: feat: Implement immediate balance refresh after transactions
I_kwDOMhAZP87GAnJx.body:
## Problem
Currently, when users complete transactions (buy/sell UUSD), their token balances in the UI don't update immediately. Users see a success message but the balance display still shows old values, creating confusion.

The UI relies on a 15-second automatic refresh cycle, which means users might wait up to 15 seconds to see their updated balances.

## Solution
Implement immediate balance refresh that triggers as soon as a transaction is confirmed on-chain.

## Implementation Details
1. Add balance refresh call to transaction success handlers
2. Update SimplifiedExchangeComponent and app.ts
3. Use `void this._services.inventoryBar.refreshBalances();`

## Benefits
- Immediate visual confirmation of transaction results
- Better user experience with real-time balance updates
- Reduced user confusion about transaction status

## Test Cases
1. Buy UUSD → Balance updates immediately after confirmation
2. Sell UUSD → Balance updates immediately after confirmation
3. Multiple rapid transactions → Each updates balances correctly
4. Failed transactions → Balances remain unchanged

I_kwDOMhAZP87CHbdy.title: Display Accurate Redemption Oracle Price
I_kwDOMhAZP87CHbdy.body:
The user interface at `uusd.ubq.fi` is currently displaying a misleading UUSD price, which is causing confusion for users attempting to redeem their tokens. The UI shows the spot price from the Curve pool, while the smart contract uses a different calculated Time-Weighted Average Price (TWAP) to determine redemption eligibility. This discrepancy leads users to believe they can redeem when the functionality is actually blocked by the contract's security mechanisms.

## Technical Analysis

The frontend currently displays two prices:

1.  **Spot Price**: Fetched directly from the Curve pool. This is what users see as the main price.
2.  **TWAP Price**: This is the value returned by `getDollarPriceUsd` from the `UbiquityPoolFacet`, which is the actual value used by the contract for redemption checks.

The issue is that the UI does not clearly indicate that the "TWAP" price is the one that governs redemptions, and it is not prominently displayed.

## Proposed Solution

To address this, we will modify the frontend to provide users with clear and accurate information about the redemption process.

1.  **Update Price Display**:
    *   The main price displayed on the redemption page should be the value returned by `getDollarPriceUsd`.
    *   This price should be clearly labeled as "**Redemption Oracle Price (TWAP)**" to indicate its role in the redemption process and its time-averaged nature.
    *   The spot price can be retained as a secondary reference but should be clearly distinguished from the oracle price.

2.  **Add Explanatory Tooltip**:
    *   A tooltip should be added next to the "Redemption Oracle Price (TWAP)" that explains why this price is used and how it is calculated (i.e., "This is a time-weighted average price used to prevent flash loan attacks. It is calculated based on the LUSD/USD price and the UUSD/LUSD price from the Curve pool.").
    *   This will provide transparency and help users understand why redemptions may be paused.

3.  **Dynamic Redemption Message**:
    *   The UI should display a clear, dynamic message that indicates whether redemptions are currently possible based on the "Redemption Oracle Price (TWAP)."
    *   For example, if the price is above the threshold, a message like "**Redemptions are temporarily paused because the oracle price is above the $0.99 threshold**" should be displayed prominently.

## Acceptance Criteria

*   The `uusd.ubq.fi` redemption page must display the price from `getDollarPriceUsd` as the primary price for redemptions.
*   The UI must clearly label this price as "Redemption Oracle Price (TWAP)".
*   A tooltip explaining the price calculation and its purpose must be present.
*   The UI must display a clear message indicating the current status of the redemption functionality based on the TWAP.

I_kwDOMhAZP86SZWbh.title: Create UI for `UbiquityPool`
I_kwDOMhAZP86SZWbh.body: There is the new [UbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/UbiquityPoolFacet.sol) contract (facet) where users can mint and redeem `Dollar` tokens for collateral tokens. Minting example: 1. User calls [mintDollar()](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/UbiquityPoolFacet.sol#L133) and sends 95 `LUSD` + 5 Governance (`UBQ`) tokens worth 5 USD 2. User gets 100 `Dollar` tokens Redeeming example: 1. User calls [redeemDollar()](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/UbiquityPoolFacet.sol#L161) and sends 100 `Dollar` tokens 2. I_kwDOI-EJSM8AAAABUmdy9A.body:
A funding wallet holds both legitimate and bogus pending permits. The Delete all / Delete action tooltip promises bogus-permit cleanup, but confirming the transaction invalidates on-chain every permit the filter selected, including legitimate payouts.

- [src/components/dashboard-page.tsx:416](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/f7e6f741c01979752ac1c60440a9d6f19983fd80/src/components/dashboard-page.tsx#L416): void invalidatePermits(invalidatablePermits) -> bulk click handler passes that entire filtered list

I_kwDOI-EJSM6sv2IK.title: Cow Swap Cash Out
I_kwDOI-EJSM6sv2IK.body:
I was doing some research on [implementing automated cowswap orders](https://github.com/0x4007/travel-stipend/blob/feat/auto-swap/src/cowswap-swap.ts) (they have an SDK) and I realize that we can do something pretty cool:

1. Only support settlements using UUSD. 
2. Allow the user to configure what asset they want to be paid in, it should be saved in localStorage. 
3. The cowswap quote can appear in place of the reward amount. For example, by default, loading the app for `100 UUSD` permit would show that. But if the user configured to get paid in USDT, then it might come out to something like `99.5 USDT`. The app will simply display `99.5 USDT` instead if their settings are set as such. 
4. The claim permit button would actually 1. invalidate their permit (if the wallet can afford the pay out) 2. initiate a cowswap order with the beneficiary address set to the permit beneficiary

Then now we can enforce people using UUSD in the backend but user facing they can receive rewards in any asset they want! 

I think this provides best of all worlds for users. For partners, we could charge a premium for them to use other tokens natively in the background etc.

I_kwDOI-EJSM7Q8VIR.title: Migrate backend to Deno-native + harden Deno Deploy
I_kwDOI-EJSM7Q8VIR.body:
Context
- Current backend uses Node-specific server (`@hono/node-server`) and `process.env` while deploying on Deno Deploy. This couples Node APIs to a Deno runtime and increases risk of incompatibilities and subtle failures.
- We already deploy via GitHub Actions OIDC to Deno Deploy (project: `pay-ubq-fi`). Frontend is built to `frontend/dist` and served by `backend/server.ts`.

Goals
- Run fully Deno-native on Deploy (no Node server adapter).
- Keep GitHub Actions deploy unchanged except for necessary tweaks.
- Preserve API behavior and static asset serving.

Scope of Work
- Replace server bootstrap with Deno-native:
  - Swap `@hono/node-server` + `serveStatic` for `Deno.serve` + `hono` fetch handler.
  - Use `Deno.env.get()` for configuration.
  - Serve SPA assets from `./frontend/dist` (index.html fallback).
- Supabase client
  - Import via `npm:@supabase/supabase-js` under Deno.
  - Validate ESM usage works on Deploy.
- Add `/health` endpoint returning 200 with basic info (uptime/version).
- Add `deno.jsonc` (server side) with:
  - `tasks` (dev/start/test)
  - Optional import map for `npm:` spec
  - Lint/fmt config
- CI/CD (pay.ubq.fi/.github/workflows/deploy.yml)
  - Keep OIDC deployctl step; ensure `entrypoint: backend/server.ts` still correct after refactor.
  - Ensure frontend build step remains and artifacts exist.
- CORS:
  - Keep current permissive CORS via `hono/cors` or stricter allowlist; document decision.
- Logging:
  - Ensure console logs appear in Deno Deploy logs; standardize error handling.

Acceptance Criteria
- No usage of `@hono/node-server` or `process.env` in runtime code.
- Server starts with `Deno.serve` and exports `app.fetch` handler.
- `GET /health` returns 200 JSON `{ status: "ok" }`.
- Static assets served from `frontend/dist`, SPA fallback serves `index.html`.
- Supabase calls succeed using `Deno.env.get` variables: `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
- CI deploy completes via `denoland/deployctl@v1` to project `pay-ubq-fi`.
- Docs updated: .rules and docs/additional/deno-deploy-guide.md reference Deno-native server and env names.

Non-Goals
- Frontend functional changes.
- Schema or Supabase policy changes.

References
- Server: `backend/server.ts`
- CI: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
- Project rules: `.rules`
- Deploy guide: `docs/additional/deno-deploy-guide.md`

Test Plan
- Local: `deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-env backend/server.ts` and open site; verify `/api/permits/record-claim` and `/health`.
- Deploy: confirm Deploy logs, static assets, and API endpoints.

Owner/Timebox
- Est: 0.5–1 day. Assign to backend engineer familiar with Deno/Hono.

I_kwDOI-EJSM7Ia4lv.title: Fix Console Warnings: Invalid Permit Data & Validation Errors
I_kwDOI-EJSM7Ia4lv.body:
## Problem Description
The application generates 300+ console warnings when loading, primarily related to invalid permit data and validation errors. This creates noise in the console and makes debugging difficult.

## Categories of Warnings

### 1. Worker Warnings (667 instances)
```
Worker: Permit [X] with nonce Y has no owner address
Worker: Permit [X] with nonce Y has no token address  
Worker: Permit [X] with nonce Y has invalid network ID
Worker: Permit [X] with nonce Y has no deadline
Worker: Permit [X] with nonce Y has invalid signature format
```

### 2. Client-Side Validation Warnings
```
Permit X: Missing permit information
Permit X: Full Permit data: [object]
```

### 3. External Resource Warnings (2 instances)
```
Failed to load resource: net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT (Google Play scripts)
```

## Root Causes

1. **Data Integrity Issues**: Database contains permits with missing or invalid fields
2. **Overly Verbose Validation**: Validation functions log warnings for every invalid permit
3. **No Early Filtering**: Invalid permits propagate through the entire data pipeline

I_kwDOI-EJSM6VGYn4.title: Add retry mechanism for partially failed virtual card order
I_kwDOI-EJSM6VGYn4.body:
In the virtual card feature, we have two parts in a single transaction to mint a virtual card.

1. Claim the permit by transferring the permit reward to the treasury wallet
2. If the step-1 is successful, order the virtual card at Reloadly

The problem is that the transaction isn't atomic because each step happens in a different system. Step-2 can fail while still leaving the permit amount in the treasury. Why would step-2 fail? There could be one of the many reasons.

- virtual card suddenly becoming out of stock
- any network error on user side or Reloadly side
- user closing browser before the permit transaction confirmation
- change in the best picked card, suddenly a better card becomes available or currently picked card becomes unavailable
- [RPC-handler](https://github.com/ubiquity/rpc-handler) failing to find rpc for backend to use, or if it finds one but the rpc stops working

Currently, the solution to this problem is manual. It is either a manual refund or manual resending of the card order request to `/post-order` with some parameters (productId, tx hash, country).

We can improve this by implementing one of the following solutions.
- a manual refund can become automatic by issuing a new permit of the same amount
- resend the mint request to backend to `/post-order`

I am inclined towards resending the mint request. One problem is that `/post-order` needs the transaction hash of the permit transfer to the treasury. Sometimes you will have it, and you can store it in the cookies/local storage. But sometimes you will not have it and you will have to read it either from blockchain or ask the user to manually insert the transaction hash to retry minting. I think you can read it from blockchain by looking into [permit2 events](https://gnosisscan.io/address/0x000000000022d473030f116ddee9f6b43ac78ba3#events) 

The goal of this issue is to implement a mechanism to resend the mint request or a better solution if you can think of one. 

Since the best-picked virtual card can change in this duration, a better option is to rename the mint button to "Retry Mint" and let the user click first so that user can see they are ordering a different card now. 

Please note that the virtual cards feature is present in `beta` branch at the moment. But it can move to development branch anytime. So, keep an eye on that and open a PR accordingly.

I_kwDOI-EJSM6bfw8r.title: Add support for gift card with SKU 18732
I_kwDOI-EJSM6bfw8r.body:
We have the feature of minting gift cards for crypto rewards which works this way:
1. `pay.ubq.fi` checks contributor's country
2. If contributor's country is in the [MC allow list 3052024.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16492174/MC.allow.list.3052024.xlsx) then offer gift card with SKU 18597
3. Otherwise try to find the best card SKU from [MasterCard International.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16492175/MasterCard.International.xlsx)

Reloadly has recently added a new tokenized card SKU:
```
We have a new sku that may be of interest to you: 

SKU: 18732
Name: Mastercard Prepaid USD Debit (Virtual only) US
5 - 1000 USD

Product Description:
Your Virtual Promotional Prepaid Mastercard can be used online, for phone/mail orders, or in stores that accept mobile wallet where Debit Mastercard is accepted. This card must be used within 6 months from the time you receive your link. Please Note: A 2% currency conversion fee will apply if the merchant settles in a currency other than USD

This card works in 130 Countries
```

[SKU_ 18732 - Countries covered (5).xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17493171/SKU_.18732.-.Countries.covered.5.xlsx)

It makes sense to support a new SKU 18732 this way:
1. `pay.ubq.fi` checks contributor's country
2. If contributor's country is in the [MC allow list 3052024.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16492174/MC.allow.list.3052024.xlsx) then offer gift card with SKU 18597
3. If contributor's country is in the [SKU_ 18732 - Countries covered (5).xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17493171/SKU_.18732.-.Countries.covered.5.xlsx) the offer gift card with SKU 18732
4. Otherwise try to find the best card SKU from [MasterCard International.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16492175/MasterCard.International.xlsx)

So as a part of this issue we should make sure that SKU 18732 is supported in these pages:
- https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/9b88dd6ffe04a13650d51a055441696a13047be9/static/index.html (redeem gift card)
- https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/9b88dd6ffe04a13650d51a055441696a13047be9/static/ubiquity-dollar.html (mint gift card for UUSD)

Related [comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/259#issuecomment-2268350042).

I_kwDOI-EJSM6eL5Z6.title: fix live reload
I_kwDOI-EJSM6eL5Z6.body:
This is the same as in `work.ubq.fi` check [this issue](https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/issues/164).

This repo's `package.json` start command uses wrangler pages to serve instead of `esbuild-server`:

```json
"serve": "npx wrangler pages dev static --port 8080"
```

This killed the live reload feature, and [according to this issue in wrangler's repo](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/4824) we have to pass in a directory after `wrangler pages dev` to hear changes from. Wrangler only looks specifically inside the directory given (non-recursive), in this case `static`, so even though HTML changes are captured, typescript ones aren't. Therefore it is extremely unreliable to get global ts changes. So I wrote an observer using esbuild API that watches and rebuilds based on file change. This spec might be a lil weird because I am extremely tired as I write it.

I_kwDOI-EJSM6P7H69.title: Simplify virtual cards - offer only supported cards for user location
I_kwDOI-EJSM6P7H69.body:
Currently, we offer all available visa and mastercards provided by Reloadly.  There is no geolocation filtering. The bounty hunters can claim their permit in any virtual card. Additionally, Reloadly offers 
- fixed price cards: in which the value inside the card is fixed
- variable price cards: in which we can specify the exact amount that we want inside the virtual card. 

The goal of this issue is to simplify the feature. 
- Only offer the cards to user according to their location. Reloadly API supports that.
- Only use variable price cards, and ignore fixed price cards. 
- Remove the "Also available in" part from the UI.

Please note that the virtual cards feature is present in `beta` branch at the moment. But it can move to `development` branch anytime. So, keep an eye on that and open a PR accordingly.

I_kwDOI-EJSM6Qp04F.title: Mint card for Ubiquity Dollars
I_kwDOI-EJSM6Qp04F.body:
[This](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/pull/226) PR introduced a feature of card minting.

How it works:
1. Contributor opens `pay.ubq.fi` to redeem our "standard" permit reward
2. Contributor sends permit reward to the treasury address
3. Contributor sends transaction hash to the `pay.ubq.fi` backend
4. A new reloadly gift card is minted to the contributor

Any user with Ubiquity Dollars should be able to mint a gift card (not only the ones with ready to use permits).

What should be done:
  - create a new page (for example `pay.ubq.fi/cards`) where users will be able to send Ubiquity Dollars to the treasury address and get reloadly gift cards in return

Notice:
1. Gift cards feature is located in a [separate](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/tree/beta) branch so it makes sense to open a PR towards that branch
2. Try to minimize [backend code](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/tree/16e7052ed8cb1427d2191800c5bfbc1d2deff5db/functions) changes in order not to complicate it further

I_kwDOI-EJSM6SH7uN.title: Pick & offer the single best virtual card to user
I_kwDOI-EJSM6SH7uN.body:
Currently, the virtual card feature is offering all visa & mastercard to users based on their location. 

As discussed in https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/259#issuecomment-2252453717 and https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/259#issuecomment-2266190734, pick and offer only single virtual card to the user. 

Important files
- [MasterCard International.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16514698/MasterCard.International.xlsx)
- [MC allow list 3052024.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16514700/MC.allow.list.3052024.xlsx)


How to pick the best card for a user? 
- offer only mastercard from `MasterCard International.xlsx` because they are tokenized.
- pick the card SKU based on user's location.
- offer mastercard SKU 18597 to users who are not in the `MasterCard International.xlsx`, but present in the `MC allow list 3052024.xlsx`.
- We probably will not fetch a product list from Reloadly anymore. Presence of this previously was taking care of not offering card to users out of `MC allow list 3052024.xlsx`. If so, make sure user's country is in the `MC allow list 3052024.xlsx` before offering them a mastercard.

Please note that the virtual cards feature is present in `beta` branch at the moment. But it can move to `development` branch anytime. So, keep an eye on that and open a PR accordingly.
