I_kwDOPpQwy87PCfIz.title: CI (GitHub Actions) – Handoff
I_kwDOPpQwy87PCfIz.body:
# CI (GitHub Actions) – Handoff

Objective
- Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs lint, unit tests (Bun test), build, and E2E smoke (Playwright/preview) on PRs and pushes to `development` and `main`.

Context
- Repo: `stake.ubq.fi` (branch `pr-1`)
- Tooling: Bun, Vite, ESLint, Vitest (new), Playwright (new)

- Workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with jobs:
  - `lint`: install + `bun run lint`.
  - `unit`: install + `bun test`.
  - `build`: install + `bun run build` cache artifacts.
  - `e2e`: depends on `build`, serves preview (`vite preview`), runs `bunx playwright test` (Chromium only).
- Bun setup using `oven-sh/setup-bun@v1`.
- Node version pinned to `22.12.x` or newer `22.x`.
- Cache `~/.cache/bun` and repo `node_modules/.bun-*` automatically (action handles).

Acceptance Criteria
- CI runs on PRs and push to `development` and `main`.
- All steps green on the current branch.
- E2E job starts preview server and hits base URL successfully.

Constraints & Guidance
- Keep workflow readable and < 150 lines.
- Fail fast: unused matrix entries or browsers not required.
- Use `if: always()` only for uploading artifacts on failure when helpful.

Suggested Steps
1) Add `oven-sh/setup-bun@v1` and `actions/setup-node@v4`.
2) Split jobs and set `needs` for ordering.
3) Use `bun install --frozen-lockfile` if lock constraints enforced.
4) Add `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0` only if downloading browsers in CI; otherwise rely on `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`.
5) Gate E2E with a short timeout for server readiness.

Validation
- Open a PR; confirm 4 jobs run and pass.

Out of scope
- No Docker use.

I_kwDONY-32c7XvS9B.title: Migrate to Bun: runtime, tests, and CI
I_kwDONY-32c7XvS9B.body:
This change migrates the project fully to Bun for runtime, package management, testing, and CI. It replaces Yarn/PnP and Jest with Bun equivalents, updates scripts and workflows, and removes obsolete files to keep the repo clean.

- CI Build workflow uses oven-sh/setup-bun@v2, caches Bun, runs `bun ci`, lint, typecheck, `bun test` (uploads junit.xml & coverage), then `bun run build` and uploads static artifact.
- Build workflow reads Supabase envs from GitHub secrets (no hardcoded keys), name remains "Build" for deploy workflow compatibility.

I_kwDONY-32c7bi0BK.title: Auth: auto-logout when token is invalid
I_kwDONY-32c7bi0BK.body:
When GitHub tokens expire or become invalid, the app currently spams 401s, hides the login avatar, and leaves notifications empty. Implemented an auth-failure handler to clear Supabase/local session, sign out, and re-render the login button so users can immediately re-auth and restore notifications.

Acceptance:
- Bad credentials on /user or /notifications trigger sign out and show the GitHub login button in the toolbar.
- Latest-comment fetches respect 401s and also force logout without breaking the UI.
- Reloading after token invalidation no longer leaves the app in a broken state; notifications load after re-login.

I_kwDONY-32c7biUL7.title: Auto-mark on view + resilient cache for notifications
I_kwDONY-32c7biUL7.body:
Implement auto-mark-on-view and resilient notification caching so refreshes are predictable and work offline.

Acceptance:
- Mark unread threads as read when 50%+ in view via IntersectionObserver queue; throttle requests, retry failures, and persist pending IDs locally (do not auto-mark off ubq.fi by default).
- Save raw and aggregated notifications to IndexedDB with ~5 minute TTL; rebuild aggregated data from cached raw when needed and use cached data offline.
- Pull-to-refresh clears in-memory and IndexedDB caches and signals the service worker to drop API cache before refetching.
- Service worker uses network-first for GitHub API with ~10 minute TTL and handles CLEAR_API_CACHE messages.
- Empty-state rendering works when no notifications and when filters remove items (e.g., bot/slash-command skips).

Files:
- src/home/rendering/render-github-notifications.ts:1
- src/home/home.ts:1
- src/home/getters/get-indexed-db.ts:1
- static/progressive-web-app.js:1
- src/home/fetch-github/fetch-data.ts:1

I_kwDOM2UEbM7e6ORK.title: UbiquityOS Sprint Management Dashboard
I_kwDOM2UEbM7e6ORK.body:
This is a stub task.

We should make a simple sign up experience meant to convert paying customers, engineering managers specifically.

My vision is to post on places like [hackernews](https://news.ycombinator.com) twitter etc and do a quick writeup on how AI team managers are here, highlighting benefits X, Y, Z...

Then bring them to some marketing/landing page with a sign in with GitHub button. At this time our system can scrape their GitHub organization, generate vector embeddings, and start planning their upcoming sprint.

The user logs into a simplified version of the dashboard that basically shows

1. a calendar view of their real team members and what tasks they should be assigned to (we will need to define priority levels somehow[^1], normally a manager labels each priority level on the task individually.) and we can automatically estimate the time of each task by reading their specifications.
2. Quantitative metrics of how much value the system provides to their team i.e. saves X amount of time assigning tasks (assuming it takes 5 minutes to assign each task from the backlog to the right person etc) and saves Y amount of dollars in a typical engineering manager salary etc. The numbers should be a lot more impressive with larger backlogs (perhaps we can support importing tasks from other platforms like asana etc)

### General Steps

1. Backend
2. Landing Page/Conversion Funnel UI/UX Design
3. Implementation

[^1]: a tinder like view with swiping left (low) right (high) up (urgent) to quickly set priority levels on tasks could be interesting to bootstrap the system's data. But otherwise we can ask the AI to think of what is most likely to drive revenue (business priority) tasks, and we can provide examples like internal developer tooling may be lower priority than fixing breaking bugs.

I_kwDOM2UEbM7cRAxh.title: Copilot assignment via the Github API
I_kwDOM2UEbM7cRAxh.body:
**Putting myself out of a job here, but here we go 😅**

[As of yesterday](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-12-03-assign-issues-to-copilot-using-the-api/), it’s now possible to assign **Copilot** to issues via the REST and GraphQL APIs.

This opens up some interesting opportunities we could explore:

- A plugin or kernel extension that directly bridges the kernel with Copilot.
- Automated weekly or monthly **refactoring** tasks planned and executed by Copilot — either within a parent issue with a few sub-issues, or as a single “spec → plan → execute” workflow.
- Automated **documentation updates** across all plugins and projects on a set schedule.

If some of these don’t fit as new plugins, they could still be packaged as reusable workflows. I’m sure there are more ideas along these lines, but these are a few clear starting points.

rfc @0x4007

I_kwDOM2UEbM7TATiW.title: Automate beta → prod merge after inactivity timeout
I_kwDOM2UEbM7TATiW.body:
Automate merging of the `development` branch into `main` after a period of inactivity (e.g. 3 months) with no new commits to `development`.

Purpose: ensure tested features in `development` eventually promote to `main`.

Scope:
- A scheduled job (cron under @ubiquity-os) runs daily or weekly.
- Checks if `development` has had no commits for a defined timeout period (default: 3 months).
- If no commits within that period, automatically merges `development` → `main`.
- If new commits are pushed to `development`, reset the inactivity timer.

Remarks:
- Authenticate as our GitHub App.

I_kwDOM2UEbM6h828r.title: Custom Notifications Viewer
I_kwDOM2UEbM6h828r.body:
- I did some research in the past with custom notifications viewer. https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/pull/126
- Original specification here https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/issues/117

Fork work.ubq.fi because it has a lot of good qualities for list viewing, progressive web app features, styling etc. Tear out all the proposal/task related viewing logic, and focus only on notification viewing so that the code is simpler. 

## Custom Notifications Viewer

As activity continues to pick up and my notifications become slower to get through, it would be useful to make a simple ui that allows for more intelligent notification filtering. 

### Prioritization Sorting Algorithm

- We need to detect the priority level of the task the notification is associated with.
   - If the notification is not associated with a task, consider not showing it on this view at all. 
   - If the notification is a pull request, it must be linked to a task with a priority label.
- Reverse chronological order, meaning that neglected/old notifications should appear higher than new ones. 
   - The reason for this is that active conversations will continue to produce more notifications, which can easily cause the reviewer to check it multiple times in a sitting (as I try to get to inbox 0 this happens to me, so I intentionally start from older notifications for this reason.)
- Top of displayed list is highest priority, then work your way down to low priority. 

### Blocking Tasks

If it thinks without my input the task is blocked, it's a higher priority notification.
- Linkbacks: if the notification is associated with a task with many linkbacks then it should be considered higher priority, it usually means its blocking other pulls/tasks

Perhaps we could have an AI layer on top one day to summarize and/or reorder notifications from most important to least.

### Remarks
- Always exclude draft pulls.

## Notification Scoring

We should associate each notification with "scores" so that we can quantify where it would render on the page. 
- Time score: the older it is, the higher its score. We can take the current posix timestamp and subtract the timestamp of the notification to achieve this. 
- Linkback score: we can count how many times it was cross-referenced. The more times it was cross-referenced, the higher it should render on the page. We should prioritize those with higher linkbacks. If two notifications have the same amount of linkbacks i.e. 0, then we sort based on the time score only. 

We need to ensure that priority level always has precedence. For example, `priority 2` associated notifications should always appear higher than `priority 1`.

I_kwDOM2UEbM6s8n2c.title: User XP CLI
I_kwDOM2UEbM6s8n2c.body:
Generated by ChatGPT 


A minimal command-line interface (CLI) to calculate XP earned by users.

Read all earnings from supabase. Sum them up to figure out users XP. 

### Usage

Calculate XP by user:

- **Global XP** (all orgs/repos):
  ```bash
  xp-cli calculate --user=username
  ```

- **Organization-specific XP**:
  ```bash
  xp-cli calculate --user=username --org=organization_name
  ```

- **Repository-specific XP**:
  ```bash
  xp-cli calculate --user=username --org=organization_name --repo=repository_name
  ```

### Output Format
```
User:  username
Global XP: 1234
```

For org-specific or repo-specific calculations, clearly specify the context:
```
User: john_doe
Organization (my-org) XP: 567
```
```
User: john_doe
Repository (my-repo) XP: 89
```

### Optional Caching
- Caching support optional, enabled if performance is slow.

I_kwDOLcmjKM7zkXPE.title: Prevent deep estimate dispatch for manual /time commands
I_kwDOLcmjKM7zkXPE.body:
## Summary
Manual `/time <duration>` commands still dispatch the deep-estimate workflow, even though they should only set the time label directly.

## Expected behavior
- Bare `/time` estimates time and dispatches the deep-estimate workflow.
- `/time <duration>` sets the time label manually and does not dispatch the deep-estimate workflow.
- Issue-opened behavior remains unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- Raw comment and parsed command flows use the same dispatch gate.
- Whitespace-only `/time` input is treated the same as bare `/time`.
- Tests cover bare `/time`, explicit-duration `/time`, and parsed explicit-duration commands.
- README documents the updated workflow behavior.

I_kwDOLcmjKM7zg1Hq.title: Deep-estimate dispatch fails on dist artifact branches
I_kwDOLcmjKM7zg1Hq.body:
`ACTION_REF` now points to `dist/<source>` for deployed plugin runs, but `.github/workflows/deep-estimate.yml` is not published into artifact branches. As a result, `/time` and issue-open deep-estimate dispatches fail with a workflow-not-found error when they try to dispatch `deep-estimate.yml` against the artifact ref.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `deep-estimate.yml` is present on published `dist/<source>` branches
- deployed plugin runs can dispatch `Deep Time Estimate` successfully from the artifact ref
- the sync only updates the artifact branch when the workflow file changes
- non-artifact deploy modes keep their current behavior

The daemon-pricing bot posts a warning message stating "You are not allowed to set labels" but doesn't actually undo the label setting action, making the warning ineffective.

## Metadata from the incident
- Caller: `onLabelChangeSetPricing`
- User: @whilefoo
- Request ID: 7arbfe0477zr

The bot should either enforce the permission check before allowing the action or implement proper remediation by removing unauthorized labels.

I_kwDOLcmjKM6qBo0D.title: Suggest Time Estimates based on past issue threads
I_kwDOLcmjKM6qBo0D.body:
The current time estimate relies on the user/contributor to suggest accurate time estimates, which are often inflated. 

The pricing strategy should award natural time estimates and penalize inflated ones in the final reward calculation.

One such strategy to calculate would be to fine-tune a LLM with past issue threads and the corresponding time estimates to make time estimate predictions, and use this for calculation. Before we start fine-tuning, we would need a good corpus of issue threads, with at least 250 to 300 clean examples. 

-  #82 

Once this is done, we should be able to build the fine-tuned model.

I_kwDOLcmjKM6Y0b0d.title: Refactor `publicAccessControl`
I_kwDOLcmjKM6Y0b0d.body:
I realize that contributors cant add labels unless there is an issue template that allows them to create an issue and select labels when creating issues, but this is an unusual scenario that projects need to go out of their way for. 

- Remove all references to `publicAccessControl.setLabel`
- Refactor `publicAccessControl` to only be a boolean called: `fundContributorClosedIssue`, default is false.

https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/assistive-pricing/blob/9984131a66eb9167dd0f60147a99e41ae382c43b/src/types/plugin-input.ts#L23-L29

### Note

The reason why `fundContributorClosedIssue` exists is because if: 
1. an outside party files an issue
2. we fund it
3. self assign

Then they can mark the issue closed as completed using the GitHub UI (because they created the issue) which makes an easy attack vector. 
###### Similar [^01^]

- "(Medium) p1"
- "(High) p2"

This in turn would easily allow us to check for pricing attempts with outdated tags, like when we remove priorities for example.

I_kwDOLcmjKM6C0-oI.body:
Currently, the TypeScript types that are generated by Supabase are committed in the repository. It might be a better practice to generate them on a build step. This would give some benefits:
- less likely to merge conflict between contributors
- types always up to date on a build, which would fail compilation if they changed

The drawback would be that for contributors who do not have a Service Role Key, they would only be able to generate the schema locally.

The expected fix would be to have a `prebuild` step that generates the types properly.

Refers to https://github.com/ubiquibot/assistive-pricing/pull/1#discussion_r1529509069

## Overview

- If we add @ubiquity-os-simulant as a collaborator then they can really pretend to be like a normal team member. 
- My vision is that the human user watching the demo could act as "the manager"
- What this means is that @ubiquity-os-simulant can file the issue, and set a time label as we do in our culture at Ubiquity.
- Then we can write a comment as @ubiquity-os-simulant saying "Can you please set a priority label?" 
- Once the priority label is set, they can self assign `/start` and proceed with the script. 

## Requirements

This would require the demo.ubq.fi client to be able to 
1. invite @ubiquity-os-simulant and 
2. the @ubiquity-os-simulant immediately accepting invitations (listen to invite webhook?)

Based on the research below, we may need a simple Cloudflare Worker that has the PAT, and we can hit its endpoint from demo.ubq.fi to let it know that a new repository was just created and the configuration was pushed by the user. 

Then the simulant can open the issue, and send back its completion status to the demo.ubq.fi UI to render the button to start the demo. 

## Deliverables

- Cloudflare Worker backend that protects PAT exposure from dao.ubq.fi user. 
   - We send the owner/repository that was created and the worker should be able to accept the invite with the PAT, file the issue, and set the time label. 
- Changes to this UI to send an invite 
- Changes to `/demo` to listen to the `Price: ` label being set so it can `/start`
   - If another label other than `Price: ` or `Priority: ` set, it can complain and say "No, you should assign a Priority level so the pricing is set!"

> 	1.	Get pending invitations:

> 
> 	2.	Accept an invitation (if pending):

I_kwDONLx-s86uN9u5.title: Octokit helper methods
I_kwDONLx-s86uN9u5.body:
We are using two GraphQL queries for fetching linked issues and fetching linked PRs so the code gets duplicated in each plugin that needs it. 

I think this is helpful for a couple of reasons:
- No duplication of code
- Less bugs because currently each repo have its own implementation (daemon-pull-reviewer's implementation was typed wrongly causing a bug)

Octokit supports plugins which essentially add methods to the Octokit object.

octokit.helpers.getLinkedIssues({

  repo,
  prNumber
})

  owner,
  repo,
  issueNumber
})

I_kwDONLx-s86vofeJ.title: Octokit types mismatch
I_kwDONLx-s86vofeJ.body:
I've encountered an issue multiple times when writing tests that require spying on an Octokit method. The problem arises because `@octokit/rest` is not explicitly listed in `package.json` but is installed indirectly via `plugin-sdk`.

### Example:
From [this PR](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pull-review/pull/27):

```ts
import { RestEndpointMethodTypes } from "@octokit/rest";

jest.spyOn(context.octokit.rest.issues, "get").mockImplementation(
  async (params) =>
    ({
      data: {
        number: params?.issue_number,
        title: "issue",
        url: `https://github.com/${params?.owner}/${params?.repo}/issue/${params?.issue_number}`,
        body: "This is an issue",
        repository: {
          name: params?.repo,
          owner: {
            login: params?.owner,
          },
        },
      },
    }) as unknown as RestEndpointMethodTypes["issues"]["get"]["response"]
);
```

### Problem:
- The `plugin-sdk` includes `@octokit/rest` in its `package.json`, but it is only used for an empty string checker.
- The SDK actually uses a custom Octokit (`customOctokit`), which is created by attaching plugins such as `@octokit/plugin-rest-endpoint-methods` to `@octokit/core`.
- `@octokit/rest` itself is another version of Octokit that also uses `@octokit/plugin-rest-endpoint-methods`, but potentially a different version.
- This version mismatch causes type incompatibilities when trying to use `RestEndpointMethodTypes` from `@octokit/rest`.

### Proposed Solution:
1. Remove `@octokit/rest` from `plugin-sdk` entirely, or at least move it to `devDependencies` to prevent it from being installed in projects using the SDK.
2. Modify the SDK to export `RestEndpointMethodTypes` from `@octokit/plugin-rest-endpoint-methods`, ensuring that projects can use the exact same types as `customOctokit`.

This change will eliminate the type mismatch issues and make testing more consistent.

I_kwDONLx-s87ZlWUD.title: SDK configuration fetch
I_kwDONLx-s87ZlWUD.body:
We will definitely need to add that feature in the SDK because it might be used by many different plugins

_Originally posted by @gentlementlegen in https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/185#discussion_r2548671154_

It would be great to have helper functions exposed to fetch the configuration of the plugin from its current repo and organization. It should now be possible since the configuration keys are ensured to be unique.

## Features
- helping function to retrieve the repo (and if missing) org configuration
- handle both dev and prod configuration
- decode and return the populated configuration

## Post resolution actions
- update `command-start-stop` https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/185#discussion_r2563336726
- update `text-vector-embeddings`
- update `plugin-sdk`
- update the configuration files

I_kwDONLx-s87G66Ci.title: Remove `empty-string-checker` workflow
I_kwDONLx-s87G66Ci.body: Remove the deprecated workflow, add the `eslint-rule` and eventually fix empty string errors.

I_kwDONLx-s87hKjZP.title: Allow URLs to be parsed to retrieve configurations
I_kwDONLx-s87hKjZP.body:
## Feature proposal

The SDK currently recognizes the configuration of a plugin within the `yml` by assuming every item is `org/repo:workflow@config`. It is fine for now as we do not support urls within the configuration file. The feature would be that the SDK would also be able to retrieve the configuration by looking up the url corresponding to the plugin.

## Recommended approach

We should be able, given an `org/repo` combination, to get the related `manifest.json` from the plugin. Then, within that `manifest`, we can check for the `homepage_url` to retrieve the corresponding configuration, and, if missing, fallback to the `short_name`.

## What is to be implemented
 
- handle either URLs or `org/repo:workflow@branch` patterns
- properly retrieve the corresponding manifest
- use either the `homepage_url` or `short_name` against the config to retrieve the corresponding plugin config

I_kwDONLx-s87GlQAm.title: Reduce or truncate payload size to avoid GitHub API denying the call on dispatch
I_kwDONLx-s87GlQAm.body:
Sometimes plugin runs get denied because the payload is too large for GitHub API to process, resulting in a rejected run.

Example of error:
```

An error occurred while processing the plugin chain, will skip plugin {"owner":"ubiquity-os-marketplace","repo":"daemon-merging","workflowId":"compute.yml","ref":"development"} HttpError: inputs are too large. - https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflows#create-a-workflow-dispatch-event
    at fetchWrapper (file:///node_modules/.deno/@octokit+request@9.2.4/node_modules/@octokit/request/dist-bundle/index.js:122:11)
    at eventLoopTick (ext:core/01_core.js:178:7)
    at async sendRequestWithRetries (file:///node_modules/.deno/@octokit+auth-app@7.1.5/node_modules/@octokit/auth-app/dist-node/index.js:388:12)
    at async requestWithGraphqlErrorHandling (file:///node_modules/.deno/@octokit+plugin-retry@7.2.1/node_modules/@octokit/plugin-retry/dist-bundle/index.js:36:20)
    at async Job.doExecute (file:///node_modules/.deno/bottleneck@2.19.5/node_modules/bottleneck/light.js:405:18) {
  name: "HttpError",
  status: 422,
  request: {
    method: "POST",
    url: "https://api.github.com/repos/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-merging/actions/workflows/compute.yml/dispatches",
```

Which corresponds to the plugin not being called here: https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/402#issuecomment-3197860856 or even here https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/402#issuecomment-3170643373

The payload should be trucated in such case, I think the limit was around 65k characters.

I_kwDONLx-s87SHshp.title: Handle Deno running on GitHub Action environment
I_kwDONLx-s87SHshp.body:
When we are running a Deno project on a GitHub environment, Deno environment variables are unavailable (since it's not hosted in Deno) but rather GitHub environment is set. This doesn't stop the plugin from running, however on comment posting we end up with the wrong metadata being posted. Example with `@ubiquity-os/daemon-disqualifier`:

```

We can see the `undefined` values and the Deno URL instead of the GitHub url. Technically, it identifies the runtime correctly through Hono, but should actually understand that GitHub is the host.

I_kwDONLx-s87BTjlB.title: Expose the `metadata` header function
I_kwDONLx-s87BTjlB.body:
Some plugins like https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pull-review post a comment with the pull-review, which would benefit from having the metadata in the posted comment. Since the SDK does not provide a method to pull-review with a comment, it would be easier for that plugin to have the metadata function exposed so it can append it to the posted review.

I_kwDONLx-s86oPwQe.title: Handle error arrays like `AggregateError` for proper display
I_kwDONLx-s86oPwQe.body:
maybe we should also handle `AggregateError` inside the SDK to have this functionality everywhere

_Originally posted by @whilefoo in https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/133#discussion_r1936395440_
            

Multiple aggregated errors do not get displayed properly by the SDK using `postComment`, because it is an array of errors instead of a single error with a single message. Error messages should get concatenated altogether.

I_kwDONLx-s86gUok4.title: Improve Cloudflare Worker `postComment` metadata

I_kwDONLx-s86n6Rai.title: Add posting to pull-request review comment capability
I_kwDONLx-s86n6Rai.body:
The SDK should be able to post to pull-request threads. The API is a bit different for these as it should directly use `pull` from the REST API.

What happens right now:
- if "pull_request" is present in the payload, try to post to the pull-request itself
- if we wanted to post to the thread, we would need to use `octokit.rest.pulls.createReplyForReviewComment` or `createReviewComment`
- same thing goes for updating the comment that needs a different API
- maybe we could consider having an extra argument in the options to specify a pull-request comment ID

I_kwDONLx-s86dx5Jt.title: Allow for reuse of previously posted comments during a run
I_kwDONLx-s86dx5Jt.body: The SDK should allow to reuse the same comment during a run to avoid posting multiple comments about a result, like for example with `text-conversation-rewards` that posts a waiting comment during its run. This capability should be implemented within the SDK.

Within actions this is easy to get, within workers I don't think this is possible, instead we could probably use the version id? _Originally posted by @gentlementlegen in https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel/pull/169#discussion_r1818077183_

I_kwDONLx-s86hxP1q.title: Runs triggered with `KERNEL_PUBLIC_KEY` empty fail
I_kwDONLx-s86hxP1q.body:
When no `KERNEL_PUBLIC_KEY` is supplied, the runs fail saying the given key is too short. My suspicion is that the default key is not used but `""` is used instead. See this run for reference: https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pricing/actions/runs/12128570532/job/33815214041

SDKs will need to get updated across plugins as well.

I_kwDOOIWYKc7xEH8D.title: Fix command routing: ignore non-/config comments and align manifest listeners
I_kwDOOIWYKc7xEH8D.body:
## Summary
`command-config` currently posts `No editor instruction found in comment. Skipping.` even when the incoming comment is not intended for this plugin.

## Current behavior
- Plugin reacts to unrelated comments/commands.
- It posts a skip message instead of staying silent.

## Expected behavior
- Only handle explicit `/config` command invocations.
- If comment does not target `/config`, do nothing (no response comment).
- If command is not `/config`, do nothing (no response comment).

## Additional change
- Ensure `issue_comment.created` is not included in generated manifest listeners for this plugin unless explicitly needed for `/config` routing.
- Manifest/listener configuration should match the intended trigger surface to avoid noisy or accidental invocations.

## Acceptance criteria
- Non-`/config` comments no longer trigger command-config responses.
- `/config` path still works normally.
- Manifest listeners no longer include unintended events for this plugin.

Relates to ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel#320

I_kwDOOIWYKc7WA24F.title: Update plugin parser for configuration
I_kwDOOIWYKc7WA24F.body:
Due to the changes within the spec https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel/issues/54 this plugin's parser will be unable to decode the configuration properly. The parser has to be updated to match the new schema once the changes are merged.

See the file https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-config/blob/development/src/config/plugin-schema.ts for more details.

I_kwDOOIWYKc7Loem8.title: Cleanup output to avoid unexpected parsing
I_kwDOOIWYKc7Loem8.body:
The command sometimes fail due to the output having `yaml` at the start. A Guard should be added for this, the same way we did in other plugins like `text-conversation-rewards`.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ef14e8a-0a4f-4d48-91d8-dbecaac54e87)

https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/blob/e4ea1332350d7fb428daaae58991a3122ddc78c8/src/parser/content-evaluator-module.ts#L462

"No pull-request was created" should also be a warning instead of an info.

I_kwDOOIWYKc7CCvDd.title: Configurable Model
I_kwDOOIWYKc7CCvDd.body:
1. I don't see where we can configure the model: https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-config/blob/77b43214c9dba26e30f56d4bb317c9e32e2c28be/manifest.json https://command-config-development.deno.dev/manifest.json, as highlighted here: https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/.ubiquity-os/pull/23
2. We should also have the system be instructed to throw an error or notice if there's no change like what happened here.

I_kwDOOIWYKc67YLVy.title: Add user feedback on "no pull-request opened"
I_kwDOOIWYKc67YLVy.body: In some cases, no pull-request gets open by the plugin, which is an expected behavior but the user gets not feedback on the processed task. We should also probably add some "In Progress" status so the user sees that the command is running perhaps.

I_kwDOOIWYKc6uAP8J.title: `dev` config not being detected in the org
I_kwDOOIWYKc6uAP8J.body: The plugin fails to detect `dev` config in the org level. The target-builder should be fixed to handle the `dev` config targets.

I_kwDOOIWYKc67T3I-.title: Buffer is not defined
I_kwDOOIWYKc67T3I-.body:
## What happened

After adapting this plugin to Deno, it seems that it crashes during runtime with `Buffer is not defined` error.

## What was expected

Buffer import might not be the same import for Deno (see https://docs.deno.com/api/node/buffer/) so it should be fixed and run properly.

## How to reproduce

- run the /config with some command
- observe the run crash

Link to the crash logs:
https://dash.deno.com/projects/command-config-development/logs?filters=%7B%22query%22%3A%22%22%2C%22timeRangeOption%22%3A%22custom%22%2C%22recentValue%22%3A%221hour%22%2C%22customValues%22%3A%7B%22start%22%3A%222025-06-13T07%3A10%3A54.606Z%22%2C%22end%22%3A%222025-06-13T07%3A12%3A54.606Z%22%7D%2C%22logLevels%22%3A%7B%22debug%22%3Atrue%2C%22info%22%3Atrue%2C%22warning%22%3Atrue%2C%22error%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22regions%22%3A%7B%22gcp-asia-southeast1%22%3Atrue%2C%22gcp-europe-west2%22%3Atrue%2C%22gcp-europe-west3%22%3Atrue%2C%22gcp-southamerica-east1%22%3Atrue%2C%22gcp-us-east4%22%3Atrue%2C%22gcp-us-west2%22%3Atrue%7D%7D

I_kwDOOIWYKc6uDXId.body:

I_kwDOJhaJks6atZzO.title: Too Long of Partner Names Can't Sync
I_kwDOJhaJks6atZzO.body:
If the org/repo name is too long, the issue will not sync.

### Context

Based on the error messages in the log, it appears there are recurring issues with creating new GitHub issues. The main problem seems to be related to label validation. Here's a summary of the types of issues:

### Label Validation Errors:
The most common error is: 
```
"Validation Failed: {"value":"Partner: [repository name]","resource":"Label","field":"name","code":"invalid"}"
```

This occurs for various partner repositories, including:

- ubiquity/uniswap-v3-liquidity-provider-indicator
- ubiquity-os-marketplace/tet-conversation-rewards
- ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop
- ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-disqualifier

### Summary

The root cause appears to be an issue with the label names being used when creating new issues. The "Partner: [repository-name]" label format is being rejected by the GitHub API as invalid. This could be due to length restrictions, character limitations, or other label naming constraints imposed by GitHub.

# Task

I think we can safely delete this Partner label because it doesn't seem to be read anywhere.

I_kwDOJhaJks5mIe7L.title: Opt Out & Opt In
I_kwDOJhaJks5mIe7L.body:
Enable support for both "opting in" and "opting out" model on the repository-level. 
- The main issue I was inspired by right now is that I would like to be able to quickly create new repos and issues in old repos under @ubiquity without having to manually add each repo here every time. 
- I would like for us to be able to add approved partners, like us (@ubiquity) and automatically import all of their public repositories. 

`opt.json`

```json
{
    "out": [
        "ubiquity/devpool-directory",
        "ubiquity/.github"
    ],
    "in": [
        "alpha-labs-global/blockalizer",
        "uniswap/interface"
    ]
}
```

- Most partners will use `opt.in` to opt in specific repositories. 
- Special partners, including @Ubiquity will automatically sync all of their issues to the directory, and will be using `opt.out` to exclude repositories.

---

### Notice

- It is implied that we automatically import all of the repositories from the `ubiquity` organization. 
- "`ubiquity/`" can be parsed within `opt.out` as an organization name.

I_kwDOJhaJks5nWXB7.body:
We should have a filter that indicates the current assignment status of a bounty. This way, bounty hunters can filter the view for only available bounties. It could be annoying and tedious if all the bounties they are interested in handling are taken. It takes a few clicks right now to view the status of the bounty.

Proposed solutions:

1. Directly assign the assignee in the `devpool-directory` mirror of the issue. This may lead to unnecessary notifications (or not!) but it will be the most direct way to express that the bounty is taken.
2. Add a label on bounties that are currently assigned e.g. `Unavailable`

Both solutions will allow bounty hunters to filter for only available bounties.

I_kwDOIaGAy88AAAABSlVCgA.title: Keep the catalog failure notice visible during proposal edits
I_kwDOIaGAy88AAAABSlVCgA.body:
After a catalog fetch failure, the still-installed suggestion listener removes the recovery notice on the next proposal edit, leaving a disabled repository selector and issue link without any explanation.

Priority: P3 (Codex review severity).
Native review evidence: review `org` (ubiquity/.github proposal composer) on vps, cwd `/home/codex/repos/ubiquity/.github`, reviewed base `12609d2488f2`, reviewed head `b314c3ba466faa19c4caf791a463e58192f065ec`, exit 0, session `01a0c9b4-c1f4-7523-9479-8a13cb3988ad`.

Scenario: `loadRepositories()` fails, displays recovery instructions, and returns an empty array, but the proposal-edit listener remains installed. The next proposal edit calls `renderSuggestions()` with no results, which removes the failure notice. The user is left with a disabled repository selector and issue link and no indication of what went wrong or how to recover.

Acceptance:

- While the catalog is unavailable, proposal edits do not render suggestions or clear the failure notice.
- Recovery instructions remain visible until a retry or reload succeeds.
- Regression coverage simulates a failed catalog fetch followed by a proposal edit and asserts the notice is still present.

Files:

- `proposal-router/main.js:128` — proposal-edit listener that clears the notice

Related: ubiquity/.github#123 is the open parent feature request; this is a separate small recovery-path defect from the P2 issue on the same unpushed revision.

Publication note: the reviewed head `b314c3ba466faa19c4caf791a463e58192f065ec` is not pushed to GitHub; live `main` is the reviewed base `12609d2488f2`.

I_kwDOIaGAy88AAAABSlVCcA.title: Preserve explicit repository choice and title edits in the proposal router
I_kwDOIaGAy88AAAABSlVCcA.body:
The proposal router forgets an explicit repository confirmation when the user re-picks the already auto-selected value, and it can overwrite a custom title typed while the catalog request is still in flight.

Priority: P2 (Codex review severity, both findings).
Native review evidence: review `org` (ubiquity/.github proposal composer) on vps, cwd `/home/codex/repos/ubiquity/.github`, reviewed base `12609d2488f2`, reviewed head `b314c3ba466faa19c4caf791a463e58192f065ec`, exit 0, session `01a0c9b4-c1f4-7523-9479-8a13cb3988ad`.

Scenario, finding 1: the user opens the repository dropdown and chooses the already auto-selected repository. The native select emits no `change` event, so `explicitSelectionKey` stays null. Explicitly choosing the displayed payment repository and then changing the proposal text toward kernel/webhook topics silently retargets the issue to the kernel repository, breaking the promised preservation of explicit choices.

Scenario, finding 2: the catalog request is slow. The visible title field remains editable while execution is suspended before its input listener is registered. A custom title entered during that interval is not recorded as manual, and the initial `updateSuggestions()` overwrites it with `inferTitle(proposal)`.

Acceptance:

- Choosing the currently displayed repository records an explicit selection that later inference cannot override.
- Manual-title tracking is registered before the first await, or the field is disabled until initialization finishes, so a typed title survives catalog loading.
- Regression coverage exercises both the re-pick path and a title typed during a delayed catalog fetch.

Files:

- `proposal-router/main.js:10` — title listener registration after the catalog await
- `proposal-router/main.js:133-135` — explicit selection tracking

Related: ubiquity/.github#123 is the open parent feature request for the proposal router; implementing PRs #132, #133, and #134 are closed. It does not track these defects.

Publication note: the reviewed head `b314c3ba466faa19c4caf791a463e58192f065ec` is not pushed to GitHub. Live `main` is the reviewed base `12609d2488f2`, and `proposal-router/` does not exist on live main. Publish the branch or attach the patch.

I_kwDOIaGAy86RCx5m.title: DoraHacks Bounty Post
I_kwDOIaGAy86RCx5m.body:
https://dorahacks.io/daobounty
https://dorahacks.io/blog/guides/publish-a-bounty/

We are going to create a `daobounty` to post on `DoraHacks`. Essentially this will act as advertising space to a user base of 156K+ web3 centric users.

DoraHacks requires that you put up the bounty value via a transfer of the amount into an escrow pool. Since we handle payments we have a two options:

1. Ignore this completely and treat the value as an advertising fee for the space.
2. Create an actual reward pool and payout rules such as - $1,000 spread between 10 winners over the space of three months and anyone that successfully gets a PR merged in qualifies for an additional $100 on top of their task reward (handled manually).

I think two is the better option. It sticks to the rules of the platform and has legitimate payout and submission info. It further increases the incentive for newcomers and would be a healthy way to determine how successful this has been.

typically bounties are posted in a format such as:

#### intro

##### Task 1: Build a plugin

##### Task 2: Build devtools

##### Task 3: Wildcard

#### Submission Rules

---

Gnosis is not a supported network although BNB, MATIC, and a few others are but this is trivial.

With any decent traction from this it makes the xp-system evermore relevant

I_kwDOIaGAy85-pwlW.title: Command-Line Tool Totaling Contributor Rewards for UBQ Airdrop
I_kwDOIaGAy85-pwlW.body:
## Overview

We are looking to develop a command-line tool that automates the tallying of contributions across all Ubiquity repositories for the last year. This tool will play a crucial role in recognizing and rewarding our contributors' efforts through UBQ token payouts.

## Objectives

### Tally Contributions

The tool should accurately parse through all the "permits" (or payments for recognized contributions) generated across our repositories to identify and sum up each contributor's total contributions in terms of dollars earned.

### UBQ Token Calculation

Based on the dollar value of each contributor's total contributions, calculate the equivalent amount in UBQ tokens, with the conversion rate being 1 UBQ per dollar earned.

### Output Format

The results should be compiled into a comprehensive CSV file for each repository, detailing the contributors' names, total dollar earnings, and corresponding UBQ tokens. This CSV file will serve as the basis for UBQ token payouts.

### Automation and Execution
This script should be designed for easy execution at specific times, particularly when enabling UBQ token payouts to ensure a seamless distribution process.

## Requirements
- Use TypeScript for development to ensure type safety and maintainability.
- Utilize the @octokit/rest library for GitHub API interactions to fetch permits across repositories.
- Ensure the tool is executable through `tsx` to facilitate integration into our existing workflow.
- Include a testing mechanism that prints test results, which will be a critical part of the pull request QA process.

## Final Deliverables
- A fully functional command-line tool meeting the above specifications.
- Documentation on how to set up, use, and contribute to the tool.
- Test cases and results demonstrating the tool's effectiveness and accuracy.
- This tool is integral to our efforts to automate and streamline our reward system for contributors. It will not only enhance our operational efficiency but also ensure transparency and fairness in UBQ token distribution.

We look forward to seeing innovative solutions and contributions from the community to bring this project to fruition.

I_kwDOF4fVBs5mMP85.title: Low Security issue, Decrement storage slot hashes by one
I_kwDOF4fVBs5mMP85.body:
## Description 
The storage slots/hashes have known pre-images. For example [LibCreditRedemptionCalculator.sol#L29-L30](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0c240d095cae6be599e020a8a6ba4d0a5fcf51c6/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibCreditRedemptionCalculator.sol#L29-L30), [LibBondingCurve.sol#L19-L20](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0c240d095cae6be599e020a8a6ba4d0a5fcf51c6/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibBondingCurve.sol#L19-L20), there are many others instances with the same issue.

## Recommendation
Quote from [EIP-1967](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967)
> Furthermore, a -1 offset is added so the preimage of the hash cannot be known, further reducing the chances of a possible attack.

Current implementation is;
`bytes32 constant SLOT = keccak256("path.to.slot");`

Change it to:
`bytes32 constant SLOT = bytes32(uint256(keccak256("path.to.slot")) -1);`

I_kwDOF4fVBs5mQtfi.title: `call()` should be used instead of `transfer()` to transfer ether.
I_kwDOF4fVBs5mQtfi.body:
## Summary
`call()` should be used instead of `transfer()` to transfer ether.

Plase view;
- https://www.theblock.co/post/225364/zksync-unfreeze-millions-stuck

## Vulnerability Detail
The `transfer()` and `send()` functions forward a fixed amount of 2300 gas. Historically, it has often been recommended to use these functions for value transfers to guard against reentrancy attacks. However, the gas cost of EVM instructions may change significantly during hard forks which may break already deployed contract systems that make fixed assumptions about gas costs. For example. EIP 1884 broke several existing smart contracts due to a cost increase of the SLOAD instruction.

## Impact
The use of the deprecated transfer() function for an address will inevitably make the transaction fail when:

- The claimer smart contract does not implement a payable function.
- The claimer smart contract does implement a payable fallback which uses more than 2300 gas unit.
- The claimer smart contract implements a payable fallback function that needs less than 2300 gas units but is called through proxy, raising the call's gas usage above 2300.
- Additionally, using higher than 2300 gas might be mandatory for some multisig wallets.


## Code Snippet

- [UbiquiStickSale.sol#L122](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/contracts/src/ubiquistick/UbiquiStickSale.sol#L122)
- [UbiquiStickSale.sol#L128](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/contracts/src/ubiquistick/UbiquiStickSale.sol#L128)
- [LibCollectableDust.sol#L65](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibCollectableDust.sol#L65)

I_kwDOF4fVBs5rNUMQ.title: Add UI diamond hook
I_kwDOF4fVBs5rNUMQ.body:
After implementing the diamond proxy in the [contracts package](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/tree/development/packages/contracts) most of our contracts (i.e. [facets](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/tree/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets)) have the same address (which basically equals to the deployed `Diamond` contract). The only exception (regarding the address) are the [core contracts](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/tree/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/core) which should be deployed with the own upgrade mechanism because function names from the [core contracts](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/tree/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/core) overlap with the ones in the [facets](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/tree/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets) and Diamond proxy doesn't support function clashing.

So basically this code:
```typescript
const managerAddress = "0x4e037B9A8Ce977462DA4E10Fc164363C827abfc6";
const managerContract = await getUbiquityManagerContract(managerAddress, provider);
```
is the same as this one:
```typescript
const diamondAddress = '0xbe0efAbc83686a81903C1D4a2515f8111e53B5Cb';
const managerContract = await getUbiquityManagerContract(diamondAddress, provider);
```

There is the [react hook](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/dapp/components/lib/hooks/contracts/use-manager-managed.tsx) that returns all of the contract instances

We should take all of the [facets](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/tree/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets) and make sure that this [hook](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/dapp/components/lib/hooks/contracts/use-manager-managed.tsx) returns all of the contract instances (i.e. facets) by a single diamond address

We can either refactor the [existing hook](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/dapp/components/lib/hooks/contracts/use-manager-managed.tsx) or create a new one

This "return contracts" hook will be referenced in the next github issues (regarding the `dapp` package) where we will make sure, one by one, that all of the pages work fine with the diamond proxy

I_kwDOF4fVBs5c73gd.title: Deep Fuzzing on Newly Modified Solidity Files
I_kwDOF4fVBs5c73gd.body:
Random thought I had but since I [wrote that action](https://github.com/ubiquity/bounty-bot/blob/c1c6c99336f34ac5e94efaed49c9f218fb7a2d76/.github/workflows/push.yml#L36-L43) that will: 

1. read the bounty-bot repo and 
3. build if any source code changes occur, and then 
4. commit the built file to the repo 

It inspired me to think of what other compute we can delegate to the cloud to make the dev experience better. 

What if we do something similar with deep fuzzing, but only on modified Solidity files? I understand that deep fuzzing takes a lot of time, so we could run it for the entire codebase one time, and then only run it on modified Solidity files moving forward? I vaguely recall a discussion related to how deep fuzzing is super slow.

transmissions11 has a Foundry template that does a deep fuzz on everything when merged to main, which served as another point of inspiration for me.

```yml
      - name: Run tests
        run: forge test
        env:
          # Only fuzz intensely if we're running this action on a push to main or for a PR going into main:
          FOUNDRY_PROFILE: ${{ (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.base_ref == 'main') && 'intense' }}
```
https://github.com/transmissions11/foundry-template/blob/0bf8e53589f2e8f72e41baf672c25aa35ba57295/.github/workflows/tests.yml#L28-L32

I_kwDOF4fVBs5rD67G.title: Better docs
I_kwDOF4fVBs5rD67G.body:
Project documentation is pretty outdated right now.

We have 3 sources of documentation:
1. https://dao.ubq.fi (documentation for non-tech users)
2. https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/wiki (high level documentation for developers, pretty outdated)
3. solidity natspec comments

It is really time-consuming to keep all 3 doc sources relevant. We should keep at least 1 of them to be 100% relevant at all times. It is easier for bounty hunters to update docs in natspec comments compared to [wiki](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/wiki) or [notion website](https://dao.ubq.fi).

Forge has a feature of creating md docs from solidity natspec comments. If you run `forge doc --build` you will get the following [output](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/blob/feat/demo-docs/packages/contracts/docs/src/SUMMARY.md). As you can see the output docs are not really relevant/accurate. It should be fixed.

When we have pretty natspec docs we can compile them together with wiki [docs](https:// github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/wiki) and get a nice developer documentation.

What should be done:

I_kwDOF4fVBs5K9_7d.title: Proxy Yield Aggregator v1.0.0 - ERC4626 Compatible Deposit Contract
I_kwDOF4fVBs5K9_7d.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar-development/discussions/171
Originally posted by **pavlovcik** May 14, 2022 # "Bring Your Own Yield Source" For the next iteration of the Proxy Yield Aggregator (PYA) program a user should be able to bring their own [ERC4626](https://github.com/fei-protocol/ERC4626/blob/7a947f2507b760ae470578cfb106f71ff5b1a14b/src/ERC4626Router.sol) compatible yield source, and connect it to our deposit contract. This product is intended for users to be able to stack the total yield that they can receive from their favorite yield bearing sources. Upon withdrawal, the user interface should present a slider which represents risk tolerance of the user. ## Example 1. The user likes a new ERC4626 Compatible Yearn USDC vault that promises 20% APR. 1. The user "connects" the ERC4626 vault to our deposit contract. 1. Implementation details must be researched, but I hope that we can avoid a contract redeployment, a la deploying a new Uniswap market. 1. The user deposits 1000 USDC, and the USDC is immediately transferred to the underlying yield source. 1. One year later, the user seeks to withdraw their 1200 USDC, and returns to our user interface to withdraw. 1. The user interface presents a slider, which seeks to understand the user's risk/reward tolerance 1. For example, the user can withdraw with no additional risk (1200 USDC) or the user can withdraw with max risk (2400 uCR) 1. The idea is that the user can convert the USDC into our uCR for a premium 1. In exchange, the Ubiquity Dollar is able to raise collateral for the dollar in perpetuity. 1. User withdraws at "25% r/r" netting them something like 900 USDC and 900 uCR (premium curve formula to be determined) 1. "50% r/r" would be 600 USDC and 1200 uCR 1. "100% r/r" is 0 USDC and 2400 uCR 1. "16.7% r/r" is 1000 USDC and 400 uCR // I imagine that many would, in this example go here or lower in order to only convert yield, and to receive the principle back. ## Adjustable Parameters 1. uCR Premium, a math formula (default would be a linear calculation, 1 USDC -> 2 uCR) 1. This would be deployed as a separate smart contract 1. This gives us flexibility to implement exponential or logarithmic functions which may more efficiently produce our desired economic outcomes! 1. Yield token whitelist (default would be an array with the following contract addresses: USDC, DAI, LUSD) 1. The idea is that, because the user is able to bring their own yield source, we wouldn't want a situation where they give assets that we do not want (like UST) 1. Rejection should happen upon deposit, not withdrawal; in case we change our accepted assets after the user already has deposited their tokens. ## Remarks It would be very interesting to match the uCR Premium (math formula) with the bond of the associated asset. That way we are purchasing at the same price premiums ecosystem wide. As long as we're mindful of 1. the interface implementation, and 2. that we architect it so we can associate the uCR Premium PER asset, then I think we can easily share the same formula between our bonds and the PYA.

I_kwDOF4fVBs5LvX9V.title: Lootbox v1.0.0 - Cashback Rewards
I_kwDOF4fVBs5LvX9V.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar-development/discussions/158
Originally posted by **pavlovcik** May 13, 2022 # v1.0.0 - Proof of concept - Cashback on ANY NFT Purchases on OpenSea We want to increase usage of the uAD by giving people a reason to purchase NFTs with uAD. Introducting Ubiquity Credit Cashback Program, similar to credit cards! + #158 + #165 + #166 ## Overview > アレクサンダー.eth | U B I Q U I T Y: i came up with a hack to make the opensea thing work > アレクサンダー.eth | U B I Q U I T Y: > > アレクサンダー.eth | U B I Q U I T Y: so basically we modify our linkedin chrome extension (already has great infra, client side!) to modify the opensea ui > アレクサンダー.eth | U B I Q U I T Y: then we deploy one or two contracts to middle man the transaction > アレクサンダー.eth | U B I Q U I T Y: in these contracts, we take, for example, a 2.5% fee (just like a credit card/payment processor company) and then give them cashback; for example up to 10% in Ubiquity Credits (uCR) or the total of all sum fees (e.g. 2.5% OpenSea, 5% creator fee, 2.5% our processing fee) > アレクサンダー.eth | U B I Q U I T Y: this gives us a new revenue source > アレクサンダー.eth | U B I Q U I T Y: behind the scenes, we swap the ubiquity dollar for eth/weth used for the purchase and complete the opensea transaction > T Flex 👀: i wouldn’t replace the button but add another one ## Smart Contract The purpose of the "middle-man" contract would be to perform the following: 1. receive the user's uAD 1. set aside uCR valued at 10% of this uAD amount 1. for security reasons, we should top up this contract manually with uCR 1. check now for the NFT price, and what asset the NFT is priced in (WETH, ETH, DAI, USDC?) and if the uAD amount is valued at 102.5% of the NFT price, not including slippage on the uAD swap. 1. we should automatically handle choosing and swapping for the correct purchase asset as an extra convenience for the user 1. swap for ETH using the user's uAD (this should be valued at 102.5%+ of the NFT price) 1. purchase NFT with 97.5%, and keep 2.5% of the purchase amount, in the swapped for asset, e.g. ETH 1. send back NFT + uCR "cashback" to user ### Setters We should be able to set the following variables 1. transaction fee (default at 2.5%) 1. cashback percentage (default at 10%) 1. account for slippage (default true) ## Remarks This gives us a reason to do a bond for uAD-ETH and grow its liquidity.

I_kwDOF4fVBs5XUObI.title: DNS Hijacking UI Protection
I_kwDOF4fVBs5XUObI.body:
Perhaps a more practical solution would be to compare the UI with this repo's latest `production` commit. 

There might be a means to hash the entire UI codebase and match the hash with some request on the frontend. This probably requires just a little bit more research before creating this bounty, but I think this is a relatively simple to implement layer of protection because this repository is open sourced.

> Since DNS hijacking is on the rise (we've seen it recently with the curve.fi UI being compromised) an idea would be to have a badge on the UI that does an ajax request to get the commit hash of the current instance (`uad.ubq.fi`) and compare with the other deployments (`netlify.ubq.fi`, `fleek.ubq.fi`, `cloudflare.ubq.fi`) 

> This would require a compromise of all UI deployments simultaneously to thwart this detection.

> If there's any difference then we can get the user's attention and explain that something is fishy and to be aware of any new approvals!

I_kwDOF4fVBs5ZgIDM.title: `uCR-NFT` ⮕ `uCR` Conversion
I_kwDOF4fVBs5ZgIDM.body:
Allow users to convert Ubiquity Credit NFTs to Ubiquity Credits (fungible).

Depends on #115 (we need to know the redemption rate of `1 uCR` for `? uAD` as it has less redemption power over time)

## Background

- We know that uCR-NFT is always worth 1 uAD
- We know how much uAD is 1 uCR worth at any given point in time
  - Depends on #115
- We know what duration of the uCR-NFT remains in percentage

## Math
 
 ```
(1 uCR-NFT) * (Remaining duration %) * (uCR/uAD conversion rate)
```

> Example:
> 
> 10 000 uCR-NFT with a total duration of 6 months has been around for 4 months, so they have 33% duration remaining.
> uCR/uAD redemption rate is 1.5
> So the user can get: 10 000 * 33% * 1.5 = 4 950 uCR (which is currently worth 3300 uAD)

_Originally posted by @hpiyankov in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/105#issuecomment-1115346883_
      
## Note

In #112 it is emphasized where to implement this function

> Right now if you convert uCR-NFT to uCR with the CreditManager you get a 1-1 conversion, no > mater how close the uCR-NFT token is to expiring. While if expired does not allow you to > convert at all.
> 
> The relevant function is burnCreditNftsForCredits
> 
> What needs to happen
> Using the CreditClock we should consider the price of the uAD-uAD-equivalent of the uCR-NFT > amount (right now it converts 1-1) (this means dividing it by the CreditClock > creditRateAtBlockNumber, the result should be a higher amount of uCR (because it's devalued))
> At mint time the conversion should be 100%
> At expiration time the conversion should be 0%
> In between we lower it linearly using the expiration time

I_kwDOF4fVBs5I6sOL.title: `uCR -> uAD` official exchange rate contract "DebtClock"
I_kwDOF4fVBs5I6sOL.body:
We need a new contract that helps us calculate the uAR deprecation rate.

Details about the math available on [\[0094-UBQY\] uAR simple calc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12gGDjRw4s1TRH4mT9v3yb_TFnFDKfzKgTjTfIKtoAMM/edit)

### Policy

The R value is determined by policy and the latest policy is that `The depreciation rate of uAD is defined in such a way, that at the time of uDEBT expiration, UAR is worth 70%`

The formula to get R is the following:

`(1+R)^(blockCountIn30Days) = 1/valueAfter30Days`
`R = (1/valueAfter30Days)^(1/blockCountIn30Days)-1`

So let's say we have 194.404 blocks in 30 days. And our valueAfter30Days is 0.7 (70%):

`(1+R)^(194404) = 1/0.7`
`R = (1/0.7)^(1/194404)-1 = 0.000001835`

But we don't need to know this for the contract, we just get the R value directly.


### Context

So the initial spec of the DebtClock called for a rate that can be updated multiple times. It called for storing the block the rate is updated and the rate itself; this way we can calculate the price of uAR for any block.

However, Ben mentioned that over time, as we update the rate and the array keeps getting longer, this can cause issues with the maximum gas fees. To prevent this we'll be removing the possibility to calculate the uAR price for any block, we will only be able to get the price for any block onward since the rate was last changed; older rates won't be stored.

### Customizable Variables

**.ratePerBlock**

This is the deprecatio rate. How much uAD is deprecated on each block.

Ex: 0.05 = 5% deprecation per block

**.rateStartBlock**

This is the block height from where we start applying the rate. Before this start block we won't have price information.

**.rateStartValue**

This is the exchange rate of uAR for the start block.

### Methods

**.setRatePerBlock(ratePerBlock)**

- Should set the `ratePerBlock`
- Should set the `rateStartValue` to the current rate value before it's changed
- Should set `rateStartBlock` to the current block height
- Should be only callable by admin

**.rate(blockNumber)**

- Should return the amount of uAR you would get for 1 uAD at the specific block number.
- If blockNumber isn't given then use the current block number.
- Require that blockNumber is less than **`rateStartBlock`**

### Rate math

```tsx
rateStartValue * ( 1 / ( (1 + ratePerBlock) ^ (blockNumber - rateStartBlock) ) )
```




## To be used on:

- DebtCouponManager: Adjust the uAR minting and burning to the rate
- YieldProxy: Adjust the uAR reward minting to the rate

I_kwDOF4fVBs5WIRbI.title: Optimize pre-commit hook
I_kwDOF4fVBs5WIRbI.body:
In order to keep development workflow clean and without delays, commits should be fairly thin in terms of checks. Devs should be capable of rebasing their own branch locally if they need to fix anything before pushing, which can reject after many larger checks of the codebase such as spell check and lints. It may also be worthwhile to consider dropping prettier altogether, given that it is basically doing the same job as eslint. I would propose the following checklist, not necessarily in this order.

- [x] drop prettier
- [ ] shift to pre-push rather than commit
- [x] utilize workspaces
- [ ] fix [cross package ignore requirements](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/pull/318/files#diff-e7e195d3d8fa5b82fa51ed952f3a179d429cbc46c0432ce1f7b357c54c162822R6) by scoping linting appropriately

I_kwDOF4fVBs5YlLfc.body:
I did an interactive rebase and pushed to https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/tree/devsupport-org/development

I think there were a lot of unnecessary commits and I suggest that you do experimentation/research on a branch off of your main branch when working on complex features. That way, if you make changes for exploratory reasons, and eventually revert, you can drop the branch and you don't add the unnecessary commits to your PR. Unnecessary commits can make merges (or in my case, rebasing) more complex than it needs to be. 

Unfortunately the CI from my interactive rebase seems far from working and I'm not sure of the best solution here other than starting on a clean branch. 

On one hand, we technically should have revoked the bounty after week 2 (this is a 1 week bounty) but it seemed like you were making good progress. On the other hand, if we can't figure out how to solve these sort of issues, I think that our decentralized development is going to struggle to scale. 

@0xcodercrane this is the exact type of problem I was seeking to avoid when I asked you to look into merging https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/pull/351

I think we should have an all hands meeting with the other pro devs in our org to get their opinion on how to best solve this type of issue.

I_kwDOF4fVBs5WxsIe.title: Upgrade TWAP to poll data based on a controller
I_kwDOF4fVBs5WxsIe.body: The twap price we will target is an aggregation of various data sources grouped depending on their gas cost and origin, current groups are ChainLink price feeds Uma optimistic oracles Median aggregation of dexes Web3 api These data sources will be called based on market conditions. When there is not a lot of volume amount of transactions is minimum and volatility is low only the cheapest price feeds will be called, as the conditions change to a harsher, more lively market data sources will progressively be added until the twap becomes an aggregation of all possible data sources This has the purpose of making our oracle calls as efficient as possible by reducing the gas used determining the twap by reducing our set of data sources in “safer” market conditions while at the same time being able to ramp the robustness during higher volatility periods These calls will be determined by a proportional controller (this ideally will evolve into full PID in future versions) based on Volume per unit of time (daily, hourly or block based) Amount of tx per unit of time (daily, hourly or block based) The controller will work based on 3 variables, a simplified version of them is 1. Volume and tx aggregation (V), as the process variable 2. Oracle base polls (BP), as the set variable. which has 2 elements P is the actual amount of polls per unit of time B is a baseline variable, its a function that will increase or decrease overtime to change the net polls done and is affected by the third variable generated at the output, it's the feedback element of the system 3. Poll rate(R), the output variable. is the result of the V-BP proportion, it will increase P variable (the actual amount of polls) as well as the delta of B The resulting equations will be then V-BP=R, since the controller always wants to be at 0 and V is what where measuring then; R=BP, as B is an independent function of time only P can be changed as a result of an R change In this simplified example when volume rises the difference between the base polls (BP) and volume (V) increases causing the poll rate (R) to increase, since the controller always wants to be at 0 the net polls (P) increase As the difference goes back to 0 due to base polls increasing in tandem with volume the baseline (B) increases as an effect of the R increase allowing the net polls go down while the baseline stays the same, as this new volume is deemed “new normal” When volume decreases P has to go down to bring the difference back to 0, as R is a negative number. This negative R causes B to also go down over time, increasing the net polls after given amount of time Baseline function This will change what the controller defines as “normal volume” , a simple way to see it is in an unit of time the controller wants it to be the equal to R By example “it should go from 1 to 3 in a week” Contract structure The current contract structure is based on the way I design electronics, this means it will probably be shit in some aspects, for a more exact spec look at RAI controller contracts an individual contract for each individual data source, in this version that means 4 Individual interfaces to normalize the data sources to a common format for the controller to read, another 4 A controller contract This puts the total to 9 in this current iteration

I_kwDOF4fVBs5U1WCg.body:
# Ubiquity Card

![Image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4975670/196578548-8bea6201-df66-44a9-b7ef-65328de3840b.png)

Low priority, but I'm very curious about how easy it is to launch a card (Visa claims its pretty easy.) I would be really keen to use it myself, so I'm sure over time after adding enough features I would personally want, we could probably commercialize it. In the near-to-mid-term, we could simply gate access to UbiquiStick holders.

https://partner.visa.com/site/programs/fintech-program.html

Still need to apply (waiting on some paperwork from incorporation document holding company)

# Features of Interest

## Ubiquity Credit (uCR) Cashback Rewards Program
1. Rewards program to incentivize usage
2. We should be earning like 1-2% on purchases directly afaik, 
    1. Meaning we can take this money to back the dollar (meaning uCR should become more liquid)
3. We could model it off of Starbucks' wildly successful rewards program and even simulate "expiring stars" with uCR-NFT

## Automatic loans via Liquity/MakerDAO
1. Covers small and short term liquidity crunches for when you're out and don't want to rehypothecate funds on chain to buy something    
2. You stake $1000 in some liquid Ubiquity asset (uAD, UBQ)        
    1. Curious to know if we should put it in a vault to make yield, or if staking uAD is good enough.
3. You deposit $1000 into your Ubiquity checking account (uAD, and maybe USDC/DAI/USDT)

I_kwDOF4fVBs5LvbE3.title: `uCR` & `UBQ` Economy-Wide "Risk Premium"
I_kwDOF4fVBs5LvbE3.body:
## Overview
### Objective
- The purpose of this smart contract is to allow talent to convert their cash (intended for base payroll) into uCR and/or UBQ.

### Benefits
- We can incentivize talent to leave cash equivalents (e.g. USDC/DAI) with us to reduce our burn rate.
- We can skip negotiating the `uCR`/`UBQ` compensation with talent during the hiring process and have them handle it permissionlessly via this contract.

## Specification

The contract should...

- be pausable.
- be manually topped up with UBQ and uCR for security reasons.
- have a token acceptance whitelist (we can start with USDC, DAI, LUSD)
- have a risk premium getter/setter for UBQ
- - this should be defined as a separate smart contract to allow for algorithmic risk premium
- have a risk premium getter/setter for uCR
- - this should be defined as a separate smart contract to allow for algorithmic risk premium
- automatically transfers to the Ubiquity Treasury

### Draft Contact Methods

```solidity
setTreasuryAddress(address treasuryCalculator) onlyTreasury // treasuryCalculator should query the [manager contract](https://etherscan.io/address/0x4DA97a8b831C345dBe6d16FF7432DF2b7b776d98) for the address of the treasury
getTreasuryAddress() returns (address)

setGovernanceTokenAddress(address tokenAddress) onlyTreasury
setGovernanceTokenRiskPremium(address riskPremiumCalculator) onlyTreasury
getGovernanceTokenRiskPremium() returns (uint256)

setCreditTokenAddress(address tokenAddress) onlyTreasury
setCreditTokenRiskPremium(address riskPremiumCalculator) onlyTreasury
getCreditTokenRiskPremium() returns (uint256)

depositForGovernanceTokens(uint256 amount) pauseable // transfers UBQ to caller; transfers deposit to treasury.
depositForCreditTokens(uint256 amount) pauseable // transfers uCR to caller; transfers deposit to treasury.

freeze() onlyTreasury // pauses all
```

## Context

I was thinking we could assign an economy wide "risk premium" for uCR. This can represent the rate we pay it out. e.g. 

"2" means `2 uCR` = `1 USDC`
"1.5" means `1.5 uCR` = `1 USDC`

(This also can apply for UBQ.)

- I think it makes sense to think in these terms because now that it is a full blown bear market, perhaps the risk premium should be something higher, like "5"

- Would be amazing to set at the smart contract level, that way the talent we pay out can decide on their own how much they want to gamble. They could, for example, be always paid the base rate of USDC/DAI, but then have the ability to deposit into the smart contract to mint uCR. If the risk premium is 5, then $1000 of USDC will mint 5000 uCR.

- This way we no longer have to negotiate this, as the worker can decide how much risk they want on the fly.

- Theoretically we could do the same for UBQ.

### Algorithmic Risk Premium (UBQ)

Another interesting idea is to algorithmically define the risk premium by calculating ETH price from the peak. 
If ETH peak price was the following according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum):

All-Time High
`$4,878.26` -76.0%
Nov 10, 2021 (7 months)

Ethereum Price
`$1,168.76`

`4878.26 / 1168.76 = 4.1738765872`

Risk premium could be `4.1738765872` for `UBQ`. 

I think the risk premium for alts should be a function of the entire market. I also think that UBQ risk premium should consider the UBQ market price (Uniswap etc) although this is more exploitable due to its smaller liquidity compared to ETH

### Algorithmic Risk Premium (uCR)

This should be a function of the TWAP and consider how often we go above peg. 

- The idea is that if we're constantly above peg, and uCR is redeemable most of the time; a reasonable person should conclude that the risk (and its associated premium) should be lower for holding uCR.
- If we're in a situation like we have been, where its been a long time since uCR has been redeemable, then its risk premium should go much higher!

MDU6SXNzdWUxMjIzMzQ4NTI3.title: [CONTRACTS] - Implement Debt Cycle Timeout Condition
MDU6SXNzdWUxMjIzMzQ4NTI3.body:
Ubiquity's algorithmic dollar is not epoch-based, but is built around arbitrarily long or short debt cycles which adaptively modify the stabilization algorithms at play. Currently, the length of debt cycles depends on the TWAP crossing $1, whether decreasing or increasing in price. Because of this, the debt cycle can - in theory - never actually complete, or continue for an arbitrarily long enough time that would ultimately lead to destabilizing downstream effects on the protocol.

Although the epoch-less nature of the protocol offers many potential upsides with respect to adaptively dynamic algorithms acting on an effectively 'continuous' basis. However, the fact that debt cycles are arbitrarily long entails potential stability issues with respect to the debt algorithms that requires the debt cycles to end in order to trigger.

A design for a debt cycle timeout condition should be identified and implemented which would both rectify this potential stability vulnerability, while also respecting the epoch-less and continuous nature of Ubiquity's protocol.

MDU6SXNzdWUxMjIzMzQ4OTQ0.title: [CONTRACTS] - Integrate or Create Keepers/Oracle Service to Replace Static blockCountInAWeek Estimate for Bonding Durations
MDU6SXNzdWUxMjIzMzQ4OTQ0.body:
Currently, bonding deposit times are being estimated using a static value:
`uint256 public blockCountInAWeek = 45361;`
See: https://github.com/ubiquity/uad-contracts/blob/main/contracts/Bonding.sol#L27

While unlikely, the value associated with the number of blocks verified over the period of one week can be subject to sudden change, and will at the least entail some small degree of drift over time. 

Once the DAO's governance rollout is complete, the time needed to make decisions to change code to the protocol's smart contracts may increase, creating a potential vulnerability in the protocol in cases of extreme discontinuous change in the rate blocks are being verified. 

A Keeper or similar oracle service, whether integrated externally or implemented by us, would allow us to update the contract with accurate and reliable external-time based triggers or notifications, side-stepping the issue of having to estimate the block verification rate and modify its hard-coded constant value via governance voting.

I_kwDOF4fVBs5H9UkD.body:
Right now the APY is calculated without compounding taken into account.

Right now it's calculated like this:

```ts
const apy = (reward.toNumber() / 1_000_000_000 / 5) * 365 * 100;
```

We gotta calculate it as if we compounded it every 5 days instead.

## Overview

Vercel fails to build when deploying. When we refactored everything into a monorepo we also significantly automated the build process. Unfortunately this new build process does not seem to work for Vercel.

## Findings

* Please login to the @ubiquity-vercel account, then login to Vercel in order to access our staging environment.
* Vercel is programmed to run `yarn run vercel-build` automatically; so I hooked in a debugging script for this task `./build-scripts/vercel-build.sh`
* This debugging script replicates the build process, but in series instead of in parallel to make it easier to see what's happening.
* I suggest you debug the build process by editing this shell script, and directly pushing to the `@ubiquity-vercel/ubiquity-dollar-staging` repository.

[19:20:27.730] error Command "hardhat" not found.

I_kwDOF4fVBs5H3OZ3.title: Allow users to explicitly manage their ERC20 tokens allowances
I_kwDOF4fVBs5H3OZ3.body:
Right now most of our contracts ask for the specific allowance needed for the transactions to be done.
Some advocate for setting infinite allowance; others for what we are doing right now. [Both have their pros and cons.](https://kalis.me/unlimited-erc20-allowances/)

So I suggest we allow users to set the allowance themselves (allow them to set to infinity if they want); and maybe even build an UI so they can see the allowances they've got with each of our contracts (and allow them to revoke the allowance too).
