I_kwDOJOvPRM5oBL0Q.title: Thales/snx grant
I_kwDOJOvPRM5oBL0Q.body:
## GitHub Sports

Using Thales and their already existing betting infrastructure from overnight markets we can increase the amount of options developers have and to earn from and give traditional non tech users access to web3 biggest sport. Development

## Betting Formats

 - How much time will this bounty take?
	 >In this format Developers can bet on how long an individual bounty will take, effectively turning the developer community into an oracle where the estimated time will be a weighed average

	This will take into account 2 factors
			1) Developer reputation or ELO, the more bounties done in time or less the Higher
			2)Bettor ELO, the more bounties correctly guessed the bigger the ELO

	### This creates the following scenarios
	

 - Good ELO hunter does Bounty in a bit less time than than estimated
	 >This probably means the hunter is good/has solved similar issues in the past allowing him to solve this quickly and the time estimate was correct
	 
	-	This leads to an ELO increase for the hunter and he gets the extra money from completing the bounty earlier as his incentive 
	-	The bettors who estimated improperly get rekt and the money gets distributed to the ones who did estimate correctly 
	-	The ELO of the Bettors gets affected accordingly
	-	we can study the possibility of the house (us) getting a cut from the betting pool to cover our "losses" caused by paying extra to the hunter 

 - Good ELO hunter does Bounty in More time than than estimated but not excessive (like a 1 week estimate took 1.5 weeks or something)
	> This Probably means despite the hunter being a good dev he didn't get there in time due to the time given was unrealistic

	 -  The ELO of the hunter remains the same (increasing elo would mean giving good hunters incentives to being late)
	 - Bettors who estimated improperly get sligly rekt and the money gets distributed to the ones who did estimate correctly (the time the good dev took)
	 - The ELO of the Bettors gets affected accordingly
	 - The money that was destined for the "house" in the above case goes to the hunter to cover him getting underpaid (this can lead to disproportionate comp compared to what he would've gotten incentivizing good hunters to "hunt" unreasonable timelines
	 -  in this scenario if its obvious the hunter didn't perform as expected and tried to exploit this rule he gets treated like the case below 


- Good ELO hunter does Bounty in a lot More time than than estimated (1 week bounty took >2 weeks)
	> This Probably means despite the hunter being a good dev he got lazy
	 
	 - The ELO of the hunter drops a lot 
	 - Bettors who estimated closer to the grace period get the most money 
	 - The ELO of the Bettors gets affected accordingly with the monetary rewards
	 - House gets a small cut

- Good ELO hunter does Bounty in a lot less time than than estimated 
	> This means the timeline was a bit generous or the hunter is just too good, doesnt seem fair to punish people too hard in this scenario
	 
	 -	This leads to an bigger ELO increase for the hunter and he gets the extra money from completing the bounty earlier as his incentive 
	-	The bettors who estimated improperly get rekt and the money gets distributed to the ones who did estimate correctly but a small amount less than expected
	-	The ELO of the Bettors gets affected accordingly
	-	house takes a smaller/No cut that and more money is given to the hunter

- Bad ELO hunter does Bounty in considerably less time than than estimated
	> This probably means the estimated time was so overkill a bad developer managed to beat it 
	
	-	This leads to an big ELO increase for the hunter and he gets the extra money from completing the bounty earlier as his incentive 
	-	The bettors who estimated improperly get rekt and the money gets and the ones who did estimate correctly smaller portion (bets ticks earlier can be given more money as that would be closer to the real time)
	-	The ELO of the Bettors gets affected accordingly in a harsher way
	-	House takes a bigger cut


- Bad ELO hunter does Bounty by a bit less less time than than estimated
	> This probably means the estimated time was so overkill a bad developer managed to beat it 
	
	-	This leads to an ELO increase for the hunter and he gets the extra money from completing the bounty earlier as his incentive 
	-	The bettors who estimated improperly get rekt and the money gets and the ones who did estimate correctly smaller portion (bets a few ticks earlier can be given more money as that would be closer to the real time)
	-	The ELO of the Bettors gets affected accordingly in a harsher way
	- House cut up by a small margin

- Bad ELO hunter does Bounty in more time than than estimated but not way more
	>This probably means the estimate was accurate 
	
	- ELO of the hunter drops
	- bettors get their money and ELO as expected
	- house gets a smaller cut

- Bad ELO hunter does Bounty in way more time than than estimated 
	>This probably means the estimate was a bit unrealistic because even someone "bad" didn't manage to get there in time 
	
	- ELO of the hunter drops
	- bettors get their money and ELO as expected with rewards skewed at the longer end
	- house gets the normal cut

- any ELO hunter completes the bounty in the expected Time 
	>estimate was accurate

	- ELO of the hunter increases
	- Bettor get the expected amount of money/ELO
	- House takes its cut



## General Reasoning/Potential issues/Random things
1) Implement the "tennis game logic" between bettors and hunters 
2) Reward good hunters with perks like the essential "grace period" they get but also punishing them way harsher for doing a bad job to prevent resting on laurels 
3) Having bad ELO can be dodge by just making another account so it will probably be a bad idea but its a starting point
4) we will need data to get the correct standard deviation to calculate things like "this one was off for like 2-3 days"
5) punish bettors for overpaying/giving too much time and incentivize reputable hunters to find rushed and unrealistic deadlines
6) House cuts mean extra revenue source to help make the devpool itself free of fees for partners 


## Gauntlet style bets (essentially a normal sports tournament parley 
 
 Another Popular type of bounty is the "free for all" where developers (or teams) compete for the best solution to a problem, in this scenario people can bet on who will win, this format has the advantage that normal people can participate as the track record of hunters can be used to bet on who will win 

This format con be extended to a full style sports tournamet where we do either bracket style matches or publish a set of free for alls and people can bet on who will win in batches 

## example of additional formats available for eveyone
1) bet on who will be at the top of the leatherboard
2) bet on who will complete the most bounties
3) bet on who will have claimed the most amount of money
4) bet on who will the biggest perfect streak//less time than expected

I also want to highlight Rune (founder's) vision for additional context: 
1. https://twitter.com/RuneKek/status/1656731619753852951
2. https://forum.makerdao.com/t/the-5-phases-of-endgame/20830

He wants AI to be used in facilitation, not decision making, which makes sense. 

> This is an important point and something that is core to the design. The key will be to not have AI actually “run” governance, but just use it as a redundant assistant tool that is especially optimized to help participants that are more on the periphery of the ecosystem, and aren’t necessarily able to spend full time diving into the deep nuances of Maker Governance. With Governance AI Tools they have a chance to find out what’s going on, and be directed towards which areas they should be focusing because there is more critical data or controversy. Ultimately, in case of significant internal failure the Governance AI Tool may alert outsiders to wrongdoing or negligence by insiders that are operating within areas that would normally be completely obscured due to complexity, so they enable a lot more parallelization and specialization without putting governance security at risk.
> 
> Actual decisions should be done by domain experts, primarily the Advisory Council Members, but AI tools can be a massive productivity boost by helping them dealing with paperwork, reporting, and formatting everything correctly according to the Alignment Artifact data structure, so they can focus just on being subject matter experts and don’t have to wrangle with governance complexity.
> 
> False positives can be dealt with by ensuring that the AI tools are never relied on as the source for any decision, but that they simply help with automating boring work or paperwork, and are used to get suggestions for where to direct attention or how to learn about an advanced concept. 

[Source](https://forum.makerdao.com/t/the-5-phases-of-endgame/20830/5)

I_kwDOUS-HkM8AAAABX_sn0w.title: Accept the ai.ubq.fi #1162 interface change in the VPS release bridge
I_kwDOUS-HkM8AAAABX_sn0w.body:
ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1162, which fixes ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1146, was merged as [`6c3afe42`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1). It makes the pinned driver's import graph loadable by Deno. That satisfies the "the driver offers a Deno-loadable lock" option in #150's acceptance.

It also adds host requirements for the bridge that neither #150 nor #161 records, and it leaves release preparation Bun-only. The ai.ubq.fi side of that gap is tracked in ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1178.

## What changed

| | Before #1162 (ai.ubq.fi `9f98f131`) | After #1162 (`6c3afe42`) |
|---|---|---|
| Driver import graph | `ops/vps-release-journal.ts` imports `ops/deploy-lock.ts`, whose line 2 imports `bun:ffi`. `ops/io.ts` runs commands through `Bun.spawn`. Deno fails with `Unsupported scheme "bun"`. | No module reachable from `ops/vps-release-driver.ts`, `ops/vps-release-metrics.ts` or `ops/vps-metrics-storage.ts` names a `bun:` module. The Bun FFI lock moved to `ops/deploy-lock-bun.ts`. It loads through a URL-built dynamic import, and only when `globalThis.Bun` is defined. |
| Deploy lock ([`ops/deploy-lock.ts:11-47`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/deploy-lock.ts#L11-L47)), taken by `withVpsDeployLock` for every driver operation and for each `createVpsJoinFileStorage` load and save | Bun FFI `flock` | On Deno it uses `Deno.open` and `FsFile.tryLockSync(true)`: the same `flock(LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB)`, polled every 100 ms with a 240 s deadline. The lock file must be mode `0600` and owned by `Deno.uid()`, so the host needs `--allow-sys=uid` plus read and write on `<root>/.data`. Without `--allow-sys=uid`, every acquisition throws `NotCapable` and no operation runs. It also needs a Deno that has `FsFile.tryLockSync` (verified on 2.9.7). |
| Command runner: `runVpsCommand` ([`ops/vps-release-driver.ts:44`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-driver.ts#L44)), which goes through `command` and `runOutput` ([`ops/io.ts:98-120`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/io.ts#L98-L120)) | `Bun.spawn` | `Deno.Command` on Deno, which needs `--allow-run`. The normal runner needs no env grant. Sparse mode, used only by release preparation, reads `PATH`. |
| Release payload preparation | Bun-only | Still Bun-only. On Deno, `prepare` for a candidate not already under `.data/releases/<sha>` throws `ReferenceError: Bun is not defined`. The only way around it is a bridge-supplied `preparePayload` that avoids `Bun.version`, and ai.ubq.fi has none yet (ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1178, item 1). |
| Ingress helpers | `ops/deploy.ts` | Moved unchanged to `ops/vps-ingress.ts`, except that `ensureCaddyIngressReady` lost its default arguments. |

One more requirement predates #1162. `runVpsJournalCommand` ([`ops/vps-journal-reader.ts:113`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-journal-reader.ts#L113)) spawns through `node:child_process`, and Deno's implementation of it reads `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` even when the child gets an explicit `env`. I checked with Deno 2.9.7. With only `--allow-run`, an `execFile` call throws `NotCapable: Requires env access to "NODE_V8_COVERAGE"`. Adding `--allow-env=NODE_V8_COVERAGE` lets it run.

## Sentinel files involved

I checked these with `git grep` on `development` (`87e28fd4`) and on the #150 branch `origin/codex/master-plan-gfa795549e5` (`8e34ff6f`):
- `src/host/vps-release.ts:291` on `development` and `:389` on the #150 branch call `createVpsDeploymentDriver({...})` without `preparePayload`. The driver therefore falls back to the Bun-only `prepareReleasePayload`.
- Nothing imports `ops/deploy.ts`, `ops/vps-ingress.ts` or `ops/deploy-lock*.ts`, and nothing names `ensureCaddyIngressReady`, so the ingress move needs no change here. `src/release/vps-port.ts` hashes the whole pinned release tree, so the two new files need no list update.
- No file in this repository sets the bridge's Deno permission flags. The forced command is installed by the owner (`ops/vps-release-bridge.ts:1`), so the permission changes are an installation step, not a code change.

## Impact

Nothing is broken live today. `sentinel-release` is disabled, and the bridge's pinned driver is `21e4a2a9`.

Once the driver is re-pinned at or after `6c3afe42`, these are the risks:
- **Permissions.** Without `--allow-sys=uid`, every locked driver operation and every metrics checkpoint load or save fails with `NotCapable`, so every VPS release is refused. Without `--allow-env=NODE_V8_COVERAGE`, journal reads fail, so metrics cannot sample.
- **Preparation.** Every release whose candidate is not already under `.data/releases/<sha>` is refused at `prepare`. This lasts until a Deno-safe `preparePayload` exists and the bridge passes it.

## Acceptance

- The bridge host grants:
  - `--allow-sys=uid`;
  - `--allow-run`;
  - read and write on the target root's `.data`;
  - `--allow-env=NODE_V8_COVERAGE`, plus `PATH` if it uses sparse preparation.

  It also runs a Deno that has `FsFile.tryLockSync`.
- Once ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1178 item 1 provides a Deno-safe `preparePayload`, the bridge passes it to `createVpsDeploymentDriver`. Until then, record that releases can only be driven for candidates already prepared on the VPS.
- The interface pin test asked for in #150 also loads and exercises the pinned driver under the exact Deno permissions the bridge host uses. Then a missing grant fails CI instead of failing at release time.
- Land this together with #150 and #161.

I_kwDOLUK0B86kwXFE.title: Flesch-Kincaid Clarity Module
I_kwDOLUK0B86kwXFE.body:
> We are exploring methods to evaluate comment readability and conciseness using **Flesch-Kincaid** readability metrics. These formulas assess the complexity and clarity of text based on sentence length and word syllables:

> 1. **Flesch Reading Ease:** Rates text on a scale from 0 (difficult) to 100 (easy). Scores can help determine how easily a comment can be understood.

> These metrics can help us identify verbose comments vs. concise, high-value inputs

This seems a lot more interesting compared to word count but we should test. 

_Originally posted by @0x4007 in https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/97#issuecomment-2363145914_
            
We can use an npm package to do most of the work, but I think that tweaking the weighting of the output of this module might take time to get right, which is why I made the time 4 hours instead of something like 1 hour. 

As an extension of this, if it is successful, then we can consider removing word counting from the scoring criteria, and instead use the amount of html tags as a proxy for comment length. 

For example, a comment with many list items, images, and links is more likely to be "longer" than a comment without. This may place the emphasis on higher Flesch Reading Ease (more easily understandable) and useful elements (images, links) vs writing verbose comments with low information density etc.

I_kwDOLUK0B86lXrPR.title: Implement retry mechanism for LLM failures
I_kwDOLUK0B86lXrPR.body:
I would like to do that, but the endpoint is changeable so if another API is used (I know that shiv recommended others) the return code of the API can differ (and actually the return code of OpenAPI doesn't indicate that the comment is too long as far as I remember, just a failure) and parsing the error message feels unreliable.

See error code 429: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/error-codes

_Originally posted by @gentlementlegen in https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/pull/225#discussion_r1903285110_
            

## Description

Currently if the LLM fails, we throw and abort the run completely, which cancels all the rewards and results, and needs a new run to be triggered afterwards. While some errors are not recoverable, the ones like us sending too many tokens to be handled can be avoided by splitting the prompt and retrying with a smaller prompt until it fits with the given model.

## Needed changes

We should implement:
- a retry mechanism which, on errors that are not fatal, would give another try with the LLM
- covering cases like the token amount sent being too large, responses having truncated JSON content, network failures
- post a message saying the results are being retried
- set a failure limit
- throw in the end if every try is unsecessfull
- add related tests

I_kwDOLUK0B86e9fo7.title: Assignee Timestamp Based Comment Crediting
I_kwDOLUK0B86e9fo7.body:
We don't reward assignees for their comments because it's too easy to game this. 

We need to be more precise (right now we allow for rewards on the issue, just not on pull) and check the timestamp of the comments they made. 

They should receive rewards for their comments while they are not the assignee, and should not receive rewards while they are the assignee. 

We should cross reference the assignment events (and their associated unassigned events) and then measure every comment and determine whether it was while they are the assignee and while they are not. We should then credit accordingly. 

This should support the edge case of being assigned and unassigned multiple times. 

I wonder if it makes sense to blanket and just check for the first assignment time and the last unassignment time and exclude rewarding comments from between. It would simplify logic and it may also prevent gamification. 

https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/175#issuecomment-2481300459_

I_kwDOLUK0B86P9cUz.title: Add symbol coefficient and make html tags configurable per target group
I_kwDOLUK0B86P9cUz.body:
> I do not know what `symbols` represent as we don't have that.

I am not sure what the clearest way to express this is, but the idea is that we have "word count" currently. I figured a generalized way to approach this was to target symbols instead. 

The way that we count the amount of words is by counting the spaces. 

Extending this logic, I figured we could credit sentences by assigning value to punctuation (`!`, `.` etc)

We can credit paragraphs by assigning value to double line breaks (`\n\n`)

Do you see where I am going with this?

---

Perhaps it makes sense to use regex notation instead in the config:

```yml
...
  symbols:
    "\s": 0.1 # word counter
    "\.": 0.5 # sentence counter
    "!": 0.5 # sentence counter
    "\?": 0.5 # sentence counter
    "\n\n": 1 # paragraph counter
```

---

I am mostly happy with this config syntax because it allows us to fairly clearly express, and finely adjust the incentives.

```yml
select: [ PULL_AUTHOR, PULL_SPECIFICATION ]
  html:
    a: 5
    h1: 1
  symbols: 
    spaces: 0.1 # implies words?

select: [ ISSUE_AUTHOR, ISSUE_CONTRIBUTOR, PULL_CONTRIBUTOR ]
  html:
    a: 5
    h1: 1
  symbols: 
    " ": 0.1 # implies words?
    ".": 0.5
    "!": 0.5
```

_Originally posted by @0x4007 in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-config/pull/18#discussion_r1680319560_

I_kwDOLUK0B86CZnbv.title: Make this work - version one
I_kwDOLUK0B86CZnbv.body:
## Context

Implement a mechanism to reward contributors based on their comments by evaluating:
- **Word count** as a `quantitative` metric, focusing on content formatting.
- **Relevance** to the topic as outlined in the issue specification, marked as `qualitative`[^1].
- **Clarity** of articulation, ensuring comments are easily understandable[^2].

Exclude:
- Comments from bots.
- Bot commands, identified by syntax like `/wallet 0x...`.

Due to architectural changes, avoid generating permits in this module. Determine an appropriate return value to pass to the kernel for subsequent handling, aiming for:
1. A final permit generation interface formatted as `Record<Username, string>`, e.g., `{ "pavlovcik": "50" }`[^3].
2. Inclusion of reward amount metadata to transparently explain the rationale behind each reward[^4].

## Score Calculation

The final score is a product of the three metrics: `quantitative (sum)` * `qualitative` * `clarity`. Word counts are adjusted by element type, excluding blockquotes.

## Scope

Transition from the monolithic `ubiquibot` to a kernel-plugin structure, addressing:
- Migration and reimplementation of conversation rewards logic.
- Integration of "data aggregation" for activity related to issues and pull requests.
- Reward calculations based on `quantitative`, `qualitative`, and `clarity` evaluations.
- Display of scoring metrics in a detailed manner as in the current [reward comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/issues/26#issuecomment-1996890295).

## Requirements

- Achieve 80%+ code coverage with Jest tests.
- Ensure scoring configurability, with initial hardcoding acceptable.
- Define the kernel-plugin interface, focusing on core logic testing independently of the kernel.
- Develop a method for returning structured data conducive to HTML table formatting by another plugin for comprehensive reward displays.

## Remarks

- Main entry point of old version. https://github.com/ubiquibot/comment-incentives/blob/main/src/handlers/issue/issue-closed.ts
- You can see I tried classifying contributor types for the sake of our config. At a high level we had four contributor main types: assignee, issuer (the issue author) collaborator (somebody added to the team) and contributor (default)
- We also need to be able to configure the scoring for all of those classes, and also, the scoring of commenting on the issue or the pull request. I think my mistake the first time around was collecting each of these individually then scoring. This time around I'm collecting everything at once, and then I think it makes sense to classify and score.


[^1]: Previous implementation used GPT-3.5 to assess how on-topic each comment is, assigning a float score accordingly.
[^2]: Clarity evaluation may involve GPT-3.5 or GPT-4 for assessing the clearness of a comment's meaning or summarizing key points from verbose contributions.
[^3]: Permit generation focuses on specifying an amount and the corresponding wallet address, without concerning itself with the underlying metadata.
[^4]: Consideration for a dedicated permit generation module that solely manages permit details to minimize the attack surface area.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_sWdA.title: Follow-up from #1162 (issue #1146): make release preparation work under the Deno bridge, catch Bun globals in the bridge graph, and stop the Deno lock following a final link
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_sWdA.body:
PR #1162 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1162) fixed #1146 and was merged as [`6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1). The merged head, `71658ec5`, is the reviewed head `9ecc552e` with `development` (`b24353e5`) merged in, and its tree is identical to the clean merge of those two. The review found no P0 or P1 problem. It left one P2 and three P3 findings. Three are filed here and one was dropped (see the end).

Line references are to the merge commit. No file under `ops/` has changed on `development` since then (tip `0d726874`). I re-checked each finding against that code, using real Deno 2.9.7 for the runtime checks.

None of this affects production today: `sentinel-release` is disabled, and Sentinel's bridge still pins driver `21e4a2a9`. These findings start to matter once the bridge is re-pinned to a revision at or after `6c3afe42` (ubiquity/sentinel#150). The Sentinel-side requirements that #1162 adds are tracked in ubiquity/sentinel#162.

## 1. P2: under the Deno bridge, the driver still cannot prepare a new release

**Where:**
- [`ops/vps-release-driver.ts:144`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-driver.ts#L144) `prepare` calls `checkedRelease(binding.revision, true)` at [`:188`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-driver.ts#L188).
- [`ops/vps-release-store.ts:148-162`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-store.ts#L148-L162): `checkedRelease` calls `expectedRelease(sha, !present)`. That reaches `_prepareBunPayload` at [`:122`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-store.ts#L122) and [`:131-137`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-store.ts#L131-L137).
- [`ops/vps-release-store.ts:52`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-store.ts#L52): the default `_preparePayload` is `prepareReleasePayload`.
- [`ops/release-artifact.ts:105`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/release-artifact.ts#L105) asserts `Bun.version === "1.4.0"`. [`:124`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/release-artifact.ts#L124) runs `process.execPath install`.
- [`ops/vps-release-store.ts:28-37`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-store.ts#L28-L37): `bindPreparedVpsPayload`, the only other `VpsPayloadPreparation` factory for normal releases, also ends in `prepareReleasePayload` (`:37`).

**Problem:** #1146 covered the lock, the journal and the runner, and #1162 fixed those. Release payload preparation is still Bun-only.

Sentinel's bridge builds the driver without `preparePayload` (sentinel `development` `87e28fd4`, `src/host/vps-release.ts:291`), so the store falls back to `prepareReleasePayload`.

The "Known limitations" section of #1162 says this fails closed "unless the bridge passes the existing `preparePayload` capability". In fact no Deno-safe preparation exists: `bindPreparedVpsPayload` reaches the same `Bun.version` check. The cutover's `reuseCutoverPayload` only reuses a captured cutover artifact, so it does not help normal releases.

**Failure scenario:** after a re-pin, a Sentinel VPS release whose candidate is not already under `.data/releases/<sha>` reaches `prepareReleasePayload`, which throws `ReferenceError: Bun is not defined`.

I checked this on `development` `0d726874` with `deno run --no-config --no-lock --allow-read`. The store's default preparation is `prepareReleasePayload`, and calling it throws exactly that error. The release is refused before it writes anything, so this is safe. But end-to-end Sentinel VPS releases stay blocked.

Removing the version check alone would not fix it. Under Deno, `process.execPath` is the Deno binary, so `install --frozen-lockfile` would run the wrong tool.

**Suggested fix:** export a Deno-safe `VpsPayloadPreparation` for the bridge that never evaluates `Bun.version` in the calling runtime. One way: run the pinned Bun runtime as a subprocess through `runOutput`. Locate it with `selectedRuntime`/`runtimePath` from `ops/bun-runtime.ts`, check it with `verifyRuntimeBinary`, and run it on `ops/release-artifact.ts prepare <release> <sha> <archive>` (the CLI at `:184-194`). Then extend `ops/tests/vps-bridge-host.test.ts` to exercise the prepare path with no `Bun` global. Sentinel then passes this as `preparePayload`.

## 2. P3: the bridge-graph guard catches `bun:` imports but not `Bun.*` globals

**Where:** [`ops/tests/vps-bridge-host.test.ts:18-19`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/tests/vps-bridge-host.test.ts#L18-L19) (`MODULE_SPECIFIER`, and `BUN_ONLY = /["']bun:/`) and [`:45-50`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/tests/vps-bridge-host.test.ts#L45-L50) (the graph test).

**Problem:** the in-repo guard copies Sentinel's gate, which only refuses a file that names a `bun:` module. Nothing checks a path the Deno bridge evaluates for a `Bun.*` global such as `Bun.spawn`, `Bun.sleep`, `Bun.file` or `Bun.version`.

**Failure scenario:** this gap is already live on `development`. Walking the three bridge entries the same way the test does reaches 18 files. Four `Bun.` references turn up:
- `ops/io.ts:59`, inside `spawnBun`, which only runs when `globalThis.Bun` is defined;
- `scripts/build-native-kv.ts:74` and `:116`, reached only through a type-only import;
- `ops/release-artifact.ts:105`, which is item 1 and does throw under Deno.

The guard and Sentinel's gate both pass anyway. A later change that adds, say, `await Bun.sleep(100)` to `ops/vps-release-journal.ts` or `ops/vps-ingress.ts` would pass both checks too. It would then fail only at release time on the Deno host.

**Suggested fix:** in the same test, also flag `\bBun\.` in every reached module. Keep an explicit allowlist for host-selected branches (`ops/io.ts` `spawnBun`) and type-only edges, and remove the `release-artifact.ts` entry once item 1 lands. Alternatively, run the lock, journal, runner and prepare paths in a test with `globalThis.Bun` hidden, or under Deno in CI.

## 3. P3: the Deno lock follows a final-component link when it opens

**Where:** [`ops/deploy-lock.ts:12`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/deploy-lock.ts#L12) (`deno.open(path, { write: true, create: true, mode: 0o600 })`), which is checked after the open at [`:14-25`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/deploy-lock.ts#L14-L25). The `lstat` before the open is in `withVpsDeployLock`, [`ops/vps-release-journal.ts:69-75`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/6c3afe42cc2399c9496da7eec47328b6ae3cbaf1/ops/vps-release-journal.ts#L69-L75).

**Problem:** `Deno.open` has no `O_NOFOLLOW`. A link swapped in between `withVpsDeployLock`'s `lstat` and the open is followed. Only the inode and `lstat` comparison after the open refuses it. The Bun host opens with `O_NOFOLLOW` and never follows the link.

**Failure scenario:** a process running as the same owner, with write access to the `0700` `.data` directory, replaces `.data/deploy.lock` with a link during that window. I measured this on Linux with Deno 2.9.7, calling `acquireDenoDeployLock(Deno, link)` directly to stand in for the race:
- **Link to an existing owner file:** Deno opens the target for writing, without truncating it or changing its contents. It then refuses with "Deployment lock is not a private owned regular file".
- **Dangling link:** the open fails with `ENOENT` and no file is created. The review expected an empty `0600` file at the target in this case. That did not happen on this Deno version, but the outcome depends on Deno's own behaviour, not on this code.

The attacker already has the owner's rights, the lock is refused, and exclusion is unchanged. So this is hardening only.

**Suggested fix (optional):** make the final component impossible to follow. For example, create the file first with `node:fs` `openSync(path, O_CREAT | O_WRONLY | O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)` and close it (first check that Deno's `node:fs` passes `O_NOFOLLOW` through). Then call `Deno.open` without `create` and keep the inode check. Or record the residual window as accepted in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.

## Dropped

- **Review P3: the #1162 PR description does not use the house-style closing lines.** This concerns the PR's description, not code on `development`, and the PR is already merged, so there is nothing to change in the repository. The commit trailers are correct.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_p-cA.title: Follow-up from #1156 (issue #1132): track the two owner-only items it closed over, and tighten the live-relay docs and runner test
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_p-cA.body:
PR #1156 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1156) fixed issue #1132. It was merged from head `57bbd2f1` in commit 0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e). This issue collects the review findings from that PR that still apply on development.

All line numbers are at the merge commit `0d726874`, which is also the current development tip. The review found nothing at P0 or P1.

## 1. Two owner-only items from #1132 are now tracked nowhere (P2)

**Where.**
- [`docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md:178`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md#L178) says the hard cap was "declined by the owner on 2026-10-16 (issue #139)".
- [`scripts/test-network.ts:150-152`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-network.ts#L150-L152) and [`README.md:24`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/README.md?plain=1#L24): a Darwin live run refuses every non-loopback `BASE_URL`, including the default `https://ai.ubq.fi`.

**Problem.** #1156's `Resolves #1132` closed #1132 as completed on merge (2026-10-18 01:56Z). Only an owner can act on two of its items, and #1156 listed both only under Known limitations in its PR body:
- **#1073 item 2.** The retention doc cites a decline by the owner on 2026-10-16 in #139. That decline is recorded nowhere: #139 has only bot comments, and `docs/DECISIONS.md` has no entry for #139 or the hard cap. #139 is still closed as "completed", but no eviction was built.
- **#1077 item 2.** On macOS, live e2e can reach only a host-loopback `BASE_URL`. The default `https://ai.ubq.fi` fails closed at validation. #1077 left a scoped CONNECT relay (or similar) for non-loopback destinations as an owner decision.

**Failure scenario.** Now that #1132 is closed, these items appear only in a merged PR's description. A reader who follows the retention doc's "(issue #139)" citation finds no decline, and #139's "completed" close reason suggests eviction was built. No open issue asks for the macOS decision, so it is never made.

**Suggested fix.**
- Owner: record the 2026-10-16 decline, either in a comment on #139 or in a short dated `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry. Optionally, change #139's close reason to "not planned".
- Owner: decide on non-loopback live e2e for macOS. Either accept the limit (`README.md:24` already describes it), or open a task for a destination-scoped CONNECT relay.
- No code change is needed until the owner decides.

## 2. No test checks that the runner's main loop wraps each file in `withLiveRelayParent` (P3)

**Where.**
- [`scripts/test-runner.ts:308`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-runner.ts#L308): `main()` calls `withLiveRelayParent(item.policy, (policy) => runFile(...))`.
- The helper is at [`scripts/test-runner.ts:174-182`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-runner.ts#L174-L182).
- The SIGKILL test at [`tests/live-network-policy.test.ts:93-129`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/tests/live-network-policy.test.ts#L93-L129) calls the helper directly. No other test imports `scripts/test-runner.ts`.

**Problem.** The test proves that the helper removes a SIGKILLed relay's directory. Nothing proves that `main()` sends each live file through the helper. The review confirmed that a mutation dropping `relayParent` inside the helper fails the test, but a `main()` that bypasses the helper does not.

**Failure scenario.** A later refactor of `main()` goes back to calling `runFile(file.path, item, ...)` directly, and every test stays green. From then on, a live relay killed by timeout escalation, CI cancellation or the OOM killer leaves its `uos-live-*` directory in `TMPDIR`, as it did before #1156.

**Suggested fix.** Use either of these:
- Move the per-file loop out of `main()` into an exported function that takes `runFile` as a parameter. Test it with a stub `runFile` and a live policy, and assert two things: the policy the stub receives has a `relayParent` named `uos-live-run-*`, and that directory is gone after the call returns.
- Run the `e2e` segment against a loopback fixture gateway, SIGKILL the relay in the middle of a file, and assert that no `uos-live-run-*` entry remains in the run's `TMPDIR`.

## 3. The README overstates how isolated the Linux live relay is (P3)

**Where.**
- [`README.md:24`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/README.md?plain=1#L24) says the run uses "a destination-scoped relay that serves only the run's own namespace".
- The actual mechanism is at [`scripts/test-network.ts:170-175`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-network.ts#L170-L175) and [`:233-237`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/scripts/test-network.ts#L233-L237). The host-side relay accepts only streams that start with the per-run key. The forwarder inside the namespace reads the key from fd 3 and puts it in front of every stream it forwards.

**Problem.** The relay serves anything that reaches the key-holding forwarder, not only the run's namespace. A same-user host process can join the run's namespaces and use the forwarder. No document in the repository names this limit. #1156 named only the ptrace limit, and only in its PR body.

**Failure scenario.**
1. A same-user host process opens `/proc/<forwarder pid>/ns/user` and `ns/net`. That needs only `PTRACE_MODE_READ`, which Yama `ptrace_scope=1` does not restrict.
2. As owner of the child user namespace, the process holds `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` there. It can `setns` into the namespace (for example `nsenter -t <pid> -U -n --preserve-credentials`) and connect to the forwarder's listener.
3. The forwarder adds the key, and the stream reaches the approved destination.

This is the same class of limit as ptrace. It does not reopen the threat #1077 fixed: a deterministic test child of another run sits in a sibling user, pid and mount namespace and cannot do this.

**Suggested fix.** Reword the README to "a destination-scoped relay that serves only the run's key-holding forwarder". Then list both namespace entry (`setns` through `/proc/<pid>/ns`) and ptrace by a same-user host process as known limits, in the README or in the relay comment at `scripts/test-network.ts:170-175`.

## 4. The terminal handoff still points to the old name of the narration correction (P3)

**Where.**
- [`docs/handoff/gateway-terminal-truthfulness-handoff-2026-09-21.md:36`](``https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/docs/handoff/gateway-terminal-truthfulness-handoff-2026-09-21.md?plain=1#L36)`` says "the measurement-artifact correction in `docs/DECISIONS.md`".
- [`:47-48`](```https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/docs/handoff/gateway-terminal-truthfulness-handoff-2026-09-21.md?plain=1#L47-L48)``` say "the qualified measurement-artifact correction".
- #1156 renamed the target heading to "CORRECTION: the narration symptom counts are unverified - 2026-09-21" ([`docs/DECISIONS.md:1172`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/0d7268741f5c61abe6ad493aa00ee93ffb21a60e/docs/DECISIONS.md?plain=1#L1172)). The old name now appears only in a quotation at `:1183`.

**Problem.** Both pointers in the handoff name a heading that no longer exists.

**Failure scenario.** A reader searches `docs/DECISIONS.md` for the name the handoff uses. They find it only inside the quoted old heading in the 2026-10-16 qualification note ("CORRECTION: the narration symptom was itself a measurement artifact"), not as a section heading. No anchor link breaks.

**Suggested fix.** In both places, name the new heading: `See "CORRECTION: the narration symptom counts are unverified - 2026-09-21" in docs/DECISIONS.md`. #602 and #605 cover other parts of the same handoff, so all three can be fixed in one pass.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_Nr0A.title: Follow-up from #1161 (issue #1129): catch credentials split across brief log items, and tighten the new redaction rules
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABX_Nr0A.body:
PR #1161 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1161), which fixed #1129, merged as https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/2c7f1378de16d3d3927ac087cbeb1254dd4a8fc0. Its review found no P0 or P1 issues and CI was green on the reviewed head `452b88c4`, so it merged. The review left the four findings in sections 1 to 4 open. Sections 5 and 6 are two gaps from the PR's own Known limitations that are worth fixing.

I checked each one against development at `b24353e5`. `src/codex/supervisor-brief.ts` and `src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts` have not changed since the merge, so the line numbers at the merge commit `2c7f1378` are also current. I reran every example below with Bun on that code. The "before" results come from the merge's first parent, `2c47de19`. All six items still apply.

## 1. P2: a credential split across two log items now reaches the summarizer

**Where:**
- `src/codex/supervisor-brief.ts:510`: `redactedField` redacts each recorded value on its own.
- `src/codex/supervisor-brief.ts:512-517` (`describeTurn`) and `:519-550` (`buildSupervisorBriefPrompt`): these build the prompt from those values, and the assembled prompt is no longer redacted as a whole.
- `src/codex/supervisor-brief.ts:348` and `:422`: each item was already redacted on its own during assembly.
- `src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:16`: the private-key pattern needs both the BEGIN line and the END line in the same text.

**Problem:** #1129 asked that the prompt-level pass stop running its bracketed reading across the prompt's framing. #1161 removed the prompt-level pass entirely. Before the merge, that pass ran over the joined log, so it still caught a credential split across two adjacent items. Now each item is redacted alone, and a half that matches no rule by itself goes out in the clear.

The PR's Known limitations says: "The same was true of a credential split across two items before, because each item was already redacted on its own." That is not correct. Before the merge, the whole-prompt pass redacted all three cases below.

**Failure scenario:** a tool's output is split across two rollout-tail items, as happens with `exec_command` and `write_stdin` chunks. Each case below is two items of type `tool` run through `buildSupervisorBriefPrompt`.
- (a) Item 1 is `tool output: -----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\nb3Bl…` and item 2 is `tool output: QyNT…\n-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----`. Before: the log held `tool output: [redacted]`. Now: the whole key body is in the prompt.
- (b) Item 1 is `{"api_keys": ["zqfirstsecretvalue", ` and item 2 is `"zqsecondsecretvalue"]} done`. Before: both values were redacted. Now: `"zqsecondsecretvalue"]} done` is in the prompt.
- (c) Item 1 is `password: "zqfirsthalf` and item 2 is `zqsecondhalf" done`. Before: `[redacted] done`. Now: `zqsecondhalf" done` is in the prompt.

This is rare, because a credential has to straddle two records.

**Suggested fix:**
- (a) Run only the bounded rules over the joined `<session_log>` body, never over the framing. Those are the lazy PEM pattern and the closed quoted or bracketed values. An unclosed value then cannot swallow the framing, which was the #1129 bug.
- (b) Alternatively, in each item, redact an unterminated `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----` through the end of the item, and redact a leading body that ends in `-----END … PRIVATE KEY-----` from the start of the item. This covers only case (a); cases (b) and (c) still need option (a).
- Add a `buildSupervisorBriefPrompt` test for each two-item case above.

## 2. P3: backtick quoting changed the JSON/Python reading instead of adding a new one

**Where:** `src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:127` (`opensString`), and the quote readings at `:92-99`.

**Problem:** #1161 made a backtick open a string in reading 0, the JSON, Python and JavaScript reading. Every reading's spans are kept, so adding a reading can only widen a redaction, but changing an existing one can narrow it. Reading 0 can now end a value earlier than before, even with no apostrophe after a word. The PR says every difference from development comes from the apostrophe change. This is a second source.

**Failure scenario:** this input gave `[redacted]` before the merge and gives `[redacted]E ` now:

```
tokens: [`A 'B \'C `D ]E 
```

The review exhaustively enumerated every structure of up to 5 symbols after `tokens: [`, `{"api_keys": [` and `api_key: {a: `. It found 8 such cases per prefix in 271,452. It found none where #1161 leaves in the clear something the rules before #1122 removed.

**Suggested fix:** restore reading 0 so that a backtick is plain text there, as before. Add a fourth reading, for JavaScript, in which a backtick opens a string. Because every reading's spans are kept, this can only widen the union.

## 3. P3: the new `=>` separator matches arrow functions whose parameter is a credential word

**Where:** `src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:253-257` (`valueStarts`). The key pattern is at `:32`.

**Problem:** #1161 accepts `=>` as a separator for PHP, Perl and Ruby. It also matches a JavaScript arrow-function parameter named `token`, `key`, `secret` and so on. The bare-value and bracketed rules then redact the rest of the callback. Nothing leaks, but code-heavy transcripts lose whole expressions. That is the same kind of context loss that #1129 item 2 set out to reduce.

**Failure scenario:**
- `const lengths = tokens.map(token => token.trim().length);` becomes `const lengths = tokens.map([redacted]`.
- `apiKeys.forEach(key => {\n  const label = describe(key);\n  console.log(label);\n});\nnext();` becomes `apiKeys.forEach([redacted]);\nnext();`.

Before the merge, both were left unchanged.

**Suggested fix:** accept `=>` only after a quoted key (`"api_key" =>`, `'password' =>`) or a Ruby symbol key (`:api_key =>`). Another option is to reject it when the key directly follows `(` or `,`, which is parameter position. Add both examples above as tests that must come back unchanged.

## 4. P3: `redactions` can differ from development when the redacted text is identical

**Where:** `src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:446-450`, the count returned by `redactSupervisorSecrets`.

**Problem:** the PR kept the count development reported, but it checked count parity on random strings only. On the review's structured inputs, about 0.04% of the cases with identical output text got a different count, 36 to 47 per roughly 99,000 cases per seed. The admin panel shows this count as "N secrets redacted", so the effect is cosmetic.

**Failure scenario:** this input gives `[redacted]` both before and after the merge. Before the merge it counted 1 redaction; now it counts 2.

```
a_key=>[users'ZQ0abcdZ0Q"key=[users'}ZQ1abcdefgZ1Q}, apiKeys=>{},b''password'=>'ZQ2abcdefghZ2Q'''max_tokens=>ZQ3aZ3Q
```

**Suggested fix:** no code change is needed. Note in the comment above `redactSupervisorSecrets` (`:421-436`) that the count follows the previous rules' steps and can differ by one on rare inputs. Do not switch to counting merged spans, because `tests/codex-supervisor-inventory-coverage.test.ts` expects `token=Bearer …` to count 2.

## 5. P3: a quoted key with a bare value is not redacted (pre-existing, listed in the PR)

**Where:** `src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:280`, the `if (key.quoted || value === text.length) continue;` line in `scalarValueSpans`.

**Problem:** after a quoted key, only a quoted or bracketed value is redacted, so a bare value goes out in the clear. This was already true before #1161, and the PR lists it under Known limitations. The PR did not apply the bare-value fallback here because that rule would take the rest of a compact JSON line such as `{"password":"x","model":"y"}`.

**Failure scenario:** each of these comes back unchanged, both before and after the merge:
- YAML: `"password": hunter2hunter2`
- JSON: `{"password": 12345678, "model": "m"}`
- PHP or Perl: `'password' => SECRETCONSTANT1`

**Suggested fix:** after a quoted key, when the value does not start with a quote or a bracket, redact it up to the first `,`, `}`, `]` or whitespace, and keep the 8-character minimum. The value then ends at the JSON or flow-scalar boundary, so it cannot take the rest of a compact line. Add the three examples above as tests.

## 6. P3: string prefixes that are not on the list no longer open a string

**Where:** `src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:107` (`STRING_PREFIX`) and `:116-122` (`apostropheOpensString`).

**Problem:** an apostrophe right after a word character now opens a string only after a listed Python, C or SQL prefix. Perl `q'…'` and `qq'…'`, Ruby `%q'…'` and Elixir `~s'…'` are not on the list. The scan reads their quote as text, so it can end the value at a bracket inside the string. Before the merge, development redacted these.

**Failure scenario:** `api_keys: [q'zq]alpha', 'zqbravo'] done` gave `[redacted] done` before the merge. Now it gives `[redacted] 'zqbravo'] done`, which leaves the second element in the clear. The same input with the listed prefix `b'` is still redacted whole.

**Suggested fix:** add `q`, `qq` and `s` to `STRING_PREFIX`. The pattern is already case-insensitive, so this also covers `%Q'` and `~S'`. The check reads the word right before the apostrophe, so `%q` and `~s` are read as `q` and `s`. Opening a string can only widen a redaction. Add `q'…'`, `qq'…'`, `%q'…'` and `~s'…'` as tests.

## Not included

- **The apostrophe trade-off.** An apostrophe right after a word is now read as text. So in a value whose quotes were already unbalanced, the value can end at a later bracket where development redacted through the end of the text. The PR chose this on purpose to fix #1129 item 2. The differences the review inspected were text outside a correctly closed value, which development had over-redacted. Neither the PR's fuzzing nor the review's found a case where #1161 leaves in the clear something the rules before #1122 removed.
- **CPU cost.** The redactor now takes about twice development's time: about 190 ms against 100 ms for 1 MiB. It scales linearly and runs only on the admin route `/admin/codex/supervisor/brief`.
- **The #1161 PR description.** The review also raised a P3 about the description's footer. Section 1 above corrects its "same as before" sentence. Both concern the merged PR's text, not code, so they are not separate items here.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABSlU_Sw.body:
Two P2 review defects in the benchmark fixture: a non-root candidate can leave unauthorized changes behind when permissions block the snapshot or rollback, and a shell failure during final verification escapes the adapter and aborts the whole benchmark batch.

Priority: P2 (Codex review severity, both findings).
Native review evidence: review `ai_after_gateway` (ai.ubq.fi later integrations) on mac, cwd `/Users/nv/repos/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`, reviewed base `5609fdc318bacfefd35914a66e3d4533634811d4`, reviewed head `2cc1c1c0cfc110ba9a9b89a4cec8865dc98a6893`, exit 0, session `01a0c9b9-c14c-7c91-9e87-6272539ba8f9`.

Scenario, finding 1: a non-root runner executes `chmod 000 protected/keep.txt`; the post-command snapshot throws before rollback starts. Alternatively it modifies the file and runs `chmod 500 protected`; the snapshot succeeds but `removeWorkspaceEntry()` cannot restore the file because directory modes are applied only after descendant restoration. Acceptance:

- Snapshot and rollback recover the required access permissions from saved metadata before reading or restoring affected entries.
- Permission-driven scope violations surface as `write_scope` or a failed verification outcome, never as an internal error.
- A candidate that fails final verification records its trajectory and result files and cleans up its workspace before the batch continues.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABTdqE4g.title: One failed write or health check fails the whole request
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABTdqE4g.body:
What happened

I found that a few places use Promise.all for a group of independent jobs. When one job in the group fails, the full request fails too, even when the other jobs are fine.

Where it hurts


- GET /health/providers returns 500 if only one provider check fails. It should return the rest with that one marked unknown.

- Terminal logging in src/handler/terminal-log.ts waits on five writes with one Promise.all. If one write fails, the other writes are dropped and the error comes out of logging.
- Embeddings jobs read many KV keys with one Promise.all (src/embeddings/jobs.ts). If one KV read fails, the job throws instead of going through the normal fail or queue path. Job cleanup with kv.delete has the same problem and can leave half-deleted inputs.
- Provider capacity in src/provider/capacity.ts had a catch on the metered side but not on the codex side.

What I suggest

- Keep waiting for all jobs, but let each job fail on its own. A failed KV read should count as a cache miss. A failed health check should count as unknown. Cleanup deletes should finish the rest even if one fails.
- Do not change the API shape. Only stop one failure from taking down the group.

How to check it

- Make one KV get fail while loading embeddings cache. The job should still reach failJob or queueJob, not throw.
- Make one provider health read fail. GET /health/providers should still return 200 with that provider marked unknown.
- Make one terminal log write fail. The other writes should still run.

The `/docs` Markdown renderer only recognises pipe tables that have outer delimiters, so standard pipe tables written as `Name | Value` with a `--- | ---` separator are rejected and rendered as paragraph text. `splitTableRow` already strips optional outer pipes, so the table branch is simply never reached for that valid form.

The parser gap is real and confirmed in current source, but no currently published document is affected: every table row in the served `static/docs/llms-agents.md` uses outer pipes and renders correctly, and the only pipe-bearing non-table line is prose (line 375, an endpoint list using `text-embedding-3-small|text-embedding-3-large`). This is a robustness/standards-compliance improvement for future documentation, not a live user-visible defect.

Acceptance:

- `isTableRow` accepts optional outer pipes, so `Name | Value` style rows and `--- | ---` separators are recognised as table rows.
- A table written without outer pipes renders as a `<table>` instead of paragraph text.
- Existing outer-pipe tables continue to render identically.
- A separator such as `--- | ---` is still required for the table branch to trigger, so ordinary prose containing a single `|` is not converted into a table.

Files:

- `static/docs.js` — `isTableRow` (line 76), `isTableSeparator` (lines 78-82), `splitTableRow` (lines 68-74), and the table branch (lines 199-212).

Current evidence (read-only inspection of the canonical worktree):

- `static/docs.js:76` is `/^\s*\|.*\|\s*$/`, which requires a leading and trailing pipe, so `Name | Value` and `--- | ---` do not match.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqU0iQ.title: A resumed eviction is recorded as a payload expiry
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqU0iQ.body:
## Problem
`resumeEvictingRows` (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:1265-1273`) re-derives why the row was claimed from the current clock:

```ts
const kind = victim.row.expires_at_ms <= nowMs ? "expired" : "evicted";
```

A budget eviction that claimed an unexpired capture, failed to finalize, and resumes after the payload TTL has passed is therefore written as `payload_expired` with its eviction counters omitted, even though budget cleanup removed the recording.

## Expected
Persist the claim cause on the row and use it when finalizing, instead of inferring it from the current time.

## Acceptance
A fixture that claims a victim for budget eviction, advances past its payload TTL, then resumes finalization records an eviction, not an expiry.

Source-only inspection at open PR #437 head [a7b48ff8](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/a7b48ff83847ad2de0ce45e61e6cd31ac6b54a5f) (unmerged; rechecked unchanged 2026-10-02T15:07Z). I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUuEQ.title: Orphaned staged chunks are counted as zero bytes during bootstrap

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnoACg.title: Fail an Ultra refusal over when the requested model id is spelled with different case
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnoACg.body:
## Problem

The dispatch table normalizes model ids case-insensitively — `lithosUpstreamModelFor` compares `model.trim().toLowerCase()`, so `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-ULTRA` is accepted and dispatched to the canonical Ultra model. The failover ladder does not: `lithosFailoverLadderFor(modelRaw)` is an exact-case `Map` lookup (`src/provider/lithos-rate-limits.ts:21-32`), and its callers pass the client's raw spelling (`src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts:394`, `:523-525`). A differently-cased accepted id therefore has an empty ladder, and a 429 on it is never load-balanced onto the healthy `-fast` tier.

This was originally reported by a native Codex review of PR #501 ([P2] Canonicalize the model before looking up its sibling, original cite `src/provider/lithos-rate-limits.ts:241`); the review predicted the replacement ladder lookup would retain the case-sensitive behavior, and it does at `development` `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded`.

## Acceptance

- The ladder, ladder-target check, and sticky-window lookups resolve the canonical id that dispatch already accepts.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUw-A.body:
## Problem
Publication is prepared with `now_ms: context.now` (`src/sentinel_replay_capture.ts:1802-1807`), and `publishAttemptRow` rejects only when `row.expires_at_ms <= context.nowMs` (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:632`). `context.now` is the value captured when the request started (`src/sentinel_replay_capture.ts:1905-1906`), not the current clock.

Read a fresh clock value at each lease check instead of reusing the capture timestamp.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbzPA.title: Advertised per-message forwarding bound is enforced per payload part
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbzPA.body:
## What is wrong

The catalog advertises `forwarding_policy.per_message_limit` of 65,536 bytes on the gateway-served records (`src/catalog/models.ts:225`, also `:302` and `:378`) and the recorded decision describes a per-message byte limit (`docs/DECISIONS.md:169-178`; the policy itself is `src/deepseek/forwarded-payload-policy.ts:30`, and `:19` states that the limit bounds the forwarded payload including its elision marker). Enforcement is per part, not per message: tool output and each image are measured individually (`src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:46-47` and `:176-182`), while ordinary text parts are forwarded untouched (`:26-29`) and a text-only message is collapsed to one joined string with no bound check (`:85-87`). A single 70,000-character ASCII text message, or one message with two 40 KiB image URLs, therefore travels without rejection or elision even though the callers were told the message is bounded.

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b` (`development`)
- Location: `src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:26-29` (text parts returned untouched), `:46-47` (images checked one at a time), `:85-87` (text-only message collapsed to a joined string), `:176-182` (tool output checked per item)
- Advertisement: `src/catalog/models.ts:225` (and `:302`, `:378`) with the value defined at `src/deepseek/forwarded-payload-policy.ts:30`
- Links: [text parts](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts#L26-L29), [images](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts#L46-L47), [tool output](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts#L176-L182), [advertised bound](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/catalog/models.ts#L225)

## Trigger

Replay a 70,000-character text message, or one message containing two image parts of 40 KiB each, and compare the forwarded bytes with the advertised bound.

## Acceptance

Enforce the declared bound on the assembled message (or narrow the declared field to the payload types and parts actually bounded) so the advertised contract cannot be exceeded; a focused projection test covers both examples.

## Validation

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbyDw.title: Lithos Responses requests omit the declared default reasoning effort
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbyDw.body:
## What is wrong

When a Responses request omits `reasoning.effort`, the translator leaves `chatBody.reasoning_effort` absent (`src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:494-508`, which returns early at `:500` when `reasoning` is absent and at `:503` when no effort is named). The Lithos Responses handler then computes a telemetry label that falls back to `LITHOS_DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT` (`src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts:814`) but dispatches `chatBody` unchanged (`:833`), so the vendor's own unprobed default decides the run while the catalog advertises `default_reasoning_level: "medium"` (`src/provider/lithos.ts:113`, `src/catalog/models.ts:274`). The Chat route does send the value: it applies the same declared default at `src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts:112-115` and puts `reasoning_effort` on the wire at `:572-575`, so the two wires disagree.

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b` (`development`)
- Location: `src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:494-508` (applyReasoning returns without setting `reasoning_effort` when the field is absent), `src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts:814` (telemetry label falls back to `LITHOS_DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT`) and `:833` (dispatch sends `chatBody` unchanged)
- Declared gateway default: `src/provider/lithos.ts:113` (`LITHOS_DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT = "medium"`), published at `src/catalog/models.ts:274`
- Chat-route contrast: `src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts:112-115` and `:572-575`
- Links: [translator early return](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts#L494-L508), [label fallback](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts#L814), [dispatch](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts#L833), [declared default](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/provider/lithos.ts#L113)

## Trigger

Omit `reasoning.effort` on `/v1/responses` for a Lithos model and capture the upstream body: `reasoning_effort` is missing although the label records `medium`.

## Acceptance

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUyiQ.title: Status pruning samples keys, not the oldest timestamps
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUyiQ.body:
## Problem
`statusCandidates` (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:468-489`) lists each prefix with `{ limit: STATUS_PRUNE_SCAN }` (128, `:78`) and only then sorts that subset by `captured_at_ms`. Request-status keys are keyed by request id, not by time, so the subset is a lexicographic sample.

With more than 128 rows, pruning can delete recent statuses while older rows outside the sample survive; tombstone keys have the same problem because they are keyed by fingerprint.

## Expected
Select the oldest rows by timestamp across the namespace rather than pruning a fixed key-order sample.

## Acceptance
A fixture with more than 128 status rows whose ids sort against recency verifies that the deleted set is the oldest by timestamp.

## Source

Source-only inspection at open PR #437 head [a7b48ff8](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/a7b48ff83847ad2de0ce45e61e6cd31ac6b54a5f) (unmerged; rechecked unchanged 2026-10-02T15:07Z). I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUwOA.title: Stranded reservations in the middle of the accounting prefix are never reaped
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUwOA.body:
## Problem
`reapCandidates` (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:812-824`) scans two bounded windows of the accounting prefix (oldest and newest, `limit * 4` entries each) and keeps no cursor. A revoked or expired reservation surrounded by at least 32 stored rows on either side is inside neither window.

Every maintenance pass revisits the same two windows, so the stranded charge is held until the payload TTL releases it.

## Impact
Enough stranded reservations produce `storage_full` while reclaimable capacity exists.

## Expected
Use a resumable scan that eventually visits the middle of the prefix (or a second index) rather than fixed end windows.

## Acceptance
A fixture that strands one expired reservation between many stored rows reclaims it within the configured number of maintenance passes.

## Source

Source-only inspection at open PR #437 head [a7b48ff8](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/a7b48ff83847ad2de0ce45e61e6cd31ac6b54a5f) (unmerged; rechecked unchanged 2026-10-02T15:07Z). This defect is open-head-only and is not present in development commit `dfcb8228`; it must not be assessed against development. Cited paths at that head: `src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts`. Original review: [PR #437](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/437). Source priority: P2 (repo label `Priority: 2 (Medium)`).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbreQ.title: Hovering a toast still consumes its lifetime
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbreQ.body:
## Problem
`static/toast.js:121-129` pauses on hover by clearing the timer but keeps the original absolute `deadline`. On `mouseleave` the timer resumes with `Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now())`.

Hovering therefore still consumes the notification's lifetime: a 3500 ms success toast entered after 1000 ms and hovered for 2000 ms disappears 500 ms after the pointer leaves, and hovering past the deadline dismisses it immediately on exit.

## Expected
Capture the remaining time on `mouseenter` and restart with that same remaining time on `mouseleave`.

## Acceptance
A fake-timer test that hovers past the original deadline and then leaves shows the toast surviving for the full remaining duration it had when the pointer arrived.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUvnw.title: The 50,000-record bound is neither reclaimed nor enforced atomically
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUvnw.body:
## Problem
Two related gaps in the record bound:

1. Admission refuses when `ledger.records + 1 > SENTINEL_REPLAY_MAX_RECORDS` (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:1403`), but `reclaimAdmissionCapacity` (`:1360-1364`) targets bytes only and `evictSentinelReplays` stops as soon as `ledger.stored_bytes <= target_bytes` (`:1313-1318`). With 50,000 small captures whose bytes are below the clean target, reclamation returns `false` and every new capture is answered `storage_full` until payloads expire, instead of replacing the oldest recording.
2. A reservation increments only `reserved_bytes` (`:1427-1439`), and publication increments `records` with no cap check (`:686-695`). Concurrent admissions therefore all see the same pre-cap count and can publish past the declared bound.

## Expected
Make reclamation target record-count pressure as well as bytes, and enforce the record bound atomically (reserve a record slot with the reservation, or check it in the publication commit).

## Acceptance
Approaching 50,000 stored records, one admission evicts the oldest recording and succeeds; N concurrent reservations cannot publish beyond the bound.

## Source

Source-only inspection at open PR #437 head [a7b48ff8](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/a7b48ff83847ad2de0ce45e61e6cd31ac6b54a5f) (unmerged; rechecked unchanged 2026-10-02T15:07Z). This defect is open-head-only and is not present in development commit `dfcb8228`; it must not be assessed against development. Cited paths at that head: `src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts`. Original review: [PR #437](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/437). Source priority: P2 (repo label `Priority: 2 (Medium)`).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajOsw.title: Report per-model usage across the whole waterfall (Codex-subscription traffic is not in the paid-fallback ledger)
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajOsw.body:
## Context
The quota-runway feature (PR #135) computes per-model stats exclusively from paid-fallback ledger rows (metered/surplus). Requests served by the Codex subscription path never enter the ledger, so the per-model numbers understate real model usage.

## Gap
- Model-level runtime/quota stats cover only paid spend.
- There is no per-model consumption signal for subscription-capacity runs (capacity history gives bucket-level Codex percentages, not per-model splits).
- Forecasting 'how long can we run model X' can therefore be misleading when the model mostly runs on subscription capacity.

## Proposed
Either (a) add a lightweight per-request accounting row for all routes (model, provider/route, tokens, timestamps — no upstream IDs) and extend the rollup writer to it, or (b) add route-level per-model counters at the gateway admission boundary. Aggregate into the same hourly rollup scheme so the projection can show both the paid balance runway and an 'observability' view.

## References
- PR #135 caveat section, docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajUdw.title: Measure and monitor KV storage growth for the paid-fallback ledger and rollups
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajUdw.body:
## Context
The retention design (PR #135) was sized on estimates: a settled raw row serializes to ~800 B (≈0.8 GiB per 1M rows), rollups are ~25 KB per model per day, and the admin projection reads are window-bounded. None of these numbers are measured in production, and docs/deno-usage-optimization-plan-2026-08-09.md already called for a KV operation/byte baseline.

## Gap
- No rows-per-day or bytes-per-row instrumentation for the ledger.
- No alerting when the raw-row store approaches the storage budget, so the 365-day horizon or the (future) eviction cap cannot be tuned with evidence.
- The admin projection endpoint adds periodic list reads whose real cost per 30/90-day window is unknown.

## Proposed
Add a lightweight counter/leaderboard (daily aggregates of settled rows, bytes, rollup counts; read units per admin view) exposed on the admin providers view, and a storage-growth alert threshold. Publish the measured numbers back to the design doc.

## References
- docs/deno-usage-optimization-plan-2026-08-09.md, docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md 'Follow-ups'

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABSlU_BA.title: Preserve final answers and fence follow cleanup in the supervisor transcript
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABSlU_BA.body:
Two P2 review defects in the supervisor transcript and follow path: the rollout log projection discards assistant messages whose phase is `final_answer`, and the admin follow client inspects and clears the wrong session's controller after a session switch.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnoTgw.title: Client ETag reuses the upstream validator, so a widened catalog still answers 304
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnoTgw.body:
## Confirmed defect

storeCodexCatalog stores etag = trimmedHeaderValue(input.etag) (store.ts:268) i.e. the UPSTREAM validator, while the stored bytes are the widened body (store.ts:252 body = widenCodexCatalogWindows(...) ?? input.body). catalogOnlyResponse (index.ts:52-57) sets ETag: catalog.metadata.etag and 304s on a match, and never calls the body-derived catalogBodyEtag helper defined at index.ts:48-49 (used only at index.ts:165). A client that cached the pre-warm narrow body holds that same upstream ETag, so the post-warm widened body is served as 304.

## Where

- Validated against: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded`

- Source PR: #335 (closed, merged=true), original head `37396c12786e639e1de514de01ff87162e508242`, merge `adaa36f5540a9df9e07c962057d261535cfda698`

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUu2w.body:
## Problem
`deleteClaimedVictimPayload` (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:1084-1095`) returns as soon as the manifest is missing:

```ts
const manifestEntry = await kv.get<SentinelReplayManifest>(manifestKey);
if (!isSentinelReplayManifest(manifestEntry.value)) return;
```

The stale dedupe pointer survives until its TTL, suppressing recapture of the same fingerprint or throwing when the missing evidence is bound.

## Expected
Perform the exact-reference dedupe CAS even when the manifest is already gone.

## Acceptance
A resumed cleanup after a manifest-only deletion removes the matching dedupe row and leaves a non-matching row untouched.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlZ5wQ.title: Cerebras incomplete 200 terminal still records a successful provider observation
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlZ5wQ.body:
A Cerebras HTTP 200 whose payload terminal is `response.incomplete` records an upstream_error observation and then unconditionally records success for the same HTTP 200, so the unsuccessful request advances `last_success_at_ms` and, when the two observations land in different milliseconds, replaces the latest-state classification.

## What is wrong
- `src/provider/cerebras-responses.ts:143-152` (`recordCerebrasResponsesTerminal`): a non-completed terminal records `recordCerebrasProviderHealth("upstream_error", ...)` and then always calls `recordCerebrasResponseHealth(upstreamStatus, ...)`.
- `src/provider/cerebras-handlers.ts:45-63`: `recordCerebrasResponseHealth` classifies every status below 400, including 200, as `success`.
- `src/provider/health.ts:274-304`: `latestObservation` selects by `observed_at_ms`, and `last_success_at_ms` is read from the success observation, so the failed request advances the success timestamp either way.

## Acceptance
- A terminal that is not `response.completed` records no `success` provider observation (`last_success_at_ms` unchanged, state not overwritten by the same request).

Source confirmation at development 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded: [src/provider/cerebras-responses.ts:143-152](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/provider/cerebras-responses.ts#L143), [src/provider/cerebras-handlers.ts:45-63](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/provider/cerebras-handlers.ts#L45), [src/provider/health.ts:274-304](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/provider/health.ts#L274).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABU0PR6A.title: Keep Lithos failover targets paired with their tier reset deadlines
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABU0PR6A.body:
Overlapping refusals or different tier reset times can combine the newest target with the longest deadline, redirecting requests to a refused tier or bypassing recovered capacity.

Acceptance:
- Preserve independent refused-tier deadlines and select a legal available rung without shortening an unexpired refusal window.
- Cover out-of-order overlapping refusals and reversed ultra/fast reset lengths; recovered tiers become eligible at their own resets.
- Preserve the current no-provider-fallback-on-transient-failure and bounded wait contracts.

Files: `src/provider/lithos-rate-limits.ts`

Current static evidence at `4439e8546bb74653f8eeab29bae223c3038be972`: src/provider/lithos-rate-limits.ts:35-65 stores one deadline/target pair and writes Math.max(deadlines) with the latest target. Static source support only.

Duplicate check: complete all-state inventory contains 226 of 226 issues. Closed #614 fixes shortened deadlines for a single open window; these new records concern mixing that deadline with another rung target and independent tier expiration. #613 concerns non-finite delays; #620 concerns should-retry and #616 telemetry.

Official review provenance:

PR #823; reviewed head `bf02513afe21d8036a8b266781028ed66d970602`; reviewed base `4305d2b9e5db5dc7ed84691e362042cfd3d0db0c`; review `5399909455` by `chatgpt-codex-connector` at 2026-10-03T09:11:02Z; finding `4172457389` (P2) at `src/provider/lithos-rate-limits.ts:65`. Original: https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/823#discussion_r4172457389

Original finding text (verbatim):

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the target paired with the deadline that produced it**

When requests overlap, a delayed refusal from a shallower rung can replace a deeper target while inheriting its longer deadline: request A can record fast's 60-second refusal as target base, then request B's late ultra 1-second refusal stores target fast with A's 60-second deadline. Subsequent traffic is sent to fast even though it is the tier known to be unavailable for that window, causing avoidable 429/failover churn and continuing to bypass ultra after its own reset. Keep the deeper unexpired target when retaining its deadline, or store separate per-rung windows instead of combining the maximum deadline with the latest target.

Original finding text (verbatim):

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Track reset deadlines per ladder tier**

When consecutive ladder rungs report different reset windows, combining the latest target with the maximum deadline conflates independent rate-limit buckets. For example, if `-ultra` refuses for 60 seconds and `-fast` then refuses for 1 second, this stores the normal tier until the 60-second deadline, so requests continue bypassing `-fast` for roughly 59 seconds after its bucket recovered. Preserve reset state per refused tier and select the highest-capability rung whose own window has expired.

Original: https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/840#discussion_r4172740906

Original finding text (verbatim):

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expire each Lithos tier's failover window independently**

When successive independent tiers return different reset windows, this combines the latest, deepest target with the maximum deadline. For example, if `ultra` is unavailable for 60 seconds but `fast` resets after 1 second, requests continue going directly to the base tier for the full 60 seconds instead of returning to `fast`; with the deadlines reversed, recovered `ultra` is similarly bypassed. Because the file explicitly models these as independent buckets, retain a deadline per refused rung and select the deepest tier whose predecessors are still unavailable rather than pairing one target with the longest deadline.
