I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbpOg.title: Reduced-motion toast overrides lose to the toast state selectors
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbpOg.body:
## Problem
The toast styles use `[data-toaster] > [data-toast]` (`static/style.css:1386`) and `[data-toaster] > [data-toast][data-visible]` / `[data-exiting]` (`static/style.css:1405-1414`). The `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block (`static/style.css:1468-1491`) resets the transform with a single attribute selector `[data-toast] { transform: none; }` and overrides `transition-property` on the `[data-toast]` entry in its list.

Those declarations have lower specificity than the base state rules, so a reduced-motion user still gets the slide/scale entrance at `--duration-med` and the transform-based exit transition.

## Impact
The toast surface animates in exactly the case the user asked it not to.

## Trigger
Load the console with the OS reduce-motion setting enabled and trigger any toast.

## Expected
Override the actual toast-state selectors (or raise specificity) so no transform transition or movement remains.

## Acceptance
A CSS-level test or computed-style check with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` reports `transform: none` and no transform transition on the toast node in all three states.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUwbs7w.title: Defer live Caddy reload until the deployment candidate is ready
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUwbs7w.body:
The deployment preflight reloads live Caddy before the immutable candidate is extracted, selected or restarted. A candidate ingress incompatible with the running release can therefore break public traffic during preparation, and any later failure leaves that route on the incompatible candidate configuration. Keep read-only ingress validation early and apply the live configuration only when the candidate is ready.

Acceptance:
- Permission/configuration validation fails before publishing or selecting the candidate, while preserving the currently serving ingress.
- The mutating Caddy reload occurs only after candidate preparation/selection at the safe activation boundary with gateway restart; final public and loopback release identity remain mandatory.
- A synthetic deployment fixture records validation, archive/selection, Caddy reload and restart order, and proves a preparation failure never reloads the live proxy. No production service mutation is needed to prove the code ordering.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Defer the live Caddy reload until the candidate is ready**

When a candidate changes `ops/Caddyfile` incompatibly with the currently selected release—such as the port-cutover case described above—this call executes `systemctl reload caddy` while `.data/current` and the running gateway still reference the old release. Public traffic therefore switches to the candidate ingress before archive extraction, selector replacement, or service restart; this creates an outage window, and any later failure leaves the route broken indefinitely. Keep validation here, but defer the mutating reload until the candidate has been published and can be restarted immediately.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUzfA.title: Unavailable retention accounting is rendered as an empty store
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUzfA.body:
## Problem

```js
const used = (retention.stored_bytes ?? 0) + (retention.reserved_bytes ?? 0);
```

Treat null metrics as unavailable (not zero), so the panel says the accounting cannot be read.

A payload with a corrupt ledger renders an unavailable-accounting message and never the string `0 recordings`.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnpaPw.body:
## Confirmed defect

The diagnostic builder maps messages.map((message, index) => ...) over the complete history (upstream-wire.ts:785-792) with no cap or sampling, while the request reader accepts 32 MiB bodies. The bounded upstream error-body read does not constrain this request digest, so a large history produces an unbounded log entry exactly while the provider is failing.

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded`
- Location: `src/upstream-wire.ts:785-792`

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsb1UQ.title: Single-account catalog refresh does not clear a learned model rejection
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsb1UQ.body:
A successful single-account catalog is returned directly without recording its account/model evidence (`src/models/codex-models-fetch.ts:170-181`). Recording occurs only on the multi-account union path (:348-355), so a newly advertised model cannot clear that account's earlier learned rejection through the single-account refresh. `mergeCodexAccountCatalogs` already clears advertised models from the rejection map (:108-136), but this branch does not call it.

Trigger: while a learned rejection is still valid, refresh a single account's catalog that explicitly advertises the same model. The catalog can advertise the model while routing still answers local `model_not_found`. Rejections age out after seven days (`src/models/codex-models-availability.ts:13,278-305`), so this is delayed recovery within that lifetime, not permanent exclusion.

Acceptance:
- Record successful single-account catalog evidence so explicit advertisement clears the learned rejection.
- Preserve the response body, ETag and 304 revalidation contract.
- Cover the learn-then-advertise single-account sequence with a focused regression.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaXkA.title: Local API-key quota refusal is masked as an OpenRouter upstream failure
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaXkA.body:
A local API-key quota refusal is thrown from the transport's `beforeDispatch` hook as `ApiKeyQuotaDispatchError`, but `dispatchFailure` converts every error that is not an `OpenRouterError` into 502 `openrouter_upstream_unreachable` and records an OpenRouter `upstream_error` health observation although no upstream fetch occurred, dropping the 429 and its quota headers.

## What is wrong
- `src/provider/openrouter-handlers.ts:88`: `beforeDispatch` calls `usageContext.beforeProviderDispatch?.("openrouter")`.
- `src/provider/openrouter.ts:89`: `dispatchOpenRouter` awaits that hook, so the typed error surfaces inside the transport call.
- `src/provider/openrouter-handlers.ts:72-74`: `dispatchUpstream` catches it and calls `dispatchFailure`.
- `src/provider/openrouter-handlers.ts:50-58`: the non-OpenRouter error path records `upstream_error` health and returns 502 `openrouter_upstream_unreachable`.
- `src/api-key-policy.ts:53-71,490-509`: the typed error carries the client-facing refusal and quota headers.

## Acceptance
- The typed quota error propagates unchanged, so the client receives the 429 with its quota headers and no provider-health failure is recorded for a request that never dispatched.

Source confirmation at development 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded: [src/provider/openrouter-handlers.ts:50-59,68-85,87-97](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/provider/openrouter-handlers.ts#L50), [src/provider/openrouter.ts:89](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/provider/openrouter.ts#L89), [src/api-key-policy.ts:53-71,490-509](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/api-key-policy.ts#L53).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUl6RNw.title: A later shorter refusal shortens an open failover window and reopens the saturated tier early
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUl6RNw.body:
## Original finding
- Native Codex review of PR #506, finding 1: [P2] Preserve longer unexpired failover deadlines (original cite lithos-rate-limits.ts:45-47).
- PR #506 original head f05395c2c1074c06f3f09b5071276266167ab6d5, base 4ef4a55ff57550ba32b1b94797f780f26116e2ba. Provenance: thread 01a0fc31-4e29-7a11-a446-5ebc0a299f4d / turn 01a0fc31-a2d5-7a63-be5e-000231c7345f / review result 01a0fc3f-eb86-7132-903d-5f010a82a14d (exitedReviewMode).

## Current state (verified at current upstream default)
Current development @ 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded; both files byte-identical to frozen checkout HEAD 98ccd167 (blob equality checked).
- lithosOpenFailoverWindow unconditionally replaces the stored window (lithos-rate-limits.ts:60-63: lithosFailoverWindows.set(modelRaw, { deadlineMs: nowMs + waitMs, target })).
- Every retryable refusal opens a window from its own headers (lithos-handlers.ts:324-328 lithosOpenFailoverWindowFrom, called at lines 394-395), and lithosRateLimitWait derives the advertised delay from retry-after-ms/retry-after/x-ratelimit-reset-* of that single response (lithos-rate-limits.ts:275-289).
- Nothing compares the new deadline with an existing unexpired one, so response order decides the window length.

## Trigger
1. Two Ultra requests are in flight; an older refusal advertises a 60-second reset and opens the window.
2. One second later a newer refusal with a 1-second hint is processed and overwrites the deadline with now + 1s.
3. Requests resume addressing the still-saturated Ultra tier about two seconds after the first refusal, and the tier refuses again.

## Acceptance
- Keep the later of the unexpired deadlines (or refuse to shorten an existing window) so response order cannot reopen an exhausted tier prematurely.
- Unit test: open a 60-second window, then a 1-second window, and assert the failover target is still returned after ~2 seconds and only clears after the longer deadline.

The `/docs` article element carries `aria-live="polite"` while `static/docs.js` replaces its entire contents with the fully parsed article via `innerHTML`, so assistive technology can announce the whole document on every load. - The load and error paths in `static/docs.js` update that status region rather than relying on the article's live region.
- `aria-live` is removed from `[data-docs-content]`; `aria-busy` handling continues to reflect load state.
- The successfully parsed article is not announced as a live-region update.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE2qA.title: Metered Codex catalog fallback advertises OpenRouter rows while the provider is disabled
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE2qA.body:
When the stored Codex catalog is unavailable, `meteredCatalogResponse` builds the fallback rows with `withOpenRouterModels(...)` unconditionally (it only requires an API key), so disabled OpenRouter rows are offered to Codex clients even though every inference handler refuses to route them.
## What is wrong
- `meteredCatalogResponse` computes a selection-gated `openRouterModels` value used only for the "is anything configured" test (`src/catalog/index.ts:176`, `:183`), then builds the answer with the ungated helper (`:187-191`).
- `withOpenRouterModels` appends rows whenever `readOpenRouterApiKey() !== null`, with no `isProviderEnabled("openrouter", selection)` input (`src/catalog/models.ts:454-459`, key check at `:407-409`).
- The only later narrowing is the operator whitelist (`src/catalog/index.ts:194-198`), which is a different authority and may be empty or absent.
- The Responses handler requires `isProviderEnabled("openrouter", ...)` before dispatch (`src/responses-handler.ts:806`), so a client that selects an advertised OpenRouter row gets a refusal rather than inference.
- PR #572 (merged 2026-10-02) tightened whitelist ordering on this path but deliberately left the append itself selection-ungated.
## Current evidence
- `src/catalog/index.ts:173-209` (esp. 176, 183, 187-191, 198).
- `src/catalog/models.ts:407-409`, `:454-459`.
- `src/responses-handler.ts:806`.
- Codex review: discussion_r4151102057 on PR #563 head 9531d8b81635.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnn_Uw.title: Classify OpenRouter 402 credit exhaustion as exhausted, not reachable
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnn_Uw.body:
## Problem

`recordSystemOneResponseHealth` classifies OpenRouter outcomes for `/health/providers` and the admin badge. It handles 401/403 as `auth_invalid`, 429 as `quota_exhausted`, and anything `>= 500` as `upstream_error`, but every other `>= 400` status — including **HTTP 402 for insufficient credits** — is recorded as `reachable`, which `stateForObservation()` maps to `degraded` (`src/provider/health.ts:101-110`). An exhausted OpenRouter account is therefore reported as merely degraded, and its exhaustion history is never recorded, while the same account answered 429 is reported as `exhausted`.

This was originally reported by a native Codex review of PR #557 ([P2] Classify OpenRouter credit exhaustion as exhausted, original cite `src/systemone/handlers.ts:112-115`), and the classifier is unchanged at `development` `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded`.

## Acceptance

- HTTP 402 is recorded with the paid-capacity exhaustion vocabulary (`quota_exhausted`) alongside 429, matching `recordLithosResponseHealth()`.
- `/health/providers` reports `exhausted` after a 402 and retains the exhaustion observation.
- A focused fixture asserts the same state for 402 and 429.

## Files

- `src/systemone/handlers.ts:110-128` — the classifier
- `src/provider/health.ts:101-110` — state mapping

## Provenance and evidence class

Native review thread `01a0fc52-fcaa-7cf0-9247-84452896619c` / turn `01a0fc53-565e-7c73-8a19-dedc652ec9cd`, result `01a0fc5a-6995-7b81-b63b-b2d2c51d35e2` (PR #557). I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL4pQ.title: Run the ingress preflight before publishing the release and switching .data/current
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL4pQ.body:
`ops/deploy.ts` publishes the candidate release and moves `.data/current` before it validates the Caddy ingress, so a failed preflight leaves the rejected candidate selected for the next gateway restart.

## What is wrong
- `ops/deploy.ts:109` renames the staged directory to `.data/releases/<sha>` and `:113` repoints `.data/current`; `ensureCaddyIngressReady()` runs afterwards at `:114`.
- `ensureCaddyIngressReady()` (`:46-74`) fails closed for an unreadable Caddyfile, a stopped Caddy, or an invalid composed configuration, and only `finally` releases the lock.
- The running gateway stays on the old release, but the launcher resolves `.data/current` at startup, so the next automatic restart loads the rejected candidate.
- The remedy printed at `:51` ("run `chmod 644 ops/Caddyfile` and redeploy") cannot work for the same SHA because the existing-release guard at `:96` aborts first.

## Trigger
Deploy a revision whose `ops/Caddyfile` mode hides it from the `caddy` user: the deploy aborts after `.data/current` already points at the new release, and the documented remedy fails.

## Acceptance
- Ingress preflight runs before the final release directory is created and before `.data/current` changes, or the selector is rolled back on preflight failure.
- The remedy path for a permission fault works for the same SHA, with a focused check for the abort ordering.

## Duplicate search
- Local index (`preflight`, `.data/current`, release/selector) — #263 (release configuration isolation) and unrelated entries; no issue.
- Fresh GitHub search, 2026-10-02: `repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi is:issue preflight` → no relevant issue.
- Current upstream rechecked: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` (`development`); `ops/deploy.ts` is byte-identical to the reviewed snapshot.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaH-Q.title: Sideband pre-open queue bounds frames by count only and flushes without the byte check
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaH-Q.body:
While the upstream handshake is pending, an authenticated client can enqueue 32 arbitrarily large text frames: the queue checks only frame count, and the flush that drains it bypasses the buffered-byte check. With the 4 MiB downstream payload cap and the 8 MiB buffered limit, 32 x 4 MiB retains and enqueues about 128 MiB.

## What is wrong
- `src/live/sideband.ts:143-149`: `preopenFrames.length >= LIVE_SIDEBAND_PREOPEN_MAX_FRAMES` is the only bound before `preopenFrames.push(text)`.
- `src/live/sideband.ts:151-154`: the `bufferedAmount` check exists only on the open send path.
- `src/live/sideband.ts:189-196`: the open handler flushes queued frames without any byte check.
- `src/live/upstream.ts:19-23`: 4 MiB max payload, 8 MiB buffered limit, 32 pre-open frames.

## Acceptance
- The pre-open queue enforces a cumulative byte limit (and per-frame payload limit) before retaining a frame, and the flush respects the buffered-byte limit; an oversize or over-limit client is failed closed.

Source confirmation at development 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded: [src/live/sideband.ts:139-149,151-154,186-196](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/live/sideband.ts#L139), [src/live/upstream.ts:19-23](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/live/upstream.ts#L19).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUueVfA.title: Validate metadata pruning candidates after an over-cap scan
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUueVfA.body:
Over-cap reconciliation can return before examining every candidate namespace, while metadata pruning accepts any non-null eviction object. A malformed or key-mismatched tombstone can then be deleted with an arbitrary encoded-size subtraction instead of failing closed.

Acceptance:
- Validate the key and row contract of every selected status/tombstone candidate before deletion or ledger subtraction, including candidates from namespaces not exhausted by the over-cap scan.
- A native-KV regression with an over-cap request namespace and malformed/key-mismatched eviction candidate preserves that row and the ledger charge.
- Valid over-cap data still enters bounded pruning; preserve CAS checks, hard bounds and the refusal to commit partial recount totals.

Source confirmation: both reviewed heads have identical replay-retention-metadata.ts blob 0411519254bd36c7cd35fa57f15fabb1e02ccfce. Its scan returns over_limit at line49; replay-retention.ts:150-160 accepts any eviction object and assigns a missing timestamp zero, while :179-203 prunes those candidates and subtracts their current bytes. Static source confirmation only; no tests or production operation.

Official review provenance (both P2; one duplicate defect):

PR #788; review 5398521532 by chatgpt-codex-connector[bot] at 2026-10-03T02:11:51Z; finding 4171285920 at src/sentinel/replay-retention-metadata.ts:49.

Original finding text (verbatim):

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate every prunable prefix before returning over-limit**

When the request-status prefix alone contains more than 50,000 valid rows, this return occurs before the eviction prefix is examined. `pruneCaptureOwnedStatusMetadata()` nevertheless handles `"over_limit"` by collecting candidates from both prefixes, and `statusCandidates()` accepts any non-null object from the eviction prefix; a malformed or key-mismatched eviction row (especially one without `evicted_at_ms`, which sorts first) can therefore be deleted and have its arbitrary encoded size subtracted from the ledger instead of making the operation fail closed. I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUl6RMg.title: A non-finite retry-after-ms (309+ digits) is stored as Infinity, pinning the failover window until the process restarts
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUl6RMg.body:
## Original finding
- Native Codex review of PR #506, finding 2: [P2] Reject non-finite delays before opening a failover window (original cite lithos-handlers.ts:497-499).
- PR #506 original head f05395c2c1074c06f3f09b5071276266167ab6d5, base 4ef4a55ff57550ba32b1b94797f780f26116e2ba. Provenance: thread 01a0fc31-4e29-7a11-a446-5ebc0a299f4d / turn 01a0fc31-a2d5-7a63-be5e-000231c7345f / review result 01a0fc3f-eb86-7132-903d-5f010a82a14d.

## Current state (verified at current upstream default)
Current development @ 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded; both files byte-identical to frozen checkout HEAD 98ccd167 (blob equality checked).
- lithosIntegerHeader accepts any all-digit string and converts it with Number (lithos-rate-limits.ts:215-219), so a 309+ digit value becomes Infinity.
- retry-after-ms has top precedence in lithosRateLimitWait (lithos-rate-limits.ts:277-278), and lithosOpenFailoverWindowFrom opens the sticky window with that value unchecked (lithos-handlers.ts:324-328).
- lithosOpenFailoverWindow stores deadlineMs = nowMs + waitMs (lithos-rate-limits.ts:60-63); Infinity never satisfies the expiry comparison nowMs >= window.deadlineMs (lines 49-57), so lithosFailoverTargetAt returns the sibling indefinitely.
- The 75-second cap that would have rejected the value exists only in the inline wait planner (lithos-rate-limits.ts:134, lithosRefusalWait), not on this sticky-window path.

## Trigger
1. A malformed or hostile upstream refusal supplies a numeric retry-after-ms with 309 or more digits (for example 9 repeated 310 times).
2. The gateway stores deadlineMs = Infinity for the requested tier and pins the ladder target forever.
3. Ultra requests keep being routed to the sibling tier until the process restarts, and the refusal never surfaces as a window expiry.

## Acceptance
- Reject non-finite parsed delays/deadlines before storing sticky state, while preserving the intended finite vendor reset deadline on the failover-window path.
- Unit test: an oversized numeric retry-after-ms is rejected and yields no permanent window and lithosFailoverTargetAt still expires.

## Duplicate search (fresh, 2026-10-02)
- Corpus scan (596 issues): non-finite/Infinity terms match 0 issues; retry-after-ms matches 3 issues (#500, #503, #506, the merged PRs themselves).
- Fresh GitHub search q=repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi+retry-after-ms -> 25 hits, none an issue for this defect; refuseStream -> reviewed PRs only.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbqgQ.title: Loading toasts auto-dismiss because Infinity is rejected
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbqgQ.body:
## Problem
`toast.loading` (`static/toast.js:162`) requests a persistent notification with `duration: Infinity`, but the normalization at `static/toast.js:67` is

```js
const duration = Number.isFinite(options.duration) ? Math.max(0, options.duration) : DURATION_BY_TYPE[type];
```

`Number.isFinite(Infinity)` is `false`, so the loading toast silently receives the 4000 ms info default and disappears while its operation is still pending.

## Impact
The progress notification vanishes mid-operation and the eventual result toast appears without context.

## Expected
Treat `Infinity` as "no auto-dismiss" (or have the helper use the supported zero-duration convention) instead of falling back to the per-type default.

## Acceptance
A test that calls `toast.loading`, advances the clock past 4000 ms, and asserts the node is still present until it is dismissed or updated.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsboJA.title: A pending stream flush overwrites the terminal chat message
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsboJA.body:
## Problem
`static/chat.js:906-918` schedules stream rendering through `pendingStreamFlush` (an animation frame, or a 16 ms timeout when frames are unavailable). When `streamSse` settles, `static/chat.js:942` calls `flushAssistantText()` directly; that clears `pendingStreamFlush` but does not cancel the already-registered callback.

The terminal writes then happen at `static/chat.js:944-957` (stream failure or missing completion) and `static/chat.js:969-977` (abort writes `[stopped]`). When the pending callback later runs, it overwrites that terminal text with the raw partial `assistantText`.

## Impact
A user who was told why the response was incomplete (or that it was stopped) instead sees unexplained partial output. Background tabs make this likely, because frames are deferred until the tab is visible.

## Trigger
Send a text delta and then a stream failure in the same frame, or abort a stream while a flush is queued.

## Expected
Cancel the queued frame/timeout (or make the callback a no-op once a terminal has been written) before any terminal message is rendered.

## Acceptance
A test that queues a flush, settles with a failure, then drains the frame/timeout queue shows the failure text still in place.

A bootstrapped legacy metadata store above the row cap cannot enter bounded pruning: the capped scan returns an over-limit result as a generic reconciliation failure, so the pruning caller exits without deleting any valid candidates. Preserve strict failure handling for corrupt, partial or conflicting scans while allowing over-cap stores to make bounded cleanup progress.

- Distinguish a valid over-cap scan from an unusable recount; never commit partial totals.
- Prove bounded pruning and subsequent progress with a native KV store above the row cap.
- Preserve TTL reconciliation, corruption/read-failure refusal, CAS race protection and deletion limits.

- Preserve the gateway's existing `refresh_token_reused` handling and provide evidence that the normal Codex CLI and Mac gateway remain usable after a token refresh.
- Keep the change separate from VPS deployment and production auth state.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUrfw.title: Expired status rows leave permanent phantom metadata charges
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUrfw.body:
## Problem
Status and tombstone rows are written with their metadata charge in one commit (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:445-464`), but the row is written with `expireIn: input.ttl_ms`. When KV deletes it at TTL, nothing decrements `status_records` or `metadata_bytes`.

The only subtraction path, `pruneCaptureOwnedStatusMetadata` (`:493-531`), subtracts rows that still exist, and a completed bootstrap never recounts (`:417`, `:1473-1521`).

## Impact
The 64 MiB metadata reserve accumulates charges for rows that no longer exist; once full, `prepareStatusMetadataRoom` refuses publication and every new capture is rejected while stored payload looks unchanged.

## Expected
Reconcile the ledger when status rows expire, or derive the counters from a pass that also accounts for TTL-deleted rows.

## Acceptance
A fixture that writes a status row, advances past its TTL, runs maintenance, and then admits a capture shows the metadata counters returning to their pre-row values.

## Source

Source-only inspection at open PR #437 head [a7b48ff8](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/a7b48ff83847ad2de0ce45e61e6cd31ac6b54a5f) (unmerged; rechecked unchanged 2026-10-02T15:07Z). This defect is open-head-only and is not present in development commit `dfcb8228`; it must not be assessed against development. Cited paths at that head: `src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts`. I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUtJQ.title: A restarted bootstrap double-counts every row it already scanned
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUtJQ.body:
## Problem
`runBootstrapBatch` folds the sweep delta into the durable ledger (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:1036-1043`). When the sweep completes but an invalid in-scope row was seen, it stores `bootstrap_complete: false` with `bootstrap_cursor: null` and keeps the incremented counters.

The next call parses a null cursor back to index 0 (`:1016`), clears the sticky error (`:1019`), starts from an empty delta and adds the same rows to the already-incremented counters.

## Impact
Usage is inflated on every retry, and removing the corrupt row completes bootstrap with phantom charges still present, which can refuse later captures.

## Expected
Restart a failed sweep from fresh counters (or resume from the cursor) instead of adding another copy of the authoritative row set.

## Acceptance
Two consecutive sweeps over a dataset containing one invalid row leave counters equal to a single pass over the valid rows.

## Source

Source-only inspection at open PR #437 head [a7b48ff8](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/a7b48ff83847ad2de0ce45e61e6cd31ac6b54a5f) (unmerged; rechecked unchanged 2026-10-02T15:07Z). I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUsVg.title: Staged replay chunks are written after the fence check, not with it
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUsVg.body:
## Problem
`storeReplayEnvelope` advances the staging fence per batch (`src/sentinel_replay_capture.ts:1768-1780`) and then writes the batch with unconditional `kv.set` calls (`:1783-1787`). Nothing in those writes is conditional on the accounting row's versionstamp, fence or state.

A writer that pauses after a successful fence commit, exceeds the 120-second reservation lease, and is reaped can therefore still land its chunks after the accounting row is gone (the reaper observes an empty chunk prefix and releases the charge). Another admission can then consume the released capacity, and a crash leaves the chunks unaccounted until their TTL.

## Expected
Include the accounting versionstamp/fence in the chunk-write commit (an atomic check per batch), so bytes cannot be staged for a released reservation.

## Acceptance
A test that revokes the accounting row between the fence commit and the chunk writes observes no chunk rows for that capture.

## Source

Source-only inspection at open PR #437 head [a7b48ff8](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/a7b48ff83847ad2de0ce45e61e6cd31ac6b54a5f) (unmerged; rechecked unchanged 2026-10-02T15:07Z). I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUqrw.title: Legacy replay captures are charged without reclaimable accounting rows
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUqrw.body:
## Problem
`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:911-917` charges a manifest that has no accounting row into the bootstrap delta:

```ts
const accounting = await kv.get(sentinelReplayAccountingKey(value.captured_at_ms, value.capture_id));
if (isAccountingRow(accounting.value)) return delta;
return addDelta(delta, { stored_bytes: sentinelReplayManifestCharge(value), records: 1 });
```

Bootstrap never writes an accounting row for such a capture: the only creation site is admission (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:1433-1439`), and the accounting prefix is swept read-only (`:849-864`). Eviction and expiry reclamation scan only the accounting prefix (`:1285`), so these charges can never be released, even after the legacy payload expires.

## Impact
A host upgraded from the pre-accounting format stays permanently `storage_full` once its legacy captures fill the payload budget.

## Expected
Materialize durable accounting rows during the migration sweep (or account their bytes through the reclamation path).

## Acceptance
A bootstrap over a seeded legacy manifest leaves a reclaimable accounting row whose removal decrements `stored_bytes`/`records`.

## Source

Source-only inspection at open PR #437 head [a7b48ff8](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/a7b48ff83847ad2de0ce45e61e6cd31ac6b54a5f) (unmerged; rechecked unchanged 2026-10-02T15:07Z). I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUxvg.title: One eviction pass can delete far more chunks than its configured limit
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUqUxvg.body:
## Problem
`evictSentinelReplays` computes `remainingDeletes` (`src/sentinel_replay_retention.ts:1317`) but never passes it to `finalizeClaimedVictim`, which always calls `deleteChunkBatch(kv, row.capture_id, EVICTION_MAX_CHUNK_DELETES)` (`:1141`, 512 per call). Because `remainingDeletes` is clamped with `Math.max(1, ...)`, the later `if (remainingDeletes <= 0) break;` can never fire.

With several large victims the pass performs many serial batches while reporting a bounded pass, including on capture admission and admin requests.

## Expected
Thread the remaining allowance into finalization and stop once it is exhausted.

## Acceptance
A fixture with at least two multi-chunk victims observes no more than the pass limit in total deleted chunks.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbl6Q.title: Toast eviction spins forever when a fourth notification arrives
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbl6Q.body:
## Problem
`static/toast.js:95-99` evicts over-limit toasts by re-counting every `[data-toast]` node inside a synchronous `while` loop:

```js
while (host.querySelectorAll("[data-toast]").length > MAX_VISIBLE) {
  const oldest = host.querySelector("[data-toast]");
  if (oldest === toastEl) break;
  dismissToastEl(oldest, null);
}
```

`dismissToastEl` (`static/toast.js:34-39`) only marks the node `data-exiting` and schedules its removal with `setTimeout(..., EXIT_MS)`. The node therefore stays in the DOM and in the count, so the loop selects the same oldest node again; the second `dismissToastEl` call returns early because `data-exiting` is already set, nothing changes, and the loop never exits. Because the loop blocks the event loop, the removal timer can never run.

## Impact
Any fourth toast (rapid admin saves, repeated chat failures) freezes the page.

## Trigger
Call `toast.info(...)` four times in a row with no dismissal in between; the third toast leaves three nodes, and the fourth enters the loop.

## Expected
Evict the oldest toast synchronously, or exclude `[data-exiting]` nodes from both the count and the selection, so the loop always reaches `MAX_VISIBLE`.

## Acceptance
A test that queues more than three toasts returns and leaves exactly three non-exiting toast nodes plus whichever nodes are still animating out.

Source proof:
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/static/toast.js#L34-L39
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/static/toast.js#L94-L99

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsb0dQ.title: Forwarded-payload reduction can split a surrogate pair when it reserves the marker
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsb0dQ.body:
## What is wrong

`utf8Head` guards only its first cut for a trailing high surrogate (`src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:116-119`), and its own byte-trim loop re-cuts at `:120` with no code-point check. `reduceForwardedPayload` may then shorten the prefix repeatedly with `head.slice(0, Math.floor(head.length * 0.9))` while reserving room for the marker (`:145-163`, cut at `:162`) and appends the marker to that head at `:149`. Neither the marker-reservation loop nor `utf8Head`'s reduction loop checks code-point boundaries, so a prefix ending inside an astral character leaves an unpaired high surrogate in the retained content — corrupting the text instead of producing the declared byte prefix (`forwardedByteLength` at `:98` encodes with `TextEncoder`, which replaces a lone surrogate with U+FFFD).

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b` (`development`)
- Location: `src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:114-122` (`utf8Head` guards only its first cut, and its own reduction loop is also unchecked) and `:142-163` (`reduceForwardedPayload` shortens with `head.slice` with no code-point check while reserving room for the marker)
- Links: [utf8Head](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts#L114-L122), [reduceForwardedPayload](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts#L142-L163)

## Trigger

A tool output whose prefix ends just before an emoji plus a marker that forces one more cut; the retained prefix ends with `\uD83D` without its pair.

## Acceptance

After every shortening step (including the marker reservation), drop a trailing unpaired high surrogate before appending the marker; a focused projection test asserts the retained prefix is always well-formed UTF-16.

## Validation

Static source read at `5c58eca8` (`development`); no test, browser, inference, or production action was executed. Source PR: [ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#512](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/512) (merged).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaCXA.title: Live calls and sideband reconnects never refresh an expired account token
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaCXA.body:
Live-call creation and sideband reconnect send the stored account access token as-is. `getAuthPoolEntry` only reads the pool and `fetchCodexResponseWithAuth` only injects `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`, so when the access token has expired but the refresh token is still valid the upstream answers an authentication failure instead of the gateway using its coordinated credential-refresh path.

## What is wrong
- `src/live/calls.ts:142` and `:223` read the pool entry and dispatch with those credentials; the 401/403 retry re-selects rather than refreshing.
- `src/codex/auth.ts:538-556`: no refresh in `getAuthPoolEntry`.
- `src/codex/dispatch.ts:188-190`: the access token is injected verbatim; no refresh call in `fetchCodexResponseWithAuth`.
- `src/live/sideband.ts:221-230`: `liveCallAccountToken` returns `account.access_token` from the pool read.

## Acceptance
- The selected/mapped account goes through the existing coordinated refresh before dispatch (live call creation and sideband reconnect), with `liveCallAccountToken` re-reading the refreshed credential.

Exact evidence:
- Reviewed head: 54668f28d3fe2d5776dcb516b86cc7f9b0a9b8e0

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Redact past backslash-prefixed YAML quote escapes**

When a valid YAML single-quoted credential contains a literal backslash immediately before an escaped quote—for example `client_secret: 'abc\''def'`—the `\\.` alternative consumes the backslash and the first quote of the doubled pair, so the final quote closes the match early and redaction produces `[redacted]def'`. I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL9CQ.title: Do not replace a Codex auth slot on an inconclusive local probe
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL9CQ.body:
The repair planner treats any probe result other than `valid` as a broken slot, so a timeout or a 403/5xx on an unexpired token can cause `--apply` to overwrite a healthy account.

## What is wrong
- `src/codex/auth-repair.ts:149`: `localUsable = entry.probe.outcome === "valid" && (localExpMs === null || localExpMs > input.nowMs)`; every inconclusive outcome makes the slot repair-eligible.
- `:156-175` then selects a replacement candidate for that slot, and `:198-212` writes it into the pool.
- `probeAccessToken` classifies inconclusive results as unable to justify a write, so the planner contradicts its own probe contract; unrelated healthy slots can also be rewritten while one account is being repaired.

## Trigger
A local token is unexpired but its probe times out (or answers 403/5xx) while an SSH/source candidate authenticates: `--apply` replaces a potentially healthy account without evidence of invalidity.

## Acceptance
- A slot is preserved unless rejection or verified expiry establishes that replacement is needed.
- Inconclusive probe outcomes are reported as inconclusive, with a focused test for the timeout and 403/5xx cases.

## Duplicate search
- Local index (`inconclusive`, `probe result`, `codex-auth-repair`) — no issue.
- Fresh GitHub search, 2026-10-02: `repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi is:issue "auth repair"` → 0.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaKNg.title: System One requests never commit the API-key request reservation before dispatch
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaKNg.body:
With OpenRouter configured, a bounded API key can call `/v1/systemone` without consuming its request allowance. The terminal wrapper supplies `usageContext.beforeProviderDispatch`, but neither `handleSystemOne` nor `fetchOpenRouterSystemOne` invokes it; `reserveApiKeyUsageV3` uses `deferWhenFull: true`, so an exhausted window is refused only by that hook, and the uncommitted reservation is released after upstream inference. The same defect was independently reviewed on PR #550 (finding 550-a) and is covered by this one issue.

## What is wrong
- `src/handler/terminal-route.ts:327` builds the usage context with `beforeProviderDispatch` and `:503` passes it to `handleSystemOne`.
- `src/systemone/handlers.ts:153-208` never calls it (only `recordRequestUsage`/`recordCompletionUsage`/`attachResponseTelemetry`).
- `src/provider/openrouter.ts:143-166` dispatches the System One fetch directly, with no hooks parameter.
- `src/api-key-policy.ts:490-509` throws `ApiKeyQuotaDispatchError` when the deferred window has no reserved request; `:661-664` documents the deferred reservation.

## Acceptance
- An API key whose request allowance is exhausted is refused (429 with the quota headers) before any upstream fetch, and a successful request commits its reservation.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE3Zw.title: DeepSeek Responses stream closes truncated tool calls as completed before the incomplete terminal
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlE3Zw.body:
The DeepSeek Responses translator finalizes tool-call items before it decides the terminal, so a `finish_reason: "length"` truncation that lands mid-arguments still emits `response.function_call_arguments.done` and `response.output_item.done` with a `completed` item, and only afterwards emits `response.incomplete`.
## What is wrong
- In `src/deepseek/responses-stream.ts` the `finish()` path builds `[...startEvents(), ...closeMessage(), ...flushPendingReasoning(), ...closeToolCalls(), ...closeReasoning()]` and then pushes the terminal envelope, so every tool item is closed as complete before the terminal kind is known (lines 586-592).
- `closeToolCalls()` emits `response.function_call_arguments.done` and `response.output_item.done` unconditionally (lines 493-517), and the item it stores comes from `functionCallItem(...)`, whose `status` is the literal `"completed"` (`src/deepseek/responses-payload.ts:27-34`).
- The terminal envelope does map `length` to `response.incomplete` (`src/deepseek/responses-payload.ts:146-175`), so the stream corrects itself only after a consumer has already been told the truncated call is executable.
## Current evidence
- `src/deepseek/responses-stream.ts:493-517` `closeToolCalls` (no terminal-kind check).
- `src/deepseek/responses-stream.ts:586-592` event order: item closes, then terminal event.
- `src/deepseek/responses-payload.ts:27-34` `functionCallItem` hardcodes `status: "completed"`.
- `src/deepseek/responses-payload.ts:166-175` `length` maps to `{ type: "response.incomplete", incomplete_details.reason: "max_output_tokens" }`.
- Codex review on the original head: discussion_r4064335828, PR #367 (that PR was closed unmerged; the same code moved into the split modules).
## Reproduction
- Static only, no execution claimed: follow `finish()` for a stream whose last chunk carries `finish_reason: "length"` plus a `tool_calls` delta with partial arguments; read the emitted event order in `src/deepseek/responses-stream.ts`.
- Optional dynamic proof if the owner wants it: a focused unit test on the DeepSeek stream translator that drives a length-terminated tool call and asserts the item-done event is not `completed` (or is only emitted after the incomplete terminal).
## Acceptance criteria
- A length-terminated tool call must not be announced as `status: "completed"` before the terminal, or the terminal must be decided before items close and the item marked incomplete.
- A focused test covers the length-plus-tool-call ordering and passes in the repository's own test task.
## Duplicate search
- Searched the frozen issue snapshot (365 issues, #115-#573) by the exact finding id, the review id, and terms `closeToolCalls`, `function_call_arguments`, `truncated arg`, `tool call`: no matching issue. PR #367 itself was closed unmerged and is the source, not a dedup target.

Current upstream rechecked: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` (`development`). The affected implementation files are unchanged from the validator's `98ccd167cca1db4309e2d7f4d961b7109b119502` snapshot.

Source locations: [src/deepseek/responses-stream.ts:493-517](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/deepseek/responses-stream.ts#L493), [src/deepseek/responses-stream.ts:586-592](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/deepseek/responses-stream.ts#L586), [src/deepseek/responses-payload.ts:27-34](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/deepseek/responses-payload.ts#L27).

Codex review evidence: https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/367#discussion_r4064335828, https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/367#pullrequestreview-5269330285.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaBbA.title: Sideband attachment is not bound to the gateway principal that created the call
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaBbA.body:
`/v1/live` authenticates the request but discards the principal, and the sideband join resolves the call id to the upstream account stored at creation. Any authenticated gateway principal that learns a call id can therefore attach to another principal's call and use the creator's upstream credentials, exposing transcripts and permitting context/delegation injection across principals. The auth result already carries a principal identity (`{ok, token, method}`), so the binding is available to the route.

## What is wrong
- `src/live/handler.ts:26-29`: `authResult` is checked for `ok` only; `handleLiveSideband` receives just `route.callId`.
- `src/live/sideband.ts:240-257`: the mapping read -> `Deno.upgradeWebSocket` -> bridge has no principal comparison.
- `src/live/upstream.ts:122-129`: `writeLiveCallAccount` persists `{account_id, created_at_ms}` only.

## Acceptance
- A sideband join by a different principal than the call creator is rejected before the 101 upgrade (or the creating principal is stored at call creation and checked on join), with a regression test covering two valid principals.

Source confirmation at development 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded: [src/live/handler.ts:22-31](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/live/handler.ts#L22), [src/live/sideband.ts:240-257](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/live/sideband.ts#L240), [src/live/upstream.ts:122-129](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/live/upstream.ts#L122).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnqSQQ.title: Narrowing the subscription pool reassigns durable routing slots
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnqSQQ.body:
## Confirmed defect

evaluateSerialRoutingAccounts derives each account's slot from its index in the pool it is given: `for (const [slot, auth] of pool.accounts.entries()) ... byId.set(auth.account_id, { slot, ... })` (routing-serial.ts:48-50). prepareCodexSerialAdmissionRows normalizes routing state against the full durablePool (routing-serial.ts:306) but then evaluates against the narrowed pool from selectedCodexSubscriptionPool (routing-serial.ts:310-311), so with pool [A,B] and only B selected, B becomes slot 0 while the active selection still identifies A at slot 0; the slot comparison in src/codex/account-routing.ts rejects it before transport.

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded`
- Location: `src/codex/routing-serial.ts:46-51,306-311`
- Source PR: #329 (closed, merged=true), original head `1d97ac61bcc4a85255b174be9f332d957e11260a`, merge `66e7091512f082c7f3338709ab04da4529c7650b`

## Trigger / reproduction

Static source read at `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` shows the cited code path unchanged; the exact expression is named above. No runtime, browser, or production operation was performed to confirm this.

## Acceptance

Durable routing slots must be derived from stable account identity rather than the index in a narrowed pool, so narrowing the selection does not reassign an active account's slot. Add a focused test for pool [A,B] with only B selected.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmdx9w.title: Trimmed follow cards reappear as the newest entry and evict a newer one
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmdx9w.body:
The client keeps a 200-entry window and, when trimming, deletes the trimmed node's key from followSeen (static/admin-supervisor.js:564-570). The server re-emits changed entries below the cursor, so a later revision of a trimmed key arrives as an unseen key: appendEntries creates a new card and appends it at the bottom (:549-562), auto-scrolls to it (:577), and the trim loop then removes the oldest remaining card, which is genuinely newer than the re-appended one — recorded ordering is corrupted and a newer entry disappears from the retained window for the rest of the follow.

Current source: [static/admin-supervisor.js:564-570 (trim deletes the trimmed key from followSeen); supporting :5 (FOLLOW_ENTRY_LIMIT = 200), :539-563 (appendEntries), :577 (auto-scroll)](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/static/admin-supervisor.js#L564), development 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded.

Acceptance:

- An update to an evicted entry never appends below newer output: keep an eviction cutoff or tombstone, or re-insert the updated card in recorded order before trimming.
- A regression test with a >200-entry window asserts order is preserved and the trim removes the oldest entry rather than a newer one.

Review: native Codex [PR #424](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/424), original head e44828262f0388c7bca0961125b16572b88c8cba, review turn 01a0fc46-8f66-73a0-b5f2-09ceed27f6e7.

Validation: Source-only (no render or follow session executed; a render belongs to the parent). Read at the proved-equal blob: static/admin-supervisor.js:5, :516-537, :539-578, plus the server-side re-emission of below-cursor revisions in src/codex/supervisor-follow.ts:103-111 (proved-equal blob 066e4fd3…).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmdwtw.title: Follow revisions are recorded for entries the update limit drops
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmdwtw.body:
selectFollowUpdates records `revisions.set(entry.key, revision)` for every entry it scans (src/codex/supervisor-follow.ts:103-111), but the caller keeps only `updates.filter(...).slice(-FOLLOW_MAX_ENTRIES)` (:159, FOLLOW_MAX_ENTRIES = 120 in src/codex/supervisor-config.ts:27). An entry whose revision is committed while it is dropped by that slice is never selected again: it sits at or below the cursor (entry.index <= startIndex) and its revision no longer changes, so an already-rendered command keeps its old output, status and exit code in the client even though it is still inside the UI's 200-entry window (static/admin-supervisor.js:5).

Current source: [src/codex/supervisor-follow.ts:103-111 (selectFollowUpdates records every scanned revision) vs :159 (slice(-FOLLOW_MAX_ENTRIES) after selection); src/codex/supervisor-config.ts:27 (FOLLOW_MAX_ENTRIES = 120); client static/admin-supervisor.js:5 (FOLLOW_ENTRY_LIMIT = 200)](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/codex/supervisor-follow.ts#L103), development 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded.

Acceptance:

- Revision state is committed only for emitted entries, or dropped revisions are retained and delivered on a later poll/hinted through the cursor.
- A regression test covers a sampling gap of more than FOLLOW_MAX_ENTRIES entries and asserts the completed entry is still delivered with final text, status and exit code.

Read at the proved-equal blobs: revision commit at :103-111, slice at :158-161 (with the comment context at :85-102), the config constant at src/codex/supervisor-config.ts:27, and the client window at static/admin-supervisor.js:5 and :564-570.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmISGA.title: Deferred upstream HTTP 504 is reported as a gateway deadline: HTTP 200 then a clean EOF with no error frame
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmISGA.body:
## Original finding (same defect in both relay variants)
- Native Codex review of PR #515, finding 2: [P2] Emit an error frame for deferred upstream 504 responses (original cite stream-relay.ts:211-212). Native Codex review of PR #514, finding 2: [P2] Distinguish upstream HTTP 504s from gateway deadlines (original cite lithos-handlers.ts:795-798).
- PR #515 original head 96c52bed9af1cdaff7db427111ffc1010912e097; PR #514 original head f9c9f4542f9acf97f7b2216628a1d08709905704. Provenance as in CAND-AI-RELAY-01.

## Current state (verified at current upstream default)
Current development @ 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded; the three files are byte-identical to frozen checkout HEAD 98ccd167cca1db4309e2d7f4d961b7109b119502 (blob equality checked).
- Both refuseStream copies treat every 504 like the gateway's own deadline and close silently: stream-relay.ts:180-187 (Chat) and 450-457 (Responses) settle the deadline terminal and close with no data frame.
- An upstream 504 keeps its status through toLithosUpstreamErrorResponse (upstream-wire.ts:751 returns openaiError(upstream.status, ...)), while the local deadline response is minted as 504 gateway_timeout at upstream-wire.ts:594-597. After conversion the two are only distinguishable by status, which the relay does not inspect further.
- The deferred handlers pass the resolved refusal Response straight into the stream relay (lithos-handlers.ts:601-604 Chat, 842-845 Responses), so an upstream 504 that arrives after an absorbed 429 window is relayed through the silent 504 path.

## Trigger
1. The whole ladder refuses, a waitable window is absorbed, and the deferred retry runs.
2. That retry returns an upstream HTTP 504 (provider gateway timeout) while both caller signals remain live.
3. refuseStream sees status 504 and assumes the gateway deadline: it records a deadline terminal and closes without response.failed or a Chat error frame.
4. The client receives HTTP 200 plus keepalives and a clean EOF instead of the provider's error code and message; the buffered path would have returned the 504.

## Acceptance
- Distinguish upstream 504 refusals from signal-confirmed local deadlines (for example carry provenance on the refusal Response or check the abort state before choosing the silent close) and emit the preserved error frame for an upstream 504 on both relays.
- Regression test: deferred retry answers 504 -> the streamed terminal is response.failed (Chat error frame) with the preserved code/message, not a silent EOF; a genuine gateway deadline keeps the silent close.

## Duplicate search (fresh, 2026-10-02)
- Corpus scan (596 issues): 504 term hits are #52, #283, #284, #505 and none describes this conflation; refuseStream 2 hits are the reviewed PRs only.
- Fresh GitHub search q=repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi+refuseStream -> only PRs #515 and #501; q=failover+window -> 27 hits, all the reviewed PRs or unrelated older work.
- No existing or audit-filed issue matches (all open and closed issues in this repository were paginated in full). Distinct neighbours: #576, #599, #600 (OpenRouter terminal/empty-success issues).

## Labels
Time: <2 Hours; Priority: 2 (Medium) - existing labels only (fully paginated label list, 44 labels).

Validation: static source/control-flow inspection at the current revision above; no runtime inference or repository test was executed.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmAEYw.title: Deferred Lithos absorb leaks its pending dispatch and any late upstream response on client cancellation
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmAEYw.body:
## Original finding (same defect in both relay variants)
- Native Codex review of PR #515, finding 1: [P2] Cancel late upstream bodies after abandoning a pending stream (original cite stream-relay.ts:206-209). Native Codex review of PR #514, finding 1: [P2] Propagate stream cancellation into the deferred dispatch (original cite stream-relay.ts:468-471).
- PR #515 original head 96c52bed9af1cdaff7db427111ffc1010912e097, base 69b2a319567120cd43a181e257eb17b34bc01869. PR #514 original head f9c9f4542f9acf97f7b2216628a1d08709905704, base 256b1bc6a65e89042dec1c244148e4904596f099.
- Provenance: thread 01a0fc31-43b3-7ad0-816b-6a130f5e1680 / turn 01a0fc31-633d-7262-8dee-afe269214b21 / review result 01a0fc40-2f6c-7161-b0a1-953a657ef377 (exitedReviewMode); thread 01a0fc31-45d5-7661-bff2-602af1b9f216 / turn 01a0fc31-69c7-7d01-92cb-ca34bc627f18 / review result 01a0fc40-36c9-7493-901d-4974f2c7e201.

## Current state (verified at current upstream default)
Current ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi development @ 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded; src/provider/stream-relay.ts blob 6b976a5f591d24af213e233fd37f5069e68d4f74 is byte-identical to frozen checkout HEAD 98ccd167cca1db4309e2d7f4d961b7109b119502 (git hash-object of the raw fetch equals the clone blob).
- Chat relay cancel (stream-relay.ts:260-278) aborts only the relay-local cancellation signal (line 273) and cancels only an already-resolved upstream body (lines 274-275); the pending dispatch is untouched.
- Chat ensureIterator (stream-relay.ts:204-220) awaits pendingUpstream at line 209 and returns null at line 212 once the stream closed, discarding the resolved Response without cancelling its body.
- Responses relay repeats both sites: cancel at stream-relay.ts:573-591, await at line 486, discard at line 489.
- The pending closure only sees input.requestSignal (lithos-handlers.ts:479-496) and the handlers hand the relay its own signals (lithos-handlers.ts:605-613 and 850-864), so a downstream stream cancel never reaches the pending wait or the next provider attempt.
- The dispatcher does release discarded refusals it owns (lithos-handlers.ts:398, 418, 432 call cancelResponseBody); the relay does not.

## Trigger
1. A streamed Lithos request opens its SSE response and defers an absorbed rate-limit retry (waitForLithosRetry pending).
2. The client cancels the SSE body before the pending attempt resolves.
3. The relay closes, but the wait and the following upstream attempt keep running on requestSignal.
4. When that attempt resolves with a successful upstream SSE Response, ensureIterator returns null and nobody reads, cancels or releases the body: the upstream stream stays unread/unreleased and the gateway continues generating tokens for a disconnected client.

## Acceptance
- Propagate stream cancellation into the pending deferred dispatch, and cancel any Response that resolves after the stream closed.
- Regression test: cancel the response body while the pending source is unresolved; assert the late upstream body cancel() runs exactly once and no further upstream read occurs.
- Keep the existing behaviour of emitting no error frame for a client cancellation.

## Duplicate search (fresh, 2026-10-02)
- Full open and closed issue corpus (596 entries) scanned: refuseStream 0 hits, pending dispatch 0, unreleased/unread no match; the 33 cancellation hits never describe this deferred-relay leak.
- Fresh GitHub search: q=repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi+refuseStream -> 2 results, both the reviewed PRs (#515, #501); q=repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi+deferred+dispatch -> 6 results, none an issue for this defect.
- All issues filed by this audit (41) and its filed documentation issues (#602-611) contain no match. Nearest but distinct: #119 (reader release inside src/bounded-response-body.ts), #597 (admin UI superseded health responses).

## Labels
Time: <2 Hours; Priority: 2 (Medium) - existing labels only, from a fully paginated /repos/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/labels?per_page=100 (44 labels).

Validation: static source/control-flow inspection at the current revision above; no runtime inference or repository test was executed.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL2hw.title: Correct the Cerebras null-content failure guidance
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL2hw.body:
`AGENTS.md` tells agents that a budget-stopped Cerebras reply with `content: null` fails closed as a 502. The code rejects only omitted content, so an explicit `null` becomes an empty string and the buffered route answers 200.

## What is wrong
- `AGENTS.md:67-68`: "A Cerebras response that stops at the token budget can carry reasoning only, with `content: null` and `finish_reason: "length"`. The gateway fails that closed as `cerebras_upstream_invalid_response` (502) ...".
- `src/provider/cerebras.ts:463-464` (`choiceHasNoPayload`): the test is `content === undefined && !toolCalls?.length && !refusal`.
- `src/provider/cerebras.ts:467-469` (`choiceContent`): an explicit `null` with no tool call or refusal becomes `""`, so the guard at `:490` never fires and `handleCerebrasChatCompletions` returns HTTP 200 with an unusable empty completion.

## Trigger
A Cerebras reply with `content: null`, `finish_reason: "length"`, no tool call and no refusal reaches the buffered Chat route: the documented 502 does not occur.

## Acceptance
- `AGENTS.md` describes the omitted-content rejection separately from the explicit-`null` path, or the code fails the explicit-`null` reasoning-only case closed as documented.
- A focused test pins whichever behaviour is chosen.

## Duplicate search

- Fresh GitHub search, 2026-10-02: `repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi is:issue cerebras null` → 0.
- Current upstream rechecked: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` (`development`); `AGENTS.md` and `src/provider/cerebras.ts` are byte-identical to the reviewed snapshot.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmdu7w.title: Singly-quoted YAML credential with a doubled quote is only partially redacted
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUmdu7w.body:
SUPERVISOR_SECRET_PATTERNS applies the quoted single-quote pattern \b\w*(?:key|token|secret|password)\w*["']?\s*[:=]\s*'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*' (src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:17) before the unquoted fallback \b\w*(?:key|token|secret|password)\w*\s*[:=]\s*\S{8,} (:18). YAML escapes a single quote inside a single-quoted scalar by doubling it, so for `password: 'firstpart''secondpart'` pattern :17 matches only `password: 'firstpart'`; replacing it removes the credential key and separator, so the fallback can no longer match and the generic prompt-level call cannot either. redactBriefText (= redactSupervisorSecrets, src/codex/supervisor-brief.ts:78, applied at :348) therefore sends `[redacted]'secondpart'` — the tail of the credential — in the brief request body to the external summarizer. The module's own stated contract accepts deliberately over-broad redaction, so consuming the complete assignment is the safe direction.

Current source: [src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts:9-19 (pattern list), finding at :17; consumer src/codex/supervisor-brief.ts:78 (redactBriefText = redactSupervisorSecrets) and :348](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded/src/codex/supervisor-secret.ts#L9), development 1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded.

Acceptance:

- Patterns consume the complete singly-quoted scalar, including doubled-quote escapes (or drain the whole assignment), so no part of the value survives redaction.
- A focused regression case is added next to the existing quoted-JSON cases in tests/codex-supervisor-brief.test.ts, asserting the doubled-quote form redacts to a single [redacted] with the tail removed.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL0vw.title: Gate the DeepSeek thinking extension on the enabled provider route
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL0vw.body:
The Chat Completions envelope accepts the DeepSeek `thinking` extension based on the model id alone, while dispatch decides on the enabled provider route. A request can therefore be accepted with `thinking` and then answered by the Codex/paid bridge, which drops it.

## What is wrong
- `src/chat/envelope.ts:115`: `isDeepSeekRoute = deepSeekUpstreamModelFor(model) !== null` widens the OpenAI-schema allowlist with `DEEPSEEK_CHAT_EXTENSION_KEYS`; there is no provider-selection check.
- `src/chat/envelope.ts:566-574`: DeepSeek dispatch requires `isProviderEnabled("deepseek", selection)`; otherwise the same body continues into the ordinary Codex/paid path, where `thinking` is not forwarded and is reported as `thinking_ignored`.
- With the direct DeepSeek provider disabled and an official DeepSeek model available in the paid catalog, the caller's thinking switch is accepted without being applied on a route documented as retaining the strict OpenAI schema (`AGENTS.md:21-22`).

## Trigger

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaRGA.title: Superseded provider refresh responses can overwrite a newer health snapshot
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlaRGA.body:
Provider loads have no cancellation or generation check: `load()` aborts only the sessions controller, and `renderProviders` replaces the list from whichever response pair resolves last, so an older pair can overwrite a newer health snapshot (for example reverting a fresh invalid/exhausted badge to an earlier healthy state).

## What is wrong
- `static/admin-supervisor.js:191-206`: `loadProviders` performs two fetches and renders whenever a selection payload parsed; there is no request identity.
- `static/admin-supervisor.js:730-733`: `load()` starts `loadProviders()` and aborts only the previous sessions request via `controller`.
- `static/admin-supervisor.js:774-787`: the visible-tab tick re-enters `load()` every 15 s, so overlapping provider loads are routine on a slow link.

## Acceptance
- Provider loads get their own lifecycle and responses superseded by a newer load or target change are rejected before rendering.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlZ46A.title: Cerebras Harmony probes record the pre-projection roles, not the wire they sent
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUlZ46A.body:
The live Harmony/Cerebras probe records `built.metadata.messageRoles` before dispatch, but the Cerebras transport rewrites every `developer` message to `system` and collapses the system messages. Saved probe results therefore attribute upstream outcomes to a request shape that was never sent, which makes the native-versus-generic protocol evidence misleading.

## What is wrong
- `src/harmony/probes.ts:303-306` builds the recorded `roles` from `built.metadata.messageRoles` before `runHarmonyTurn` dispatches.
- `src/harmony/adapter.ts:132`/`:207` fill `messageRoles` from the caller's messages, so a DSH-style `developer` turn is recorded as `developer`.
- `scripts/probes/cerebras-harmony-probes.ts:70-73` runs the manifest through `createCerebrasTransport`, i.e. `fetchCerebrasChatCompletions` (`src/harmony/adapter.ts:425-432`).
- `src/provider/cerebras.ts:309-313` projects the body before the fetch: `projectCerebrasMessages` maps `developer`->`system` (`:261-264`) and `collapseCerebrasSystemMessages` merges them (`:301-307`), so the wire carries exactly one leading `system` message.

## Acceptance
- Probe records are generated from the projected request, or record both the built and dispatched roles, so `docs/probes/*.jsonl` cannot attribute an upstream result to a role sequence that was never sent.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajJpg.title: Automate the paid-fallback rollup backfill (manual admin step leaves projection history empty after deploy)
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajJpg.body:
## Context
PR #135 added `POST /admin/providers/quota-projection/backfill` to fold pre-existing settled V3 rows into the new hourly usage rollups and to apply the anchored one-year raw-row TTL to rows that predate it (`src/paid_fallback_ledger.ts` `backfillPaidFallbackUsageRollups`/`backfillPaidFallbackWindowTtls`). It exists to fix the Codex review P1 'Backfill existing settlements before serving projections'.

## Gap
Nothing runs it automatically. Until an operator calls it:
- the admin projection shows an empty/partial per-model history even though raw rows exist, and
- pre-existing raw rows and window rows carry **no TTL**, so they can still grow unbounded.

The same applies to the window-TTL sweep: existing V3 window rows never pass through the live writes that set `expireIn`.

## Proposed
Run the backfill automatically at deploy bootstrap (or on first request when the rollup prefix is empty and settled rows exist), lease-guarded like the other maintenance jobs, and make window-TTL rewriting part of the same path. Keep the manual endpoint for forced re-runs.

## References
- PR #135 (merged), docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md
- Codex review threads: 'Backfill existing settlements before serving projections', 'Apply the retention TTL to existing V3 rows', 'Apply the new TTL to existing window rows' -- all comment-only in code; the automation is the missing piece.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajMRA.title: Make quota-runway estimates refill-aware (projections currently assume no further refill)
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABOajMRA.body:
## Context
The quota-runway feature (PR #135, admin#providers 'Quota runway' card + `GET /admin/providers/quota-projection`) estimates requests/run-time remaining as `balance / average quota per request` and `balance / quota-per-hour`, and explicitly states the UI assumes no further refill. Refill facts (last refill credits, completion time, cycle start) are shown alongside but not modelled.

## Gap
The Metered wallet refills on a cycle. When the refill rate exceeds the burn rate, the true answer is 'sustainable' rather than a shrinking run-time; when a refill is due soon, the exhaustion date is materially wrong. The new hourly balance history + refill observations now provide enough data to project with and without refill.

## Proposed
In `src/quota_projection.ts`, add a refill-aware branch: estimate refill cadence/amount from the retained balance samples and `latest_refill_*`/cycle fields, and report one of: sustainable (refill ≥ burn), exhausts at <date> (no refill), or exhausts at <date> (with known refill schedule). Keep the no-refill number visible for contrast.

## References
- PR #135 (merged), docs/log-retention-and-quota-runway-2026-08-25.md
- Original feature idea: estimate gpt-5.6-sol / gpt-5.6-luna run-time against quota.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABN2lxuw.title: Do not report contentless provider completions as successful chat responses
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABN2lxuw.body:
The Chat Completions stream adapter currently turns an upstream Responses `response.completed` event with no translated assistant text or tool call into a successful role-only `finish_reason: "stop"` chunk. A production `glm-5.2` request through Surplus did this across three attempts, so clients receive a syntactically successful but empty answer.

Evidence:

- Production SHA: `689a071640a2193de00e8001312f67899f1b8677`
- Observed at: `2026-08-22T23:31:44Z`
- Gateway request: `ae324d33-0e4a-4426-8c68-601d02ba77fb`
- Surplus request: `01M0NX1QD3XY9GXT9BJRYZ1SBF`
- Usage: 1,642 input tokens and exactly 2,048 output tokens
- Terminal: `response.completed`
- Two immediate retries used `minimal` reasoning and also reported exactly 2,048 output tokens with no visible answer.
- The evidence suggests either hidden reasoning exhausted the output allowance or Surplus emitted an event shape that the adapter did not translate. The gateway defect is independent: a semantically empty completion must not become a successful `stop`.

Acceptance:

- Reconcile all supported final text, refusal, and tool-call output before deciding that a completed response is empty.
- When a completed upstream response has no translated semantic output, return or stream an explicit retryable `empty_upstream_completion` error instead of a successful role-only `stop`.
- Record privacy-safe diagnostics for this condition, including provider request ID, upstream event kinds, reasoning effort, output allowance and usage, and whether semantic output was observed.
- Preserve normal streamed text, done-only output text, refusal, and tool-call behavior.
- Add regression coverage for a contentless `response.completed` stream and the successful output variants.

- `tests/openai-compat.test.ts`

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABN1-8Ow.title: Image models are advertised in /v1/models but no image endpoint exists
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABN1-8Ow.body:
## Summary

`/v1/models` lists ~29 image models (`gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `qwen-image-3.0-pro`, `gemini-3-pro-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, …), but there is no route that can serve them, so they are unreachable by any request.

## Reproduction

```
POST /v1/images/generations   → 404 {"error":{"message":"Not found","code":"not_found"}}
POST /v1/images/edits         → 404
POST /v1/images               → 404
```

Routing them through chat instead is explicitly rejected:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions  {"model":"gpt-image-2", ...}
→ 404 "The model 'gpt-image-2' does not support chat.completions. Use /v1/models for supported models."
```

`src/handler.ts` registers only `/v1/models`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and the `/uos/embeddings` family, so image requests fall through to the 404 handler.

## Why this is confusing for clients

Any OpenAI-compatible client that reads `/v1/models` will offer these models to users, and every selection fails. The curated `/uos/models/catalog` correctly omits them (186 models, no image entries), so the two catalogues disagree — `handleModels` merges the metered and surplus lists verbatim without filtering by endpoint support.

## Suggested direction

ChatGPT/Codex has no native image endpoint, but it does expose generation as an `image_generation` tool on the Responses API. An images request can therefore be rewritten as a tool-bearing Responses call and dispatched through the existing waterfall, so a live Codex subscription serves images at no extra cost and paid providers are used only as fallback — with the same quota accounting and roster checks as text.

Separately, `/v1/models` could filter out models with no usable endpoint so the catalogue stops advertising unreachable capabilities.

I have a working implementation for the first part and will open a PR referencing this issue.

I_kwDOK6Xdq86J0Ftb.title: Secure Worker routing
I_kwDOK6Xdq86J0Ftb.body:
We used to only have GitHub Actions, which can be secured using GitHub Authentication system. Now that we have workers, they are currently open endpoints, which implies security risks as anyone can access them and potentially trigger them outside of our control.

This is why we should require authentication to reach these endpoints as well. After looking at what Cloudflare offers, I stumbled upon https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/ which provides authentication system Cloudflare wide.

I need to do some more research but from what I understand, we can provide routes we would like to protect, by only allowing users, IPs, domain to be able to reach it. Before doing any request, the caller should ask to exchange some credentials for a token, used for subsequent calls. Then we would just have to check for that token within our Workers, and deny the request if none is present.

The challenge is for 3rd parties, that would have to provide their endpoint for acquiring the token so we can call their services. Maybe that's where the IP whitelisting could come in handy.

Likewise, the invocation of these workers should be secured on the kernel side, to properly handle their callback, or, directly pickup the result of the `fetch` call to trigger next plugins in the chain.

I_kwDOK6Xdq86Iwcu3.title: Worker plugins
I_kwDOK6Xdq86Iwcu3.body:
We should have the capability of running the plugins inside Workers, which would be very useful for short-lived tasks that require responsiveness like commands for example. Currently, we only support Actions, which works fine but takes ~1 minute response time, which is not user friendly when it comes to using commands with the bot.

In the configuration, for each plugin it is possible to specify a [`type`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-kernel/blob/c8da3c0e07eb2735b0e7d63d5f2997a138fd2135/src/github/types/plugin-configuration.ts#L37) that should determine what kind of plugin it is. A new value like `worker` should be added, and should make the plugin run on a worker instead of calling a GitHub Action.

I_kwDOTe4zHc8AAAABYADrLQ.title: Stop the work queue from arming a timer after stop()
I_kwDOTe4zHc8AAAABYADrLQ.body:
**Severity:** P2. **Where:** [`src/work_queue.ts:91-96`](https://github.com/ubiquity/checkout.ubq.fi/blob/2715f7c155e8de5fea070bbb965b27bfab88c6a9/src/work_queue.ts#L91-L96)

**What happens**

`stop()` can run while the D1 `entries()` scan is waiting on its HTTP response. It clears the timer and sets `started` to false, but the scan's continuation still installs another timer.

So `stop()` resolves while scheduled work can still run handlers or touch a store that has since been closed. A probe that holds the list call open reproduced a handler running after shutdown.

**Expected**

Every continuation in the scheduler checks one lifecycle guard before it arms a timer, runs a handler or touches the store. That guard can be a start/stop generation token, or `started` checked again after each await. `stop()` does not resolve while a handler it could have stopped can still start.

Found by the third `codex review` of draft PR #2 (head `2715f7c`). The review policy stops after round 3 and files what remains as an issue. A fix is in progress on the PR branch; this issue stays open until that fix is reviewed.

I_kwDOTe4zHc8AAAABYADqyw.title: Report crypto discovery success from the returned payment state, not from the claim path
I_kwDOTe4zHc8AAAABYADqyw.body:
**Severity:** P2. **Where:** [`src/payment_service.ts:476-477`](https://github.com/ubiquity/checkout.ubq.fi/blob/2715f7c155e8de5fea070bbb965b27bfab88c6a9/src/payment_service.ts#L476-L477)

**What happens**

Discovery can answer `discovery.found: true` alongside an `awaiting_payment` invoice. This happens when:

1. a concurrent coordinate claim records a confirming payment while discovery is still waiting on logs;
2. that transfer is then reorganised out;
3. `claimPayment()` refreshes the existing locator and clears the payment.

The success branch never looks at the invoice it got back. The caller is told the payment was found when the invoice has no payment. The interleaving was reproduced offline.

**Expected**

`found` is derived from the returned invoice: it is true only if that invoice still carries a current payment. Otherwise discovery keeps scanning. Every other path that reports success (coordinate claim, reconciliation, webhook delivery) should read the returned state the same way.

I_kwDOI-EJSM50_J5R.title: "Faucet" Service
I_kwDOI-EJSM50_J5R.body:
> Perhaps the bot can call the "invoke faucet" API endpoint when generating payment permits instead of pay.ubq.fi UI?

That's exactly what @Keyrxng proposed.

To sum up, as a part of this issue we should implement a server side app (in a cloudflare worker) which exposes a single API endpoint similar to `/?faucet?address=0x01` which accepts an address to fund.

The faucet service should have access to the bot's DB in order to fund only when:
- bounty hunter's wallet is registered in the bot's DB
- this is the 1st issue solved by a bounty hunter
- bounty hunter's wallet has 0 XDAI

We'll use this faucet service in the bot on permit generation.

# Original Specification Context

### Overview
To onboard normal developers who aren't crypto native, perhaps we can consider virtual wallets, in browser wallets, or for the most simple starting point: automatically transfer the funds if they don't have any gas. 

### Scenario
- A new user who never used Gnosis Chain before completes a task and we generate a payment permit. 
- They try and claim the permit but an error "not enough gas to claim" shows
- We should design a mechanism that will transfer the tokens to the user instead of showing the error message.

### Faucet Limitations
- We must send in xDAI not WXDAI or it does not quite solve the problem. 
- If we send the entire amount in xDAI the user might bridge out the whole amount, being left with no gas again. 
   - We might need educational materials around this. 
   - It would be great to charge users for the convenience of using this service, e.g. 1 xDAI, and also to disincentive them from using it.
