I_kwDOI-EJSM5rUgWL.title: `audit` dApp: Claim all button
I_kwDOI-EJSM5rUgWL.body:
- Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/110

When bounty hunters solve multiple permits it is hard for them to:
- find out unclaimed permits
- claim permits one by one

We should add a "Claim all" button that consolidates all their unclaimed permits in a single [Multicall](https://docs.uniswap.org/contracts/v3/reference/periphery/base/Multicall) transaction.

What should be done:
1. Add the "Claim all" button
2. On click bounty hunter should be authorized in metamask
3. Then we should find out all bounty hunter's unclaimed permits (we know his address from authorized metamask), consolidate them in a single transaction and call [Multicall](https://docs.uniswap.org/contracts/v3/reference/periphery/base/Multicall)

Notice that we support 2 networks: ethereum mainnet and gnosis so there could be unclaimed permits for both of the networks. We should somehow handle it, perhaps call 2 Multicall txs in a row. Perhaps there is a better solution.

Original [discussion](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/96)

I_kwDOI-EJSM5ouN-Z.title: Create UI for permit2 nonce invalidation
I_kwDOI-EJSM5ouN-Z.body:
This [payout page](https://pay.ubq.fi/) is responsible for bounty claims ([claim example](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/52#issuecomment-1524678816)). Bounty claims are generated with the help of the uniswap's [permit2 contract](https://github.com/Uniswap/permit2). Each issue has a unique bounty claim URL thanks to the [permit2 nonce](https://github.com/Uniswap/permit2/blob/main/src/SignatureTransfer.sol#L19).

Sometimes there are cases when we should invalidate [nonces](https://github.com/Uniswap/permit2/blob/main/src/SignatureTransfer.sol#L19) for some claim URLs in case of the bot's error or smth else. That is why we need a friendly UI for nonce invalidation.

What should be done:
1. Add a new button "invalidate" to the https://pay.ubq.fi page
2. The "invalidate" button should be visible only if the authorized wallet account equals to the permit signer and the nonce is unclaimed
3. On "invalidate" button click we should send a tx that invalidates the nonce

On-chain example of nonce invalidation [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/main/test/Permit2.t.sol#L333)

I_kwDOI-EJSM5fPfaY.title: Claim & Swap
I_kwDOI-EJSM5fPfaY.body:
I wonder if its possible to ONLY support Ubiquity Dollars internally, but to chain together a `transferFrom` and a `swap` PERMIT so that bounty hunters can "cash out" in any token they want. This way we will always get our swap fees, and in order to use our DevPool, you MUST top up with Ubiquity Dollars. 

> Another benefit to this is that we can allow for minting when we're above peg, which means that we'll be able to raise collateral and deploy it (like FRAX AMOs) to make yield. This and swap fees can be our indirect way to profit from all of this. 

We could consider leveraging transfer hooks in order to make it seem like its not a gimmick. If we have some unique capability that only exists in our Dollar and not other stablecoins then its easy to argue why we implemented our system this way.

---

Given that gas fees will be higher if we chain operations together, we should also look into ways that we can "roll up" permits. Ideally if a bounty hunter can "cash out" several permits combined into a single one then it could save on gas fees.

- [ ] Finalize architecture
- [ ] utilize Uniswap router api to estimate cash out amount in any asset
- [ ] Create cash out button to allow user to perform the swap from this UI

I_kwDOJhaJks8AAAABYALUyQ.title: Supply configured repository scope when aggregating historical backfill
I_kwDOJhaJks8AAAABYALUyQ.body:
Severity: P2. Affected revision: `1134dc365d8ba98e0d9a3afff4f279fdc2c5074a`; review round 3 of https://github.com/devpool-directory/devpool-directory/pull/6210.

The manual Backfill Historical workflow invokes aggregate without shard artifacts. Aggregate derives its allowed repository set only from shard sync metadata, so a legitimate renamed source repository is rejected even when its node identity and configured public eligibility are unchanged.

Reproduction:

1. Keep a mirror body pointing to a source repository's old name and preserve the source node identity.
2. Rename that repository to an allowed public destination and run Backfill Historical.
3. Backfill loads the new source URL, but aggregate receives no shard sync metadata and rejects the redirect with `source redirect leaves configured scope`.

Acceptance:

- Supply current public include/exclude discovery scope to aggregate for the historical backfill caller.
- Allow a node-stable redirect to an included public destination without creating a duplicate mirror.
- Continue rejecting excluded, private, unknown-scope, and mismatched-node destinations.
- Keep normal Matrix Sync scope validation intact and add a non-matrix backfill aggregation regression.

Current impact: The requested Matrix Sync full and incremental acceptance paths supply successful per-repository metadata. This finding affects the separate manual historical backfill path after a rename.

Files:

- `.github/workflows/backfill.yml:34` and aggregate invocation at lines 44-50
- `src/cli/aggregate.ts:74` through allowed scope argument at line 82
- `src/mirror/recover.ts:85`

Related historical tracking: https://github.com/devpool-directory/devpool-directory-tasks/issues/39. These closed issues cover earlier behavior; they do not track this affected revision and reproduction.

I_kwDOJhaJks8AAAABYALUdQ.title: Use current issue metadata returned by exact recovery reads
I_kwDOJhaJks8AAAABYALUdQ.body:
Severity: P2. Affected revision: `1134dc365d8ba98e0d9a3afff4f279fdc2c5074a`; review round 3 of https://github.com/devpool-directory/devpool-directory/pull/6210.

Exact recovery reads update a cached issue's state and timestamp but keep its cached labels and other metadata. Changed prices can therefore produce incorrect lifetime rewards, and removed prices can leave an issue in the open priced artifact and mirror.

Reproduction:

1. Persist an open cached issue with `Price: 75 USD` and omit it from the next shard delta.
2. Return the same issue from the exact recovery read as completed with `Price: 150 USD`; aggregate currently records $75 instead of $150.
3. Alternatively, return the source as open with no Price label; its cached price remains in `partner-open-issues.json` and can be PATCHed back onto the mirror.

Acceptance:

- Normalize current metadata from the verified exact response before reconciliation and statistics, including labels, title, assignees, canonical URL, state, and timestamps already represented by the source schema.
- Completed reward totals use the current verified price.
- An open source whose price was removed is excluded from the priced artifact and handled according to the existing unpriced mirror policy.
- Cancelled sources remain excluded from rewards and public opportunity artifacts.
- Preserve node identity, public configured scope, and source eligibility; test both scenarios through aggregate publication.

Current impact: This can affect core recovery when exact reads encounter source changes after the cached or shard snapshot. Source state closure may succeed while pricing or opportunity classification remains stale; acceptance must distinguish these surfaces.

Files:

- `src/mirror/recover.ts:75` and cached-source update at lines 105-108
- `src/cli/aggregate.ts:84` and lifetime-map update loop

Related historical tracking: https://github.com/devpool-directory/devpool-directory-tasks/issues/3, https://github.com/devpool-directory/devpool-directory-tasks/issues/30, https://github.com/devpool-directory/devpool-directory-tasks/issues/41. These closed issues cover earlier behavior; they do not track this affected revision and reproduction.

I_kwDOJhaJks8AAAABYALUGA.title: Preserve successful tweet tracking when another sync shard fails
I_kwDOJhaJks8AAAABYALUGA.body:
Severity: P2. Affected revision: `1134dc365d8ba98e0d9a3afff4f279fdc2c5074a`; review round 3 of https://github.com/devpool-directory/devpool-directory/pull/6210.

A successful shard can post a tweet before another shard fails. Aggregate then does not run, so the successful shard's tweet ID never reaches persisted `twitter-map.json`; a later run can post a duplicate and cannot clean up the untracked original.

Reproduction:

1. Use a test harness with a fake Twitter client and the existing scheduled or incremental controls enabled for two shards.
2. Let shard A post a tweet and produce its Twitter delta; make shard B fail its issue or PR fetch.
3. Observe aggregate is skipped, the posted tweet is absent from persisted tracking, and a retry sees the source as untracked.

Acceptance:

- Preserve successful side-effect receipts independently of aggregate success, or defer posts until the complete sync can commit them.
- A retry does not create duplicate tweets, and completion cleanup can find every successful post.

I_kwDOJhaJks8AAAABYAqq5Q.title: Recover tweet deletion receipts before clearing cleanup on reopen
I_kwDOJhaJks8AAAABYAqq5Q.body:
Severity: P2. Affected revision: `45f7070ff2c2b4330e69dd0a0f84a5a677de94dc`; review round 2 of https://github.com/devpool-directory/devpool-directory/pull/6213.

When a priced source reopens, aggregate clears `cleanupOnly` without resolving whether an earlier tweet deletion succeeded. If deletion succeeded but its receipt commit failed, the persisted `twitter-map.json` still references the deleted tweet, and clearing recovery state suppresses a replacement announcement.

Reproduction:

1. Use fake Twitter and storage clients with an existing announcement and a persisted cleanup marker for a closed source.
2. Let `deleteTweet` succeed, then fail the receipt commit so storage retains the deleted tweet ID and `cleanupOnly` marker.
3. Reopen the source with a Price label and retry aggregate. The affected revision removes the marker, retains the dead tweet mapping, and skips replacement creation.

A controlled two-case comparison passes on `5d1e3498836d4cb899c4070ebe5cf08598e4e65e` and fails on the affected revision with `persisted tweet receipt must not refer to a confirmed deleted tweet`. Local capture: `db7a45d4e385204a4c751b56642a3bca7c154e760ae1a7e67b8ba28776d479cd/67407724-6831-4adb-bbac-9d754241b8d2`.

Acceptance:

- Distinguish a failed deletion from a successful deletion followed by failed receipt publication.
- Resolve and persist deletion recovery, or retain its unresolved state, before clearing cleanup when a priced source reopens.
- Preserve a still-live announcement when deletion failed; restore one valid announcement after confirmed deletion without duplicate posts or a mapping to a deleted tweet.
- Cover both failure windows and repeat retries with fake Twitter calls and persisted receipt assertions.

I_kwDOUS-HkM8AAAABYAgFrg.body:

Preserve a bounded recovery artifact for failed/interrupted implementation attempts so a trusted continuation can use verified context and partial work after the ephemeral runner exits. This is queued for trusted owner implementation and excluded from autonomous admission; #53 retained advisory failure summaries, which do not establish resumable session state.

Evidence: run [39080597401](https://github.com/ubiquity/sentinel/actions/runs/39080597401), runtime `e48e7e110e7cb2ed3385bf1be5165f05d8a4e481`, had three interrupted turns at the four-million-event-character bound and no candidate bundles. Existing result artifacts are useful accounting evidence but cannot by themselves resume an app-server session or explain/recover partial work. This proposal does not assert that those historical runners or contexts are recoverable.

Acceptance:
- Define a sanitized recovery manifest binding run/attempt, task, reservation, exact base/runtime, submitted model/effort, protocol identity, terminal/settlement evidence and any verified partial patch/checkpoint. Keep advisory context separate from candidate or merge authority.
- Before runner teardown, preserve only the minimum resumable context/partial work through an explicitly scoped private artifact path with bounded retention and integrity checks. Never place raw transcripts, diagnostics, credentials or restricted originals in public Git or issue bodies.
- Prove whether the installed app-server supports resuming from the preserved state on a fresh runner; a thread ID alone is insufficient. When it does not, use a clearly identified fresh continuation with sanitized context instead of claiming a resumed session.
- Resume only after the original process group has settled, revalidate current source/base and target ownership, and use existing durable admission for any new inference. Preserve original charges and history; no duplicate start, silent refund, credential transfer or replay of effects.
- Exercise interruption, teardown, restart, missing/expired/tampered artifacts and changed-base refusal using real production consumers with fake external/model ports. Keep candidate validation, review, CI and publication gates intact.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABYAaxPA.title: Follow-up from #1159: coordinate signing-helper migration with active legacy rebuilds (P3)
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABYAaxPA.body:
PR #1159 contains the protected-path follow-ups for #1141. This issue tracks its remaining P3 integration finding, independently reproduced on the reviewed PR source. The conflict with #1156 was resolved in `d0595ccbbb30201689f044649d868f87493415ba`; it is not outstanding work.

### P3: migration cleanup interrupts an in-flight legacy signing helper

**Where:** [`ops/gpg-dsh.sh:136-149`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/d0595ccbbb30201689f044649d868f87493415ba/ops/gpg-dsh.sh#L136-L149), especially the unconditional deletion of the legacy lock and staging/set-aside directories at lines 143-145.

The first invocation of the new per-user-layout helper removes the legacy helper's seed, lock, and staging directories without coordinating with an old helper that is still rebuilding. If an old invocation is paused after acquiring its lock and creating its stage, the new helper deletes both. When the old invocation resumes, its copy or rename fails and that signing exits 2. The new helper succeeds, and subsequent invocations use the new layout normally. This is a one-time upgrade availability failure; the fixture does not demonstrate leaked keys or a bad signature.

**Original finding, preserved from the handoff:**

> The resolution adds code that neither parent has. The legacy cleanup now also removes <uid>.lock, <uid>.new.* and <uid>.old.* under the old $TMPDIR/dsh-gnupg parent (lines 136-149). It does this without holding a lock. It also calls rmdir on the parent even when there is no legacy seed, which reviewed head 2892d609 only did together with removing the seed. The change is disclosed, tested, and consistent with what #1141 intends, so it is integration glue and not a lost behaviour.

> Only possible while upgrading. Suppose a #1139-era installed helper is part-way through a rebuild under $TMPDIR/dsh-gnupg/<uid>.lock when the first call of the newly installed helper runs. The new call deletes that lock and the staging copy, so the old call's mv fails and that one signing exits 2. Every later call works. Reviewed head 2892d609 already had the same window for removing <uid> itself, so the size of the exposure is unchanged.

**Evidence and provenance:**

- Retained source: [`handoff/2026-10-18/reports/protected-finish.json`, `result.check`](https://github.com/ubiquity/sentinel/blob/be02faf40c77fe299c2ed7ffa91fedb00fe43c48/handoff/2026-10-18/reports/protected-finish.json). That review returned PASS, with this P3 and the now-resolved #1156 conflict.
- Original integration reviewed head: `77d3f7c56a86094ecc28c7086e17b2b1efdcb60b`; base: `b24353e5caffc8ec2f935bfcbbe3b7f441dd1aa7`. The retained report does not record the original review command or model identity; those are unavailable, not inferred.
- Independently reproduced on the documentation-resolution head `d0595ccbbb30201689f044649d868f87493415ba` against legacy helper `ed0ecdda85ee261bc8388558bb26c2c86f5ac9a5`, using fixture key strings and fake gpg/gpgconf. The helper is byte-identical on latest-base head `0a7063f994f39d958476d9257c2eef7ce9a7abc9`. A cp wrapper paused the old helper after its lock and stage existed. The new helper exited 0 and removed both; releasing the old helper made it exit 2 with `cp: cannot create regular file .../dsh-gnupg/<uid>.new.*/pubring.kbx: No such file or directory` and `gpg-dsh: cannot copy ... into ...`.
- All fixture paths were under `/workspace/evidence/finish-1159/migration-race-probe`, and the bounded probe did not read or chdir under `/tmp`.
- Actual local review mode was attempted with `codex review --base origin/development` (CLI 0.159.2, printed model `gpt-6.1-sol`, head `d0595ccbbb30201689f044649d868f87493415ba`, base `05260bfe0ac835af0742bc0d116650a6aeb98c74`). It exited 1 before review because authentication returned HTTP 401. No findings were ingested from that failed attempt and no credentials were changed.

**Acceptance:** Coordinate migration with active legacy invocations, or document and enforce an installation quiescence step. Add a deterministic fixture that pauses a live legacy rebuild, invokes the new helper, then resumes the legacy call and proves it is not interrupted. Preserve removal of abandoned legacy key copies, ownership checks, config-file refusal, and the existing per-user layout.

Related #1168 tracks stale-lock recovery and publication races within the helper. This issue is specifically cross-version migration cleanup; do not duplicate that issue's P2/P3 findings. Merging this PR does not install the helper on the owner's Mac.

I_kwDOORydAM8AAAABYCLbNg.title: Keep HTTP diagnostic Boolean parsing consistent for n
I_kwDOORydAM8AAAABYCLbNg.body:
The HTTP diagnostics DO candidate uses different Boolean parsers for refresh and health snapshot identities. `RPC_VALIDATE_CHAIN_ID=n` is false in `createRuntime()` but true in `worker.ts`, so successful refreshes write a false-validation fingerprint while `/health` reads a true-validation fingerprint and reports missing diagnostics.

Affected revision: `641918b3e6e375f77addaefda8728726466f8f3c` in PR #30, matching reviewed source manifest `6e011049766df6df0aba2beb4169344d93f81701d7ebb319979223375145f985`. Actual local review round 3 identified this single P2, with no P0/P1. Static evidence: `runtime.ts` accepts `false`, `0`, `no`, `n`, `off`; the Worker parser omits `n`.

Reproduction: in the existing isolated workerd/SQLite fixture, set `RPC_VALIDATE_CHAIN_ID=n`, send a successful `eth_chainId` request to `/1`, then read `/health` in the same version/colo. The refresh fingerprint uses `validateChainId=false`, while the snapshot read uses `true`; chain diagnostics/`lastTested` are consequently missing. These reproduction steps were not executed during issue delivery.

Current exposure: the target `wrangler.jsonc` declares no `RPC_VALIDATE_CHAIN_ID` value, so the unchanged default is true in both paths and is not affected. This issue concerns the supported optional `n` value, including case/whitespace variants, not a failure demonstrated under the default deployment configuration. No source fix is included in the current delivery round.

Acceptance:
- Refresh and read-only health use identical Boolean parsing for every supported true/false alias and case/whitespace variant; unset still defaults to true.
- A native workerd regression with `RPC_VALIDATE_CHAIN_ID=n` retains diagnostics/`lastTested` after a successful read, without `/health` refreshing diagnostics or writing snapshot rows.
- Preserve diagnostic checks, wire behavior, the shared 50-call ledger and default configuration; do not add a new flag.

Files:
- `packages/permit2-rpc-server/src/worker.ts:55-56`
- `packages/permit2-rpc-server/src/runtime.ts:29-35`
- `packages/permit2-rpc-server/src/infra/worker-diagnostics-client.ts` and `worker-diagnostics-object.ts` (identity plumbing)

I_kwDOTe4zHc8AAAABYDF6rw.title: Reverify quarantined inclusions after canonical RPC recovery
I_kwDOTe4zHc8AAAABYDF6rw.body:
A fresh account hunt must be able to reverify an inclusion that was previously quarantined after a transient canonical RPC mismatch or an orphaned block becoming canonical again. At draft PR #6 revision `e5fdf8c4d48a4b947fe66841e5eab5e7ae3c5a3b`, repeated hunts returning that same inclusion skip verification and stay pending.

Severity: P2 (payment-discovery availability/recovery). This draft has not been deployed or merged.

Evidence: the inclusion key contains chain, transaction hash, log index and block hash. A canonical contradiction persists the key; incomplete restarts retain it. The quarantine guard then calls `invalidateCoverage()` and skips the claim path, preventing completion and its normal reset. An unpaid attempt cannot use the known-payment refresh path to recover. A changed block hash or a later pass without the inclusion may escape this state, so this is specifically a repeated-same-inclusion recovery defect. The dedicated third review reported an in-memory base/candidate reproduction; the independent follow-up substantiated the source path without rerunning that reproduction. Existing 247 offline tests and the workerd harness pass but do not cover canonical recovery of the same quarantined inclusion.

Acceptance:

- Add a regression that first quarantines an inclusion, then restores consistent canonical RPC data and returns that same inclusion on a later related-event hunt; verify the payment can recover.
- Reverify fresh evidence without deleting historical contradiction records or allowing stale/incomplete coverage to release an earlier reservation.
- Preserve confirming/credit rules, ownership, idempotency and request headroom.
- Recover only through allowed events; add no cron, polling, sweep or new-payment alarm.
- Pass `bun run check`, including the real workerd harness.

Files:

- [src/account_runtime.ts:308](https://github.com/ubiquity/checkout.ubq.fi/blob/e5fdf8c4d48a4b947fe66841e5eab5e7ae3c5a3b/src/account_runtime.ts#L308): retained incomplete run.

- `src/account_review_regression_test.ts`: recovery regression coverage.

I_kwDOL-In888AAAABYIHjGQ.title: Make successful pull-request ownership decisions observable
I_kwDOL-In888AAAABYIHjGQ.body:
The pull-request ownership handler silently returns after allowing an assigned author or a non-contributor to keep a PR open. Expose that completed decision through the existing comment interface so operators can distinguish actual ownership processing from a missing invocation, while preserving the existing assignment, start and close rules.

Acceptance:

- Emit a truthful, sanitized receipt containing the actual event snapshot, PR/head/base/author and leave-open decision; do not invent delivery, invocation or build identifiers.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABYLkgGA.title: Review finding: Allow create retries after a rejected preparation
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABYLkgGA.body:
Status: **Reproduced review finding; fix pending**. A separate correction execution reproduced this finding on the unchanged reviewed implementation. This record preserves the original review and will carry subsequent correction verification.

Review priority: **P2**. Finding confidence: **0.98**.

Reviewed published module: [f424de7fb91d26adcb835e65115afd01cd1ac784](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/f424de7fb91d26adcb835e65115afd01cd1ac784). Location: [src/authority/native-authority-principals.ts:514-516](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/f424de7fb91d26adcb835e65115afd01cd1ac784/src/authority/native-authority-principals.ts#L514-L516).

Actual local review target/security argv: `codex --sandbox read-only --ask-for-approval never exec review --commit f424de7fb91d26adcb835e65115afd01cd1ac784`. Invocation-only scope/MCP settings and private output paths are retained in the command evidence. Actual reviewer: `gpt-6-astra`, effort `max`, provider `uos`; one review invocation, command exit **0**.

Original overall verdict: **patch is incorrect**, confidence **0.98**. The reviewer inspected source and archived checks without rerunning tests.

Original finding title (verbatim):

```text
[P2] Allow create retries after a rejected preparation
```

Original finding text (verbatim):

```text
If `_create` rejects before returning its commit closure—for example, because the SQLite transaction persisting its preparation fails—the rejected promise remains in `_creating`, whose entry is removed only on success. Every subsequent retry with the same operation ID awaits that already-rejected promise, so recovery of the underlying storage does not recover the operation without reconstructing the authority. Failed preparation needs a recoverable in-flight state rather than a permanently cached rejection.
```

Reproduction evidence:

Actual SQLite RED witness: retrying the same operation ID on the same authority retained the injected synthetic preparation fault after its trigger was removed. The native run reported 22 prior controls passing and three new regressions failing; exit 1 is the expected RED result. Receipt: `591bceabb6cc0ae63ee09ee9914b02c17ad0b9b53f9be3f4389670cde15755a5/d4e84b1e-5c2c-4e4d-afe5-9822bbd0f1a1`. This issue publisher read the saved output without rerunning tests.

Acceptance:

- Retain the supplied preparation-failure/storage-recovery RED regression and require correction verification to pass it.
- A corrected implementation must allow the same operation ID to progress on the existing authority after transient preparation recovery.
- Preserve successful duplicate coalescing, material binding and idempotent commit behavior.

[P1] Serialize concurrent replays of deletion cleanup

```text
If `deleteKey` is retried with the same operation ID while its original `cleanupApiLogs` call is pending, both invocations execute cleanup independently. The faster invocation clears the receipt and publishes `completed_at_ms` while the slower cleanup remains active. That makes the local completion tombstone unsafe: reprovisioning can proceed while an old key-scoped cleanup can still remove replacement state. Coalesce cleanup execution per deletion owner before publishing completion, as required by the [local deletion contract](docs/DECISIONS.md#L1893-L1898).
```

Acceptance:

- Retain the supplied controlled concurrent-cleanup RED regression and require correction verification to pass it.
- A corrected implementation must publish completion only after the deletion owner cleanup settles, preventing a late replayed cleanup from removing replacement state.
- Preserve key-wide cleanup, retry/ownership binding and safe reprovisioning semantics.

```text

```

I_kwDOUS-HkM8AAAABYhPoxw.body:
`hosted_runtime_summary` (one plain-English JSON line per runtime child, added 2026-10-20) is emitted per child invocation only. A supervisor run with matrix cells produces one summary per cell plus one for the repair aggregator, and the finalize job records none of them, so an operator reading a run still has to open several job logs to learn what the run did.

Expected: the finalize job of `.github/workflows/supervisor.yml`'s trusted launcher (`src/host/actions-supervisor*.ts`, finalize path) collects the per-child summaries from the run's job logs or uploaded artifacts and emits exactly one `hosted_runtime_run_summary` line (and a GitHub step summary) with: run/attempt, launcher and runtime SHAs, generation, purpose, per-target admitted/skipped counts, model starts, PRs touched with actions, outcome, and a one-sentence explanation plus next action. Unknown counts stay null; the line is advisory and grants no health or accounting authority. I_kwDOUS-HkM8AAAABYhPn-Q.title: Classify event-scoped CI aborts as configuration defects instead of charging CI-fix retries
I_kwDOUS-HkM8AAAABYhPn-Q.body:
When a required CI check fails on a repair candidate's head but the same check passed on the base, `src/repair/ci-rejection.ts` attributes the failure to the candidate and the CI-fix route starts a model retry. On 2026-10-20 every ai.ubq.fi repair PR (#1254–#1258) failed `rust-native`, `rust-wasm` and `validate` because the target workflow only exported `GITHUB_PR_AUTHOR` to its scope job, so downstream jobs aborted with "No Rust work selected" before running anything. The base's green result came from a `push` event with a different scope, so the comparison was not like-for-like. Each CI-fix worker correctly edited the target workflow and was then blocked by the protected-path rule, consuming a CI retry per PR and leaving the records blocked.

Expected: when a head check fails and the only green base evidence comes from a different event type (push vs pull_request), or when the failing job's log matches a configuration-abort signature (no work selected, scope mismatch, setup failure before the test command), classify it as `ci_configuration` instead of a candidate defect: do not charge a CI-fix retry, park the record with the reason, and raise one deduplicated follow-up issue on the target for the owner. Add a fake-transport regression in `tests/repair/` that feeds a green push-event base run and a failed pull_request head run with that log signature and asserts no model start and the parked reason.
